title: [MERGED #10120] Three 012-Views citation sites adjudicated separately — worker overturned the brief on two of three
description:
Three further sites cite `tools/xray/spec/012-Views.md` as a live authority for designs its own
SUPERSEDED banner lists as **NOT implemented**. Found by rf2-mfy9a's worker while adjudicating
`018:2113`, named and deliberately NOT edited; re-derived by the mayor at trunk `84759441e4`,
uncapped, repo-wide with the tracker export excluded.

**THEY ARE THREE DIFFERENT STRENGTHS OF CLAIM BEHIND ONE SPELLING, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS ONE ITEM
RATHER THAN A SWEEP.** A pattern-driven fix would edit all three identically and be wrong about two
of them. Adjudicate each and say which it is; dropping a citation is an acceptable outcome, and so is
leaving one standing with the reasoning recorded.

**THE AUTHORITY.** `tools/xray/spec/012-Views.md:2-16` is a SUPERSEDED banner pointing at
`021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §3 (rf2-ee38b.2, 2026-05-23). It enumerates what is **NOT implemented**
and **not the destination**, and the list includes, verbatim: *"three TEMPORAL groups (mounted /
re-rendered / unmounted), **subs nested under views with inline return values**, ≥50 grid clustering,
a component/sub group-by toggle, a right-click component-filter chip, per-component inline drilldown
(props-diff + Fiber metadata), and the five-state sub-status glyph taxonomy"*. It also states the
cited file names do not exist and names the live panel as `panels/reactive_panel_view.cljs` +
`panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs`.

## The three sites

**(1) `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:654` — UNAMBIGUOUS, and the strongest of the three.**
Verbatim:

    **Subs are folded into Views** — subs nest under each view row, not a separate tab. See [`012-Views.md`](012-Views.md).

**It asserts the nested-under-views design and cites, as its authority, the banner that lists that
exact design as NOT implemented.** This is the defect of rf2-mfy9a and rf2-m1qh0 word for word, one
site further on. Prose, not in a fence. It sits in a run of "folded into" statements at `:652`-`:656`
(Effects, Subs, Performance) — **the neighbours are about the Epoch panel and Chrome DevTools and are
NOT in scope**; only the Subs line cites 012.

**(2) `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:1083` — GENUINELY ARGUABLE. Adjudicate; do not assume.**
Inside a blockquote at `:1076`-`:1084`, verbatim:

    > The Views tab still exists and still owns the per-view / per-sub lens
    > ([`012-Views.md`](012-Views.md)) — what is false is that the Epoch
    > panel withholds the steps.

The passage is **already drawing a careful distinction** — it is correcting a different false claim,
and the 012 citation is incidental to its argument. The question is narrow: does the Views tab still
own a "per-view / per-sub lens"? `021` §3.2 at `:565`-`:567` retired the SUB VALUES section from that
tab under rf2-uz3wm, so the per-SUB half is at least doubtful; the per-VIEW half may well stand.
**A correction here may be re-pointing the citation rather than deleting the sentence.**

**(3) `tools/xray/spec/016-Auxiliary-Panels.md:946` — WEAKEST, AND POSSIBLY CORRECT AS IT STANDS.**
Verbatim:

    - [`012-Views.md`](./012-Views.md) — Views tab content.

A see-also pointer in a cross-reference list. **Pointing a reader at a superseded document is not the
same as asserting its content is live**, and the banner is the first thing that reader meets. The
case for touching it at all is that "Views tab content" reads as a description of current behaviour;
the case against is that a supersession pointer is exactly how a reader should reach a superseded
doc. **Rule it either way with the reasoning recorded — "leave it" is a real answer here.**

## Scope

**IN:** the three sites above, each adjudicated separately. **OUT:** `012-Views.md` itself (its banner
is correct and is what makes the others wrong); `021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md`; `018:2113`, `:634`,
`:2283`, `:76`, `:98`, `:127` (all corrected by merged PRs, and `:2113` by the PR this item is fenced
behind); `019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md:821` (rf2-qrjr5, landed). Do not renumber or reorder tables.

**Read what the landed siblings did and match their facts** — rf2-m1qh0 (PR #10111) corrected `:634`
and `:2283`; rf2-qrjr5 (PR #10108) corrected `019:821`; rf2-mfy9a corrected `:2113`. **Four specs
disagreeing about one supersession is worse than any single wording.**

## Census

`012-Views.md` is cited across this tree far more widely than these three lines, and **most of those
citations are fine** — a document being superseded does not make every reference to it wrong. The
question is never "does this line cite 012" but **"does this line assert, as live, something the
banner lists as NOT implemented"**. Sweep for the banner's own enumerated items — `nested under`,
`inline return values`, `grid clustering`, `group-by toggle`, `component-filter chip`, `sub-status`,
`mounted / re-rendered / unmounted` — rather than for the filename, and **name the root you swept
from**: a sibling item's sixth instance survived five PRs because every census was rooted at
`tools/xray/spec/` and the site sat one level up. **Never cap a locator.**

## Gates

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers `tools/*/spec` and is the live gate for both paths.
`mkdocs build --strict` stages `spec` and `migration` and **no `tools/` tree** — wrong gate, say so.
`check_readme_links.py --ci` **excludes all of `tools/*/spec/`** — say so.
**Nothing grades whether the prose is true**, and nothing grades table shape. **Count the link tokens
on each line you actually edit, after editing, and say LIVE or VACUOUS per line** — this doc family
has produced vacuous, live, vacuous-twice-over and live-only-after-the-edit on consecutive items, and
`:654`, `:1083` and `946` all carry a link, so a plant can land on the edited line itself. **The
control is the deliverable: show the gate red at exit 1 naming file and line, confirming the plant's
match count is 1 beforehand, restore, and verify against the committed blob.**

## File health

Both files are `i/lf w/crlf` — verify with `git ls-files --eol`. **Never `sed -i`.** Edit with the
Edit tool and take THREE numbers with Python on the bytes before and after — total CR, total CRLF,
bare LF — requiring CR == CRLF and bare LF == 0. A two-number check passes vacuously as `0 == 0` on a
flattened file.

description:
Shortlist item 14 of the rf2-pk4i6 senior-review wave. Size L. Source: rf2-pk4i6.1#5. **Mike ruled OPTION A.**

His recorded ruling, verbatim:

> **Item 14 (a superseded read voids its reply-to): A.** On supersession, fold the prior record's reply targets onto the superseding record (three lines; `add-reply-target` already dedupes; exactly-once holds; never stale data) and amend spec 016 at the superseded-attempt sentence to *"a superseded attempt hands its continuation to its successor"*. Reason: the read was actually caused and its continuation should arrive; making the programmer work around a void is the friction the stance rejects.

That decision is made and is not yours to reopen. If you come to believe B is better, say so in the PR body as a recommendation and build A.

## The defect

A machine that `ensure`s with `:reply-to` on a polled resource may **never receive its continuation**. A poll, focus scan, invalidation or manual refetch supersedes the in-flight attempt; the fresher attempt settles the same key and delivers to nobody; the workflow hangs, with only a generic `:rf.resource/stale-suppressed` to show for it.

## THE THING THAT MAKES THIS ITEM DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER ONE ON THIS WAVE

**The code is CORRECT against the spec today, and a test PINS the current behaviour.** The reviewer says so outright, and the triage's re-verification note reads: *"no — the reviewer states the code matches the spec; nothing to check but the ruling."*

So this is not a bug fix. **It is a deliberate change to a specified behaviour, ruled by the operator.** Two consequences you must not get wrong:

* **The existing pin is not wrong and must not be deleted as though it were.** It encodes the OLD contract. Change it to encode the new one, and say in the PR body which test moved and why — that it was pinning a behaviour the operator has now changed, not that it was broken.
* **`spec/016-Resources.md` must move in the SAME commit as the code.** If the code delivers a continuation the spec says is voided, the tree contradicts itself. The ruling names the sentence to amend and gives its replacement wording: *"a superseded attempt hands its continuation to its successor."*

## What to build

On supersession, fold the prior record's `:reply-targets` onto the superseding record. The ruling calls it three lines and notes that `add-reply-target` **already dedupes**, so exactly-once still holds and no stale data is delivered — the continuation arrives from the fresher attempt.

**Verify all three of those claims at tip before relying on them:** that `add-reply-target` dedupes, that exactly-once survives the fold, and that the superseding record cannot deliver data older than the target expects. The ruling asserts them; it did not measure them. The measured premise-failure rate on this wave is roughly one in fourteen citations, and today alone one item's headline seam was refuted outright by measurement.

**PR #9900 (shortlist item 9, rf2-pkkft) has just rewritten this artefact.** It replaced the optimistic remove's `dissoc` with a tombstone written in place, retired the `:rf.optimistic/removed` sentinel, and collapsed `optimistic-conflict?` from two branches to one. Read #9900's diff before you start; if your fold interacts with the tombstone or with the ledger bound, say so in the PR body rather than letting two guarantees meet silently.

**Yours when it does go out:** `implementation/resources/src/**`, the resources test tree, `spec/016-Resources.md`, and the EP-0019 wording if the supersession sentence appears there too.

title: schemas: the schema digest is not process-stable for fn-bearing schemas and diverges JVM/CLJS on whole-number doubles, faking Deploy drift (rf2-pk4i6 item 12)
description:
Shortlist item 12 of the rf2-pk4i6 senior-review wave (from rf2-pk4i6.13#1). Mike ruled the whole shortlist as actioned; this is the filed follow-on. Size M.

## The defect

The schema digest is not process-stable for ANY schema carrying a function, and it diverges JVM-to-CLJS on whole-number doubles. The SSR check therefore reports "Deploy drift" on identical bundles.

`[:map [:n pos-int?]]` — the idiom the how-to recommends — prints with the JVM's per-process identity hash. So a JVM ring server and a CLJS client disagree on EVERY hydrate, and the dev warning sends the reader off to compare bundles that are byte-identical.

`spec/010` (around :495) promises "cross-runtime reproducible ... byte-for-byte".

## The triage's citations (claims, to be opened at tip before editing)

- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc:82-101` — `canonicalise-schema-form` passes non-collections through unchanged.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc:103-119` — and then `pr-str`s them.
- `implementation/ssr/.../hydrate.cljc:550-575` — the consequence is a `:warning` reading "Deploy drift ... Hydrating anyway", i.e. a wrong nag rather than a refusal.
- `spec/010` §Digest and the byte-for-byte promise near :495.

Re-verified by the reviewer: YES. Anchor to CONTENT, not to line numbers.

## What the triage proposes (a proposal, verified before obeyed)

In `canonicalise-schema-form`:
- map a `fn?` value to a stable token — class name on the JVM, `.-name` on CLJS, `#fn` as the fallback;
- print integer-valued doubles as integers, per the CEDN-1 rule.

Then:
- add two parity fixtures — a `pos-int?` map, and a `{:min 1.0}` props map. `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas/digest_parity_test.clj` already exists and is where they belong.
- note in `spec/010` §Digest that a fn-bearing schema digest is host-specific under `:advanced` munging.

The once-per-process reg-time warning (the reviewer's option B) is to be taken ONLY if the printer fix is not taken. Do not build both.

## The part most likely to bite

The `#fn` fallback and the `.-name` route are not equivalent under `:advanced` munging, which is exactly why the spec note is part of the deliverable rather than an afterthought: the digest becomes stable per-host, not identical across hosts, for fn-bearing schemas. If the parity fixtures show that a fn-bearing schema still cannot agree JVM-to-CLJS, that is the finding — report it with the evidence rather than inventing a third mechanism to force agreement.

## Surface and fences

Yours: `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc`, `implementation/schemas/test/**` (notably `digest_parity_test.clj`), and `spec/010`.

You hold `spec/010` exclusively. Item 13 is live in the same artefact but in `walker.cljc` and `storage.cljc`, and is fenced OUT of `validator.cljc` and out of `spec/010` — if you find you need either of those two files, stop and tell the mayor rather than editing across the fence.

`implementation/ssr/**` is read-only for you: `hydrate.cljc` is cited as the consequence, not as a site to change.

Not yours: `implementation/core/**`, `implementation/epoch/**` and `spec/002` (item 7 is live there); `implementation/resources/**` and `spec/016` (item 11 is live there). `spec/API.md` and its manifest sidecars are hot-zone: report, do not edit.

FENCE (2026-09-16 17:29 AUSEST). Held by a live worker in C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/digestparity-k0hqk on branch worker/digestparity-k0hqk.
Do not dispatch a second worker onto this bead or that branch until it reports, or until the mayor records its death here.
Release: a completion report, or a recorded death.
The worker holds implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc, implementation/schemas/test/**, and spec/010 for the duration.
WORKER VERDICT (PR #9894, branch worker/digestparity-k0hqk) — printer fix taken, option B not built.

TRIAGE PREMISES: both citations verified true at tip. `canonicalise-schema-form`'s `:else form`
does pass functions through and `compute-edn-print` does `pr-str` them; `hydrate.cljc`'s
`check-schema-digest-fx` does emit a `:warning` reading "Deploy drift ... Hydrating anyway"
(a wrong nag, not a refusal); `spec/010` did promise "cross-runtime reproducible ... byte-for-byte"
without qualification. Measured pre-fix on the JVM: `[:map [:n pos-int?]]` printed
`#object[clojure.core$pos_int_QMARK_ 0x3aefae67 "...@3aefae67"]`, the address being
`System/identityHashCode` — fresh in every process.

ONE SUB-TASK PREMISE WAS WRONG AND WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A MIS-JUSTIFIED FIX. The triage said to print
integer-valued doubles as integers "per the CEDN-1 rule". THERE IS NO SUCH CEDN-1 RULE — CEDN-1
REJECTS floating-point values outright (`bad-number?` in `re-frame.identity` fails them closed as
`:rf.error/non-edn-identity`), and `spec/012-Routing.md` states the divergence in terms: "an
integer-valued 2.0 is even admitted by CEDN on CLJS but rejected on the JVM". The fix DIRECTION is
right, but its justification is that CLJS physically cannot spell the JVM's `1.0`, not that CEDN-1
asks for it. This matters practically: routing schema forms through `canonical-bytes` — the obvious
"reuse the existing canonicaliser" move — would FAIL CLOSED on a legal Malli schema, converting a
wrong warning into a crash. The fix therefore has to live in the digest's own canonicaliser.

THE HEADLINE FINDING, MEASURED ON BOTH RUNTIMES RATHER THAN INFERRED. The two sub-defects are not
the same kind of thing and do not end in the same place.

  * WHOLE-NUMBER DOUBLES: the hosts NOW AGREE. One shared pinned literal (sha256:256998dfe0d8dc71)
    rides in `all-fixtures` and is reached by both the JVM lane and the CLJS lane.

  * FN-BEARING SCHEMAS: the hosts DO NOT AGREE — each merely stays stable. The token is the host's
    own name for the function: JVM `#fn[clojure.core$pos_int_QMARK_]` against CLJS
    `#fn[cljs$core$pos_int_QMARK_]`. The CLJS half is a measurement, not a deduction: the compiled
    node-test output emits `function cljs$core$pos_int_QMARK_` as a NAMED declaration, so `.-name`
    returns a real name (which is also why the CLJS discrimination assertion passes). An `:advanced`

title: core/epoch: a drain of exactly :drain-depth events halts as a runaway and commits a phantom halt record that blocks restore (rf2-pk4i6 item 7)
description:
Shortlist item 7 of the rf2-pk4i6 senior-review wave (from rf2-pk4i6.2#1 and rf2-pk4i6.10#3). Mike ruled the whole shortlist as actioned; this is the filed follow-on. Size M.

## The defect

`run-one-pass!` tests depth BEFORE looking at the queue, so a clean cascade of exactly `:drain-depth` events halts as a runaway: 16 events under `:story`, 100 under the default. The frame reports an always-on `:rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded` with `:rf.epoch/outcome :blocked`, and the halt record names as its "halting event" the event that had just settled `:ok`.

The epoch side then compounds it: that phantom halt record moves the anchor, after which `restore-epoch!` of the NEWEST epoch is refused — although the state it names is the live state.

## The triage's citations (claims, to be opened at tip before editing)

- `router.cljc:3695` — `(>= depth drain-depth)` is the first `cond` arm.
- `router.cljc:3733` — `take-event!`, i.e. the queue is consulted only after the depth test.
- `router.cljc:3363-3371` — documents the empty-queue fallback as "defensive".
- `spec/002-Frames.md:1998-2006` — the pseudocode comment describing the drain.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/drain_test.clj:264` — the neighbouring pin.

Re-verified by the reviewer: YES for the router half (the three router citations were re-read). Anchor to CONTENT, not to line numbers.

## What the triage proposes (a proposal, verified before obeyed)

One fix in the router:
- peek first, and halt only when there IS a next event;
- drop the `last-event` fallback in `handle-depth-exceeded!` once it is unreachable;
- adjust the `002:1998-2006` pseudocode comment to match;
- add an "exactly N events, settles, no halt" pin beside `drain_test.clj:264`.

Two independent epoch hardenings (~5 lines each):
- `commit-halt-record!` commits nothing when there is no halting envelope;
- `commit-frame-owner-record!` does not move `last-settled-epoch` for a non-`:ok` record.

The two epoch hardenings are independent of the router fix and of each other: each is worth landing on its own merit even if the router fix alone would mask the symptom.

## Pins

The deliverable is a pin that reds against the unfixed tree. "Exactly N, settles, no halt" is the router pin. The epoch hardenings want their own coverage: a halt record committed with no halting envelope, and a non-`:ok` record that must not move `last-settled-epoch`.

## Surface and fences

Yours: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc`, `implementation/epoch/src/**` (notably `state.cljc`), `implementation/core/test/**`, the epoch test tree, and `spec/002-Frames.md`.

`spec/002-Frames.md` is hot-zone and you hold it exclusively — change the cited pseudocode comment as this bead specifies rather than rewriting the section.

Not yours: `implementation/resources/**` and `spec/016` (item 11 is live there); `implementation/schemas/**` and `spec/010` (items 12 and 13 are live there). `spec/API.md` and its manifest sidecars are hot-zone: report, do not edit.

Citations re-verified at content, not by line number:
- router.cljc: `(>= depth drain-depth)` IS the first `cond` arm, and `take-event!`

that the halt discards "the remaining queued events (the next, *halting* event never
runs)" — which presupposes a next event. So the implementation was diverging from the
SPEC, not merely from intuition. That made the fix direction unambiguous.

The three fixes:
1. router `run-one-pass!` — the depth arm is now `(and (>= depth drain-depth) (seq
   (:queue @router)))`. Not on the hot path: `and` short-circuits, so the queue read
   happens at most once per drain.
2. router `handle-depth-exceeded!` — the `last-event` fallback DROPPED. The guard above
   makes it unreachable (only the drainer pops, and nothing pops between the two peeks).
3. epoch `commit-halt-record!` commits nothing when `trigger-event` is nil (buffer is
   still harvested — residual-capture clearing is a separate hygiene property);
   epoch `commit-frame-owner-record!` moves `last-settled-epoch` only for an `:ok`
   record. The halt record is STILL appended to the ring and still reported as the
   dispatch's commit observation, so devtools keep their "drain halted here" marker.

NOTHING depended on the old halt-record shape. `commit-halt-record!` has exactly one
production caller (the router, via the `:epoch/commit-halt-record!` late-bind hook) and
no test called it directly. `commit-frame-owner-record!`'s other caller,
`record-synthetic-replace-epoch!`, builds with outcome `:ok` and still anchors. No test
anywhere asserted an anchor moving onto a non-`:ok` record.

`drain-depth-halts-after-exactly-drain-depth-events` drives a RUNAWAY cascade, which
always has a pending event at the halt seam. The defect lived only in the TERMINATING
case, which that pin cannot reach. The new pin drives a cascade that stops.

- epoch `epoch_test.clj`: three deftests beside the existing depth-0 phantom-anchor
  gates. 7 failing assertions before the fix, including the headline — `restore-epoch!`
  of the anchored epoch refused with `:rf.epoch/restore-non-ok-record` although the
  state it named was the live state.
Every pin asserts its own preconditions, and the `commit-halt-record!` pin carries an
inline control (the same call WITH a halting event does commit), so none can pass
vacuously.

False: Part 3 itself returns `:sensitive [[:auth :token]]` beside `:db` and calls it a commit-plane effect (`03-auth-and-forms.md:373` and `:430`). 3. `:revalidate-on` and the never-stale-when-omitted default are not taught anywhere in 01–05. title: http managed-machine wrapper declares no :final? state, so the :spawn-all join recipe never resolves (rf2-fzbj.16 F3)
description:
FILED 2026-09-13 by the mayor, routed out of PR #9773 (skillsc-a). rf2-fzbj.16 STAYS OPEN for this finding — it is F3, the one thing that worker could not do, because the repair is a library change and its fence was `skills/re-frame2/**`.

THE DEFECT. `skills/re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md` puts two `:rf.http/managed` children under `:spawn-all` and promises each reaches a `:final?` state. The shipped wrapper HAS NO `:final?` STATE AT ALL, so that join never resolves. The recipe is unresolvable as published.

EVIDENCE, measured rather than argued. `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/machine_wrapper.cljc:89-95` declares `:succeeded` and `:failed` as `{:entry :dispatch-done/:dispatch-error :meta {:terminal? true}}` — neither declares `:final?` or `:output-key`. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:3866` settles that these are not synonyms in as many words: "`:meta {:terminal? true}` on such a leaf is redundant with `:final?`; declare `:final?` alone." The review's runtime probe shows both requests firing, both children reaching `:succeeded`, and the parent stuck in `:hydrating` with `:done #{}` and `:resolved? false`; its control, changing only the two terminal states, reaches `:done` with the children torn down.

`implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_machine_cljs_test.cljs:60-62` PINS the non-final shape, so this is a real integration gap and not a missing artefact — the test will have to move with the fix.

THE FOUR-PART CHANGE, as worked out by the worker that found it:

1. `machine_wrapper.cljc:89-95` — replace `:meta {:terminal? true}` with `:final? true :output-key :rf/result` on `:succeeded`, and `:final? true :error? true :output-key :rf/result` on `:failed`.
2. Move the extraction into `:record-value` / `:record-failure` so `:rf/result` holds `(:value payload)` / `(:error payload)` rather than the whole envelope. `:output-key` MUST yield the same value the single-`:spawn` path already delivers to `[parent-id [:succeeded value]]`, or a join parent and a spawn parent see different shapes.
3. Guard `:dispatch-done` / `:dispatch-error` on `(nil? (:rf/join-child data))`. A `:final?` state's `:entry` STILL RUNS, so without this a joined child reports twice — once through the carrier and once as a spurious `:succeeded` into a parent that may declare `:on {:succeeded ...}`. The review did NOT name this part; the worker derived it. Single-`:spawn` addressing is unchanged, which is what keeps the existing recipe and its tests green.
4. `http_managed_machine_cljs_test.cljs:60-62` moves from asserting `:meta {:terminal? true}` to asserting `:final?` / `:output-key` / `:error?`, plus integration coverage for `:join :all` on two successes, `:join :any` cancelling a live sibling, and an accepted child error reaching `:on-any-failed`.

RE-VERIFY EACH PART AT YOUR TIP before acting: line numbers are from trunk 7f15b1998c, and part 3 in particular is a derivation rather than a measurement — check that a `:final?` state's `:entry` really does still run before you build the guard around it.

NO DOC CHANGE IS NEEDED. `managed-http.md` was deliberately left untouched and correct-as-written: the moment the wrapper is final, the recipe works. Do not edit it.

CLOSING NOTE. When this lands, rf2-fzbj.16 can be closed — F1 and F2 landed in PR #9773, and this is its last open finding. Say so on both beads.

GATES. `jvm-http` and the CLJS lane for `http_managed_machine_cljs_test.cljs`, plus `npm run test:cljs`. `spec/005-StateMachines.md` is a HOT ZONE and needs no edit here — cite it, do not touch it.
notes:

WHAT CHANGED — implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/machine_wrapper.cljc
1. :succeeded / :failed are :final? leaves with :output-key :rf/result; :failed also has :error? true. The :meta {:terminal? true} entries are gone.
2. :record-value / :record-failure store (:value reply) / (:error reply) under :rf/result. The terminal :entry now reads that same slot, so the single-:spawn [:succeeded value] / [:failed failure] and the :spawn-all join result are one value. A test pins this on both paths.

title: Resources RealWorld: bind editor write replies to their page
description:
Gate Resources editor save/delete continuations on the originating editing session before changing the editor or navigating. A completed write currently pulls the user back from a newer unrelated page.

Remediation fence: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. Independently implementable Resources editor part of confirmed finding 4 in rf2-fzbj.21, freshly revalidated under rf2-gwye. HTTP editor and Resources article-detail paths are separate issues. No remediation authorization.

Ownership: examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/article_editor.cljs:275-286,309-322,405-469; routing.cljs:154-187. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; inspected HEAD 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879.

Trigger/reproducer: open an existing clean article in the Resources editor, click Delete and hold its mutation response, navigate to a profile, then release success. The leave is permitted because the original draft is clean. A save can similarly finish after the user has chosen to leave its editor.

Expected: the write/cache reconciliation may finish, but the profile route remains selected and no departed editor overwrites a later session. Actual: :editor/replied checks only :status. For a bodyless success it clears the editor and navigates home; for a saved :article it replaces the slice and navigates to that article. Route-owned read release does not retire this independent mutation continuation.

Scope precision: entering New Article or another edit route clears the shared :editor/save instance, and the framework suppresses a late mutation result for a cleared instance. Therefore the confirmed Resources reproducer is the detour to a profile, which does not clear the instance. Do not claim every cleared old mutation survives a new-editor entry. A continuation already queued must still respect the originating session.

Suggested repair: carry the originating committed route/nav-token in :reply-to and gate page-local slice changes and navigation in :editor/replied against it. The current routing state already exposes :nav-token. Keep server/cache consequences handled by the mutation runtime. Scope any cleanup to the completed operation so a stale callback cannot clear a newer :editor/save incarnation. Avoid a framework change or generic mutation manager.

Acceptance: in the existing external Resources harness, hold the real editor Delete, navigate to profile/eve, release success, and assert unchanged profile route/editor session. Cover a departed save, positive same-page save/delete, and new-editor instance reset/refusal without stranded controls. Preserve invalidation and normal current-owner navigation. No example-local specs.

Validation performed: source-probe.clj evaluates the current source's editor helpers and :editor/replied. probe-examples_real_apps-1.log/.exit: exit 0, correct SOURCE_ROOT banner. With current route profile/eve and an independent draft, successful delete returns a blank editor plus home navigation, and successful save returns the old article draft plus article navigation. Inspected current route guards/entry events, mutation clear-handler at implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:1463-1507, and success continuation dispatch at :1850-1876. No browser or complete mutation/route runtime sequence was executed.

title: routing: preserve trailing slash data in splat URLs
description:
Preserve trailing slash data when encoding splat parameters. A splat decoded successfully by match-url currently loses data when route-url reconstructs its address, and an all-slash splat produces a URL the same route cannot match.

Ownership and remediation boundary
- Surface impl_routing; implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url.cljc (encoder), registry.cljc (emission/matching), match.cljc (capture decoding); regression tests under implementation/routing/test/re_frame/.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; source rechecked at 9238907fec4e0cc708bc518aa7fa83db6c0182e7, with no owned-path differences from baseline.
- P2, split from Finding 2 of rf2-fzbj.12. Preserve [FENCE: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj]. Review and issue creation authorize no remediation; prior statuses, notes and decisions remain unchanged.

Source / reproducer
url.cljc:148-158 implements url-encode-splat with the two-argument clojure.string/split, which drops terminal empty segments. registry.cljc:1462-1465 and :2021-2027 call this encoder for splats; :1201-1209 removes raw trailing URL slashes before matching. match.cljc:640-665 decodes captures.

(reg/reg-route :probe/files {} "/files/*rest")
(let [m (reg/match-url "/files/a%2F")
      emitted (reg/route-url {:to (:route-id m) :params (:params m)})]
  [(:params m) emitted (:params (reg/match-url emitted))])
;; Actual: [{:rest "a/"} "/files/a" {:rest "a"}]

Other actual current-source rows:
- /files/%2F -> {:rest "/"} -> emitted /files/ -> nil match.
- /files/a%2F%2F -> {:rest "a//"} -> /files/a -> {:rest "a"}.
- Controls /files/a/b and /files/a//b preserve the decoded splat.

Expected / impact
A successfully matched splat must survive rebuilding its URL. Named navigation can currently retain {:rest "a/"} in the active slice while publishing /files/a, which reloads as {:rest "a"}; link hrefs and current-route URL reconstruction likewise change resource identity. This is encoded route data, not the accepted equivalence of a raw trailing slash: Node's native URL parser preserves /files/a%2F verbatim.

Suggested repair
Keep normal embedded separators structural while encoding the terminal slash run as data (for example a/ -> a%2F; / -> %2F). Preserve the existing raw-trailing-slash matching rule. Merely retaining empty split chunks and joining with literal slashes is insufficient: normalize-match-path would still remove those literal terminal slashes. Keep the repair local to splat emission without widening route grammar.

Acceptance
- JVM and CLJS regressions preserve splat values a/, a//, /, //, a/b and a//b through route-url followed by match-url.
- Match/re-emit/rematch rows /files/a%2F, /files/%2F and /files/a%2F%2F preserve their decoded params.
- Named navigation state, route-link href and a later history/initial match agree for those values.
- Raw URL trailing-slash equivalence and reserved-character/Unicode/interior-double-slash controls remain intact.

Validation / limits
Executed five current-source JVM match/emission/rematch rows, asserting three defects and two successful controls. Node independently asserted that the encoded trailing slashes survive browser URL parsing. The JVM probe printed and checked absolute SOURCE paths under the owned routing source root. The CLJS branch uses the same splat split/join implementation; no CLJS compile/browser run is claimed.
Evidence: ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_routing/probe-impl_routing-1.clj/.log/.exit and probe-impl_routing-2.cjs/.log/.exit. Both exits 0 mean defect witnesses and controls passed. No source edits, full suite or build. Existing reply-envelope suite separately passed 9 tests/60 assertions.

Deduplication / references
Read current rf2-fzbj.12 and newest three history snapshots; current tracker splat search returned only that two-finding aggregate. No dedicated open issue covers this defect. Completed rf2-j3tud (encodeURIComponent host parity/surrogates) and rf2-k2d2t (decode parity) address other boundaries. Preserve the interior-double-slash and no-window decisions already recorded in the old report; no policy reopening is needed.
notes:
VERDICT (worker routing-a, 2026-09-13): FIXED in PR #9749 (branch worker/routing-a). One PR covers all four beads: rf2-fzbj.12 carries two findings, and rf2-gwye.26 and rf2-gwye.28 are those two findings split out one per bead. rf2-gwye.29 is a separate finding on the same surface.

Re-verified at trunk 6186726167 before any fix: all three defects reproduced. The new regression tests failed against the unmodified source on both hosts. JVM: 18 failures, all in the two new JVM-visible deftests. CLJS: 36 failures, all in the three new deftests, with the ordinary-URL control rows green.

1. Raw navigate URL normalisation (rf2-fzbj.12 finding 1 = rf2-gwye.26). `navigate.cljc` now runs `rf.routing.url/request-url->app-url` once, after the external-URL refusal. It is the same helper the link door uses. The resulting effective URL feeds `url-resolution`, `unmatched-url`, the not-found fallback params, and `requested-url`, which the guards, pending state and history all read. The route plan's `:source` keeps the caller's original string as provenance. On the JVM, or with no window, the helper is identity, so the fail-closed no-window policy is unchanged. Regression test: `routing_history_cljs_test.cljs`, `navigate-raw-url-normalizes-before-matching-cljs-rf2-fzbj-12`. It covers same-origin absolute, same-origin protocol-relative, rooted dot-segment, an ordinary rooted control, a query-only reference, a fragment-only reference, and an unmatched normalised reference that carries the browser's location in both the not-found params and history.

2. Splat trailing-slash data (rf2-fzbj.12 finding 2 = rf2-gwye.28). `url-encode-splat` now splits only the body before any terminal run of `/`, and encodes that run whole: `a/` emits `a%2F`, `/` emits `%2F`. Raw trailing-slash equivalence is unchanged. Regression test: `routing_url_encoding_parity_cljs_test.cljc`, `splat-trailing-slash-data-survives-route-url-on-both-hosts`, which runs on JVM and CLJS. It covers the values a/, a//, / and //, with controls a/b and a//b. It also covers the URL rows /f/a%2F, /f/%2F and /f/a%2F%2F through re-emission and a second match, plus a raw trailing-slash control.

3. Base root followed by ? or # (rf2-gwye.29). `strip-base-path` now accepts `?` and `#` as post-base boundaries, alongside end-of-string and `/`. So /app?tab=all strips to /?tab=all and /app#section to /#section. Sibling rejection and the blank-base no-op are unchanged. The fix is in the one shared ingress rule, so the initial sync and the listener both get it. Regression tests: `routing_url_strategy_test.clj`, `with-base-path-strips-mount-root-before-query-and-fragment` (pure strip rows plus the wrapped decode), and `routing_url_strategy_cljs_test.cljs`, `history-base-mount-root-before-query-or-fragment-cljs-rf2-gwye-29` (initial sync at /app?tab=all, decode of each form, and the real popstate listener).

Spec 012 gained two sentences: the URL-string escape hatch resolves to the browser's location before matching, and a terminal splat slash emits as %2F.

Not built, per the stance. Each finding got its fix and a regression test, nothing more.
- No separate guard or pending-state test for finding 1. The guards receive the resolved target plus the URL derived from it, which is the same value the tests assert on, so normalisation reaches them by construction.
- No named-navigation or route-link href test for finding 2. Both emit through `route-url`, which the round-trip test pins directly.
- JVM dot-segment resolution is left as it was. The bead's own repair says to keep the JVM/no-window policy, and the JVM pushes into no browser.

Gates. All ran on the final base, trunk e9a6e3dd54, with the branch head at bc41f1dacf. Each exit code was captured from the runner itself.

- `scripts/test-routing-prod-gate.sh` (CI job `jvm-routing-prod-gate`): exit 0, 563 tests, 3187 assertions.

- `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (CI job `verify-readme-links`): exit 0. To prove it read this worktree, I planted a broken anchor on the edited spec line: exit 1, naming the file, line and anchor. The restore was verified by blob hash.
- Ratchets over the touched paths all exit 0: retired spellings, require-alias dialect, ambient durable reads, and escaped continuations on the spec page.

JVM+CLJS regression covers a/, a//, /, // and the URL rows /f/a%2F, /f/%2F, /f/a%2F%2F, with a/b and a//b as controls; raw trailing-slash equivalence is unchanged. title: spec/conformance/fixtures: six fixtures carry a bare ::after-elapsed token that is not EDN; its meaning lives only in six reference test loaders, so every non-Clojure port fails at Step 0
description:
Found by the rf2-uj8m review of skills/re-frame2-implementor (2026-09-13, trunk d0f0263787); corpus-side, so filed apart from the skill bead. The mayor re-verified the six files and the loader rewrite at implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj:158.

WHAT: `rg --pcre2 '(?<=[\s(\[{])::[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*'` over spec/conformance/fixtures/ reads exactly 6 standalone tokens, one per file, all `::after-elapsed`: after-hierarchy.edn, after-single-delay.edn, after-stale-detection.edn, cross-spec-machine-after-hydration-rearm.edn, machine-timeout-spawn-fire.edn, machine-timeout-state-fire.edn (e.g. `:event [::after-elapsed 5000 1 [:loading]]`). The other 17 `::` hits are inside CEDN byte strings ("k::answer") and are valid EDN. clojure.edn itself rejects a bare ::name (rf2-6r9j.49 close reason). The reference resolves it by a regex rewrite ::name -> :rf.machine.timer/name in SIX loaders (conformance_test.clj:150-158, conformance_fixtures.clj, and the machines / flows / ssr / ssr_streaming conformance tests). Spec 005 names :rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed 5 times, so the namespace is load-bearing.

WHY IT MATTERS: the harness the implementor skill prescribes "reads every fixture; filters" (conformance.md:29), so even a Q1=no minimum port parses these six before any capability filter and a spec-conformant EDN reader throws on all six. No fail-loud floor names the case, spec/conformance/README.md does not (0 mentions of ::, auto-resolve or after-elapsed, while promising a ~200-line reader suffices), and the namespace to substitute is a reference-test artefact a port cannot derive without reading implementation/ -- the route conformance.md:87 forbids.

FIX: replace the six tokens with :rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed (six one-token edits). The six loader rewrites become inert and may stay (rf2-6r9j.49 removed the schemas loader's rewrite only and warned not to touch the others -- leaving them inert is consistent with that). Then a one-line guard: `rg --pcre2 '(?<=[\s(\[{])::' spec/conformance/fixtures` must read 0; put it wherever the corpus's other shape checks live.

GATES: scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh (core / machines / flows / ssr / ssr_streaming corpus runs exercise every loader). Not a hot zone; spec/conformance/README.md may want one sentence saying fixtures are plain EDN.

The guard lives in scripts/check_conformance_fixture_edn.py, the corpus's existing shape gate (rf2-x91a). It now refuses any `::` outside a string or comment. The scanner already lexes strings, comments and char literals, so the 17 `"k::answer"` CEDN byte strings stay legal. Two self-test cases pin both directions. CI runs it in test.yml job verify-skill-mcp-drift ("Repo invariant checks"), in steps "Self-test the conformance fixture EDN gate" and "Validate every conformance fixture is one well-formed EDN form". title: resources: report loaded-feed page-zero refresh failures as refresh-error
description:
Settle a failed page-zero refresh of an already loaded infinite feed through the refresh-error channel. Preserve page-error for a load-more failure, as the subscription contract requires.

F3 — P2: infinite background-refresh failure is reported as load-more failure

Sources: src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:3014-3016 defines only first-load? (page index zero with no accumulated pages). Its non-abort/non-first-load fallback at :3187-3207 unconditionally calls entry-page-failed and emits :rf.resource/page-failed, including page zero of an already loaded feed. state.cljc:1204-1228 writes :page-error; the existing entry-failed helper at :1015-1045 is the refresh-error branch for entries with data. Public readers at src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:251-256 and :413-418 expose the two distinct error slots.

Trigger/reproducer:
1. Register an infinite feed, ensure page 0 and accept {:items [1 2] :next :cursor} (with :page->items :items).
2. Refetch the already loaded feed with cause :focus. Deliver the accepted page-zero failure {:kind :rf.http/http-5xx :status 503} through the generated page-failed reply shape.
3. Read the refresh-error and page-error projections.
Expected: the visible feed survives, status returns to :loaded and :refresh-error records the failed background refresh. :page-error means failed load-more, as specified at spec/016-Resources.md:1542, :1554 and :1570; the worked view renders a load-more retry from that field. A load-more failure should continue to use :page-error.
Actual measured: status :loaded and data unchanged, but :refresh-error nil and :page-error equal to the 503 envelope. The actual public refresh-error projection returned nil and the page-error projection returned the envelope. A real load-more failure control produced that same page-error shape, demonstrating that the two distinct operations are collapsed.
Impact: consumers following the documented UI grammar suppress the background-refresh warning and instead offer a misleading 'could not load more' retry. That retry can append the next page while the failed refresh target remains stale.

Repair: distinguish a refresh of existing feed data from an append failure at the accepted page-failure boundary. At minimum, page zero with existing data must use the existing refresh failure transition and :rf.resource/refresh-failed trace, while page-zero first load retains :error and actual load-more retains :page-error. Preserve the current accumulated pages and stop any failed sweep coherently. Do not reinterpret the existing page>0 sweep regression without checking its established rule; this finding directly proves the ordinary/default page-zero refresh case.
Acceptance:
- One public event/subscription regression covers successful page 0, failed default refetch, :refresh-error envelope, nil :page-error, unchanged data and :loaded status; the next successful refresh clears the refresh error.
- Pair first-load page-zero failure (:error) and load-more failure (:page-error) controls, plus abort controls (no user-visible failure). Preserve established multi-page sweep failure behavior unless deliberately clarified.
- A negative control routing the refresh through entry-page-failed must make the new refresh projection assertion red.

title: Story: execute inherited and composed loaders from the resolved plan
description:
Execute registered variants' resolved loader world throughout allocation, phase 1 and teardown. A normal variant that inherits or composes a loader fixture currently skips the fixture, reports :pass/:ready, and also skips its cleanup. The compiler already computes the correct world; the runtime must consume it.

Surface and revision
- Ownership: tools_story, tools/story/**. Fresh correctness review under rf2-gwye.
- Reviewed source: 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261, 2026-09-13. No owned-path movement from the review baseline at verification.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- This is the independently actionable split of finding 1 in rf2-fzbj.3, revalidated after the intervening Story changes. No implementation is part of this review.

Source evidence
- runtime.cljc:277-284 defaults run-loaders! to frames/variant-body, the raw registration; :951-963 only supplies a normalized :loader-body for inline contexts.
- frames.cljc:739,773 and :811-814 classifies allocation from raw v-body, so an extends-only/compose-only child enters the events-only :ready fast path. run-loaders! then short-circuits at runtime.cljc:280-283.
- frames.cljc:1015-1018 reads cleanup from raw registration again.
- plan.cljc:1542-1552 and :1746-1758 correctly carry composed/inherited :loaders, :loaders-teardown and completion policy on [:world ...]. prepare-context already compiles that plan once at runtime.cljc:717-770.
- tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:1496 specifies composed loaders/teardown followed by the extends-merged variant chain. This is supported ordinary authoring, not invalid input.

Concrete reproduction
With actual source loaded, initialize re-frame with re-frame.substrate.plain-atom/adapter and call story/install-canonical-vocabulary!. Register :review/load to append :load to a calls atom and set app-db :loaded true; register :review/close to append :close. Then:

    (story/reg-story :story.review {})
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/base
      {:loaders [[:review/load]] :loaders-teardown [[:review/close]]})
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/child {:extends :story.review/base})
    (select-keys (:world (plan/variant-plan :story.review/child))
                 [:loaders :loaders-teardown])
    ;; => both event vectors, correctly resolved
    @(story/run-variant :story.review/child)
    (story/destroy-variant! :story.review/child)
    ;; Actual calls: []; result :status :pass, :lifecycle :ready.

The same witness using reg-fragment :fragment.review/loader and a variant with only :compose [:fragment.review/loader] has identical failure. Direct-base control runs the SAME event handlers and yields [:load :close]. Thus the absence is in fixture resolution/execution, not handler setup or the probe.

Expected: each run executes its resolved fixture; setup/play respect its completion predicate; teardown executes the resolved cleanup. Actual: inherited/composed fixture work disappears while run success is reported. Derived scenarios can test or show uninitialized state and falsely appear usable. The completion-predicate branch is source-traced, not separately dynamically exercised by this probe.

Suggested repair
Thread the already-compiled plan's resolved loader slots through registered allocation classification, run context and teardown, as the inline path does. Repairing only the ready short circuit is insufficient: phase 1 and teardown still read raw bodies. Keep the registrar's raw-body contract; do not add eager registration-time resolution. Store resolved cleanup with the run so the separate hot-reload cleanup-ownership finding can retain the correct lifetime.

Acceptance
- End-to-end run-variant/destroy tests for direct, extends-only, compose-only and composed-plus-own loader ordering; assert actual event calls/app-db, not just variant-plan output.
- A derived false completion predicate prevents setup/play in the headless run and reports loader-incomplete.
- Reset and destroy run the resolved cleanup once, preserving loader-before-decorator order. Retain direct no-loader and inline controls.

Validation and limits
Executed process-local JVM witness ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_story/probe-tools-story-1.clj using current actual CLJC source, Clojure 1.12.4/Malli 0.20.1 from the existing cached classpath and the plain-atom adapter. Exit 0 means the defect witnesses and controls reproduced as asserted, not that Story passed a suite. Evidence: probe-tools_story-1.log and .exit in the same ignored directory. No build, dependency resolution, network, browser or source edit occurred. Full CLJS/browser/package suites were not run.

Do not reopen those decisions.

title: [implementation/core] Preserve subscription ownership across one-shot reads and concurrent cache clears
description:
Recommendation: repair two confirmed subscription ownership defects using the core's existing identity-aware release and atomic cache primitives. Keep this bead open for implementation. This focused surface review found 2 actionable defects, both P2; it does not propose public API expansion or extra caller ceremony.

Owned slice and revision
- Ownership: implementation/core/**.
- Reviewed revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
- WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- The findings' production paths are implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc and implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/cache.cljc. No production or test file was changed.

Coverage and boundaries
Inspected selected execution paths in router.cljc (envelope construction, exact event/target authority, dispatch admission, pre-commit validation, partition commit and post-commit effects), frame.cljc (frame/incarnation access and commit boundaries), fx.cljc (reserved dispatch, delayed-timer ownership, override/cascade propagation, source-ordered effect execution), interop.clj (timer binding and reaction disposal), interceptor.cljc (before/after unwinding), subs.cljc (recursive materialization, collision adoption, reactive and pure reads, one-shot lifetime, release), subs/cache.cljc (reference counting, invalidation closure, cache clears and destroy disposal), substrate/plain_atom.cljc, the core.cljc public init/configuration/adapter doors, and live_frame.cljc's generation-resolution seam. Inspected core/deps.edn and relevant lifecycle, cache-concurrency, generation-refresh and dispatch-later test coverage; consulted spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md and existing review/repair beads.
This was a focused correctness review, not a line-by-line audit of every core file. CLJS spine/render scheduling, full trace/privacy/egress correctness, every facade macro, optional feature artefacts, packaging publication, browser behavior, and broad conformance suites were not independently executed. No finding is inferred solely from a missing test.

CONFIRMED FINDING 1 -- P2: subscribe-once can release a replacement reaction owned by somebody else
Source: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1919-1928, especially the address-only (unsubscribe target query-v) at 1927. The existing exact-reaction release is at 2551-2555; cache-level identity checking is implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/cache.cljc:283-301.
Contract: spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1198-1205 says a one-shot read retains no reference and a concurrent reactive subscriber keeps its slot alive; it is explicitly JVM-runnable. The source's own docstring at subs.cljc:1948-1953 says the one-shot decrement only disposes when it owned the last reference.
Trigger: a one-shot read is evaluating its acquired reaction A while another thread clears/replaces that cached query and a different consumer acquires successor reaction B. When the read of A returns, subscribe-once releases by (frame, query), so it decrements B instead of recognizing that A's acquisition already died with eviction.
Expected: the one-shot returns its value; B stays cached with its owner's reference, and B's on-dispose callback does not run.
Measured actual: B's on-dispose callback runs once; B is absent from the cache and has no remaining ref-count. A no-eviction control with an existing independent holder retains that identical held reaction, ref-count 1 and zero disposal callbacks. Both the defect and its control use actual subscribe/subscribe-once/cache-clear calls, with a promise in a constant-valued sub body solely to fix the otherwise ordinary JVM preemption window.
Impact: an advanced one-shot read used by JVM SSR/headless tooling can retire another live consumer's acquisition during supported cache invalidation. Further releases/lookup now operate on a missing or rebuilt entry. Reactive consequences on a different substrate are a risk, not something this JVM probe measured.
Repair: release the specific reaction acquired by subscribe-once using the existing unsubscribe-if-reaction path. Preserve current public arities, missing-frame recovery, returned-value semantics and synchronous final-reference disposal. No new ownership API is needed.
Acceptance: add a deterministic JVM regression that pauses the one-shot deref, clears that query's old cache, acquires a successor with its own owner, resumes, and asserts the successor identity/ref-count 1/no disposal. Include a no-eviction shared-owner control and a final-owner one-shot case. Exercise the same semantic assertions with the real load-time production flag.

CONFIRMED FINDING 2 -- P2: cache clear can erase a concurrently acquired reaction without disposing it
Source: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/cache.cljc:473-492. It reads snapshot with @cache at 475 and separately resets the atom at 478, then disposes only snapshot entries. The same non-atomic extraction spelling is present in dispose-all-for-frame-destroy! at 557-568; the executed trigger here is explicit clear-sub-cache!, not a claim that a destroy admission race was also reproduced.
Trigger: clear-sub-cache! captures old entry A, then a different thread subscribes another query B before reset! empties the cache. The reset removes A and B; only A was in snapshot, so only A's reaction is disposed.
Expected: the clear's cache extraction and condemned batch must agree. A concurrent B either remains in the cache because it linearized after the clear, or belongs to the removed batch and is disposed exactly once. There is no valid outcome where it is erased and never disposed.
Measured actual: cache is {}; A's on-dispose callback ran once; B's on-dispose callback ran zero times. The probe pauses immediately before the real reset! with a scoped redef that matches ONLY the exact frame cache atom and {} value. The other thread uses real subscribe to add B, proves B was cached, and resumes the clear. The redef delegates unchanged to the real reset!: it widens the source's read/reset window without changing its cache contents or disposal algorithm.
Impact: the runtime loses ownership bookkeeping for a reaction it never retired. Ordinary unsubscribe can no longer find B, disposal callbacks/resources can be stranded, and a later subscribe creates another identity for the same query. This is a JVM concurrency defect; CLJS cannot interleave ordinary threads at these two statements.
Repair: atomically take and empty the cache with reset-vals! and dispose the captured OLD map, preserving the intentional remove-before-callback ordering and the existing disposal cause/trace behavior. Apply the same extraction discipline to the adjacent frame-destroy helper so the two batch paths do not diverge; do not replace the existing per-entry best-effort disposal policy.
Acceptance: a deterministic concurrent-clear/acquire regression must show every removed entry is disposed exactly once, while any acquisition after the atomic extraction remains live. Include the existing eager reacquisition/shared-input scenario to ensure callbacks may still rebuild after extraction without the old batch deleting or decrementing their successors. The real production posture must satisfy the same ownership assertions.

Executed reproduction (process-local JVM, no source/build writes)
Run from C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/core using the existing cached classpath. In PowerShell:
$reviewCp = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath 'C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/core/.cpcache/C320C3A15E22B037087E3C558D48097E.cp'
Feed the Clojure program below to java -cp $reviewCp clojure.main - with a PowerShell single-quoted here-string. For the production repetition use java '-Dre-frame.debug=false' -cp $reviewCp clojure.main - (quotes on the JVM option are necessary under this shell).

(require '[re-frame.core :as rf] '[re-frame.subs :as subs]
         '[re-frame.subs.cache :as cache] '[re-frame.frame :as frame]
         '[re-frame.interop :as interop]
         '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as plain])
(println :source-root (System/getProperty "user.dir")
         :debug-enabled interop/debug-enabled?)
(rf/init! plain/adapter)
(let [id :review-once/frame q [:review-once/value]
      entered (promise) resume (promise) disposed (atom 0)]
  (rf/reg-sub (first q) {}
    (fn [_ _] (deliver entered true) @resume :value))
  (rf/make-frame {:id id})
  (let [job (future (subs/subscribe-once q {:frame id}))]
    (assert (= true (deref entered 5000 :timeout)))
    (cache/clear-sub-cache! id)
    (let [held (subs/subscribe q {:frame id})]
      (interop/add-on-dispose! held #(swap! disposed inc))
      (deliver resume true)
      (assert (= :value (deref job 5000 :timeout)))
      (println :one-shot-race
        {:held-disposed @disposed
         :held-cached (contains? @(-> (frame/frame id) :sub-cache) q)}))))
(let [id :review-clear/frame old-q [:review-clear/old]
      late-q [:review-clear/late] entered (promise) resume (promise)
      disposed (atom [])]
  (rf/reg-sub (first old-q) {} (fn [_ _] :old))
  (rf/reg-sub (first late-q) {} (fn [_ _] :late))
  (rf/make-frame {:id id})
  (let [state (:sub-cache (frame/frame id))
        old (subs/subscribe old-q {:frame id})
        original-reset! clojure.core/reset!]
    (interop/add-on-dispose! old #(swap! disposed conj :old))
    (with-redefs [clojure.core/reset!
                  (fn [a v]
                    (when (and (identical? a state) (= {} v))
                      (deliver entered true) @resume)
                    (original-reset! a v))]
      (let [job (future (cache/clear-sub-cache! id))]
        (assert (= true (deref entered 5000 :timeout)))
        (let [late (subs/subscribe late-q {:frame id})]
          (interop/add-on-dispose! late #(swap! disposed conj :late))
          (assert (contains? @state late-q))
          (deliver resume true)
          (assert (nil? (deref job 5000 :timeout)))
          (println :cache-clear-race {:cache @state :disposed @disposed}))))))
(shutdown-agents)
(System/exit 0)

Observed dev output:
:one-shot-control {:eviction false, :held-disposed 0, :held-still-cached true, :ref-count 1}
:one-shot-race {:eviction true, :held-disposed 1, :held-still-cached false, :ref-count nil}
:cache-clear-race {:late-still-cached false, :old-disposes 1, :late-disposes 0}
Observed real production output (debug-enabled false asserted):
:one-shot-race {:held-disposed 1, :held-cached false}
:cache-clear-race {:cache {}, :disposed [:old]}
Both completed probes exited 0; those exits mean the reproducer reached and measured the defects, NOT that a product test suite passed. Each printed the intended implementation/core source root. Initial JVM smoke exited 0. A first production invocation with an unquoted JVM option failed in Java argument parsing (exit 1, no framework code executed); corrected quoted invocation produced the production evidence above. No tests/gates, CLJS compilation, browser session, installed dependencies, or shared compilation output were created.

Dedupe and prior work
- rf2-1frc is CLOSED; its latest close reason records PR #9405's fix for address-only releases in three layer-2/input ownership paths and the earlier mounted-hook repair. Those fixes are present and are not reopened here. The still address-only internal one-shot at subs.cljc:1927 is a separate uncovered caller of the same ownership rule.
- rf2-4lp1 is CLOSED; reviewed its current body/notes/close reason and newest-first history. Generation-change invalidation now fires and is not being re-reported. Finding 1 uses an actual eviction that already works.
- sub_cache_concurrency_test.clj identifies historical rf2-3mww7 / rf2-spr6q fixes for retriable swap side effects and tests concurrent replacement, per-entry disposal, decrement and miss-install races. Those paths use swap-vals! and are distinct from finding 2's remaining @cache/reset! batch extraction. Historical ids rf2-awhtpc and rf2-j538f7.2 were consulted through source references; the latter is no longer fetchable in the current tracker, so no claim is made to have read its missing bead.
- Searched current open bead titles and the available tracker export for cache, subscription, subscribe-once and clear-sub-cache references. No live owner of these two residuals was found.

Unverified/disconfirmed risks
A delayed-dispatch incarnation-retargeting candidate was NOT promoted: JVM interop/set-timeout! uses bound-fn and carries the event owner's dynamic authority, so a missing token in a grep of inherited opts alone is insufficient evidence. No additional delayed-dispatch defect is asserted. No correctness verdict is claimed for the excluded CLJS/reactive or optional-feature surfaces.

before the final gate run; every quoted number is from that final base).

## THE PREMISE HOLDS — STEP 3 IS SATISFIABLE, AND IT LANDED

This bead's own release note said step 3 was "only satisfiable if the DYNAMIC surface
carries an app-directed command that the Static one did not", and told whoever took it to
RE-MEASURE before building. Measured, and it does.

**The command is the DYNAMIC tab ribbon's `Reset` button** — `shell.cljs`'s
`tab-bar-tree`, `data-testid` `rf-xray-tab-bar-reset`. Its `:on-click` dispatches
`:rf.xray/reset-to-epoch` through the dispatcher `tab-bar` captured with
`(:dispatch (rf/capture-frame))`, carrying the OBSERVED frame — `shell.cljs`'s own comment
says "the frame Xray is inspecting ... NOT `:rf/xray` Xray's own chrome frame" — and the
focused epoch. That event is a thin trampoline into `:rf.xray.fx/restore-epoch`
(`epoch.cljs`), which calls the framework's `rf/restore-epoch!`, whose own comment reads
"it rewinds an OBSERVED frame's `app-db` to a past epoch's `:db-after`". It is an existing
product command with a real UI control, and it is Dynamic-only: the Static ribbon has no
Reset.

## WHY THE ORIGINAL CENSUS COULD NOT SEE IT, AND WHY THAT IS NOT A CONTRADICTION

The prohibition rested on a census of `{:frame ...}` DISPATCH OPTIONS, and that census was
honest about the question it asked. `Reset` does not reach the application through a
dispatch option at all — it reaches it through `rf/restore-epoch!`, a framework call made
inside an fx handler, with the frame arriving as an fx ARGUMENT map
(`{:frame ... :epoch-id ...}`). No dispatch-option census of any spelling can see that
class. So the earlier measurement stands and the prohibition was never lifted: no product
command was invented, the BENCH was widened onto the surface that already carried one.

Re-measured at this tip as the control: of every `{:frame ...}` occurrence under
`tools/xray/src`, the dispatch-bearing ones name `:rf/xray`, `defaults/default-frame-id`,
`shell/default-frame-id`, or a `frame` / `frame-id` / `here` bound from
`(rf/capture-frame)` / `(rf/current-frame-id)` — i.e. Xray's own instance frame. The three
`{:frame here}` sites in `panels/cancellation_cascade_events.cljs` are tool-local re-
dispatches. `:rf.xray/set-target-frame` writes Xray's own `app-db`. **`Reset` is the only
Xray affordance whose effect lands in an inspected application**, which is why the new arm
is singular rather than a sample, and why `simulate_nav.cljs`'s "Xray is a lens, not a
remote control" is still the right posture statement: the one exception is an explicit,
operator-driven rewind.

## STEP 1 — THE WIDENING, AND IT COST TWO LINES RATHER THAN THE PROMISED ONE

Verified the release condition at tip rather than taking it from the merge: `(rf/reg-view`
appears in exactly FOUR files under `tools/xray/src` — `panels/machine_canvas.cljs`,
`shell.cljs`, `views/edn_inspector.cljs`, `views/resizable_table.cljs` — and `shell.cljs`'s
only survivor is `event-list` at line 2305, which cannot migrate because
`panel_registry/reg-l4-tab!` carries `:pre [... (fn? panel)]` (read the form; it is there).
`shell-view` is not among them.

`mount-xray!` now renders `[shell/ShellView {}]` — the head `mount.cljs` itself renders.
No outer `frame-provider` of our own: `impl/mount.cljs`'s `tree` already wraps a
frame-bearing root in one, and `:frame-id` defaults to `shell/default-frame-id`, which IS
the frame the harness mounts at.

**THE FINDING: the docstring promised the widening would cost one line and it costs two.**
`:rf.xray/mode` defaults to `:dynamic` (`registry.cljs`, `(get db :mode :dynamic)`), so
mounting the shipped shell and changing nothing else swaps the Static surface out from
under every row below, all of which name Static testids — "every row below is unchanged"
would have been false. `setup!` therefore pins the lens to `:static` BEFORE the mount, and
with that one extra line the promise holds exactly.

A second-order consequence, handled: `:rf.xray/set-mode` carries the
`:rf.xray.static/persist-mode` fx which writes localStorage, and `mount.cljs`'s
`::hydrate-static-mode` first-mount hook READS that slot — so a lens this harness pinned
would silently decide which surface a LATER suite's `open!` paints
(`acceptance.substrate-gap-dom-cljs-test` is the one on the same page). `setup!` clears the
slot immediately after the dispatch, returning the page to the `:dynamic` default the hook
falls back to.

## STEP 2 — THE STALE PARAGRAPH IS CORRECTED

Both stale passages, not only the one this bead named. The namespace docstring's "THE
SUBJECT: Xray's Static chrome" section asserted `shell/shell-view` was still an
`rf/reg-view` painted through the installed adapter; it is rewritten, keeping the old claim
as history and naming what changed under it. The `CRITERION 4 IS PARTIAL` note four
paragraphs above it said the same thing in different words and is corrected too, as is
criterion 4's own "WHAT THIS ROW DOES *NOT* COVER" section.

## STEP 3 — WHAT THE ROW NOW DOES

Appended to criterion 4's SHARED body (so it runs on all three adapter arms), after the
existing instrument control, which is left untouched:

  1. captures the application's last recorded epoch while it is provably still at its seed
     — the assertion immediately above is what licenses that — and asserts the ring is
     NON-EMPTY, because `rf/epoch-history` answers `[]` when the epoch artefact is merely
     absent from the build and `[]` is also what a clean ring answers with;
  2. bumps the SELECTED application off that epoch (the second application is already at
     its own distinct post-control value);
  3. aims Xray with its own tool-local events, `:rf.xray/set-target-frame` and
     `:rf.xray/select-epoch`, and ASSERTS that `:rf.xray/observed-frame` and
     `:rf.xray/focus-epoch-id` really read what was intended — the spine's `compose-focus`
     can re-derive a focused epoch from head in LIVE mode, so this is a precondition and
     not decoration;
  4. flips the lens to `:dynamic` (same mount, no second root — the mode composer swaps the
     surface) and polls until `Reset` is committed AND enabled;
  5. clicks the real button, then polls the application.

Then asserts, in the criterion's own words: the SELECTED application is rewound to the
focused epoch; the framework ACCEPTED the restore (no inline failure flash — a refused
restore leaves the application unchanged, which is the one way the first assertion could be
satisfied by a command that did nothing); the UNSELECTED application, at its own distinct
value, is UNTOUCHED; the deaf tool lever still holds its distinct tab; and no restored
application state landed in Xray's own frame.

`re-frame.epoch` is now required by the harness, for its late-bound hooks rather than for a
name (`rf/restore-epoch!` is `:on-absent :false`). It was already in the `:browser-test`
bundle via `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/cross_spec_dom_cljs_test.cljs`;
the explicit require makes the harness self-sufficient rather than dependent on a
neighbour's require.

No new product command. No new testing framework. The existing two-app fixture and the
existing controls carry the row.

## THE NEW ASSERTIONS ARE PROVEN TO BITE

A planted MISROUTE — `setup!`'s target frame aimed at `second-app-frame` instead of
`app-frame`, one line, anchor match count read as 1 before the run — turned the browser
lane RED at CAPTURED EXIT 1 with 9 failures: three assertions in
`c4-tool-local-state-and-frame-targeting` across all three adapter arms (the aim
precondition, the rewind itself reading `Expected {:count 0}, got {:count 1} — rewind
flash: "Reset failed — epoch unavailable (see Trace)"`, and the accepted-restore
assertion). That is the acceptance criteria's own disable clause demonstrated rather than
asserted.

The sabotage run reported the SAME totals as the green run — 1091 tests, 5952 assertions —
so the plant reddened assertions rather than crashing a namespace and silencing its
neighbours. Plant and restore verified by BLOB hash: committed blob

473f06ac3fa37216b8be5d9c31223f648a959fe6, and after the checkout the default-form
`git hash-object` reproduced the committed blob exactly, with `git diff --quiet HEAD`

  shadow-cljs compile browser-test      exit 0   1086 files, 5 pre-existing infer-warnings
                                                 in an unrelated fresco test, none here

  compile-node-test.cjs node-test       exit 0   1985 files, 0 warnings
  node out/node-test.js (test:cljs)     exit 0   11785 tests / 58866 assertions, 0 failures
  npm run test:xray-feature-gate        exit 0   16 scenarios, 0 failures, 13 matrix rows

All 45 `scripts/check_*.py` plus `check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh` and
`check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh` exited 0 against this tree; `check-commit-attribution.sh` and
`check-beads-pr-boundary.sh` against origin/main likewise. `cd tools/xray && clojure -M:test`
is deliberately NOT quoted — a JVM run cannot load a `.cljs` test and would report green

## ONE THING A LATER READER SHOULD KNOW

The criteria harness now mounts the shipped shell, so criteria 1-6 are evidence about
