title: [implementation/routing] Based hash decoding strips a legitimate app-route prefix
description:
Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; relevant strategy source unchanged at mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d.

Supported normal use: an app is deployed at /demos using `(with-base-path hash-url-strategy "/demos")` and registers an ordinary app-relative route `/demos/item`. Its link correctly encodes to `/demos#/demos/item`. Initial load, reload, or browser Back should select `/demos/item`; actual inbound decoding selects `/item`. A same-named shorter route can render the wrong page; otherwise the user reaches not-found. App route names must not depend on whether their prefix happens to equal the host mount point.

Cause (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc):
- hash-decode:154 reads ONLY location.hash, removing the leading #. At /demos#/demos/item it already yields the app-relative `/demos/item`; the physical /demos is outside the fragment and was never part of this result.
- with-base-path:328 correctly prepends base outside the encoded href, as required by the settled outbound rule.
- But :329 blindly calls strip-base-path on the wrapped strategy's already-decoded path. strip-base-path:269 removes `/demos` and yields `/item`.
- The same mistake occurs in the :install-listener! wrapper at :343-344: the hash listener (:201-204) passes the decoded app path and the wrapper strips its legitimate leading route segment. history.cljc:139-164 dispatches the damaged value for both browser changes and initial sync.

Spec 012 URL strategies explicitly supports wrapping BOTH shipped strategies and its Round-trip law requires decode at push(encode p) to return p. The prior rf2-irygd6 amendment requires the deployment prefix OUTSIDE the fragment; preserve that rule. The existing hash-base-links-and-address-bar-agree-irygd6-cljs test (implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_url_strategy_cljs_test.cljs:316) covers /active and /completed, which do not collide with /demos, so accidental stripping remains inert in its examples.

Executed tiny isolated bb probe over actual with-base-path/encode/strip implementation (core+routing source classpath). Only the browser-reading decode leg is supplied as the exact value that hash-decode returns; no CLJS/browser or history listener execution is claimed:

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.routing.strategy :as s])
(let [hash (s/with-base-path
             (assoc s/hash-url-strategy :decode (constantly "/demos/item"))
             "/demos")
      history (s/with-base-path
                (assoc s/history-url-strategy :decode
                       (constantly "/demos/demos/item"))
                "/demos")]
  (prn :hash-href ((:encode hash) "/demos/item")
       :hash-decoded ((:decode hash))
       :history-decoded ((:decode history))))
```

Output: :hash-href "/demos#/demos/item", :hash-decoded "/item", :history-decoded "/demos/item". Corrected probe exits 0 (~0.26s); first attempted expression had an unmatched parenthesis and did not execute. Exact browser causal trace independently comes from hash-decode source. Actual examples use with-base-path/history in both RealWorld apps and bare hash in TodoMVC; no existing example combining a colliding route with based hash was found. The shipped combined-strategy test is the concrete supported caller.

Smallest repair: make inbound base composition operate on the physical deployment component, never an already-decoded hash route. Keep the current outbound encode authority and five-leg public strategy contract; do not put base inside the hash or add another public strategy. Align the combinator's ingress sentence as narrowly needed.

Focused acceptance: extend the existing browser strategy fixture with base /demos and app paths /demos and /demos/item (plus query/fragment). Assert encode/decode round trip, initial route sync, and installed hash listener all preserve those app paths. Keep history /demos/demos/item -> /demos/item and the existing /demos#/active egress assertions green.

Dedupe: current all-status searches base-path, base path and hash, plus base-path memories. Historical IDs rf2-irygd6/rf2-g8pbwg/rf2-33uv27 no longer resolve in current tracker or exact-ID tracked JSONL; fully read their current normative carry in Spec 012 URL strategies and the named regression source. This is an inbound residual, not a reopening of outbound base composition. No compilation, suites, browser or shared runtime mutation performed.
close_reason: Fixed on PR #9376 (b14a27fe9f). with-base-path's ingress leg now strips the base only for a PATH-form strategy, whose decode reads the pathname the base prefixes; a FRAGMENT-form strategy's decode reads location.hash, which never carried it, so its already-app-relative result passes through. Form derived once at wrap time from the strategy's own :encode (fragment-form-strategy?), so a custom fragment-form strategy classifies correctly with no sixth key on the five-leg contract and decode pays nothing; one strip-ingress closure backs both :decode and :install-listener! so they cannot drift. Settled outbound rule untouched (:push!/:replace! unwrapped, base outside the fragment). Failing-first: npm run test:cljs exit 1, 8 failures across the three new hash deftests, then exit 0 / 0 failures (11363 tests, 57341 assertions); the history control deftest passed in both runs. implementation/routing clojure -M:test exit 0 (558 tests, 3554 assertions). spec/012-Routing.md ingress sentence narrowed; mkdocs --strict + check_doc_slugs.py both exit 0.

title: [implementation/hicasso] Reacquire mounted readsets after later-task frame recreation
description:
Surface: implementation/hicasso runtime collector. Source snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; relevant source unchanged at mayor HEAD 37fe77aad297bda18684d1904e37f207ad72f795. This is a source-supported functional defect; no CLJS compilation or React/browser execution was performed.

Expected: when a same-id frame successor arrives in a later task, an existing Hicasso boundary that rerenders under that live successor must regain reactive subscription ownership. Merely reading its value once is not enough. This recovery is explicitly promised by docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md:522-525 and repeated in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/reincarnation_cells_cljs_test.cljs:235-237. No change to the settled pre-paint microtask repair or exact no-successor teardown is requested.

Actual causal trace:

1. A committed boundary reads one query in frame F. Its readset entry E has refs=1; make-subscribe retains its registration and an array containing cell C (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs:770-800).
2. Destroy F, and let its invalidation microtask run before creating a successor. invalidate-cell! finds no incarnation and calls dispose-cell! (collector.cljs:318-331). That function marks C disposed, removes its watch/table slot and unsubscribes (161-167), but neither evicts E nor changes E's subscribe identity. E remains claimed until React actually unmounts or changes readset. The only Hicasso frame-destroy hook drops frame-op memo rows, not React roots or entries (impl/frames.cljs:155-169).
3. In a later task create F again. Force a normal props rerender of the SAME component, leaving its query/readset unchanged. cold-read!/read-key! can read the successor, as documented; render-body resolves the same E because entry-for matches only the query keys (collector.cljs:714-742). E's subscribe closure is identical. The dev view-subscribe wrapper is also cached per entry/name (1023-1053), so this is not a production-only issue.
4. React does NOT call subscribe again just because the snapshot or component props changed. Installed react-dom 19.2.0 cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:8194-8195 calls updateEffectImpl(...,[subscribe]); changing the snapshot schedules updateStoreInstance, not a fresh subscription. Hicasso shell likewise passes the same subscribe (collector.cljs:1142-1149). Thus no acquire-cell! runs for the mounted boundary, the replacement value was only a cold probe, and E's committed registration is still attached to disposed C.
5. A subsequent event changing the successor's queried value has no live cell/watch/reader edge to notify. The visible value remains frozen until an unrelated rerender, readset change or remount. Even if a second boundary creates a new C for this query, E's original registration is not transferred to it.

Minimal proposed DOM reproduction (not executed): initialize the Hicasso adapter; register :demo/value reading (:value db) and :demo/set returning {:db {:value v}}; define a stable Hicasso view whose props include :revision but whose body always reads [:demo/value]. Create F and seed A; mount that view with revision=0 and retain the root handle. Destroy F without unmounting the root. In setTimeout (or after explicitly draining the invalidation microtask), recreate F and seed B, then h/render! the same head with revision=1. Verify B paints, proving the component rerender happened. Dispatch :demo/set with C into F and settle React. Expected: C paints and one committed cell/reader exists. Source-predicted actual: B remains, with no collector cell for this sole reader. Finally unmount the root. Do not manually call commit-boundary! a second time in the test: that would supply the reacquisition React intentionally does not perform and mask the defect.

Impact: a mounted tenant/account view or retained native island becomes nonreactive after the supported later-task frame recreation. The boundary can paint the new tenant correctly on a forced render, making a value-only recovery assertion appear successful while subsequent updates are lost. The same collector entry mechanism backs native/use-sub; no distinct native-hook issue is needed. No current external application taking this precise asynchronous replacement sequence was demonstrated.

Smallest repair direction: make removal of a cell with committed readers retire the affected cached subscription identity so the next actual render commits fresh memberships (or an equally narrow ownership repair). Keep render probes non-owning, keep genuine no-successor teardown at zero live cells, preserve same-task rewire and shared-reader symmetry, and do not broaden this into a frame API change or another per-render acquisition path. If using entry invalidation, account for multi-key/shared entries and still release old registrations exactly once.

Focused acceptance: cover the later-task sequence in a real DOM test with a forced same-head props rerender and a subsequent successor write; assert both painted C and actual reacquired membership. Keep synchronous reincarnation and no-successor teardown rows green, plus final unmount returning cells/edges to zero. A native single-query hook control should exercise the same underlying entry behavior, not duplicate a new implementation.

Dedupe: current all-status searches for reincarnation, collector, cell and same-id plus the relevant reincarnation memory; read closed rf2-6r9j.194 fully (lexical rename only). Historical rf2-2l17/rf2-hic-013 no longer resolve in the tracker or checked tracked JSONL; their surviving full ruling in docs/design/hicasso/product/invariants.md:111-119 was read, including microtask/pre-paint and zero-cell no-successor requirements. This extends the documented later-task recovery beyond its untested one-off cold read, not a reversal of that ruling. Related rf2-1frc is UIx's independent cached-reaction eviction/acquisition mechanism, not the Hicasso collector.
acceptance_criteria: Real DOM: keep the same query/view mounted, destroy the frame and drain the microtask, recreate it later, force same-head props rerender, then change successor data. Verify live value and one reacquired membership, then zero residue on unmount. Preserve synchronous reincarnation, exact no-successor teardown and shared/multi-key cleanup.

title: [implementation/core/observability] Deferred error projection borrows ambient event classification
description:
Reviewed source: 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd. Current-main HEAD bc868b065a4656390e69426375bcac47511899ae checked before filing; projection.cljc, classification.cljc, registrar.cljc, live_frame.cljc and error_emit.cljc are unchanged from the snapshot.

Expected / actual
`rf/project-egress` promises that an explicit frame, or a recognised record's own frame, governs projection. For event-shaped slots it additionally applies the dispatched handler's own registration classification (spec/015-Data-Classification.md:247; projection.cljc:60-74). In an image-local application, that handler belongs to the owning frame's resolved generation, not the process registry or the tool's ambient frame.

Actual: projection.cljc:242-267 invokes `:classification/redact-event-by-registration` with only the event. classification.cljc:189-200,395-401 resolves that event's marks through registrar/handler-meta, which deliberately consults ambient `*generation*` (registrar.cljc:224-244,832-855). project-egress at projection.cljc:594-617 seeds the owner only into the leaf walker's opts and never establishes the owner's registration-resolution scope. The image-local event declaration is therefore absent, or replaced by an unrelated ambient declaration. The app-db walker cannot recover transient event-payload classification. An error with a declared-sensitive password ships the password under the default off-box-observability profile after dispatch returns.

Supported caller and context loss
The current public corpus error listener is specifically available to custom cross-frame recorders (core.cljc:2195-2228; spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1319). error_emit.cljc:637-646 delivers its event-centric error record with the event after only app-db elision, before the separate frame sink route. A recorder can retain it, add the documented :rf.observe/error discriminator, and invoke the public projection boundary on export. Once dispatch returns, its target-generation binding is gone. The isolated witness below captures a REAL handler error through `rf/register-listener! :errors`, returns from `rf/dispatch-sync`, and then calls `rf/project-egress`. The source of the input is not a fabricated handler/registry stub.

The current raw listener retirement is already owned by rf2-kuky.69; this issue does not preserve or redesign that door. The durable defect is the independently public record-projection operation accepting an owner but borrowing another registration universe. Direct project-egress callers and explicit target overrides remain affected regardless of the listener migration. Ordinary inline sink routing while the owning generation is already bound is the passing control, not the claimed failure.

Small isolated actual-source witness (Babashka, core src classpath; no build or test fixture):

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.core :as rf]
         '[re-frame.image :as image]
         '[re-frame.live-frame :as live-frame]
         '[re-frame.classification]
         '[re-frame.substrate.adapter :as adapter]
         '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as plain])
(adapter/install-adapter! plain/adapter)
(live-frame/make-frame
  {:id :review/owner
   :images [(image/image
              {:id :review/image
               :registrations
               {:reg-event
                [[:review/login {:sensitive [[:password]]}
                  (fn [_ _] (throw (ex-info "review failure" {})))]]}})]}
  [])
(def errors (atom []))
(rf/register-listener! :errors :review/retain #(swap! errors conj %))
(try (rf/dispatch-sync [:review/login {:password "secret" :user "ann"}]
                       {:frame :review/owner})
     (catch Throwable _))
(def record (assoc (first @errors) :kind :rf.observe/error))
(defn projected-password []
  (get-in (rf/project-egress record
            {:rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-observability})
          [:event 1 :password]))
(println (projected-password)) ; actual "secret", expected :rf/redacted
(println (live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution
           :review/owner projected-password)) ; :rf/redacted (control)
```

The executed extended witness also built another image frame with the same event id but no sensitive declaration. Output, exit 0:
`:global-event-meta nil`
`:owner-declaration {:sensitive [[:password]]}`
`:projection-under-owner :rf/redacted`
`:projection-after-owner-scope secret`
`:projection-under-other secret`
`:confirmed`
`:captured-error-password secret`
`:deferred-captured-error-projection secret`

Impact / priority
P2: declared-sensitive transient args reach a real off-box projection result in supported image-local usage. No claim of arbitrary taint tracking, positional-argument privacy, an exception-object sanitizer, or a compromised sink. The password is explicitly classified at its actual owning event declaration.

Smallest repair
Run the registration-owned event projection under the same explicitly resolved target frame/generation already governing the record's leaf walk, using the existing frame-resolution seam. Preserve presence-aware owner precedence and nil/dead-frame fail-closed behavior. Do not globally change registrar reads, create a new API/profile/redaction policy, or add a parallel classification cache.

Focused acceptance
- Real inline-image-only event with :sensitive [[:password]]: deferred :rf.observe/error projection redacts password with opts frame omitted, and explicit target frame overrides a different ambient generation.
- Same-id event in another frame/global store has a conflicting declaration: target owner's declaration wins; unclassified sibling payload remains visible.
- Existing owning-scope sink behavior, registration :large paths, explicit nil/dead owner fail-closed, default handled-event omission, and raw subscription-query identity exception remain unchanged.
- Exercise the public boundary in CLJ and focused CLJS tests; do not rely solely on directly binding registrar internals in the regression assertion.

Dedupe and limits
Searched active AND closed classification/redaction/egress/image-local records and relevant memories. rf2-zimh is subscription-cache metadata joining ambient registrar, a different consumer; rf2-kuky.5 fixed key-presence frame selection for leaf walking, not registration resolution; rf2-kuky.65 owns lost producer attribution, and .67/.69 own process sink defaults/raw-listener retirement. No implementation changes or full suites/builds were run. Evidence is an isolated actual-source Babashka execution plus source/spec/caller tracing; CLJS execution and production optimized bundle verification were not performed.
acceptance_criteria: Image-local declared event password redacts through public project-egress after dispatch returns and under a conflicting ambient frame; owner precedence and nil/dead fail-closed stay intact, as do unclassified siblings, large marks and subscription query identity. Focused CLJ and CLJS regression.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9384: the event-slot registration pass in re-frame.projection now runs inside the resolved record owner's generation via a new late-bind seam :live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution (published at live-frame ns load; projection.cljc deliberately requires nothing but elision/error/late-bind). New .cljc regression error_projection_owner_scope_cljs_test exercises the public project-egress boundary with the owning generation unbound - red before, green after - plus both conflict directions and the unchanged global/frameless controls.

title: [implementation/core/views] Direct Form-3 reg-view* input is called as a render function instead of mounted
description:
Surface: implementation/core/views. Source review at snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd. Compared with mayor HEAD e8afc5fba80a638c1cdf436ae5f27127c3fc677b: relevant core views, registration macro/facade and reagent-slim constructor source unchanged; the API page only changed an unrelated clear-trace-buffer! entry.

Expected: reg-view* accepts the documented direct Form-3 shape `(rf/reg-view* :id (r/create-class {...}))`. Mounting `[(rf/view :id) args]` should let React construct the component, render its :reagent-render, and run its lifecycle methods.

Actual and causal trace:
- docs/api/re-frame.core.md:383 explicitly advertises that direct create-class argument as an app-facing use of reg-view*. core.cljc:815 also names Form-3/create-class bodies in the function contract.
- The CLJS facade passes the supplied value unchanged to rf.views/reg-view* (core.cljc:824); views.cljs:851 sends it through compose-view. For Reagent, neither adapter wrap nor componentize hook changes the value into a class-mounting render function.
- build-frame-aware-view calls `(apply render-fn args)` unconditionally at views.cljs:595. When the supplied render-fn IS the create-class constructor, this calls the constructor as an ordinary function. It does not return an element mounting the class and does not invoke its :reagent-render under a real class instance. React never receives that class as the component to construct, so its lifecycle is lost and the render result is invalid or the constructor throws, depending on its this/argument shape.
- The class discrimination in views/source_coord_annotation.cljs:76,147 is too late: it examines the OUTPUT of the call, not the registered INPUT. That guard correctly handles an outer render function returning a class, but cannot protect a constructor that has already been called.
- The repo-owned reagent-slim class constructor independently shows why a normal function call is not rendering: implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:665-674 calls React.Component against this, assigns state and argv, and returns this; its actual render and lifecycle methods are installed on the prototype at 687 onward. It needs React construction, not apply.

Minimal supported reproduction to add to a focused stock-Reagent DOM test (source-derived; not executed during this review):

```clojure
(rf/init! adapter/adapter)
(rf/make-frame {:id :class-probe})
(def lifecycle (atom []))
(def panel
  (r/create-class
    {:reagent-render (fn [label] [:div {:id "class-probe"} label])
     :component-did-mount (fn [_] (swap! lifecycle conj :mount))
     :component-will-unmount (fn [_] (swap! lifecycle conj :unmount))}))
(rf/reg-view* ::panel panel)
(def root (adapter/client-root))
(adapter/render! root
  [rf/frame-provider {:frame :class-probe}
   [(rf/view ::panel) "hello"]]
  mount-element)
;; Flush with the existing DOM harness's act/flush helper.
;; Expected: #class-probe has text hello; lifecycle is [:mount].
(adapter/unmount! root)
;; Expected after flush: lifecycle is [:mount :unmount].
```

Impact: an author taking the advertised direct Form-3 escape hatch gets a component that cannot mount correctly, rather than a registered lifecycle-owning component. This is not a request to broaden reg-view to native UIx/Hicasso macros or to redesign registration.

Smallest repair: normalize a recognized Reagent-family class input into a stable class-mounting render boundary before it reaches the ordinary render-function call. Preserve the class's identity, arguments and lifecycle; avoid modifying the supplied constructor. The neutral structural class recognition already exists in source_coord_annotation. Keep Form-1/Form-2 paths and the existing outer-fn-returning-class path unchanged. Correct any direct-class contract wording if the repaired mounting spelling needs precision.

Dedupe: searched all statuses using the full issue list plus reg-view/create-class/Form-3 searches, and relevant Form-3/reg-view memories. rf2-oz7wr and rf2-8mkmb concern adapter-dependent lookup/cache derivation; rf2-02w1 concerns component-valued defwrapper hooks, not this registration input. rf2-kuky.60 concerns Hicasso descriptors/spec lines, not class registration. rf2-e6hsn no longer resolves in bd; its durable regression source was read: reagent_slim_source_coord_form3_cljs_test.cljs registers `(fn [] slim-class)` and tests the returned class by manually constructing it. The stock form_3_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs:172 also registers an outer fn returning the class. Neither is the direct-class shape here.

Verification limits: source-only causal proof. No CLJS compilation, browser/React execution, full suites, implementation edits, dependency installs or shared runtime mutation. In particular, the exact runtime error text is not claimed as measured. A focused DOM mount of the direct-class input is the acceptance witness; direct invocation under with-frame is not a substitute.
acceptance_criteria: Focused stock-Reagent DOM test passes an actual create-class result directly to reg-view*, mounts rf/view beneath a frame-provider, verifies rendered props plus exactly-once mount/unmount lifecycle, and covers pre-init registration. Preserve normal Form-1/Form-2 and outer-fn-returning-class controls; verify production too because the erroneous apply is not debug-only.
notes:
2026-09-07 (worker corebugs-a, PR #9384): premise RE-VERIFIED at tip and LEFT OPEN, no code change. views.cljs still calls (apply render-fn args) unconditionally at the build-frame-aware-view render site (now inside the rf.performance/mark-and-measure bracket, the only drift since the review snapshot), and views/source_coord_annotation.cljs's reagent-class? discrimination still inspects the OUTPUT of that call, never the registered input - so a create-class value handed straight to reg-view* is invoked as a plain function. Not repaired here for a GATE reason rather than a difficulty one: the acceptance witness is a stock-Reagent DOM mount with exactly-once mount/unmount lifecycle, whose only lane is the CLJS browser suite, and this dispatch's gate policy ruled that lane out (~1h sequential locally; CI runs it in parallel). A failing-first red-then-green could not be shown locally, and this fix should not land unwitnessed. Re-dispatch to a worker whose nominated gate IS that lane. Sketch for whoever takes it: normalize a recognized Reagent-family class at compose-view/registration time into a stable class-mounting boundary, ahead of the render call - note the annotation path's vector branch will then see [TheClass & args] as the root, so the pass-through has to be arranged so the class identity survives without the outer view trying to annotate it.
2026-09-07 (worker corev-a, PR #9387): PREMISE MEASURED AND IT DOES NOT REPRODUCE ON STOCK REAGENT. Left OPEN, narrowed. This dispatch nominated the CLJS browser lane precisely so the acceptance witness corebugs-a could not run would run; it ran, and it acquitted the code. The source reading in the description is CORRECT and was never executed: views.cljs still ends in an unconditional (apply render-fn args), and source_coord_annotation's reagent-class? still inspects the render OUTPUT rather than the registered INPUT. The directly registered create-class mounts correctly anyway. Measurement, three runs of npm run test:browser from implementation/, each exit code captured on the runner's own command line: (1) with a candidate repair in place (normalize a recognized Reagent-family class into a class-mounting boundary at the head of compose-view) exit 0, 819 tests / 4481 assertions, 0 failures. (2) repair DISABLED, and the disabled form verified in the COMPILED bundle - 'var render_fn = registered_fn;' in out/browser-test/js/cljs-runtime/re_frame.views.js, so the change reached the runtime and not merely the source - exit 0, the same 819/4481, 0 failures. Every direct-class assertion still passed: rendered props from :reagent-render under a real class instance, and exactly-once :component-did-mount / :component-will-unmount. (3) fault planted in the FIXTURE itself, exit 1, exactly 1 failure - so the green in (2) is not a fixture that never ran. A green sabotage run is a reason to stop, so the src change was withdrawn and the branch touches neither views.cljs nor views/source_coord_annotation.cljs. WHAT SURVIVES AS A HYPOTHESIS: reagent-slim, which the measurement does not reach. Its class is built differently - constructor tagged cljsReagentClass with prototype.render rather than prototype.reagentRender, and its constructor calls React.Component against this and returns this (adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs). The description already cites that as independent evidence; it is now the ONLY unrefuted arm. A re-dispatch should target the reagent-slim lane (npm run test:reagent-slim:smoke and the slim testbed), not stock Reagent. COVERAGE LANDED REGARDLESS: implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/form_3_direct_class_dom_cljs_test.cljs pins the advertised direct Form-3 shape for pre-init (top-level ns-load) and post-init registration, with Form-1 and outer-fn-returning-class controls. Nothing covered that shape before - both existing Form-3 fixtures register an outer fn that RETURNS a class - so if the direct shape ever does break, this is what says so. The candidate repair is preserved in this branch's history (first commit on worker/corev-a, reverted by the second) if the slim arm turns out to need it.
MAYOR ERRATUM 2026-09-08 00:3x AUSEST — the close reason above lost three tokens to shell expansion when it was written (unquoted backticks in a double-quoted argument were run as command substitutions and their output spliced in as empty). Nothing about the verdict changed; three identifiers vanished mid-sentence. Restored here:

- "handed a JS function with no cljs" should read: handed a JS function with no  cljs$lang$applyTo  property.
- "so  is the constructor object itself" should read: so  this  is the constructor object itself.
- " is therefore a reagent-class? value" should read: the RETURN VALUE (bound as  out  at the call site) is therefore a reagent-class? value.

The verdict is unchanged and stands: rf2-xccd is refuted on both stock Reagent and reagent-slim, the output-side discrimination is sufficient, and no input-side fix is wanted.

GENERIC LESSON worth keeping: prose containing backticks, dollar signs or parentheses must not be passed to a shell inside double quotes. Use a quoted heredoc. This failure is silent in exactly the way that matters — the command reports success, the record looks complete, and only a re-read finds the gaps.
close_reason: REFUTED ON BOTH ARMS, and the mechanism is now recorded in the tree. Closed on the fence this bead set for itself: PR #9387 (worker corev-a) merged at 284d82daac and carries the acceptance witness, implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/form_3_direct_class_dom_cljs_test.cljs. HISTORY, because this bead was measured three times: (1) corebugs-a re-verified the PREMISE at tip and left it open for a gate reason — the witness needs the CLJS browser lane, ~1h sequential locally, which that dispatch's gate policy ruled out. (2) corev-a then measured it ON that lane across three runs, including the repair disabled and verified absent from the compiled bundle plus a planted fixture fault taking the lane red, and REFUTED it for stock Reagent — withdrawing its own repair on the green sabotage run, which is the right response to a sabotage that does not bite. It narrowed the bead to one unrefuted arm, reagent-slim. (3) viewfix-a closed that arm by finding the MECHANISM corev-a had not: cljs.core/apply, handed a JS function with no cljs, bottoms out in (.apply f f ...) so  is the constructor object itself. Both supported constructors end (React.Component.call this props ...) ... this — stock Reagent 2.0.1 create-class's cmp, read from the jar in ~/.m2, and reagent2.impl.component/create-class* in adapters/reagent-slim — so calling one as a plain function stamps fields onto the class object and RETURNS THE CLASS.  is therefore a reagent-class? value, which inject-source-coord-attr's Form-3 branch passes through untouched and each substrate mounts as [klass & args]. The direct Form-3 shape reduces in one step to the already-covered outer-fn-returns-class path. CONCLUSION: the output-side discrimination is SUFFICIENT, not 'too late'; no input-side fix is wanted, which is also why the sabotage came back green. Form-1/Form-2 are untouched because the defect never reaches them — they hand a render fn, not a constructor. PR #9400 (open at close time, 86/87 with one check finishing) adds 29 lines of comment at the (apply render-fn args) site recording that the apply SPELLING is load-bearing: rewriting it as a direct call or (.apply render-fn nil ...) binds  to undefined and breaks the advertised direct Form-3 shape on every substrate at once, with nothing in the tree naming the cause. That comment is the durable protection; this close does not depend on it landing.

title: Spec 016 SSR: state the shipped projection-metadata contract at :1609 (framework computes, host records, no trace op) + projection-metadata docstring clock caveat

title: method: the dispatch preamble tells every worker to walk history fields that do not exist — notes and design are absent from bd history's schema, so the currency walk fails OPEN on the one field the mayor writes rulings into
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-04 by worker/machvest-a, which controlled the instrument in both directions before trusting it, and re-verified by the mayor on rf2-6r9j.2.

docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md's common preamble instructs every worker: 'WALK ADJACENT PAIRS NEWEST-FIRST UNTIL THE FIRST CHANGE TO A TEXT-BEARING FIELD (description, notes, acceptance, design)'.

THE FIELDS A bd history --json SNAPSHOT ACTUALLY CARRIES on this build, measured:
  acceptance_criteria, close_reason, closed_at, created_at, created_by,
  description, id, issue_type, owner, priority, status, title, updated_at

So of the four the preamble names: description EXISTS; acceptance is spelled acceptance_criteria; and notes and design DO NOT EXIST AT ALL.

WHY THIS FAILS OPEN, which is the whole defect. A worker keying its walk on 'notes' or 'design' reads null in every snapshot. Null hashes constant across every adjacent pair, so the walk reports NO TEXT-BEARING CHANGE — the exact false-clean the preamble exists to prevent, arrived at by following the preamble exactly. Nothing errors and the answer is well-formed. machvest-a hit this and only caught it because it controlled the detector against a field it knew varied.

AND THE MISSING FIELD IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. 'notes' is where the mayor writes rulings, sequencing fences, audit reopenings and salvage records — via bd update --append-notes. It is the field whose currency the walk exists to establish. bd history cannot order notes by mutation time AT ALL on this build, so the instruction promises a capability the tool does not have. Workers DO see notes rendered by bd show; what they cannot do is establish WHEN a note arrived relative to a description edit, which is precisely the ordering problem the paragraph was written to solve.

THE FIX, and it needs both halves:
1. Correct the field list to what the schema carries: description and acceptance_criteria. Drop notes and design from the enumeration.

title: validate-with-schemas how-to never says validation is whole-registry per commit
description:
docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md teaches `reg-app-schema` / `reg-app-schemas` and
never states the one fact a reader needs to use them safely: validation is NOT scoped to the
paths the committing event touched. At every `:db` commit the runtime walks EVERY registered
path over the WHOLE candidate app-db with `get-in` and rejects the entire transaction if any
one of them fails (spec/010 §Per-step recovery row 4). A path nothing has written yet reads
`nil`, so a registration made before its slice is seeded rejects every commit until the seed
lands - and if the seeds are spread across separate events, the first seed is rejected by its
not-yet-seeded siblings and app-db never leaves `{}`.

That is the whole of rf2-2xzc, and rf2-ghxt is the same defect in the sibling example. Two of
the repo's own flagship applications got it wrong, so it is not an exotic corner: the two
idioms that compose into it - a bulk `reg-app-schemas` at ns-load, and a per-feature
`:*/initialise` fan-out from `:app/initialise` - are both idioms this corpus teaches.

The remedy the corpus already knows is written only in a code comment, in
examples/patterns/boot/schema.cljs: 'Each slot below starts out nil - the boot machine fills
it in later - so every registration wears a `:maybe` to stay valid through the loading
phases.' That sentence, and the reason behind it, belong in the how-to.

WANTED, roughly a paragraph plus an example: state that the registry is walked whole at every
commit; state that an unwritten path reads nil and is validated like any other value; give
the two ways out (seed the slice before or in the same commit as everything else, or wear a
`:maybe` for the boot window); and say plainly that a production build elides the validator,
so an app that gets this wrong works in release and is dead in dev - the direction of the
dev/release split that makes this so disorienting to meet.

Gate: docs/ is inside check_doc_slugs.py's roots AND is built by `mkdocs build --strict`
(docs_dir is `docs`), so both apply to an edit here. Neither validates prose, so table columns
and anchors get checked by hand.
notes: AUDIT PR #9141: The new boot paragraph conflates the :fx-only fan-out event with the child :db seed events. The shown :app/initialise is not app-db-validated, so every child dispatch fires; each child seed is then rejected while siblings remain nil. Correct the causal account and pin both shapes.

RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: this close REVERTED and the payload is on the trunk.

Delivered by worker/docfix-a in PR #9141, MERGED. Verified in SOURCE at origin/main, not from the PR record: docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md:159 now carries the section 'Every registered path is checked on every commit'.

The worker verified the mechanism at source rather than taking it from its brief: validate-app-schema! loops storage/frame-schema-entries reading each registered path with (get-in db registered-path), and spec/010 row 4 confirms the candidate is never installed on failure. It also found the detail the brief did not have and put it in the doc — row 4 says :fx DOES NOT WALK for a rejected dispatch, which is precisely WHY a per-feature :*/initialise fan-out never fires and app-db never leaves {}. The dev/release elision direction was confirmed in spec/010 §Production builds and in the debug-enabled? gate as the outermost form of the validator.

Gates: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py captured exit 0, python -m mkdocs build --strict captured exit 0, each proved by a planted fault that went red naming the plant, restores verified by git blob hash.

title: schemas: an app-db candidate rejection (:rollback? true) also reports on the :errors stream under the dev gate (Option A, PR1: :where :app-db)
description:
RULED 2026-09-04 21:03:56 AUSEST (delegated ruling; see the RULING note for the full analysis, the reviewer positions, the contract wording, the implementation guidance, traps and acceptance criteria). This bead is PR1 of Option A: in a DEV build, an app-db candidate rejection (:rf.error/schema-validation-failure, :where :app-db, :rollback? true) ALSO fans one STRUCTURAL-ONLY record per failing registered path onto the always-on :errors stream, from inside validate-app-schema!'s existing debug-enabled? gate, through the :error-emit/dispatch-error-record late-bind hook (the union-record helper the :rf.schema/at-boundary arm uses). The dev trace stays byte-identical; production is untouched by construction; the rf2-fu75 dev console fallback then prints the rejection for free when nothing owns the stream. This is an additive SPEC AMENDMENT (spec/009 promotion criterion + row 1984, spec/010 row 4) plus code in implementation/schemas, a docstring in error_emit.cljc, three docs pages and tests. spec/009 and spec/010 are one-toucher hot-zone files - sequence at dispatch. PR2 (machine-data + malformed-schema rollback sites) is the follow-up bead created from this one and waits for this PR to MERGE.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (2026-09-04 on worker/dispatchlater-a, with a control that fired). :rf.error/schema-validation-failure (:where :app-db) is emitted through re-frame.trace/emit-error! only - implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc, emit-validation-failure! and its emit-malformed-schema! sibling - and NOT through the both-axes emitter the router uses for other errors (re-frame.error-emit/emit-error-both!). So it reaches the DEV-ONLY :trace stream and never the always-on :errors stream. On one live page, one frame, one dispatch: a listener on :errors recorded 0 records while a listener on :trace recorded 17 :rf.error/schema-validation-failure records with :rollback? true for the SAME dispatch, whose :events-stream outcome was :rolled-back. CONTROL, same frame, same listener: dispatching an unregistered event id DID reach :errors as {:error :rf.error/no-such-handler ...}, so the listener was live and the zero is real. Codex independently reproduced the split in a fresh JVM: {:db {:n 0}, :errors 0, :traces 1, :outcome :rolled-back}.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is what made rf2-2xzc cost a pilot a third of its run. An application-wide, permanent app-db rollback loop produced 0 page errors, 0 console messages of any level, 0 failed requests, and nothing on the stream an application registers to hear about its own errors. The only surface that said anything was the dev trace, which has no default listener - so unless the developer already had Xray open and knew to look, the app simply rendered empty. The class is every reg-app-schema in every app, not the boot window.

THE ARGUMENT FOR THE OLD BEHAVIOUR, weighed and overruled: the candidate validator is dev-only by design (spec/010 Production builds), so there is no production error to report, and :errors is documented as the always-on stream; error_emit.cljc 421-424 recorded trace-only as correct, not a gap. The ruling: the promotion criterion governs what MUST ride the always-on axis in every build; it does not forbid a check that is compiled out of production from reporting, in the build where it runs, that it discarded a whole transaction. Always-on describes the stream's survival, not a promise that every producer exists in every build.
notes:
DOSSIER 2026-09-04 15:45:28 AUSEST (mayor, at Mike's request): decision dossier written at ai/decisions/rf2-xpd8.schema-rollback-errors-stream.md (local-only, lives until the ruling lands). RECOMMENDATION: Option A - fan the rejection onto the :errors axis too, under the validator's existing debug gate, as a structural-only record (one per failing registered path) through the :error-emit/dispatch-error-record union helper the :rf.schema/at-boundary arm already uses; production untouched by construction (the validator does not run there). Scope to every :rollback? true producer (:app-db first, then :machine-data + :rf.error/malformed-schema in a second PR). One-line reason: rf2-fu75 (2026-08-13) already ruled that an untooled dev build must surface a framework refusal, and a transaction rejection is the one refusal that ruling's mechanism cannot reach because it never enters the axis the console fallback and the listener hang off. FACTS THE BEAD DOES NOT SAY THAT CHANGE THE WEIGHING: (1) the current behaviour is a RECORDED decision, not an oversight: error_emit.cljc:421-424 says dev schema checks staying trace-only "is correct, not a gap", and spec/009's promotion criterion leg 1 names dev-only schema validation as staying diagnostic - so Option A is a SPEC AMENDMENT (additive: a MAY route under the check's own gate), not a bug fix. (2) The rf2-fu75 dev console fallback already exists and fires for free under A (reached from both dispatch-on-error! and dispatch-error-record*), which makes Option C (a second printer in the validator) strictly dominated. (3) reason-string interpolates type-of-value, never the value ("..., got nil."), so the app-db arm's :reason can ride the always-on record - unlike the boundary arm, whose :reason was omitted for interpolating attacker-controlled payload. (4) The always-on :events stream DOES carry the rollback today as :outcome :rolled-back; it is absent only from the stream built for errors. The 0-vs-17 measurement was not re-run (no builds); it is consistent with the code.
RULING 2026-09-04 21:03:56 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-04, operator-reversible; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-xpd8.schema-rollback-errors-stream.md and its Codex Recommendation section folded here and deleted). Verified read-only at tip 1ad17a77fe (== origin/main, clean). rf2-fu75 does not resolve as a bead id on this build (bd show fails, no memory) - the ruling it names survives verbatim in error_emit.cljc lines 90-160 (RULED rf2-fu75, 2026-08-13, commit fcf866ea1d), in error_emit_dev_console_dom_cljs_test.cljs, and in spec/009 line 1283; nothing here depends on the bead itself.

THE RULING. Option A, with the Codex record-shape correction, in two PRs. A dev-gated candidate-transition rejection (:rollback? true) ALSO fans one STRUCTURAL-ONLY record per failing registration onto the always-on :errors stream, from inside the validator's existing debug-enabled? gate, through the :error-emit/dispatch-error-record late-bind hook (the union-record helper the :rf.schema/at-boundary arm already uses). The dev trace is byte-identical to today. No new printer, no knob, no new category, no aggregation, no dedup. Production is untouched by construction: the record is emitted from inside the same outermost gate as the check, so a release build carries neither. The rf2-fu75 console fallback then fires for free (reached from dispatch-error-record*) when nothing owns the stream, which is what turns a permanent silent rollback loop into red console lines naming the registered path, the event and got nil. This is a SPEC AMENDMENT (the trace-only behaviour was recorded as correct, not a gap, in error_emit.cljc 421-424 and in spec/009 promotion-criterion leg 1), not a bug fix; the amendment is additive and its exact wording is under IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE. Scope: PR1 (this bead) = the :where :app-db arm. PR2 (follow-up bead, filed below) = :where :machine-data at its :rollback? true phases plus the two :rf.error/malformed-schema :rollback? true sites. One semantic ruling, two PRs, PR2 waits for PR1 to MERGE (spec/009 hot-zone). Granularity: one record per failing registered entry (the trace's shape); the single-bounded-report idiom is NOT pre-built - its trigger is a measured unusable console, and the note records that trigger rather than a bead.

OPTIONS REJECTED. B (docs only): a doc helps only a reader who already suspects the mechanism; the incident's whole cost was that three investigators did not. Fixes nothing. C1 (console.error from the validator): a second printer with a second gate beside the one rf2-fu75 built; prints even when an app owns :errors (the nag rf2-fu75 avoided); gives the listener and the frame sink nothing. Dominated by A, which gets the console line from the existing fallback. C2 (a default :trace listener that logs :rf.error/*): the framework deliberately ships no default trace listener (spec/009 section User-side listener registration, line ~1124); would duplicate Xray on every row and need an off-switch. C3 (reg-app-schema registers a default :errors listener): registering ANY listener silences the fallback for every other category. Strictly harmful. D (do nothing): the class is every reg-app-schema in every app, not the boot window; PR #9134 and rf2-aaam reduced the odds of THIS mistake only. Also rejected: flipping :rf.error/malformed-schema's Channel column to always-on in PR2 (the dossier proposed it) - the column states what SURVIVES ELISION and nothing on that category does; the dev-gated route is named in row prose instead, so always-on-categories and the channel conformance test stay untouched in both PRs.

REVIEWER POSITIONS. Dossier (mayor, 15:32 AUSEST): recommends A, per-path, structural-only, two PRs (app-db first; machine-data + malformed-schema second), one additive criterion paragraph; proposed carrying :path and the existing :reason on the record because reason-string interpolates type-of-value rather than the value. Codex Recommendation: CONCURS on A, per-path, two PRs, no second printer, no knob, no aggregation; DISSENTS on the record shape, and the tree says Codex is right: (1) :path is NOT intrinsically structural - validate.cljc lines 58-62 and 822-847 document that a :set failure's segment is the failing ELEMENT VALUE and a :map-of key rides as the key; sanitize-sensitive-path scrubs only when the leaf is :sensitive?, so a non-sensitive set element or map-of key ships verbatim in :path today; (2) reason-string (lines 297-303) interpolates (pr-str schema) - unbounded - and the same path, so it is neither bounded nor purely an identifier even though the failing value itself is absent. So the record is BUILT FROM a closed allow-list of structural inputs, never filtered down from tags (the spec's own rule for the boundary arm, spec/010 ~line 235 and spec/009 row 1984 prose). Codex's independent evidence: reproduced the split in a fresh JVM at df66b1679496 - frame with [:n] [:int], valid seed, one event writing {:n "bad"} -> {:db {:n 0}, :errors 0, :traces 1, :outcome :rolled-back}; the always-on :events ledger carries the consequence but never the cause and never activates the console fallback. Codex's other contributions, all verified: emit the small record BEFORE the trace, matching emit-error-both!'s axis-1-then-axis-2 ordering (error_emit.cljc ~690-705), so the SSR last-write-wins buffer's final input is the richer trace; JVM SSR dual delivery is benign and documented (ssr/error_listener.cljc 333-360) but must be pinned; a non-:event schema failure must stay the projector's generic 500, never the boundary arm's 400 (error_projector.cljc 133-137 gates the 400 on :where :event, so this holds without code); cover only :rollback? true - do NOT promote recover-and-continue arms (:fx-args, :sub-return, :sub-override, :flow-output, :machine-output, machine :spawn / :update-snapshot with :rollback? false); Xray (panels/epoch/projection.cljc 2022-2186, view.cljs 5320-5383) and Story derive rollback from the trace and keep receiving it unchanged; the only material uncertainty is console volume, unmeasured. Dossier contributions preserved: the :events stream DOES carry the rollback today as :outcome :rolled-back (so the fact is absent only from the stream built for errors); the router's (false? commit-result) branch at router.cljc 2686-2689 is the single point a bounded report would hang off, but it holds only a boolean, so a single report would need the validator hook to return the paths - more surface, deferred; the Sentry bridge in docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md 62-65 is gated on production AND (not debug-enabled?), so a dev :errors listener is deliberate and rare, and one that wants to drop rollbacks keys on :rollback? true; the rf2-fu75 fallback's three conditions (debug-enabled?, browser host via js/document, EMPTY registry) all hold on a fresh dev app; the four things the dossier could be wrong about: criterion amendable additively (ruled yes - see wording), N-per-dispatch acceptable (ruled yes, bounded), dev listeners rare (yes, documented-filter problem), elision holds (the probe is the witness). CONDENSED what-the-developer-sees table (dev build, browser host, no :errors listener): Today - page renders pre-event/empty state; console nothing at any level; :errors 0 (control: no-such-handler arrives); frame :observability :errors sink nothing; :events {:outcome :rolled-back}; :trace one schema-validation-failure per failing path; Xray open shows the :db row red + Schema Violation card + rollback mute, Xray closed nothing; window.onerror nothing (no throw); network no request; release build installs everything and reports :ok. Under A - page unchanged; console one [re-frame2] :rf.error/schema-validation-failure - <reason> line + the record per failing path via the existing fallback; :errors one structural record per failing path; sink receives the projected record (dev only); :events, :trace, Xray, onerror, network, release all unchanged (a console line may coexist with an Xray row, accepted under rf2-fu75). With an :errors listener registered: the listener receives the records and the console stays quiet (the rf2-fu75 ownership rule). Under B and D every cell is today's; under C1 only the console cell changes, printed regardless of listeners.

WHAT THIS BEAD NOW IS. A dispatchable worker task (status open, type task - the behaviour it changes was a recorded decision, now amended; priority stays P2). Title amended to name PR1. One worker, one worktree, one PR. spec/009-Instrumentation.md and spec/010-Schemas.md are one-toucher hot-zone files: at ruling time PR #9182 (worker/specdoc-a, rf2-6g6e) was OPEN against spec/009 - sequence this dispatch behind its merge and re-check gh pr list for both files at dispatch.
IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (PR1, :where :app-db).
Emitter. implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc. Add a private helper (e.g. emit-app-db-rejection-record!) beside emit-validation-failure! (line 325) and call it at the app-db emit site (the (emit-validation-failure! tags) at ~line 884), immediately BEFORE the trace emit and under the SAME (continue?) guards (a stale incarnation emits nothing on either axis). Do NOT put a :where dispatch inside emit-validation-failure! - that seam serves all eight arms and a :where switch there is the shape that lets a future arm leak onto the axis by default. Reach the hook with (late-bind/get-fn-cached :error-emit/dispatch-error-record) - validate.cljc already requires re-frame.late-bind, re-frame.error and re-frame.interop, so no new require; nil hook (core's error-emit ns not loaded) -> skip silently. Never static-require re-frame.error-emit from the schemas artefact. Precedent for the call shape: router.cljc emit-boundary-rejection-record! (lines 2747-2775) and the machines / SSR union records named in spec/009 row prose. The call sits inside validate-app-schema!'s outermost (if interop/debug-enabled? ...) (line ~651), so a release build reaches neither the call nor its literals; keep the @validator-fn deref outside the gate predicate as the existing comment requires.
Record shape - BUILT FROM structural inputs (registered-path, event-id, frame-id, and the type tag of the failing leaf), never (select-keys tags ...): {:error :rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :app-db :registered-path <registration root> :event-id <event id> :failing-id <event id> :frame <frame-id> :rollback? true :recovery :no-recovery :reason <sentence> :time (interop/now-ms)}. Both :event-id and :failing-id are always PRESENT (nil only on a direct validate call outside a run - the elision probe and unit tests - which no runtime path produces), so the key set is closed and fixed. :reason is composed ONLY from the registered path and (error/type-of-value leaf-value) - a closed type vocabulary plus class names, never the value, never (pr-str schema), never the leaf path - e.g. "App-db candidate at registered path [:articles] failed its schema (got nil); the transaction was rejected and nothing installed." The got-<type> is what makes the incident self-diagnosing on the console line (seventeen lines all ending got nil), and it discloses nothing. Give the sentence a distinctive literal tail so the elision probe can prove it absent (reason-string's docstring states this convention). OMIT :path (may carry a set element value or a map-of key - see REVIEWER POSITIONS), :value, :explain, :explain-humanized, :schema, :received. The trace keeps all of those; Xray and Story keep working off it unchanged. If the leaf path proves needed on the record later, it needs a structural-path projection first (drop set-element and map-of-key segments); not in this PR.
Noise. N records per rejected commit where N = the number of FAILING registered entries for that frame - bounded above by the frame's registry size, and each record names a distinct violated registration (17 on the incident = 17 distinct absent slices). In a boot deadlock every :db-writing dispatch is rejected, so volume tracks the breakage exactly; that is the point. No dedup, no knob, no single-report shape now. The added tests exercise only `nil` and a ClojureScript string, so the fallback is unpinned.

Make the reason's type classifier total and closed over foreign CLJS values (for example a trusted host classification with a constant fallback, never the object's overridable `constructor` value or `toString`), and add a focused CLJS regression with a planted own `constructor` sentinel proving neither the record nor its reason contains it. Node probe: an own writable 'constructor' data field makes String(o.constructor) return the planted sentinel verbatim. title: hic docs: h/mount!'s config is documented as a closed three-key list, so a routed app (:url-bound?) or one with :fx-overrides has no documented way to boot
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F04 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `api`

**Trying to** Mount the migrated board while keeping the two things the frame
must carry: `:url-bound? true` (the frame owns the browser URL — the app is
routed) and `:fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :linearlite.demo/http-stub}` (the
demo backend, without which nothing loads because the app ships no server).
Under Reagent both rode on `[rf/frame-root {…}]`.

**Expected** `h/mount!`'s config to be the Hicasso spelling of `frame-root`'s
options, since the api-reference says mounting is "`rf/frame-root`'s vocabulary
reaching this arm".

**Instead** `h/mount!`'s `config` carries **exactly three** keys — `:frame`,
`:initial-events`, `:identifier-prefix` — and the reference says so as a closed
list. Neither `:url-bound?` nor `:fx-overrides` is among them, and neither word
appears anywhere in the Hicasso corpus except in the **SSR** module's
`:frame-opts` (`api-reference.md`: "for a request needing `:images`,
`:url-strategy` or `:fx-overrides`"). So the server renderer has a documented
door for frame options and the client mount does not.

**Looked at** `api-reference.md` §Roots and §"`h/mount!` and `h/hydrate!` are
not symmetric"; `cookbook.md` §"Boot" ("Seed in one place"); `00-installation.md`
§"What `h/mount!` creates"; grepped the whole corpus for `fx-overrides`,
`url-bound`, `frame-root`.

**Resolved by** A guess, from a paragraph written as a *hazard* rather than as a
recipe. Both the reference and the cookbook warn that "if you call
`rf/make-frame` yourself first, the mount joins and your `:initial-events` never
run". I read that backwards: if the mount *joins* a frame I made, then making
the frame myself is how I get options `h/mount!` cannot express. So boot is now

```clojure
(rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true
                :fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :linearlite.demo/http-stub}})
(h/mount! el {:frame :rf/default} [root-view {}])
```

It works. But nothing in the corpus says it is the intended shape, and the only
two places that mention the sequence describe it as a mistake people make. This
is the guess I would most like confirmed, and the single clearest documentation
hole I hit in the whole migration: **a Hicasso application that needs any frame
option beyond a seed has no documented way to boot.**

**Bead** Add one paragraph under §Roots: "`h/mount!` ensures a frame with
defaults. A frame needing `:url-bound?`, `:fx-overrides` or any other
`rf/make-frame` option is created first, and the mount joins it — seed from
`make-frame` in that case, not from the mount." Every routed application needs
`:url-bound?`, so this is on the critical path for most real apps, not an edge.
notes:
PR #9131 AUDIT EVIDENCE (2026-09-04): the new chapter-20 migration table now carries the exact same gap into the migration path. It says every row is only a spelling change and maps [rf/frame-root {:id :app ...}] directly to h/mount!'s {:frame :app ...} root configuration. That is safe only for the subset mount! can create: an id plus optional initial-events. Source confirms frame-root passes every rf/make-frame option through (:images, :url-bound?, :fx-overrides, :preset, and other record-config), while hicasso.impl.mount/ensure-frame! constructs only {:id frame-kw} plus optional :initial-events. A reader following the new row silently drops non-default frame configuration unless they first call rf/make-frame with the full options and let h/mount! join it. The fix for this bead should therefore update chapter 20's new row/explanation as well as the root docs it already owns.

That row still maps [rf/frame-root {:id :app ...}] directly to h/mount! config even though frame-root forwards record options and h/mount! silently ignores them. PR #9137 did not touch chapter 20. Keep this exact owner open until the migration row warns readers to pre-create the frame with its full options and let the mount join it.

Every PR this bead was sequenced behind has MERGED, and the remainder was re-verified in SOURCE at origin/main rather than inferred from the bead text. Details in the per-bead line below; the surface is free of every live worker as of this reading, but re-check before dispatching because that changes hourly.
SPECIFICS: PR #9139 (which held docs/core/hicasso/20-migration-from-reagent.md) has MERGED, and PR #9137 landed the chapter-00/07/api-reference half long since. The audit remainder is REAL and still at chapter 20 — the row now at :239 reads '[rf/frame-root {:id :app ...}] around the tree | h/mount!'s {:frame :app ...} root configuration, once the whole application is ported'. The trailing qualifier is NOT the warning the audit asked for: frame-root forwards every rf/make-frame option (:images, :url-bound?, :fx-overrides, :preset, record-config) while hicasso.impl.mount/ensure-frame! constructs only {:id frame-kw} plus optional :initial-events, so a reader following that row silently drops non-default frame configuration. Verified at source that views/frame_boundary/frame-root-opts is (dissoc props :children :fallback) so every make-frame option forwards (:url-bound?, :fx-overrides, :images, :preset, record-config), while hicasso.impl.mount/ensure-frame! builds only {:id frame-kw} plus optional :initial-events and root! reads only :frame/:initial-events/:identifier-prefix. The table lead-in now excepts the last row, the row says it is not a rename when the frame-root carries options, and a following paragraph gives the pre-create-with-make-frame-then-let-the-mount-join shape, linking the chapter 00 and 07 guidance PR #9137 landed. title: spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn has one extra closing brace — its :trace-emissions assertions are silently discarded
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 22:53 AUSEST by worker/specdrift-a while building the mechanical top-level-key census for rf2-7yth0.

DEFECT. spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn line 46 reads

    :error  nil}}}}

and needs THREE closing braces, not four. The fourth closes :fixture/expect's own map, which pushes :trace-emissions (line 48) and its two-event vector OUT of :fixture/expect and, with the file's final }, past the end of the top-level fixture map entirely. Final bracket depth is -1.

EVIDENCE. A bracket-depth scan of all 247 fixtures (comments blanked, strings and char literals collapsed to one opaque token, # before an opening delimiter treated as a dispatch prefix) returns final depth 0 for 246 files and -1 for this one — the only outlier in the corpus. Independently, the same scan reports :trace-emissions as a DEPTH-1 (top-level) key in this file alone; in the other 120 fixtures that carry it, it sits inside :fixture/expect where spec/conformance/README.md line 63 and spec/Spec-Schemas.md line 4597 both document it.

IMPACT — SILENT, NOT LOUD. Both loaders use clojure.edn/read-string on the whole file (implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_fixtures.clj load-fixture-from-file, and the JVM runner's slurp + read-string). read-string returns the FIRST form and ignores trailing text, so the fixture loads with a :fixture/expect carrying only :final-app-db and :final-runtime-db. The two trace assertions — the :rf.error/no-such-handler emission with :kind :route that is the whole point of the fixture, and the not-found route's :on-match :rf.event/run-start — are DISCARDED. Nothing errors; the fixture reports as passing while verifying less than it claims. This is the exact failure mode rf2-7yth0 exists to prevent, found by rf2-7yth0's own instrument.

FIX. Delete one } from line 46. One character.

DO NOT LAND IT BLIND. The two assertions have never executed, so enabling them may red the conformance runner. Whoever takes this runs the JVM conformance corpus (implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj) and the CLJS corpus runner before and after, and reports both. title: [method] gate-artefact cleanup uses a variable-expanded rm, which stalls on a permission prompt
notes:
FILED 2026-09-02 03:39 AUSEST from an OPERATOR REPORT (Mike, in chat), not from an audit.

THE FRICTION. Workers clean their gate artefacts with a variable-expanded deletion -
  rm -f "$SP"/*<worktree>*
- and a static permission check cannot evaluate $SP, so it must stop and ask. The ask lands
on an operator who may not be watching, and the worker stalls mid-turn with everything queued
behind it. Mike's words: "that results in the session locking up and asking me for permissions
to continue because the rm operation is potentially dangerous if $SP is blank."

THE HAZARD IS REAL, WHICH IS WHY THE CHECK IS RIGHT TO ASK. An unset or empty variable turns
"$SP"/*name* into a glob rooted at the top of the filesystem. So the repair removes the
AMBIGUITY, not the check.

SHIPPED as PR #8971 (mayor/rm-literal-path): one paragraph in the gate-mechanics block of
dispatch-prompt-template.md, beside the artefact-naming rule that generates this cleanup -
delete by the LITERAL path, never through a variable; and where a variable is genuinely
unavoidable, make the shell itself refuse an empty one ("${DIR:?}"), named as the FALLBACK
because it removes the hazard without removing the prompt.

A SECOND, STRUCTURAL OPTION WAS OFFERED TO MIKE AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE - it is his call, and
this bead is not authority for it. The template currently sends artefacts to the SESSION-shared
scratch directory, which is why the worktree-and-attempt naming rule exists and why a cleanup
command is needed at all. Writing them inside the worker's own worktree instead would let
scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh take them out on reap: no cleanup command, no glob, no
prompt, and the peer-collision half of the naming rule becomes unnecessary.

I MEASURED THE ONE THING THAT COULD HAVE BLOCKED THAT OPTION, so the decision is informed:
*.log is ALREADY gitignored repo-wide (.gitignore:14), so a gate-*.log written inside a
worktree is invisible to `git status --porcelain` (verified: clean tree with the file present)
and does not block removal (verified: the removal script's --dry-run accepted the tree). So the
structural option needs no tooling change - only a change to the instruction.

SCRIPT WART NOTED IN PASSING, not filed: remove-worker-worktree.sh --dry-run prints its
ordinary success line "OK: worktree removal complete." A reader could take that for a real
removal. It is inert - the worktree and branch were both verified intact afterwards - and not
worth a change on its own, but worth knowing before trusting that line.
