title: story: url-from-state drops every third-party query param from the address bar
description:
Found while fixing rf2-b7je1 (PR #8877); NOT fixed there — opposite defect, different surface.

## Finding

`re-frame.story.ui.url-state/url-from-state` composes the address-bar URL as
`(str pathname query-string-from-state hash)`, and its location snapshot
`current-location-shape` captures `{:pathname :hash}` only. `location.search`
is therefore discarded wholesale on every state-driven pushState: the query is
rebuilt from shell state alone, so any query param the shell does not own is
dropped from the address bar on the first state change after mount.

`embed=1` (rf2-pucku) is the concrete casualty. It is read once at mount by
`embed-flag-from-current-url` / `hydrate-embed-flag!` and seeded into
`[:chrome-visibility :embed?]`, so the running shell keeps behaving correctly —
but the URL in the address bar no longer carries the flag, so copying it, or
reloading after any interaction, loses embed mode. The same happens to any
third-party param (`from=`, analytics params, anything a host page appended).

## Contrast with rf2-b7je1

The share BUILDER (`share/variant-share-url`) is now explicitly authoritative
over exactly its own nine keys (`share/story-query-keys`) and preserves
everything else verbatim — rf2-b7je1's fix, with fixtures pinning `from=index`
and `embed=1` survival. `url-from-state` is the other writer of the same URL
and has the opposite policy: it owns the whole query string. The two writers
disagree about who owns unrelated params.

## Evidence

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/url_state.cljc` — `query-string-from-state`
  builds `?<query>` from `share/build-params` alone; `url-from-state` concatenates
  `pathname + that + hash`; `current-location-shape` returns `{:pathname :hash}`.
- `embed-flag-from-current-url` documents the flag as deliberately NOT
  round-tripped through `parse-params` ("chrome-state, not shell-state"), which
  explains why it is not in the built query — but not why it should be erased
  from the URL.

## Question for triage

Is address-bar canonicalisation (drop everything the shell does not own) the
intended contract, or should `url-from-state` preserve non-Story params the way
the share builder now does? If the latter, the natural repair reuses
`share/story-query-keys` as the ownership boundary in both writers. If the
former, say so in the `url-from-state` docstring — the asymmetry currently reads
as an oversight.

Not urgent: the live shell behaves correctly within a session; the loss is on
copy/paste and reload of an embed URL.
notes:
FENCED 2026-09-01 14:05 AUSEST by the mayor: sequenced behind PR #8877 (rf2-b7je1) MERGING. Same surface — tools/story's URL layer — and the two items are the SAME defect seen from opposite ends, which is worth stating so neither gets closed as a duplicate of the other. #8877 made the SHARE builder authoritative over the nine Story-owned query keys while preserving unrelated params (embed= among them, deliberately). This item is the other writer: url-state/url-from-state composes the address-bar URL from {:pathname :hash} only and discards location.search wholesale, so it DROPS the very params #8877 just took care to preserve. Two writers of one URL disagreeing about who owns unrelated params. Live shell behaviour is unaffected; the loss shows on copy/paste and reload. Dispatch after #8877 merges, and brief it to read #8877's story-query-keys vocabulary rather than re-deriving the ownership boundary.
FENCE CLEARED 2026-09-01 14:30 AUSEST by the mayor: PR #8877 (rf2-b7je1) is MERGED and on trunk 263735a3f0, so tools/story's URL layer is unheld. First in line when a worker slot frees; no remaining condition to test.

Carry forward from #8877 rather than re-deriving it: that change made the SHARE builder authoritative over a written-down set of NINE Story-owned query keys, now at share/story-query-keys, with a drift pin asserting that list equals what build-params can emit. embed= is deliberately NOT a member — it is chrome state, never round-tripped, and the builder preserves it. This item is the other writer of the same URL, so it should adopt that same ownership boundary rather than inventing a second one; brief it to read story-query-keys first.
VERDICT 2026-09-01 by the worker: FIXED in PR #8884 (branch worker/urlstate-gee8n).

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE, unchanged by PR #8877. The report's two claims both hold
at tip: url-from-state composed (str pathname query-string-from-state hash) from a
{:pathname :hash} shape, and current-location-shape captured those two keys only, so
location.search was discarded wholesale. #8877 did not touch url_state.cljc at all —
it landed entirely inside share.cljc and the two share test namespaces — so the file
was byte-identical to the state this item was filed against and no line number in the
report had drifted. The first-state-change-after-mount path is confirmed:
install-state-watcher! calls (url-from-state new (current-location-shape)) and hands
it to push!, whose idempotence check compares against (pathname + search + hash);
with search dropped from the candidate the two always differ, so the push always
fired and always shortened the URL.

THE TRIAGE QUESTION THE ITEM ASKED IS ANSWERED "the latter": url-from-state now
preserves non-Story params the way the share builder does, and it does so by reusing
share/story-query-keys rather than by re-deriving a boundary.

HOW THE TWO WRITERS NOW AGREE — they share the IMPLEMENTATION, not just the key
list. share/append-query-params (private) is promoted to the public
share/apply-story-params, and url-from-state merges through it against a
{:pathname :search :hash} location shape. This is stronger than sharing the
vocabulary: the two writers cannot drift on the merge ALGORITHM either — the
encoded-key comparison, the order preservation, the fragment placement. The item's
own suggestion (reuse story-query-keys as the ownership boundary in both writers) is
satisfied a level up from where it was pitched.

ANSWER TO "should the vocabulary be lifted somewhere both can see it": it already
was, and it should stay there. story-query-keys lives in share.cljc, which url_state
already required, so nothing needed moving — the defect was not that the vocabulary
was inaccessible but that the second writer never consulted it. Lifting it to a third
location would have created the extra place this class of bug lives in. What DID need
promoting was the function that applies it.

TWO THINGS FOUND THAT THE REPORT DID NOT NAME:

1. url_state carried a SECOND canonicalising composer, query-string-from-state, which
   built a canonical query with no preservation at all. It is removed — nothing called
   it once url-from-state stopped doing so, and leaving it in the file the boundary
   was just repaired in is how the defect would have recurred in a third place.

2. apply-story-params emitted a bare "?" when the merged query came out empty
   (clearing the last Story key off a search that held nothing else). Harmless for the
   share builder, but a live hazard for the address-bar writer: a bare "?" differs
   from location.search's empty string, so push! would have written a cosmetic history
   entry the shell could never match again. Fixed in the same function. The empty-base
   1-arity of variant-share-url still returns a leading-"?"-free query fragment, which
   variant-share-url-no-base pins.

Also, incidentally: the fix REMOVES a spurious history entry. Mounting from
?embed=1&variant=x now composes a URL equal to the current location, so push!'s
idempotence check no-ops where it previously pushed a shortened URL.

CONTROL. Both arms were run against the UNFIXED source first, so the red is measured
rather than assumed. JVM (clojure -M:test from tools/story, the jvm-tools-story lane):
exit 1, three failures naming the discard directly. CLJS (the consolidated :node-test
build, which carries tools/story/test on its source paths): exit 1, with embed reading
nil back through the real URLSearchParams — the API params->getter and
embed-flag-from-current-url use, whose first-value .get semantics a string assertion
cannot model. After the fix both are exit 0, with #8877's own share suites green in
the same runs, which is what shows one writer was not bent to match the other.

SABOTAGE. One line of the shared merge was then planted on the green tree ((when qidx
becomes (when false, removing preservation): NINE failures across BOTH writers' suites
at once — url_state_test.cljc and story_share_test.clj — from a single-line change to
one function. That is the direct evidence for the agreement claim. The agreement test
itself did not fail, correctly: both writers degraded identically, because there is
only one boundary left to degrade. Plant restored and the restore verified by git blob
hash against the committed object.

FINAL GATES, measured after a rebase onto the then-current trunk (four files under
implementation/core/ had landed in the interval and that tree is on the :node-test
build's source paths, so the pre-rebase CLJS green described a tree that no longer
existed): jvm-tools-story full suite exit 0, 1881 tests / 6890 assertions; :node-test
compile exit 0 with 0 warnings; :node-test full suite exit 0, 11148 tests / 54845
assertions; clj-kondo 0 errors on the four changed files. The rebase was clean and the
diffstat unchanged — no landed commit touches these four files, so nothing of anyone
else's is reverted.

NO SPEC CHANGE, and none was needed: the share invariant is already stated normatively
and the code was what disagreed with it. spec/*.md is untouched, so the hot-zone fence
was not approached.

One residue for a reader: current-location-shape is private and reads the live
window.location, so its :search addition is covered by inspection rather than by
assertion. The CLJS test drives url-from-state from a real js/URL's pathname/search/
hash — the same accessors with the same ?/# conventions — which exercises the exact
triple it produces.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8884 (worker/urlstate-gee8n). url-state/url-from-state now composes against a {:pathname :search :hash} location shape and merges through the newly-public share/apply-story-params — the same function share/variant-share-url uses — so the two writers of the address-bar URL share one ownership boundary rather than two. Story owns exactly share/story-query-keys (rf2-b7je1's nine keys, PR #8877); every unrelated param, embed=1 (rf2-pucku) included, now survives a state-driven push verbatim and in order. Also removed url_state's second canonicalising composer query-string-from-state, and stopped apply-story-params emitting a bare '?' for an empty query. Control red on both arms pre-fix; a one-line plant in the shared merge reds both writers' suites, which is the agreement evidence. No spec change needed. Full verdict in the notes above.

title: spec: register the durable :rf.runtime/machines :spawn-order slot in the reserved-key tables
description:
rf2-1vlyg (PR #8870) added a durable runtime-db sibling `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawn-order]` — a vector of actor-id keywords, oldest to newest, carrying the frame-global creation sequence that frame destroy reverses. It is written by `install-spawn!` (same swap as the snapshot install) and by `teardown/teardown-actor` (same swap as the snapshot dissoc), and is pruned when it empties.

The worker's fence permitted only spec/005-StateMachines.md, and 005 needed no change: it states the reverse-creation REQUIREMENT, which was already correct and is now met on the restore path for the first time. The false claims were in implementation docstrings and were repaired in that PR.

What is still owed is the reserved-slot BOOKKEEPING, which lives in hot-zone files that dispatch could not touch:

- spec/Conventions.md — the ':rf.runtime/machines' child list (the ':snapshots, :system-ids, :spawned, :spawn-counter' enumeration) and a new row in the Reserved runtime-db keys table.
- spec/Spec-Schemas.md — the 'Machines' schema (add ':spawn-order {:optional true} [:vector :keyword]') and the prose bullet enumerating the machine sub-slots.
- spec/002-Frames.md — the durable-runtime-db one-line enumeration.
- spec/Runtime-Subsystems.md — the Teardown row's slot list.

NOT blocking correctness: 'Machines' is an open [:map ...] with no {:closed true}, so the new key validates as-is today. The authoritative in-tree commentary already landed in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/paths.cljc's ns docstring, which is the artefact's own source of truth for these slot path vectors.

These are hot-zone one-toucher files, so sequence this behind any other spec worker rather than running it in parallel.
notes:
VERDICT 2026-09-01 — DONE. PR #8881 (branch worker/spawnorder-pg5w6, head 4ff4168413).

PREMISE CHECK: the item HOLDS in full and every file/table it names still exists at tip. All four listed surfaces were stale and all four were repaired; no fifth surface was owed. 005 §Where snapshots live was checked and enumerates only :snapshots, so it owed nothing — the item's judgement that 005 needs no change is confirmed a second time, on a different ground than the one rf2-1vlyg gave.

SOURCE VERIFICATION (read out of shipped code, not from the item's prose):
- Path spelling `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawn-order]` — paths.cljc/spawn-order-path.
- Value shape: vector of actor-id KEYWORDS, oldest→newest — spawn_order.cljc/durable-order + record-in-runtime-db. `[:vector :keyword]` is the right malli spelling.
- Write site 1 (append): spawn.cljc `install-spawn!`'s `install-fn`, inside the same `cond->` as the snapshot `assoc-in` and gated on the SAME `spec` binding, so the order tracks exactly the actors that have snapshots.
- Write site 2 (remove): teardown.cljc `teardown-actor`'s `new-db` `cond->`, inside the same swap that dissocs the snapshot.
- Pruning: `forget-in-runtime-db` dissocs the slot once the remaining vector is empty — so the slot is genuinely OPTIONAL at BOTH ends (absent before the first spawn, absent again after the last teardown). `{:optional true}` is correct, not merely convenient.
- Read: frame_destroy.cljc:219 `(spawn-order/durable-order runtime-db)`, walked reversed.
- ONE PROPERTY THE ITEM DID NOT NAME and the tables now record: the append is IDEMPOTENT BY VALUE — an id already in the vector keeps its ORIGINAL position rather than being re-appended, so a re-install cannot double-enter an actor and make frame destroy exit it twice.

DELTA vs the item's file list — the item was accurate; two clarifications:
- Conventions.md: the "child list" and the "Reserved runtime-db keys table" are the SAME table (the child list IS its :rf.runtime/machines row, line 595). The NEW ROW went into the sibling "Runtime-db sub-container catalogue" table, which is where the per-slot rows live. Both edited.
- Runtime-Subsystems.md: the item named the clause-5 Teardown row's slot list. The clause-1 Subtree row ALSO carries a slot list ("the closed slot set :snapshots / :system-ids / :spawned / :spawn-counter") and was equally stale; both were corrected. Clause 5 additionally now says WHERE the reverse-creation walk takes its order from, which is the fact rf2-1vlyg established.

Per-file line deltas: Conventions.md +2/-1, Spec-Schemas.md +11/-7, 002-Frames.md +1/-0, Runtime-Subsystems.md +2/-2. Total 16 insertions / 10 deletions across exactly the four named files. Nothing restructured: rows added, enumerations corrected, no table reshaped.

GATE — WHICH ONE COVERS spec/, SETTLED EMPIRICALLY. A broken anchor was planted at a line this PR actually edits (002-Frames.md:400, the new bullet's Cross-Spec-Interactions link), fixed-string match count 1 confirmed BEFORE the run so the plant could not silently no-op. check_doc_slugs.py went RED, captured exit 1, naming file, line and the planted anchor. check_readme_links.py --ci stayed GREEN on the identical fault, captured exit 0, empty log. So spec/ is check_doc_slugs.py's surface alone. Clean runs on the FINAL rebased base: both 0. Restore verified by GIT BLOB HASH against the committed object (core.autocrlf is on here, so a byte digest of the working file would be the wrong instrument) — pre-plant and post-restore blobs identical.

FENCE BLINDNESS DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSUMED — and it matters here because the whole schema edit lives inside a fence. The SAME broken anchor written INSIDE the Machines fence, on the exact line of the schema edit, left BOTH gates green (0 and 0) while the file's blob hash changed, proving the plant applied. So the schema edit is invisible to every gate this repo has.

HAND CHECKS in place of that missing coverage:
- The fenced EDN was parsed with the REAL Clojure reader, not eyeballed: the (def Machines ...) form read-string'd clean (captured exit 0), and the schema's key vector reads exactly [:snapshots :system-ids :spawned :spawn-counter :spawn-order], with the new entry parsing as [:spawn-order {:optional true} [:vector :keyword]]. Balance confirmed independently (depth returns to zero on the closing line).
- Every table row touched was column-counted against its own separator: Conventions.md's two tables (4 cols; edited row 595 = 4, new row 615 = 4, all five Machines rows consistent) and Runtime-Subsystems.md's machines grading table (2 cols; edited rows 117 and 121 both = 2). Zero mismatches. The counter was itself exercised against a deliberately broken copy of the new row, where it reported cols=3 against sep=4 and exited 1 — so its zero is a check that passed, not a pattern that missed.

REBASE: rebased onto a trunk that had moved twice during the work; gates re-run on the final base rather than trusting the pre-rebase green. Trunk had not touched any of the four files, and the diff against the new merge base is byte-identical to the diff against the old one — purely additive, nothing reverted.

OUT OF SCOPE, REPORTED NOT FIXED: Runtime-Subsystems.md's clause-5 teardown row spells the system-id reverse index `:rf/system-ids`; the actual slot is `:system-ids` (paths/system-id-path). It sits inside the very parenthetical this PR extends, but it is a pre-existing inaccuracy the item does not name, so it was left for a separate item. The same wrong spelling appears in two conformance-fixture comments: spec/conformance/fixtures/destroy-machine-clears-system-id-index.edn and spec/conformance/fixtures/spawn-without-system-id-leaves-index-empty.edn. Worth one small bead covering all three.

NOT A CORRECTNESS CHANGE: Machines is an open [:map ...] with no {:closed true}, so :spawn-order validated before this PR and validates after it. The deliverable is the record being truthful, and that was the bar applied.

Registers the durable [:rf.runtime/machines :spawn-order] slot that rf2-1vlyg (PR #8870) shipped, in all four reserved-key surfaces the item names: Conventions.md (the :rf.runtime/machines child list in the Reserved runtime-db keys table, plus a new per-slot row in the Runtime-db sub-container catalogue), Spec-Schemas.md (the Machines schema gains [:spawn-order {:optional true} [:vector :keyword]]; comment and prose bullet now say five sub-slots), 002-Frames.md (the durable runtime-db enumeration), and Runtime-Subsystems.md (clause-1 slot set AND clause-5 teardown projection, the latter now naming where the reverse-creation walk takes its order from). (append in the snapshot-install swap), teardown.cljc teardown-actor (remove in the snapshot-dissoc swap), pruned when empty, read reversed by frame_destroy.cljc. The schema edit lives in a fence and is invisible to both gates (demonstrated with an in-fence plant that left both green while the blob hash changed), so it was hand-verified with the Clojure reader; all touched table rows column-counted. title: hicasso: frameless error boundary silently drops vector :on-error
description:
## Scope

implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs, plus the focused browser witness in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs. Touch public complaint/catalogue prose only if the repair changes the stable complaint contract.

## Correctness finding

A frameless h/error-boundary accepts a vector-valued :on-error, but when a descendant fails it silently discards that intent. The boundary's render-time shape check admits every vector; later, report! wraps the vector arm in when-some on frame-of, so a missing frame simply returns nil. The fallback still catches and replaces the failed subtree, making the loss look like successful error handling while the declared reporting event never runs.

This contradicts the public promise that vector :on-error is dispatched through the boundary's frame and the package's own frameless rule: the boundary itself may be frameless only until an intent is present. A vector :on-error is an intent, not an optional best-effort callback.

## Evidence

- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:219-229 (check-props!) accepts :on-error whenever it is nil, a vector, or a function; it does not relate the vector arm to frame availability.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:232-235 (frame-of) can answer nil for the deliberately supported no-provider case.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:237-257 (report!) implements the vector arm as "(when-some [frame-kw (frame-of this)] ...)"; the nil case has no refusal or report and falls through to the function's final nil.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:309-328 re-establishes the frame only while lowering fallback/children. That makes an inline child intent loud, but the direct :on-error vector never passes through intent lowering and therefore misses that guard.
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs:404-449 proves that a frameless boundary with no intent is legal and an inline child intent refuses loudly. Its frameless harness uses a function-valued :on-error; there is no row for the subject boundary's own vector-valued :on-error.
- docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md:183 and docs/core/hicasso/cookbook.md:408-411 state that a vector :on-error is dispatched with the error appended through the frame the boundary is mounted under.
- implementation/hicasso/spec/invariants.md I10/I11 require intent semantics and loud stable failure rather than an accepted inert declaration.
- Review commands included targeted rg reads of the symbols/tests/docs and an all-status bead-corpus scan over on-error, componentDidCatch, report!, frameless, and no frame.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In the browser harness, mount an error boundary under adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel with :fallback markup, vector :on-error [:app/record-render-failure], and a child that throws during render.
2. Let React commit the boundary's error state.
3. Observe that the fallback is rendered, no :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary refusal is raised, and the declared event has no frame through which it can be dispatched. The only vector arm in report! returns nil when frame-of returns nil.

A source-level minimal reproduction is the direct control flow: check-props! accepts the vector; frame-of answers nil; report!'s when-some body is skipped.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A raw React root (or any tree deliberately carrying the no-provider context) renders:

    [h/error-boundary
     {:fallback [:p "That region failed"]
      :on-error [:app/record-render-failure]}
     [foreign-crasher]]

The declaration renders as valid. When foreign-crasher throws, React shows the fallback, but :app/record-render-failure is never dispatched and no Hicasso complaint is raised. The application loses its error record precisely when the error path is exercised.

Invariant: every accepted intent-bearing position either captures a live frame and routes exactly once or refuses loudly before it can become inert. Absence of a frame must never turn an accepted intent into a silent no-op.

## Recommended minimal fix

In the error boundary's own render, after resolving frame-kw and before rendering either branch, refuse a vector-valued :on-error when frame-kw is nil. Reuse :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary if its current contract fits, and carry at least the offending :intent plus :position :on-error.

Keep the check in render, not componentDidCatch: waiting until report! would replace the application's original failure only on the exceptional path and escape to the next boundary. Do not require a frame for the boundary generally. Nil and function-valued :on-error remain legal frameless because neither needs re-frame dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a focused browser row in boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs that mounts a healthy subject boundary under adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel with vector :on-error and proves first-render refusal with stable id :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary, the exact intent, and :position :on-error. A healthy child keeps the proof independent of descendant failure timing.
- Keep/load explicit positive controls:
  - a frameless boundary with no :on-error and no nested intent still renders;
  - a frameless boundary with function :on-error catches one deliberate descendant failure, invokes the function once, and renders its fallback;
  - the same vector :on-error under a live frame dispatches once with the caught error appended.
- Non-vacuity: removing the new frame/vector guard (restoring today's when-some-only behavior) makes the focused refusal row fail. Widening the guard to reject nil or a function makes the two frameless controls fail.
- Run the browser lane that executes the DOM row (npm run test:browser) and the focused Hicasso node/invariant gates used by this package. If an error id or catalogue wording changes, run the complaint-catalogue gate and update its governed rows; prefer reusing the existing intent-outside-boundary contract.
- Existing reset-key, fallback-intent, StrictMode once-per-failure, and live-frame isolation witnesses remain green.

## Non-goals

- Do not require every error boundary to live under a frame.
- Do not change function-valued :on-error, fallback lowering, reset/retry behavior, or what React error boundaries catch.
- Do not add a fallback dispatch channel, queue intents until a frame appears, or refactor generic intent lowering.
- Do not broaden this into overlay/presence frameless behavior.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all bead statuses and descriptions for on-error, componentDidCatch, report!, frameless, no frame, and boundary/frame combinations.

- rf2-czlb (closed) fixed unknown boundary props and malformed :on-error; its scope explicitly preserved the legal vector/function arms. It does not own the accepted vector's nil-frame behavior.
- rf2-4e5b (closed) addressed the analogous but separate frameless overlay :on-dismiss state.
- No open or in-progress bead owns vector :on-error being silently dropped without a frame.
notes:
## Verdict — 2026-09-01 (PR #8871)

FINDING CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, repaired, witnessed. Every file:line on this
bead re-derived at tip and confirmed EXACT: check-props!'s :on-error arm at
boundary.cljs:219-229, frame-of 232-235, report! 237-257, the render's frame
re-establishment 309-328, api-reference.md:183, cookbook.md:408-411. One
drift only, and it is trivial: the witness citation 404-449 names the
section comment three lines above frameless-root!, whose actual span is
407-449.

The 309-328 claim also holds as stated, and it is the shape of the fix: the
boundary re-establishes the frame around the codec walk of :fallback and
:children, so an intent at either is caught and named, while :on-error is
read straight off the props map by report! and passes through no lowering at
all. That was the one intent position a frameless boundary accepted and then
dropped.

### Site chosen: check-props!, in render

Not report!. A refusal from componentDidCatch would replace the
application's real error with a complaint about the declaration and escape
to the next boundary up — the namespace docstring already argues exactly
this for the existing shape check, and React runs render before it can run
componentDidCatch. A missing frame sharpens the argument: it is the case
where refusing late is not merely worse but indistinguishable from working,
because the fallback renders either way.

Within render the guard went into check-props! rather than inline, because
all three refusals are one class — a declaration the boundary wears while
nothing consults it — and belong at one site. check-props! now takes the
caller's frame-kw; render binds frame-kw first.

report!'s when-some on frame-of was REMOVED. It is provably dead once the
same render refuses the frameless case, and left in place it would still be
the silent drop, one guard later.

### Complaint contract UNCHANGED

Reuses :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary with :position :on-error
and the offending :intent. impl.overlay/dismissal-handler already refuses an
unroutable :on-dismiss under that id (the rf2-4e5b analogue), and
implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md's row — "lowered or fired an
intent with no frame-locked dispatch bound" — covers this site as written.
So complaints.md is untouched, and so is invariants.md: the repair makes the
code conform to I10/I11 rather than changing what they promise. That also
avoided the three-Chromium-lane toll a spec/ prose edit carries (rf2-7rzg).

### Control

Landed RED FIRST. Commit 1 is the witness alone against unrepaired source:
exit 1, 3 failures of 54 assertions, all three in
a-frameless-boundarys-own-on-error-vector-is-refused-at-first-render, with
"Escaped: nil" — nothing raised at all, the silent acceptance stated as a
measurement. After the repair: exit 0, same 11 tests and the SAME 54
assertions, so nothing skipped or crashed out of the lane. Re-run as an
explicit sabotage afterwards (checkout of the pre-repair blob) reproduced
exit 1 with the identical three failures; shadow-cljs reported "4 compiled",
which is the positive evidence the runtime observed the plant rather than
serving a stale compile. Restore verified by git blob hash against the
committed object.

Positive controls all green and all pre-existing except one: frameless with
no :on-error still renders (row 6); the same vector under a live frame still
dispatches (row 9's near miss); with the error appended, exactly once (row
10, StrictMode). Added: a frameless boundary with a FUNCTION :on-error
catching a real descendant failure and firing once — the near miss on the
exact axis this guard could have over-reached, and it passed against
UNREPAIRED source too, so it is a genuine control rather than a co-moving
assertion.

### Gates

Local, captured exit codes: full :browser-test lane 753 tests / 4115
assertions, exit 0; :node-test 11128 tests / 54669 assertions, exit 0;
check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, and exercised against a planted broken link which
it caught (exit 1, naming file and line), so its green is a check that ran.
CI on PR #8871: 84 checks, 47 pass / 37 skipping / 0 failures — including
the three-engine cljs-hicasso-controlled gate and MkDocs build, neither of
which was runnable locally.

### One scope addition, stated

docs/core/hicasso/17-errors.md gained ONE troubleshooting row for the new
refusal, beside the fallback-intent row that raises the same id. The
complaint contract did not change, so this is teaching prose rather than
catalogue prose; without it the chapter that teaches h/error-boundary would
be silent about a user-visible refusal at its own component. It mirrors the

title: surface-review(skill-pair): keep Story work on the attached browser runtime
description:
## Scope

Make `skills/re-frame2-pair/` one honest live-SPA skill: every runtime operation it teaches or pre-authorises must target the browser heap reached by Pair's shadow-cljs nREPL connection. Remove the eight `mcp__re-frame2-story-mcp__*` tools and the headless-JVM procedures from Pair's published surface. Keep Story variants powerful inside a live pair session through the already-shipped browser path: `eval-cljs` over `re-frame.story/*`, followed by ordinary Pair frame reads, dispatches, traces, and diffs.

Cover the smallest coherent carrier set: Pair's frontmatter/router, the overlapping Story/variant recipes, the skill meta-docs, and the drift/prompt checks that currently enforce the hybrid split. Do not change Pair-MCP, Story-MCP, re-frame2 Story, or `re-frame2-pair.runtime` behavior.

## Findings

1. Pair's contract is one attached browser runtime. Its description, setup, and first-contact loop install the Pair MCP server plus `re-frame2-pair.runtime`, then run `discover-app` -> `orient` -> a targeted read against the live shadow-cljs build. The package/plugin metadata and human install docs do not install or configure Story-MCP. Nevertheless `SKILL.md` allow-lists eight tools from the separate `re-frame2-story-mcp` server in addition to all 33 Pair tools and five editor tools: 46 entries total.

2. The two servers cannot share runtime identity. `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md` and `tools/story-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md` define Story-MCP as a headless same-JVM adapter over a process-local Story registry, with no nREPL, socket, or JVM-to-browser bridge. They define Pair's `eval-cljs` channel as the one live browser door. A keyword such as `:story.login/success` existing in both processes does not make the two frames the same object.

3. Pair's own Story leaf states the correct boundary, then contradicts it. `references/stories.md:15` says Story-MCP cannot see the browser tab's registry and instructs live work through Pair `eval-cljs`. Lines 81-116 still advertise the eight headless tools, and lines 116-171 claim every Story-MCP tool targeting a variant operates on the same frame Pair reads and teach `Pair subscribe -> Story-MCP run-variant -> Pair snapshot/dispatch`. That composition runs the variant in the JVM while Pair observes the browser, so a headless pass can leave the SPA untouched and Pair can legitimately report no such frame. `references/recipes.md:331-414` repeats the split by starting from a running Story-enabled browser but invoking headless `run-variant` and `read-failures` in the procedure.

4. No live capability requires the second server. The browser recipe already enumerates with `re-frame.story/ids` / `variants-of`, awaits `re-frame.story/run-variant` through Pair `eval-cljs`, projects the verdict before egress, and then addresses the variant through the normal Pair frame tools. The 4,004-line runtime helper has no Story runtime dependency; its only Story-specific behavior is a comment/example on generic `frame-diff`. Removing headless tool permissions therefore subtracts a wrong host choice without weakening live inspection, mutation, or variant-as-frame.

5. The hybrid also defeats progressive disclosure. `stories.md` is 187 lines / 18,177 bytes, `variant-as-frame.md` is 104 lines / 12,819 bytes, and three Story sections occupy roughly the final quarter of the 420-line recipe catalogue. A Story prompt is routed through SKILL plus both leaves and may then cross to the authoring skill, despite the router's at-most-two-references rule. One browser-native variant leaf can carry enumerate -> run -> operate/diff without a second host catalogue.

6. Existing checks preserve prose, not host correctness. `tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` is 679 lines but has no canonical Story prompt and only checks that named words remain in sections. `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py:172-272` explicitly enforces the old HYBRID ownership and makes missing Story-MCP tools in Pair a failure. The live Pair fixture proves connect, dispatch, trace, and hot reload but never composes the two Story hosts. The impossible workflow is therefore green by construction.

7. History shows additive layering. The five Story-MCP run/assert tools entered Pair on 2026-05-13; three read-only tools followed. Commit `1967eff870` (2026-07-11, rf2-s99lw4) added the correct live-browser `eval-cljs` recipe after the one-live-door ruling, but retained the older headless integration and wrapped it in warnings instead of deleting it. This is pre-alpha surface residue, not compatibility worth preserving.

8. The rest of the live loop is coherent and should remain: Pair's preload sentinel/freshness ladder gives an honest attach, `orient` supplies bounded first contact, structured tools cover common gestures, and `eval-cljs` carries the long tail. A second process-local Story host is the outlier; no attach redesign or new tool is needed to remove it.

## Recommended Action

Take a clean single-host cut:

- Remove every `mcp__re-frame2-story-mcp__*` entry from Pair's `allowed-tools`. A published Pair invocation should require only its own MCP server plus editor tools.
- Retain one concise browser-Story procedure: enumerate the live registry with Pair `eval-cljs`; await/project `re-frame.story/run-variant`; then use `set-operating-frame`, `read-sub` / `snapshot` / `dispatch`, epoch reads, and `frame-diff` against that same browser runtime.
- Collapse `references/stories.md` and `references/variant-as-frame.md` to one live-browser leaf (keep either filename), and prune the headless tool catalogue, false same-frame compositions, self-healing cross-server loop, and duplicate Story recipes. Link outward for explicitly headless Story-MCP work; do not teach it as part of Pair.
- Remove the Story-MCP <-> Pair HYBRID mapping from `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py` and replace it with the simpler invariant that Pair's MCP permissions use only the `re-frame2-pair` prefix. Reconcile `spec/design.md`, `spec/authoring-prompt.md`, `spec/inputs.md`, and current docs with that boundary.
- Add one focused row to the existing prompt-regression table for “run this variant in the app I have open”: it must route through Pair `eval-cljs` with `await`, then a Pair frame read, and must not mention the Story-MCP prefix. Extend the existing structural harness only; do not build a general conversation-eval platform for this cut.

Do not transfer compatibility aliases into Pair or add dedicated Pair Story tools. `eval-cljs` is already the explicit, powerful long-tail surface and the invoker selected a live Pair session.

## Evidence

- Pair's advertised/allowed surface: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:1-68`; current count is 33 Pair MCP names + 8 Story-MCP names + 5 editor names.
- Pair-only setup/distribution: `skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/LOCAL_DEV.md:11-43,121-128`, `README.md:152-209`, `package.json`, and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`; none configures Story-MCP.
- Normative host split: `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:41-66`; `tools/story-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md:72-82`; `tools/story-mcp/README.md:14-19`.
- Internal contradiction: `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md:15,75-81,116-171`; `references/recipes.md:327-414`; `SKILL.md:210`.
- Existing complete browser route: `references/stories.md:13-77`; generic variant addressing/diff: `references/variant-as-frame.md` and `preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:1399-1416`.
- Runtime independence: no production `re-frame.story` or Story-MCP reference exists in `runtime.cljs` or `pure.cljc`; the helper remains a generic frame/epoch/DOM runtime.
- Enforcement gap: `tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj:76-168,167-220`; `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py:172-272`; `docs/TESTING.md:126-172` explicitly calls Claude-in-loop behavior future work.
- History: Story-MCP Pair permissions originate in `5753b4211e` / `8a10d146bf`; the live-browser route lands later in `1967eff870`. The later commit added “one live door” but left the earlier cross-host procedures intact.
- Duplicate search: all-status title, description, and notes searches for Story-MCP Pair, browser registry, one live door, HYBRID split, live-session tools, cross-host, split-brain, and same-frame found no owner for this subtraction.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md` contains zero `mcp__re-frame2-story-mcp__*` permissions and no instruction to start or call a second MCP server during a live Pair workflow. Pair's editor permissions and surviving Pair-MCP permissions remain intact, subject to the separate `rf2-ahjbc` catalogue reduction.
2. Current Pair docs expose exactly one Story host: the attached browser. A copyable enumerate -> await run -> pin/read/dispatch/trace procedure operates entirely through `mcp__re-frame2-pair__*` calls and projects the run verdict before raw eval egress.
3. No Pair doc claims that a Story-MCP variant frame and a browser Pair frame are the same frame, or composes state/trace reads across the two processes. Explicitly headless/JVM Story work routes out to Story-MCP's own docs or the appropriate authoring context.
4. Pair has one Story/variant reference leaf after the router, not the current overlapping `stories.md` + `variant-as-frame.md` pair. The surviving leaf retains variant-id-as-frame semantics, mount/reset/destroy gotchas, browser enumeration/run, and cross-frame diff; headless catalogues and duplicate self-healing prose are removed. Net Pair prose decreases materially.
5. `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py` no longer encodes Story-MCP <-> Pair HYBRID ownership. Its self-test and ordinary run pass while a controlled reintroduction of one `mcp__re-frame2-story-mcp__*` Pair permission makes the focused boundary check red.
6. The existing prompt regression has a Story-in-the-open-app row that requires Pair `eval-cljs`, `await`, and a same-runtime frame read and forbids the Story-MCP prefix. Existing Pair prompt/runtime structural tests remain green; no new general eval runner is introduced.
7. Skill meta-docs, README/status/capability material, routing tables, and current tool-count prose agree with the single-host boundary. Historical design records may describe the former hybrid only when clearly labelled historical, not as current instruction.
8. No Pair-MCP tool, Story-MCP tool, Story API, runtime helper function, permission gate, compatibility alias, bridge, background service, or dedicated browser-Story tool is added or changed for this outcome.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning Pair's attach/preload mechanism, `discover-app`, `orient`, the remaining Pair-MCP catalogue, or the runtime helper.
- Removing Story variants, variant-as-frame, browser `re-frame.story/*` access, frame diffs, or Pair's generic `eval-cljs` workhorse.
- Changing Story-MCP's 20-tool headless catalogue, teaching it to bridge into a browser, or deciding its complete ownership across every other skill.
- Adding a `list-stories` / `run-variant` Pair tool, generic command abstraction, compatibility shim, deprecation window, or second permission layer.
- Building a new behavioural-eval platform or broad-rewriting unrelated Pair recipes.

## Related beads

- `rf2-ahjbc` (open) retires Pair-MCP progress streams in favor of turn-shaped results. It shares `SKILL.md`, recipes/references, tests, and drift carriers; land it first or rebase this subtraction onto its reduced catalogue.
- `rf2-cfq8a` (open) makes a consumer project's headless JVM stories reachable on Story-MCP first launch and explicitly preserves Pair as the one live-browser door. Complementary, not a dependency.
- `rf2-7htk7` (open) retires Xray's duplicate agent runtime so Pair is the single out-of-process live runtime. This applies the same one-runtime boundary at the skill/tool-selection layer.
- `rf2-7dewo` (open) changes Story variant vocabulary and may sweep skills prose after its runtime slice; coordinate the surviving browser Story leaf, but neither outcome depends on the other.
- `rf2-wyza` (closed) replaced a duplicated 33-tool onboarding catalogue with routing rules after measuring the context tax. This task applies the same trust-the-agent/subtract-the-wrong-choice posture to a second-server catalogue.
- Historical lineage: `rf2-s99lw4` / commit `1967eff870` established the browser `eval-cljs` path; the one-live-door ruling is recorded in Story spec as `rf2-3fc89f.22`.

title: surface-review(flows): make dynamic flow toggles settle automatically
description:
## Scope

Change the runtime semantics of the existing `:rf.fx/reg-flow` and `:rf.fx/clear-flow` effects so their app-db consequences settle automatically on the dispatching frame. Keep the existing effect ids and 3-slot registration payload. This includes the flows runtime, the core fx/router integration it uses, focused tests/conformance, Spec 013, the API/core guides, and the shipped cart example.

## Verified Findings

- The reserved flow effects run after the event's flow transform. A flow registered by an event therefore has no output until another event drains; a flow cleared by an event leaves its old output in app-db until another event drains.
- The clear case is observably incoherent at the dispatch boundary: the registry row is already gone while the derived value it owned is still present.
- The documented solution makes every caller invent and dispatch a no-op event. The shipped cart defines `:cart/touch` solely for this purpose and emits it after both apply and remove. This is ceremony in the event catalogue, trace stream, tests, docs, and generated code, not application behavior.
- The current tracker contains no open, in-progress, deferred, or closed issue that owns automatic settling for flow lifecycle effects. Spec 013 itself labels synchronous re-walk as an untracked note.

## Recommended Action

After a successful `:rf.fx/reg-flow` or `:rf.fx/clear-flow`, have the runtime request one private, same-frame settling drain for the parent event. Reuse the existing run-to-completion queue and ordinary flow pass: this is the framework performing the exact follow-up drain it currently tells every application to hand-write. Keep one app-db install per individual event; do not re-run flows inline in the original fx walk. The private transport must not become an application-facing event or option.

Make this the only default. Delete the lag workaround contract instead of adding a synchronous variant, a `:settle?` flag, or compatibility behavior.

## Concrete Evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:858` through `:869` calls the lag the least-obvious behavior and instructs callers to dispatch a follow-up no-op event.
- `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj:1148` through `:1184` proves clear removes the registry entry while leaving `[:wizard :result]` stale until `:touch`; `:1186` through `:1220` locks the registration lag and workaround.
- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:149` through `:191` spends a full handler plus two extra `:dispatch` pairs on `:cart/touch`, whose only purpose is to cause another flow walk.
- `docs/core/flows.md:299` through `:321`, `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md:153`, `spec/013-Flows.md` under "Sequencing"/"Open questions", and `spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-toggle-via-fx.edn` all publish or pin the same lag.
- Git history shows the behavior was documented rather than removed: `256e6693aa` (rf2-1smwp) added the mid-event signpost, and `16bbd2f349` (rf2-2qd9wp) extended the lag to in-drain clear semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dispatching one event whose only lifecycle action is `:rf.fx/reg-flow` leaves the flow registered and its initial output materialized once the synchronous/run-to-completion dispatch settles, without an app-authored follow-up event.
- Dispatching one event with `:rf.fx/clear-flow` leaves the flow absent, its output path vacated, and existing dependent flows recomputed against that absence by the same settle boundary. The cart's apply/remove actions update `:cart/discount-rate` and `:cart/total` after one user dispatch.
- Automatic settling is frame-correct, uses the normal topo/dirty-check pass, and preserves the one-app-db-install-per-event invariant and existing derive-failure reporting.
- The public effect ids and payloads do not change, and no public settle event, flag, alternate effect, or new lifecycle API is added.
- Focused CLJ and CLJS tests fail under the old lag behavior and pass under the new default. The conformance fixture is flipped from "next app event" to automatic settle.
- The cart deletes `:cart/touch` and both manual settle dispatches. Spec 013, API/core docs, comments, and tests no longer teach or assert a user-authored no-op workaround.

## Non-goals

- Do not perform a second app-db install inside the original event.
- Do not add fixed-point iteration, conditional/liveness policies, a general scheduler abstraction, or a public "run flows now" command.
- Do not redesign the 3-slot `reg-flow` grammar, static boot registration, the optional-artifact boundary, tooling projections, classification, or exact-incarnation machinery in this task.
- Do not preserve the lag behind a compatibility switch; this is pre-alpha.

## Related beads

- No duplicate owner exists in the current 1,060-issue tracker corpus (all statuses searched across title, description, notes, and close reason for the effect ids, lag, no-op follow-up, dynamic toggle, and settle terms).
- Historical rf2-1smwp documented the registration lag; historical rf2-2qd9wp made in-drain clear preserve the same next-drain behavior. They explain the current contract but do not own removing the application workaround.
- Spec 013 "Synchronous re-walk after `:rf.fx/reg-flow`" is explicitly marked post-v1 and untracked. This task takes the smaller route: automate the already-supported follow-up drain rather than re-walk inline.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-08-30 21:44:09 AUSEST (read-only agent at e159c96fbf, premises all HOLD). See the mayor's dispatch note when it comes; queued behind a free slot.
VERDICT 2026-09-01 AUSEST (worker, PR #8893). NOTE-START-MARKER-KH73V.

PREMISES ALL HOLD, re-verified at source. Every cited line number in the item
was still exact after today's `implementation/flows` merge — zero drift:
`implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:858-869` is the ONE-EVENT LAG comment
verbatim; `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj:1148-1184` is
`fx-reg-flow-and-clear-flow-round-trip` (its lag pin is the `(= 9 ...)` at
:1179) and `:1186-1220` is
`fx-reg-flow-mid-event-lag-and-followup-dispatch-workaround` (its pin is the
`(nil? ...)` at :1213); `examples/core/flows/core.cljs` carried `:cart/touch`
at :192-195 with dispatches at :175 and :184.

WHAT THE POST-TRANSFORM ORDERING WAS PROTECTING. Exactly one `app-db` install
per event (Spec 013 Drain integration property 4), and with it the
pending-effect-transform model and the atomic-commit contract. The old fx.cljc
comment, the Spec 013 Sequencing section and the Open-questions entry all say
the same thing and all make the same assumption: that closing the lag requires
a SECOND INSTALL inside the registering event. A second EVENT closes it
instead. The `:fx` walk now enqueues one framework-private `[:rf/settle-flows]`
on the dispatching frame, which drains in the same run-to-completion pass. Each
event still installs once; nothing re-runs the transform after `:fx`.

The separation buys a second property the item did not ask for and that an
inline re-walk would have LOST: the failure boundary. A newly registered flow
whose `:derive` throws now aborts the SETTLE, not the registering event, whose
own `:db` write has already committed. An inline re-walk would have made a bad
`:derive` retroactively abort the registration.

SETTLE-TIME DERIVE FAILURES USE THE EXISTING PATH, no new one. A settle is an
ordinary event, so a throw goes through `flows-after-interceptor`'s existing
catch, is stashed under `:rf/flow-error`, and surfaces via
`emit-flow-eval-exception!` as `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` carrying the
structural `:phase` discriminator (`:derive` vs `:output-write`) that
`flows.cljc/evaluate-flow!` assigns by which `try` caught it. No code was added
on that path.

DESIGN CHOICE WORTH RECORDING: `:rf/settle-flows` is NEVER REGISTERED. Not into
the registrar, not into the EP-0023 image standard registry. It resolves through
the router unresolved-handler seam (new `router/framework-private-handler-metas`,
consulted ahead of the machines actor resolver in `resolve-unhandled`). The
alternative was the `:rf/set-db` template, a private `registrar/register!`, and
it was rejected for the reason the item itself gives: registering it would put a
row into every app event catalogue, tooling projection and generated code, which
merely MOVES the ceremony from the app into the framework instead of deleting
it. The seam also removes the need for an image-standard registration, since a
generation-routed `registrar/lookup` returns nil for an unregistered id and
falls through to it. It is still listed in `events/reserved-event-ids`, for a
different reason than `:rf/set-db` is: the registrar is consulted BEFORE the
seam, so an app `(reg-event :rf/settle-flows ...)` would silently shadow the
settle and strand every lifecycle effect.

NOTE-MIDDLE-MARKER-KH73V.

FENCED CORE FILES: neither needed. The change is `fx.cljc`, `router.cljc` and
`events.cljc`. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc` and
`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc` (held by rf2-cq0yi) were not
touched — confirmed by name against the merge-base diff, not by memory.

Verified at the audited merge and fetched origin/main. The Dynamic-only ribbon was inspected by the implementation, but the Static composition contradicts the resulting statement.

Required correction: in the Static-mode paragraph, retain the frame picker alongside the mode selector and right icons; remove it from the dropped spine-only controls. Preserve the accurate raw-spine diagram, nav placement, retired focus-chip statement and the actual Static absence of navigation/filter chrome. This is a documentation correction to match the existing useful control, not a request to remove or redesign it. Verify against the Static ribbon composition; link-gate success cannot establish this behavioral claim.

No exact open finding records this defect. rf2-u95rq addresses the separate section-2 wireframe nav placement and retired focus-chip, not the false claim that Static loses its frame picker.

verified it at source at trunk `5a521c4a60` before filing.

**The site**, `tools/xray/spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md:500-501`:

> "When the target is unselected (`:rf.xray/target-frame` → `nil`, `:rf.xray/observed-frame` → `nil`), the
> panels read `nil`'s app-db (itself `nil`) and render their unselected-target state; the frame picker
> prompts a choice."

It derives `:rf.xray/observed-frame` → nil from the TARGET being unselected ALONE. That does not follow.

**The truth source**, `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_subs.cljs:91-94`: the sub is
registered over `[[:rf.xray/focus] [:rf.xray/target-frame]]` as `(or (:frame focus) target)`. So with focus
`{:frame :app/a}` and target `nil`, the observed frame is `:app/a` — NOT nil. It is nil only when the focus
has resolved no `:frame` AND the target is unselected, which is the cold start that the same file's comment
at `:86-90` identifies (EP-0002 / rf2-bd4div).

claim leads a reader into a WRONG ACTION, and 008 is the page where that bites hardest: it is the NORMATIVE
EMBEDDING CONTRACT, read by a host integrator deciding what Xray does under its app. A host that takes this
sentence at face value expects panels to show the unselected-target state whenever no target is picked, and
builds against that; what actually happens is that a resolved focus frame is observed and its app-db
rendered. Same judgement under which rf2-ezalc itself was filed.

**Follow rf2-ezalc's landed wording rather than inventing a third phrasing** (PR #10081, `014:298`): "…so it
is `nil` only when the focus has resolved no `:frame` AND the target is UNSELECTED (the cold start). A focus
that has resolved a frame is observed while the target is still UNSELECTED, so the observed coordinate is not
the selected scope." **Preserve the selected-scope vs observed-coordinate distinction — narrow the nil
condition, do not delete the distinction**, and leave the rest of the passage (`set-target-frame! nil` resets
to UNSELECTED, the `:rf/xray` own-frame singleton) untouched.

**A deliberate near-miss, so the fix does not overreach:** `tools/xray/spec/004-App-DB-Diff.md:680-687`
speaks of a nil observed frame in the FAIL-CLOSED REDACTION sense, which is correct and is NOT this defect.

`app_db_diff_cljs_test.cljs:523-526` — are correct already, being properly scoped to a cold start.

anchors only; it cannot see a false conclusion in a paragraph. `mkdocs build --strict` stages only `spec/`
and `migration/`, never `tools/`. The verification is resolving the claim against `app_db_diff_subs.cljs`.

nil in that case is wrong.

**Surface:** `008-Embedding-Contract.md` is held by no open PR. **Sequence after PR #10081 merges** so the

title: Xray Epoch: schema-violation source link always plain text for non-app-db violations — looked up under kind :schema, which is not a registrar kind
description:
## The defect

In the Epoch panel, the "schema check" source link on a schema-violation row **always renders as plain
text** for every violation whose `:where` is not `:app-db`: `:fx-args`, `:sub-return`, `:event` and
`:cofx`. The link is meant to jump to the schema's source.

## Measured at source (trunk `4b616e3dca`)

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`, in the violation row's `let` (about
  `:5688-5689`), resolves the non-`:app-db` coord with `(violation-kind-coord :schema failing-id)`.
- `violation-kind-coord` (about `:5563`) calls
  `(rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind kind :id id})` inside `(try … (catch :default _ nil))`.
- **`:schema` is not a registrar kind.** `implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:143` defines
  `kinds` as `#{:event :sub :fx :cofx :interceptor :view :frame :route :head :error-projector :flow
  :resource :mutation :resource-scope}`, and `valid-kind?` is `(contains? kinds k)`.
- So the lookup cannot find anything under kind `:schema`. The swallowing `catch` (or a nil lookup)
  degrades the link to plain text, silently, every time.
- **The code's own comment states the intent**, just above the call: "For other `:where` values, the
  schema rides on the registration's `:schema` metadata, reachable via `handler-meta`." The lookup
  should therefore use the KIND OF THE FAILING REGISTRATION: the event, sub, fx or cofx the violation
  names, derived from `:where` or from the violation record. It should not use `:schema`.

Found by rf2-y8doi.48's worker while truthing 021 (PR #10061). The chapter now documents the
plain-text behaviour, and this item fixes the code.

## Scope

The coord resolution in that one file, plus a RED test. **Derive the violation fixture from the
PRODUCER** (a real schema violation through the framework), not a hand-written row, since that is the
rf2-y8doi wave's recurring failure. Show the test RED on the current tree and GREEN after the fix.
Check at source which `:where` values map to which registrar kind; do not assume the four-way mapping
above is exhaustive. When the fix lands, 021's sentence about the plain-text behaviour becomes false,
so name it in the PR body for the mayor to route. Do not edit 021 in this change.

`.cljs` means the shadow-cljs lane: node (`*-cljs-test`) or browser (`*-dom-cljs-test`), whichever the
test's namespace suffix selects.

arrives here one level finer: the unit is not even the LINE.** Whoever takes this runs a census axis that
FLATTENS LINE BREAKS before matching, and reports the membership delta.

title: The panel-enum spec macro slurps with bare java.io while this repo already owns a recording-reader wrapper, so incremental builds grade a stale list
description:
`tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panel_enum_spec_refs.clj` slurps Xray spec markdown at
macro-expansion time with bare `clojure.java.io`, so shadow-cljs records no dependency on those files and an
incremental compile after a spec edit grades the STALE captured list. **This repo already owns the fix and
that macro does not use it.**

## Measured 2026-09-18 at trunk f82edb6193, verified by the mayor at source

- The macro requires `[clojure.java.io :as io]` at `:31` and does a bare `(slurp f)` at `:85`.
- `implementation/spec-resource/src/re_frame/build/spec_resource.clj` exists (5,213 bytes) and wraps
  `shadow.resource/slurp-resource`, **which records path and last-modified against the compiling
  namespace** — exactly the dependency edge that is missing.
- It already has a live consumer (`implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/.../cljs_publics.clj`), and
  `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` carries `spec-resource/src` as a source path with a comment block about
  `spec/` as a classpath ROOT.

So the knowledge is in the tree twice, in the wrapper's own docstring and in that source-path comment. **It
was a PLACEMENT problem, not a knowledge problem** — the bitten worker was three trees away from both.

## Why this is filed rather than done

The repair needs the Xray spec tree reachable as a classpath ROOT so the recording reader can address those
files. That is a change to `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`, **which CLAUDE.md names as a hot-zone file**,
and it is a build-configuration decision rather than a test fix. The worker on rf2-863tl named it and
declined to widen into it, which was right.

## What to do

**Re-derive all of it at tip first** and report the deltas including zeros — line numbers here are from a
single reading and the macro may have moved.

Then decide, and state the decision with its reasoning rather than just applying it:

1. Whether the Xray spec tree should become a classpath root at all, or whether the macro should instead
   address the files through a root that already exists.
2. Whether any OTHER bare-slurp macro shares the defect. **Search for the mechanism, not for this file** —
   a macro that reads a non-source file at expansion time is the class, and a census keyed on this one
   filename finds exactly one thing by construction.

**Take a control both ways on any census**, so a zero means absence rather than a broken pattern.

## Fence

    tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panel_enum_spec_refs.clj
    implementation/shadow-cljs.edn   -- HOT ZONE, source paths only, and only if the ruling above says so

**`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` is sequential, never parallel.** Confirm no other live worker holds it
before starting, and if the repair turns out not to need it, say so and leave it untouched — that is the
better outcome.

## What this does NOT change

CLAUDE.md item (x) records the READING defect and stays as written whatever happens here: even with the
recording reader in place, the general trap — a macro reading a non-source file at expansion time has a
dependency the build tool cannot see unless it is told — remains the thing a reader needs to recognise. This
item is the local repair, not a replacement for the entry.

## Gate note

A green node lane after this change proves the macro still compiles, not that the dependency edge now
exists. **The discrimination is behavioural**: edit a spec row, run an INCREMENTAL compile, and show the
guard now reddens where it previously reported success against the stale list. Without that, the change is
unverified however green the lane is.

title: A macro reading a spec file at expansion time is invisible to incremental shadow-cljs: the guard fails on a stale list and a cold rebuild fixes it with no source change
description:
A guard that slurps names out of a SPEC FILE at macro-expansion time cannot be re-graded by an incremental
shadow-cljs compile, because a `.md` is not an input the compiler tracks. The incremental run reports
success — "1 compiled" — and the guard then fails against the STALE list it captured on a previous
expansion. A COLD REBUILD turns it green with no source change at all.

## Measured

Found 2026-09-18 by the worker on rf2-y8doi.29 (PR #9959), mid-run, on a 41-file panel deletion.

`panel_enum_guard_cljs_test` reconciles THREE projections of the panel roster: the panel enum, the live
facade vars, and the `mount-<panel>!` names it reads out of `tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md` at
macro-expansion time. The worker removed a panel from the facade and the enum, the spec roster row still
named it, and the node lane failed in exactly those words. It then corrected the spec row — and the guard
**still failed**, with an incremental compile reporting `1 compiled`. A cold rebuild, with no further edit,
turned it green.

## Why this is worth a bead rather than a shrug

**It fails in the direction that manufactures a defect hunt.** The worker's visible evidence — the spec file
open in front of it, the row demonstrably corrected — contradicts the gate, and the gate is the thing
everyone is told to believe over their own reading. The natural next move is to go looking for a second,
deeper cause for a failure that has already been fixed. That is an expensive hour, and it lands on a worker
who has just done the right thing.

It is not specific to this one guard. The general shape is: **any macro that reads a non-source file at
expansion time has a dependency the build tool cannot see.** Nothing in the repo currently lists which
macros do this, and the compiler has no way to warn.

## What to do

Decide between recording and gating, and the stance argues for recording:

1. **Record it** — one sentence in the shadow-cljs neighbourhood of CLAUDE.md, and/or a comment at the
   macro's own expansion site saying that a spec edit needs a cold rebuild. This is the cheap, honest
   option and it puts the warning where the next reader meets it.
2. A gate that enumerates macros reading non-source files would be a new mechanism to keep in sync, for a
   trap that a sentence closes. **Probably over-engineering** — weigh it, do not assume it.

**Do NOT restate a count of such macros.** If more than one exists, the number is stale the moment someone
writes another, and this project has already paid for a count in a reusable text.

## Related

- rf2-9gs83 — the clj-kondo `--fail-level error` blindness, the other instrument finding out of this same
  wave. Different mechanism, same family: a gate returning a reassuring answer about a tree it did not
  actually re-read.
- rf2-ucg36 — the shadow-cljs lane recipe is already known incomplete in a different way (the `runner.js`
  check misses the direct JVM compiler). Both are about the same neighbourhood of CLAUDE.md, so **sequence
  these two rather than running them in parallel** — that file is a serial lane.

description:
IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (for the dispatched worker). Docs-truthing. Size S. tools/story/spec only. Parallel-safe. No code.

WHY THIS EXISTS. rf2-m6tu (the May 2026 Storybook/JS-world survey) was closed as superseded on 2026-09-17: every one of its §6 calls was ruled on 2026-05-11 in tools/story/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md, and that page — not the bead — owns the decisions. Two of those rulings are described in the Story spec as SHIPPED MECHANISMS that the runtime never grew. The ruling (rf2-m6tu's close reason and notes, where both reviews are preserved verbatim) is: fix each false sentence with a true sentence; build nothing. Every line cite below was verified at trunk 8bb6041d0e on 2026-09-17. Re-measure before editing: 002-Runtime.md moved three times in the three days before this was written (20038afb74, 012b3d9e5e, c5c96fea4a), so line numbers drift; the phrases quoted here are the stable handles.

RULED OPTION. Reconcile prose to code. Keep every **Decision.** and **Rationale.** paragraph in DESIGN-RATIONALE.md verbatim (they are the historical record and rf2-m6tu's close reason cites them as the home of the rulings). Change ONLY sentences that claim the shell or runtime implements the mechanism, and add a status qualification that covers the WHOLE section — the Codex review's point, which carried: qualifying only the **Implication.** leaves the **Decision.** above it still promising both mechanisms to a reader who stops there.

=== PART 1 — WORKSPACE PERSISTENCE ===

What ships (controls taken 2026-09-17; the ui/workspace.cljc and stories.cljc ranges are the Codex reviewer's, the localStorage census is the dossier's):
- Workspaces resolve their cells from the registered reg-workspace body (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/workspace.cljc:107-158,851-876); the login-form testbed authors its grid and column count directly (tools/story/testbeds/login_form/stories.cljc:288-307).
- No interactive rearrangement: in ui/workspace.cljc, drag|reorder|resiz|localStorage reads 0 (control: layout reads 20).
- No Save-layout-as: Save layout|save-layout reads 0 across tools/story/src (control: reg-workspace|workspace->edn reads 15 lines across story.cljc, registrar.cljc, lifecycle.cljc, schemas.cljc).
- workspace->edn is re-frame.story/workspace->edn (story.cljc:1008) delegating to re-frame.story.lifecycle/workspace->edn (lifecycle.cljc:35-38): it returns the REGISTERED body; it captures no rearrangement and exports no transit blob. DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:134 and 003-Render-Shell.md:346 both name it as tools.story.workspace.transit/workspace->edn — a namespace that does not exist: measured 2026-09-17, that string occurs ONLY on those two spec lines and nowhere under tools/story/src or anywhere else in the tree. Name the real entry point (re-frame.story/workspace->edn) in both places.
- Local persistence that DOES exist is chrome preference, not layout: rail widths (ui/shell/rails.cljs:52-68), mode tabs, toolbar, viewport, background — localStorage|safe-local-storage reads 147 hits across 17 src files.
- The share surface is the address bar (022-Story-UI-Docs-And-Share.md:267-269); the durable form is reg-workspace.
- tools/story/spec/API.md:395 and 002-Runtime.md:854-857 ALREADY say :story/save-layout-as is unimplemented historical vocabulary with no registered effect. Do not touch those two; they are the truth the other pages must agree with.

Sites to change:
(1a) tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md:330-348 §Workspace persistence (both modes). Lines 334-339 describe drag-resize/reorder auto-save keyed by [workspace-id breakpoint] and a "Save layout as :Workspace.x/y" button; lines 344-345 read "Stage 4 (render shell) wires the local-storage save on every layout change; Stage 4 also adds the 'Save layout' affordance." Rewrite the section to state what ships (the registered body IS the layout; chrome prefs persist locally; the address bar shares; reg-workspace is the durable form; workspace->edn returns the registered body) plus ONE sentence recording that the interactive-rearrangement + Save-layout-as pair is the 2026-05-11 decision (DESIGN-RATIONALE §both-workspace-persistence) the shell has not grown. Keep the closing link to DESIGN-RATIONALE.md §both-workspace-persistence — it is the only inbound link to that anchor (measured: 1 hit repo-wide in *.md outside the page itself). Retitle the ## heading if "(both modes)" is now false; nothing links that heading (0 hits).
(1b) tools/story/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:114-136 §both-workspace-persistence. Keep :116-124 **Decision.** and :126-130 **Rationale.** verbatim. Replace the **Implication.** (:132-136: "The render shell wires the local-storage save on every layout change and adds the 'Save layout' affordance. tools.story.workspace.transit/workspace->edn returns the serialised form.") with a paragraph in the page's own lead-in style — the page uses **Decision.** / **Rationale.** / **Implication.** / **Open flag.** / **Rejected.** / **Why.**, so either a new **Status (2026-09).** lead-in or a rewritten **Implication.** — stating: neither half shipped; chrome prefs persist locally; the registered body is the layout; workspace->edn returns the registered body; nobody has asked for either mechanism, so it stays a recorded decision, not a roadmap item. Do NOT rename the ### heading — 003-Render-Shell.md:348 links its anchor.

=== PART 2 — LOADER-COMPLETION TIMING ===

What ships (verified at source 2026-09-17):
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/loaders.cljc:362-373 loaders-default-complete? returns true unconditionally; its docstring says why (dispatch-sync has drained the queue). Blame: fa993fa5e4 (2026-05-11, "Stage 3 — runtime", rf2-von3) introduced it; 82cd4bd1c8 (2026-07-10, "align explanations with current contracts") aligned the docstring.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:289-312 dispatch-syncs each :loaders event, then evaluates the predicate EXACTLY ONCE (:305, evaluate-complete-when — the only call site in tools/story/src; finish-loaders! is reached only from :308). Truthy -> finish-loaders!; falsy -> record-loader-incomplete! -> :rf.error/loader-incomplete, lifecycle parked at :loading, phases 2-4 skipped. The code's own comment at :303-304 reads "The current predicate contract resolves synchronously after the loader events have drained."
- Nothing re-evaluates the predicate on a later drain and nothing waits for a first message. Test story_runtime_test.clj:1709-1738 (run-variant-blocks-events-when-loaders-incomplete) pins the one-shot outcome; story_play_test.clj:318-409 exercises the registered-event, vector and fn override forms with predicates already true after the loader drain — they establish the FORMS, not any waiting.
- loaders.cljc:413-440 evaluate-complete-when documents the accepted forms accurately: nil -> default; registered event id -> dispatch-sync it, read [:rf.story/loaders-complete?] from app-db; vector of event vectors -> all listed events already on the dispatched-events tape; fn -> called with the frame's app-db.

Consequence for an author: a loader that opens a websocket/interval and a variant carrying :loaders-complete-when [[:feed/first-tick-received]] records :rf.error/loader-incomplete on the spot unless the first tick was dispatched synchronously inside the loader drain. The spec must not let an author infer that Story waits for a later network response.

002-Runtime.md is INTERNALLY inconsistent, and the true sentence already exists in it: :455-457 reads "The runtime evaluates the predicate exactly once per loader-cascade settlement; it does NOT poll", and :441-446 (**Never-complete**) describes the one-shot check correctly. (2a) tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md:281-301 §:loaders-complete-when default behaviour. Lines 286-291 say HTTP fx is complete when the response event has been dispatch-synced and long-lived fx is complete "when the first message arrives"; :293-295 say the predicate "is invoked after each event drain settles"; :297-298 say the default is "first non-loader event seen by the frame, or loader's drain settles with no in-flight fx, whichever comes first." Say plainly that the runtime does not wait for an asynchronous first message or response: a loader whose readiness arrives asynchronously must make it observable synchronously within the loader drain, or the run records :rf.error/loader-incomplete. Do not invent a new async mechanism or a timeout knob; if the spec already names a supported route for async loaders, cite it, otherwise say there is none. Keep the Stage 2 macro-validation sentence (:299-301) and the link to DESIGN-RATIONALE §loaders-complete-when-predicate (:302-303 — the only inbound link to that anchor, measured 1 hit).
(2b) tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md:322-329 **Async timeout.** — "A variant whose :loaders-complete-when predicate genuinely awaits an async event (websocket first message, HTTP response) waits as long as the underlying fx takes" is false under the one-shot check, and the timeout recipe ([[:my.fixture/ready?] [:my.fixture/timeout-after 5000]]) presupposes waiting. The same recipe is repeated at :458-462. Under one-shot evaluation a timeout event cannot fire before the predicate is read, so state the contract once and drop or qualify the recipe in both places.
(2c) tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md:429-434 (JS-side note, step 1: "Use :loaders-complete-when ... to hold the lifecycle in :loading until the async work settles"). The lifecycle IS parked at :loading, but the run resolves immediately with :rf.error/loader-incomplete and never resumes; reword so "until the async work settles" does not imply resumption.
(2d) tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md:531-534 §Loader teardown contract, pattern 1 example: :loaders [[:feed/subscribe]] :loaders-complete-when [[:feed/first-tick-received]]. Under the shipped check this variant records loader-incomplete unless the first tick is synchronous. Either change the predicate to one satisfied inside the loader drain or add a one-line caveat; keep the example's point (the :exit action closes the resource on destroy) intact. This edit sits inside a fenced block, which no link gate reads — hand-check it and say so in the PR body.
(2e) tools/story/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:80-112 §loaders-complete-when-predicate. Keep **Decision.** (:82-91) and **Rationale.** (:93-98) verbatim. Replace or qualify the **Implication.** (:100-105: "loader-complete check after each loader's drain" and the "first non-loader event seen ... whichever comes first" default) with a status paragraph: the shipped runtime evaluates once, synchronously, after all loader events dispatch-sync; the default returns true; the first-message wait was never implemented (blame above). The **Open flag.** (:107-112) describes a heartbeat misfire that cannot arise under an always-true default — mark it as applying to the decided-but-unshipped default, or fold it into the status paragraph. Do NOT rename the ### heading (002-Runtime.md:303 links it).
(2f) Check, likely no change: tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md:319 reads "Covered" for :loaders-complete-when — the override FORMS are covered; leave it unless it claims async waiting. tools/story/spec/findings/** is a frozen research corpus (re-frame-2-story-feature-set.md:365 carries the original recommendation) — do not edit it.

title: spec 016: the hydration bullet's GC-clock sentence contradicts the scheduling rule and the code
description:
spec/016-Resources.md :1216 (the Hydration and clock skew bullet, final sentence) says "a hydrated entry's GC deadline starts counting only once it is owner-free on the client".

Two other sources give a different clock basis. The mayor verified the first; the second is the rf2-jqouk worker's reading, a claim:
- The same spec's scheduling rule at :1226 says "a hydrated entry's GC timer arms the first time the client's ensure/fresh-skip path re-establishes ownership".
- The code, as that worker read it:
  - the :gc timer arms after :loaded-at on settle (timers.cljc gc-kind docstring, about :89);
  - it re-arms on revival, when a new owner arrives for an owner-free entry (events.cljc about :504-518);
  - gc-fired re-arms when it finds an owner or in-flight work;
  - releasing the last owner leaves the pending check armed (events.cljc about :1910).
  On that reading the deadline never starts at owner-free, and release does not restart it.

This is the same wrong clock basis that PR #9842 (rf2-jqouk / rf2-n2onr) corrected on docs/resources/coming-from-tanstack-query.md.

THE FIX: make :1216's last sentence agree with the code. Spec prose only.
- Read the hydrated-entry GC arming path at source before writing.
- If the code agrees with :1226, rewrite :1216 to match: the GC timer is client-side and does not arm from the server timestamp, and at fire it removes the entry only if it is owner-free and not in flight.
- If the code instead restarts the deadline on owner-free for hydrated entries, :1216 is right and :1226 is the sentence to fix.
- Either way the code governs, and the report says which way it went.

Found by the rf2-jqouk worker (PR #9842), outside its fence. spec/016-Resources.md is not a hot zone.
