- Hydration arms no timer. `ssr.cljc` `hydrate-runtime-db` reconciles owners, indexes and status and emits no `schedule-timers`; its own comment reads "GC is timer-driven; hydration arms no timers".
- First client ownership arms it. `events.cljc` ensure fresh-skip branch: `was-owner-free? (empty? (:active-owners entry))`, `arm-timers? (and owner-newly-attached? was-owner-free?)`, `gc-delay-ms (when arm-timers? (positive-or-nil (:gc-after-ms spec)))`, then a full `:rf.resource/schedule-timers` reconcile. A stale hydrated entry refetches instead, and the success settle arms GC on every settle.

- Fire removes only an idle, owner-free entry. `gc-fired-handler` removes iff `(and entry (empty? (:active-owners entry)) (nil? (:current-work entry)))`, and otherwise re-arms with a partial `{:gc gc-delay}`.

title: surface-review(adapter_uix): correct capture-frame provider-resolution guidance
description: Recommendation: correct the two UIx README statements that say bare zero-arity `rf/capture-frame` cannot read a context-provided frame. Keep recommending `use-frame` for function components because it observes provider changes, resolves context only, and memoizes the captured operations by frame incarnation. No adapter runtime change is justified by this finding. Verdict: one confirmed P3 documentation-contract defect; no confirmed runtime defect in the owned UIx wrapper. Leave this bead OPEN for the bounded prose repair. This is the single consolidated deliverable for slice `adapter_uix` under rf2-fzbj, not a new implementation audit of the entire shared spine. Revision and ownership - SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2 - WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review) - Review baseline: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. - Observed HEAD: 5b89378c457e9997d7eff69b7dec56eec4e5307c. HEAD differs through tracker-only checkpoints. Both revisions name UIx subtree object 69da9df22b817420fe503987bbec8a4d9b19c0e1. `git diff --exit-code 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f -- implementation/adapters/uix` returned 0, and the owned paths had no status entries. All line numbers below refer to those unchanged sources. - Owned tracked paths, exactly the 25 entries in partition.json, all under `implementation/adapters/uix/`: LICENSE README.md deps.edn src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_after_render_dom_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_boot_order_source_coord_dom_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_client_root_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_client_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_component_recipe_docs_pin_test.clj test/re_frame/adapter/uix_component_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj test/re_frame/adapter/uix_controlled_input_default_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_dispatch_frame_capture_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_evicted_shared_child_dom_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_frame_context_read_dom_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_frame_root_ensure_dom_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_reg_view_devtools_dom_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_reg_view_direct_mount_dom_cljs_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_source_coord_dom_elision_prod_test.cljs test/re_frame/adapter/uix_use_sub_dom_cljs_test.cljs testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs testbed/index.html testbed/spec.cjs Coverage and limits Inspected the complete shipping adapter namespace and README, dependency manifest, smoke fixture and runner; followed its delegation into the shared React spine, frame resolver, use-frame hook, and frame-root lifecycle core. Inspected the UIx test entry points and relevant witnesses for query/frame key changes, same-query siblings, durable retain/release, provisional render ownership and Suspense abandonment, eviction reacquisition and stale cleanup, provider swaps and imperative effect dependencies, incarnation-aware use-frame memoization, frame-root commit ownership and child/prop marshalling, direct registered-view mounting and registration-before-init, source coordinates, after-render wiring, reusable roots, hydration, and controlled-input selection. Reviewed dependency-recipe and documentation-pin test logic. This is targeted source inspection of behavior and test construction, not execution of every listed file or proof of all transitive core behavior. No source changes, build, browser suite, broad gate, dependency install, service, or compilation output was produced. Existing CLJS artifacts were inspected and found stale (they still expose use_subscribe); they were deliberately NOT executed or used as proof of the current adapter. The LICENSE and HTML scaffolding were rostered but not independently validated for legal/rendering correctness. No release/POM publication was attempted. Confirmed finding F1 — P3: README describes the wrong imperative frame-resolution contract Owned source: `implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:14` and `:87`. Both statements say that no-arg `(rf/capture-frame)` in a plain UIx hooks component reads only the dynamic-var tier and raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` beneath a context provider. That is false when the UIx adapter is installed. Concrete path at the reviewed revision: 1. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1487-1491`: zero-arity capture-frame asks require-current-frame! for the ambient frame. 2. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:742-828`: resolve-current-frame invokes the installed :adapter/current-frame hook in the ordinary, non-refusing extent. 3. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3847-3849`: make-react-adapter routes that hook to `re-frame.adapter.context/function-component-current-frame` for UIx. 4. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs:335-376`: that reader checks the dynamic frame first, then the shared context's active value slot. It reads `_currentValue`, with `_currentValue2` fallback when the primary is the no-provider sentinel. A live provider's frame therefore resolves with no dynamic binding. 5. The owned smoke fixture already uses this exact legal form: `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs:29-31` captures with bare rf/capture-frame in its native defui, and `:58-60` mounts it beneath UIx frame-root. Its own comment at :53 correctly says the capture resolves through that boundary. Trigger/reproducer: install `rf.adapter.uix/adapter`, create a live frame `::tenant`, leave `rf.frame/*current-frame*` nil, and render a native UIx defui whose body obtains `(:frame (rf/capture-frame))` beneath `($ rf.adapter.uix/frame-provider {:frame ::tenant} ($ probe))`. This is an ordinary render extent, not an effect callback and not a Fresco refusing extent. The README predicts no-frame-context. The implementation returns `::tenant`. The testbed's root is an existing consumer of the same form under frame-root. No missing provider or uninstalled-adapter assumption is needed. Expected versus actual: documentation should match this successful render-time capture while explaining why use-frame remains the component-oriented API. Actual documentation attributes the recommendation to a nonexistent failure, conflating hook resolution with the imperative resolver. Hook context-only resolution is a deliberate rule; it did not remove the imperative resolver's context tier. Impact: incorrect public integration guidance and misleading diagnosis for consumers comparing the README against the shipped smoke fixture. It also hides the useful reasons to choose use-frame: provider-change subscription, stable callback identity within one incarnation, and independence from an unrelated dynamic binding around synchronous rendering. The provided effect recipe itself is correct; its [tile-id dispatch] dependencies must remain. Precise repair: rewrite both false clauses to distinguish the imperative reader from the hook. State that bare capture-frame can capture the current frame during a UIx render through the installed adapter's dynamic-first/context-second resolver, while use-frame reads context only, observes provider changes and memoizes the result. Keep the imperative-effect example using use-frame and including dispatch in the effect dependencies. Do not weaken no-provider failures, change the runtime resolution rule, or rewrite the valid testbed solely to make the old prose look true. Acceptance criteria: - Neither README location claims zero-arity capture-frame reads only the dynamic tier or necessarily throws under a UIx provider. - The recommendation for use-frame is justified by its actual observable behavior, and the existing [tile-id dispatch] recipe is preserved. - The prose is checked against the four source links above and the existing testbed consumer, with no changes to hook/imperative resolution semantics. - If implementation-time runtime validation is added, use the current compiled adapter with the dynamic frame explicitly cleared and assert that both bare capture-frame and use-frame obtain the provider's frame; keep a providerless negative control. A React mechanism probe alone must not be reported as that adapter test. Validation evidence Executed a bounded process-local Node probe, adapter_uix-context-mechanism-1, using the already-installed React 19.3.0 and react-dom/server. It rendered a component beneath a React Context.Provider with value ':review/tenant'. The component recorded the public useContext result and the exact primary-then-secondary slot-selection expression used by current context.cljs; both returned ':review/tenant'. The direct reader returned null before and after rendering. Output markup was `probe`. Node exit 0; assertions verified provider agreement and outside-render absence. No files or persistent service were created by that probe. This is mechanism evidence only: it executes React and a small transcription of the current slot-selection expression, not freshly compiled CLJS, rf/capture-frame, the adapter's provider wrapper, or the browser smoke. Confirmation of F1 rests on the complete current source path plus the contradictory owned consumer; no current browser pass is claimed. Prior history and non-duplication - rf2-tug6 is closed: it repaired the README effect's missing dispatch dependency and added mounted-swap/negative-control tests. F1 preserves that repair and targets the separate false premise at :14/:87. - rf2-kuky.61 and rf2-kuky.62 are closed: hooks were ruled context-only; the implementation bead explicitly kept rf/capture-frame, rf/current-frame-id and the imperative resolver out of scope. F1 is consistent with that ruling, not a proposal to restore dynamic-first hooks. - rf2-mhpo is closed at f0c2cde590: it corrected deferred handlers' nonexistent :rf/default fallback. It did not correct the two claims here. Its latest history and close reason were checked. - rf2-poxh is closed at 59e8833f3a: the UIx README is now on the migration-contract-drift roster. This is not a request to add it again; roster coverage does not make these prose claims true. - rf2-1frc is closed: cache-eviction reacquisition and identity-guarded cleanup were repaired, including shared-child follow-up. The review did not refile those repaired defects. Unverified risk, not a finding or an acceptance item The shared spine's use-sub stable tuple is [frame-id query-v], while use-frame's memo also observes incarnation. A mounted subscription surviving destroy-and-recreate at the same id deserves a direct current-runtime witness before anyone claims a defect: the inspected use-frame reincarnation test forces another render and does not itself prove use-sub behavior. This hypothesis was sent to the coordinating parent for the shared-spine/test-react reviewer. It was not reproduced here, is excluded from the finding count, and does not justify widening this README repair. title: False: batching test-map claims cascade-turn isolation that its witness does not distinguish
description:
PR #9702 (merge e60d214b63b1d6f0686c5e1a3774e25bb70cdb45) correctly removes the unsupported transition-API coverage claim, but its new test-map wording at implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md:1172 credits cascade non-flattening: a component re-queued during forceUpdate gets a fresh turn rather than joining the current drain.

The cited enqueue-during-drain-schedules-fresh-turn test in implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/impl/batching_cljs_test.cljs increments calls, requeues while calls < 3, waits several microtasks, and asserts only (= 3 @calls). It never observes a turn boundary or intermediate count. A drain that processes all three requeues in its FIRST microtask produces the identical final count and passes this assertion. Waiting multiple turns before a final count does not distinguish three turns from one. This is direct source analysis, not a claim that a mutated repository suite was run.

The production RenderQueue currently snapshots the queue before draining, so this finding does NOT allege a runtime scheduling defect. It concerns the newly added coverage claim. Keep this correction small: describe the existing witness as eventual repeated requeue/drain coverage rather than proof of non-flattening. If retaining the stronger coverage claim, first add a focused assertion that distinguishes separate turns from a flattened drain and demonstrate it fails for flattening. No new public API, scheduler redesign, or transition integration test is required.

No literal-open Bead explicitly records this defect and correction in the current census. rf2-slh2/rf2-6fxq concerned the previous transition claim; this is the replacement claim introduced by #9702.
acceptance_criteria: The test-map row no longer claims separate-turn/non-flattening coverage from a final count alone. Prefer a prose correction to the actual eventual requeue/drain assertion. If the stronger claim is kept, a focused witness must fail when the same three updates are flattened into one drain and pass with separate turns. Preserve the repaired transition-risk wording and the accurate after-render and real-DOM coverage clauses; no runtime/API expansion is required.
notes:
## 2026-09-12 — DONE via route (b). PR #9705 (day8/re-frame2), branch worker/cascade-a.

PREMISE HELD, re-derived at source. `enqueue-during-drain-schedules-fresh-turn` at
batching_cljs_test.cljs:65 asserted exactly one thing, `(= 3 @calls)`, taken after three
`next-microtask` hops. `RenderQueue.flush-render` snapshots `component-queue` and nils it before
iterating, so the runtime behaviour is correct; what could not be distinguished was the claim.

ROUTE (b) — the witness now earns the claim. The count is observed at each TURN BOUNDARY: 1, then 2,
then 3. The IMPL-SPEC 12.1 row keeps its cascade-non-flattening clause, now earned, and records how it
is witnessed. Every other clause in that row is retained verbatim, including the rf2-6fxq transition
correction. One file of prose, one deftest.

A BRIEF PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD, and it is the mechanism behind the defect. The dispatch brief
prescribed observing after the first hop of the file's existing `next-microtask` helper. That helper's
handler RETURNS a promise, and the thenable-adoption jobs cost FOUR raw microtask ticks per hop —
enough that all three drain turns fit inside one hop. Measured against a faithful JS model of
RenderQueue: with `next-microtask` the hops read 3, 3, 3 under the REAL scheduler and 3, 3, 3 under a
FLATTENING one, identical, so the brief's recipe would have gone red on correct code without
discriminating anything. A SINGLE-tick hop (`.then` on an already-resolved promise) reads 1, 2, 3 real
and 3, 3, 3 flattening. `ratom/flush!`, which `flush-queues` calls first, is fully synchronous and
enqueues nothing, so the interleave holds. That accounting is written into the test's comment so the
next author does not re-introduce the multi-tick helper here.

SABOTAGE WITNESS, PROVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the second half is the deliverable. A flattening
drain was planted in production batching.cljs (blob 3f3ef49320 -> 1831acd4b4, 49 files recompiled, so
the runtime demonstrably saw it):

  plant + NEW test : exit 1, 2 failures, both in this deftest, (not (= 1 3)) and (not (= 2 3))
  plant + OLD test : exit 0, 0 failures, 0 errors across all 11773 tests / 58800 assertions

So with a genuinely flattening scheduler in the tree the ENTIRE node lane was blind. Test and
assertion counts identical across both runs, so the plant stranded no namespace. All three touched
files restored and verified: the DEFAULT git hash-object form reproduces each committed blob
(ffa6c998e2, eb91b77188, 3f3ef49320 — all three are i/lf w/crlf, so --no-filters is the wrong form,
CLAUDE.md item (r)), and git diff --quiet HEAD exits 0 over the whole tree.

title: CLAUDE.md clause-5 discharge: a RENAMED job reads as an added job key and fakes a band move
description:
CLAUDE.md's clause-5 discharge procedure carries one sentence that is FALSE FOR A RENAME, and
a routine rename sweep in this repo triggers it. Correct the sentence; add the one-line check
that settles it.

THE SENTENCE, in CLAUDE.md's merge-criterion trap bullet (item (a), the two-space job-key
discriminator), at the end of the discharge paragraph:

    "This is no licence to discount `test.yml`, whose `pull_request` trigger is deliberately
     unfiltered -- so a key added there is a real new check every time."

True for a genuine addition. FALSE for a rename, because the discriminator only ever inspects
`+` lines and a renamed job adds a key while removing another.

MEASURED 2026-09-10 at trunk d9ba7e8ac2. Over a 24-hour window of workflow churn the two-space
form read 7 added job keys, 5 of them in `test.yml`:
    fresco-guide-samples, cljs-fresco-controlled, cljs-fresco-hmr, jvm-fresco,
    jvm-migration-fresco-codemod
Following the documented discharge to the letter gives "5 real new checks" and a band of 92.
THE BAND WAS 87 BEFORE AND 87 AFTER, measured on four consecutive PRs merged after that commit
(#9626, #9627, #9628, #9629), every one reading 87 with 0 non-terminal.

The commit is `8b17cc53d5 refactor(fresco): sweep all three case forms of the product name
(rf2-d1nr.2)`. Mirroring the pattern to count removals reads added=5 REMOVED=5, and the lists
are exact pairs: `hicasso-guide-samples` -> `fresco-guide-samples`, `cljs-hicasso-controlled`
-> `cljs-fresco-controlled`, and so on through all five. Net new jobs: zero.

WHAT TO WRITE. Two things, kept to the existing bullet rather than a new one:

  1. Qualify the sentence. A key added to `test.yml` is a real new check UNLESS the same diff
     removes one -- count removals with the mirrored pattern
     `^-  [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$` before concluding anything. Added == removed with
     pairwise-corresponding names is a RENAME and the band does not move.
  2. Record the cheaper confirmation, which needs no pattern at all: read the rollup TOTAL of
     PRs merged AFTER the suspect commit. Four PRs at 87 across a commit that "added five jobs"
     settles it immediately.

SEVERITY AND DIRECTION. This fails CLOSED -- it flags a merge that should proceed -- so it is a
nuisance rather than a hazard, and the bullet already records a fail-closed qualification for
this same discriminator, which is where this belongs. The cost is still real: it manufactures a
band that never existed, after which every PR reads five checks short of a phantom, which is
indistinguishable from a change genuinely missing five jobs, and the natural next move is to
hunt for coverage that was never missing. Rename sweeps are routine here -- there is a live gate
ratcheting the retired product name out of the tree -- so this recurs.

DO NOT weaken or remove the discriminator, and do not touch `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md`.
The method page states clause 5 generically and correctly; what is wrong is the CLI concretion
in CLAUDE.md, which is exactly the division of labour that bullet already follows for traps
(b), (p), (q) and (r).

EDITING THIS FILE HAS ITS OWN TRAP, and it is recorded in the file you are editing, item (e):
writing an entry once inserted four REAL carriage returns where an escape was meant literally,
git reclassified `CLAUDE.md` from `w/crlf` to `w/-text`, stopped normalising it, and staged 156
changed lines for a one-clause edit. After editing, confirm the total CR count equals the CRLF
count -- and take BOTH numbers with PYTHON reading the bytes
(`open(p,"rb").read().count(b"")`), never with `grep -c`, which reads 0 on this very file and
so makes the check pass vacuously as `0 == 0` (item (s)). Report both numbers and the staged
line count in the PR body.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged as PR #9635, rebased onto main at 6e46761a5c. One line changed.

WHAT WAS WRONG. CLAUDE.md's clause-5 discharge procedure ended: "a key added there is a real new
check every time." True for a genuine addition, FALSE for a rename — the two-space discriminator
only ever inspects `+` lines, and a renamed job adds a key while removing another. Following the
procedure literally after a product-name rename sweep yields "5 real new checks in test.yml" and
a band of 92, when the band never moved.

THE CORRECTED RULE now says to count REMOVED keys with the mirrored pattern before concluding
anything, and records the cheaper confirmation that needs no pattern at all: read the rollup total
of PRs merged AFTER the suspect commit.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN BRIEF, made by the worker and worth recording. I gave it "added=5
REMOVED=5" on 8b17cc53d5. That is the `test.yml`-SCOPED SUBSET. The whole-directory figure on that
commit is 7 ADDED / 7 REMOVED, identical to the 24-hour window figure because no other workflow
commit in the window moved a job key. All seven pair one-to-one. The conclusion and the pairing
are unchanged, but the scope of the number was not stated, and I have corrected the memory
`renamed-job-reads-as-added-job-key-clause-5` accordingly.

The worker also widened the band evidence beyond mine: 87 on #9564-#9567 (merged BEFORE the rename
commit) and 87 on #9626-#9629 (after) — eight PRs, all 87, nothing non-terminal. Measuring both
sides of the commit is strictly better than measuring only after it, which is all I had done.

A FINDING THAT COST A RED CI RUN, and it generalises. The passage originally named the removed job
keys by their literal PRE-RENAME spellings, and the retired-product-name ratchet (281d9a00a3)
correctly failed CLAUDE.md at that line. The gate offers `PRODUCT_EXEMPTIONS` for historical
facts; the worker DECLINED to use it, on the ground that an exemption is for an occurrence that
MUST keep the old spelling to work, and this one need not — the point being made is that the
names correspond PAIRWISE, which carries without either spelling. Widening a ratchet built to
drive that count to zero, for a convenience mention, is the wrong trade. I agree, and the
reasoning is the durable part: reworded to "the pre-rename twin of an added name", and CLAUDE.md
now carries the retired spelling zero times.

THE GENERAL HAZARD, recorded as its own memory: any brief asking someone to DOCUMENT a rename
sweep in gated prose walks straight into the gate for the thing being retired. My brief did
exactly that without noticing.

VERIFIED BY THE MAYOR at merge time, independently of the worker's report: all five clauses (87 at
band, 0 failed, 0 pending, aggregator present, 0 non-terminal runs at the full 40-character oid,
0 job keys added or removed on trunk since merge-base). And on this file specifically, because
item (e) records an edit here once staging 156 lines for a one-clause change: total CR 156 == CRLF
156, bare CR 0, `git ls-files --eol` still `i/lf w/crlf` rather than reclassified to `w/-text`,
and `--numstat` reading 1 insertion / 1 deletion.

TWO CATALOGUED TRAPS FIRED ON THE WORKER INSIDE THIS ONE TASK, both already in CLAUDE.md, and it
reported them rather than hiding them: reading a gate through a `tail` pipe and getting `tail`'s
exit 0 on a run that was actually RED, and checking for `.beads` paths with `git diff origin/main`
— which read 1 once origin/main advanced with a checkpoint, where the merge-base comparison reads
0. Having just read those entries did not prevent either. That is evidence about how these traps
work, not about this worker.

title: [MIKE ONLY - yes/no] Clear 16 permanently-unreapable worktrees: measured spent, nothing stranded
description:
[OPERATOR CALL — MIKE ONLY, and it needs only a yes/no] Sixteen worker worktrees are
PERMANENTLY UNREAPABLE by the standing reap test, and I have measured that NONE of them holds
any work. They are clutter, not risk. The question is whether to clear them.

THE STATE, measured 2026-09-10 at trunk c84a5e5157. Twenty-two worktrees exist; six are live
workers; the remaining sixteen are these:

  contrepair-a  epochkey-a  eptmpl-a   keymeta-a   keyxing-a   machpanel-a
  mdgate-a      mountdoc-a  mountstep-a samefrm-a  soelint-a   ssrdoc-a
  staticfs-a    testid-a    tracefx-a  walkgate-a

NOTHING IS STRANDED IN ANY OF THEM. `git cherry origin/main worker/<x>` reads `+`=0 for all
sixteen — every commit's content is already upstream, 1 to 4 commits each. The instrument was
controlled in both directions in the same sweep: the two live branches whose PRs were genuinely
open at that moment read `+`=2. See the memory `rev-list-calls-every-rebase-merged-branch-unmerged`
for why the obvious SHA-based check (`git rev-list origin/main..<branch>`) is useless here — it
called all sixteen "unmerged" because `gh pr merge --rebase` rewrites SHAs, and a uniform verdict
across a heterogeneous population was the only thing on screen that betrayed it.

WHY I DID NOT JUST REMOVE THEM. `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` §Reaping: "Only a worker's own
completion report authorises reaping its worktree. Not a merged change. Not a clean tree. Not
elapsed time. Not directory age." It then lists six proxies adopted in one session and each found
wrong, two of which are exactly what I had in hand — "change state — merged means the WORK
landed, not that the worker stopped" and "clean AND merged together, which still took two full
gate runs". A patch-id census is a more rigorous spelling of the merged proxy, so the rule refuses
it, and it refuses it for a good reason: reaping a tree whose agent is still running destroys that
run, and the wreckage presents as gates naming real present files as missing, which has twice been
read as a genuine regression.

AND THE OBVIOUS RESCUE DOES NOT WORK EITHER. Asking the live agent list whether the owning agent
is still running cannot settle it: these trees are from EARLIER SESSIONS, so their agents are
absent from this session's list whether they are running or not. That is the empty-sink error the
same section names — an empty search reading as "no report exists", which is the reap test's own
blocking condition, and is precisely how a tree becomes permanently unreapable.

SO THIS IS THE RULE WORKING AS DESIGNED, AND IT IS STILL AN ACCUMULATION. The count was 11 after
the last hygiene pass and is 22 now. Every future hygiene tick will re-measure these sixteen,
re-confirm they are spent, and re-decline to remove them, because no further evidence can ever
arrive. Only an operator can break that loop.

WHAT I RECOMMEND, and it is a genuine recommendation rather than a hedge: clear all sixteen. The
work is provably upstream, so nothing is lost, and the only hazard in removal is the shared
`implementation/node_modules` junction, which `scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh` already handles
— it unlinks the junction before removing the tree and re-checks the mayor's counts afterwards,
failing loudly if any dropped.

THE PROCEDURE, if you say yes — hand the script an ABSOLUTE PATH, never a bare name, since targets
resolve against the current directory:

    sh scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh "C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/<name>"

then delete each spent branch with `git branch -D worker/<name>`. Expect `CANARY_BEFORE=` and
`CANARY_AFTER=` lines to match on every run, and the mayor's `implementation/node_modules` to stay
at 103 immediate entries with 27 in `.bin` (count with `ls -A` or `find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1`,
never a bare `ls`, which omits dotfiles and so cannot see `.bin` at all).

I can execute this the moment you say go. I am not doing it unasked, because the rule that forbids
it is the one that stops a coordinator destroying a live worker's run, and I would rather bring
the accumulation to you than quietly grant myself an exception to it.

DELIBERATELY NOT PROPOSED: weakening the reap test, or adding a seventh proxy to it. The rule is
right; what it lacks is an operator escape hatch, and this bead is that hatch used once rather
than a change to the rule.
notes:
== MAYOR, 2026-09-10: CENSUS COMPLETED — the original recommendation rested on HALF a check ==

CORRECTING MY OWN FILING. When I filed this bead I wrote "NOTHING IS STRANDED IN ANY OF THEM"
on the strength of a patch-id census alone. That census answers only whether the COMMITS are
upstream. It says nothing about UNCOMMITTED work, and a tree can be fully merged by patch-id
and still hold an uncommitted analysis note or a draft. The claim was therefore stronger than
the evidence when I made it.

Found by reading `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` §Removing BEFORE doing the work rather than
on the re-read cadence — which is itself a rule that landed in the method today. That section
prescribes a "disposable-only force" that "refuses any tree holding a modified tracked file, a
note or a draft", and records that when it was written ONE worktree held four analysis files
for an OPEN item and three others carried uncommitted source and doc edits. So this is a
measured, recurring class, not a hypothetical.

THE MISSING HALF, NOW MEASURED at trunk e61e527b7d. `git status --porcelain` in each of the
sixteen trees:

    ALL SIXTEEN CLEAN — 0 modified tracked files, 0 untracked files, every tree.

CONTROLLED, because a uniform verdict is exactly what a broken probe returns: the same probe
run against the live worktrees in the same sweep reads a non-zero line count on one of them.
So the instrument discriminates, and the sixteen zeros are real absences rather than a silent
failure.

BOTH HALVES NOW HOLD. Commits upstream by patch-id AND no uncommitted state. The
recommendation stands, but it now rests on the check it should have rested on from the start.

THE CLOCK CONTROL, CAPTURED BEFORE ANY REMOVAL, as §Removing prescribes — because a count
cannot detect a delta that a listing-form change cancels, while a modification time moves on a
removal and cannot be suppressed by listing options:

    implementation/node_modules
      newest entry : .package-lock.json   2026-09-10 11:12
      canary       : immediate=103  recursive=2933

AND THE PAGE'S WARNING REPRODUCES HERE EXACTLY. It notes that on the tree it measured, the
entry carrying the newest mtime was itself one of the HIDDEN ones, so the listing form that
suppressed the count also suppressed the control. That is the case here too: the clock is
carried by `.package-lock.json`, a dotfile, which a bare `ls` cannot see at all. So both the
count and its control must be taken with `ls -A` or `find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1`. Re-read
the three numbers above AFTER the batch and require all three to be unchanged.

RUN IT DETACHED. Sixteen sequential worktree removals is a long local operation, and the method
gained a paragraph today saying the operator cannot distinguish a session busy on one from a
session that has stalled. I will run it as a background task and stay answerable rather than
going silent for the duration.

Nothing else about this bead changes: the reap rule still forbids me removing these on my own
authority, and this is still a yes/no.
== SECOND QUESTION FOR THE SAME OPERATOR VISIT, 2026-09-10: TWO SPIKE BRANCHES ==

Different decision from the sixteen worktrees above, put here rather than on its own bead so one
visit answers both. Where the worktree question is "nothing is stranded, may I clear them", this
one is the opposite: BOTH BRANCHES CARRY REAL UNMERGED CONTENT, and the question is whether that
content is wanted.

    worker/receipts-hic081    3 commits, 2026-08-11    local + on origin, NO worktree
    worker/xspike-a           1 commit,  2026-09-09    local + on origin, NO worktree

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and the measurement reversed the easy reading. `git cherry` reads `+` on
both, which is only the ABSENCE of proof of containment and is routinely produced by a sibling
change moving a commit's context lines. So I ran the real check the method prescribes — compare
each commit's whole patch against the tip at the paths it touches:

    receipts-hic081   all 3 paths ABSENT at tip, 2453 diff lines
                      implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs
                      implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/receipt.cljs
                      implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/receipt_spike_cljs_test.cljs
    xspike-a          9 of 10 paths ABSENT at tip, 1410 diff lines
                      tools/xray/testbeds/xspike/*  (only implementation/shadow-cljs.edn survives)

So these are NOT residue and must not be swept. Deleting either destroys work that exists nowhere
else.

BUT THE WORK IS DELIBERATELY UNMERGED, WHICH IS THE POINT. Both are SPIKES — every commit message
on both branches begins `spike(`. A spike's deliverable is a MEASUREMENT that informs a ruling,
not a merge. `xspike-a` is rf2-k97c.1's spike ("build the App-DB panel both ways, on two
adapters"), and rf2-k97c.1 is CLOSED — its findings were spent in rf2-k97c.2's ruling, which
chose Design B. `receipts-hic081` predates the product rename and sits on the retired
`implementation/hicasso/` path; I confirmed no fresco-named counterpart of the receipt spike
exists at the tip under any name, so it never landed and was never meant to.

THE QUESTION, and either answer is defensible:
  (a) KEEP as archive. The spike code is the only surviving artefact of two measurements whose
      conclusions are now load-bearing rulings. Costs two refs.
  (b) DELETE deliberately, accepting the loss, because the rulings they informed are recorded and
      the code was never a candidate to ship.

I am not deciding this one. It is not the reap rule blocking me — no worktree and no live agent is
involved — it is that discarding the only copy of real work is an operator's call, and "it was
only a spike" is exactly the kind of reasoning that should be said out loud before bytes go away.

IF (b): `git branch -D worker/receipts-hic081 worker/xspike-a` locally AND
`git push origin --delete worker/receipts-hic081 worker/xspike-a`, because the remote set is not a
subset of the local one and both exist on origin.

== WHAT I DID CLEAR THIS TICK, UNASKED AND UNDER THE RULE ==

Thirteen `pr<NNNN>-tmp` local branches (pr9615 through pr9628) left by the merged-PR audit
harness. Every one read `-` ONLY under `git cherry` — proof of containment, which is the criterion

on origin.

even though its content was demonstrably upstream. That is the rebase invariance — a rebase replays
commits under new identities, so a merged branch never becomes an ancestor of the trunk. Ancestry
is the wrong test here and `-D` on patch-equivalence evidence is the right one.

AND A SCOPING ERROR OF MINE, since it is the reusable part: my branch sweep was scoped to
`refs/heads/worker/` and would have missed all thirteen. The method warns that the remote set is
not a subset of the local one; the same shape bit me one level up — a NAMESPACE is not the whole

title: xray: managed-fx panel draws three disclosure triangles that nothing can open
description:
Measured under rf2-twil at base c6e008813d. Independent of the Fresco work; found while trying
to make an HD-016 regression row reach the four `edn/inspect` sites.

`panels/managed_fx_template/record-panel` builds REQUEST, RESPONSE and HANDLER DISPATCHED with
`:expanded? false`. `theme/section/section-row` renders its body under `(when expanded? ...)`
and its header draws a `▶`/`▼` glyph from that same flag. Nothing anywhere wires a toggle:
`section-row` takes no handler, `theme/section.cljc` holds no expansion state, and
`managed_fx_subs.cljs` registers none. So the three sections render a disclosure affordance
that cannot be operated, and their payloads -- the request, the response (and the failure
tags), and the dispatched handler vector -- are unreachable in the UI.

The panel's own docstring already promises the behaviour that is missing:

    "REQUEST + RESPONSE + HANDLER DISPATCHED collapsed by default (one click reveals the
     payload -- keeps the panel scannable on first paint)."

The bodies ARE computed on every render (they are positional arguments to `section-row`) and
then discarded, so this is wasted work as well as a dead affordance.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE UX. Those three sections are where all four of the `edn/inspect`
sites rf2-twil repaired live. Because a collapsed body never reaches a rendered tree, no
walker, no codec and no DOM row can grade them -- which is the whole reason three tiers of
coverage missed the HD-016 hazard rather than any of them being badly written. Wiring the
toggle is what turns those four into gradeable render paths, so it is the natural companion to
the migration slice in rf2-fcy5 even though it is not a Fresco problem.

SCOPE NOTE: `theme/section/section-row` is SHARED with `panels/event_detail` (per its own ns
docstring), so a toggle added there lands on both. Decide deliberately whether the expansion
state belongs in the shared widget or in each panel; do not add it to the shared one by
reflex.
notes:
== FOLDED IN FROM rf2-kfoq, 2026-09-10 (mayor) ==

I filed rf2-kfoq on this same finding shortly after this bead was created, from the same worker's
report. This bead is kept -- it has the decisive evidence, the panel's OWN docstring promising
"one click reveals the payload" -- and rf2-kfoq is closed. Its distinct content is here rather
than lost.

=== ONE CLAIM IN THIS BEAD NEEDS NARROWING, AND IT CHANGES THE REPAIR ===

This description says "Nothing anywhere wires a toggle". The per-file half is right --
`section-row` takes no handler, `theme/section.cljc` holds no expansion state, `managed_fx_subs`
registers none -- but read as a statement about the TREE it is false, and the difference is the
whole fix.

MAYOR-VERIFIED AT SOURCE, trunk cb71918a9a, nonsense control zero:

  theme/section.cljc:52   the contract, stated deliberately:
        "No interactivity. Click-to-toggle wiring is the caller's [responsibility]"

  panels/cancellation_cascade.cljs:689   a caller that DOES it:
        :expanded? (rf.fresco/sub [:rf.xray/cancellation-cascade-expanded?])

So `section-row` is non-interactive BY DESIGN and needs no repair, expansion state DOES exist in
this tree, and there is a working pattern one file away. `managed_fx_template.cljs` simply never
did the caller's half.

**THE REPAIR IS THEREFORE TO COPY AN IN-TREE PATTERN, NOT TO INVENT ONE**: give the managed-fx
panel its own per-section expansion state and sub, the way the cascade panel does. **Do NOT add
interactivity to `section-row`** -- that breaks its stated contract and would reach its other
caller.

Recorded at this length because the CONCLUSION was right and the REASON was not, which is the
harder case to catch: a repairer who believes nothing in the tree wires this will build it from
scratch and diverge from the cascade panel for no reason.

=== SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT -- READ BEFORE PICKING THIS UP ===

Those three sections are where all four `edn/inspect` head-position sites live. A collapsed body
is CONSTRUCTED (positional argument) and then discarded by the `when`, and constructing a hiccup
vector calls nothing -- so the sites cannot throw while the sections stay shut.

**WIRING THE DISCLOSURE IS EXACTLY WHAT MAKES THEM REACHABLE.** So this must land AFTER, or in the
same change as, the head-form repair in rf2-twil / PR #9624. Landing it first converts a latent
hazard into a live throw, and under Fresco an HD-016 throw escapes with no error boundary above it
and React unmounts the entire Xray root -- it presents as a panel that never appears rather than as
an error. That is the rf2-qhoj incident, and this bead is one merge order away from reproducing it.
SUPERSEDED BY rf2-kfoq, which the mayor filed for the same defect. Closing as a duplicate
rather than keeping two live beads on one dead affordance.

TWO THINGS FROM HERE WORTH CARRYING ACROSS, and one correction to this bead's own reasoning:

1. CORRECTION. This bead said the wiring is absent because nothing in the tree has expansion
   state. That is wrong and the mayor caught it. `theme/section.cljc` states the contract
   deliberately -- "No interactivity. Click-to-toggle wiring is the caller's responsibility"
   -- so `section-row` is non-interactive BY DESIGN, and expansion state DOES exist with a
   working caller at `panels/cancellation_cascade.cljs:689`, which feeds `:expanded?` from a
   sub. `managed_fx_template` simply passes literals and never wrote that half. The
   conclusion is unchanged; the reason was.

2. SCOPE NOTE THAT SURVIVES. `theme/section/section-row` is SHARED with
   `panels/event_detail` (per its own ns docstring). Because the primitive is deliberately
   dumb, the state belongs in the CALLER -- which is what cancellation_cascade already
   demonstrates -- so this is a per-panel change and not a change to the shared widget.
   Do not add expansion state to `section.cljc` by reflex.

3. SEQUENCING. Wiring the disclosure is what turns managed_fx_template's four repaired
   `edn/inspect` sites into gradeable render paths, so it must land after or together with
   rf2-twil's head-form repair, not before it.

title: RULING WANTED: should anything grade the TRACKER for retired spellings? (measured: 97% false positives on a naive rule)
description:
SHOULD ANYTHING GRADE THE TRACKER FOR RETIRED SPELLINGS? Filed out of rf2-j8lg, which swept the
retired product name from 14 non-terminal beads (411 occurrences) after the tree-side sweep
(rf2-d1nr.2, PR #9568) left the tracker behind. rf2-j8lg asked the question; this bead carries
the measurement and the recommendation. NOTHING IS BUILT. This wants a ruling first.

=== THE MEASUREMENT (rf2-j8lg's worker, 2026-09-10, export at 03d4af871c) ===

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is 2290 non-blank lines: 1223 `issue` records and 1067 `memory` records.
504 lines carry the retired name. By status: 370 CLOSED issues, 120 MEMORY records (which carry
NO status key at all), and 14 non-terminal issues — the ones rf2-j8lg corrected. So a naive
whole-file rule fires on 504 lines of which 490 are legitimate history: a 97% FALSE-POSITIVE
RATE, and the memory half is the part a "closed beads are exempt" rule does not even reach.

=== THE GATE ALREADY EXCLUDES `.beads`, BUT NOT BY ITS OWN STANDARD ===

`scripts/check_retired_spellings.py` rule (g) scans THE WHOLE REPO with no suffix roster, minus
three subtractions. `.beads` is pruned — but by `_EXCLUDE_DIR_NAMES`, the roster SHARED with
rules (a)-(f), described there as "generated / vendored directory NAMES" alongside
`node_modules`, `target`, `.shadow-cljs`, `.git` and `.cpcache`. Rule (g)'s own doctrine is that
"a subtraction is visible and has to justify itself", and `PRODUCT_EXCLUDE_PATHS` argues every
one of its entries in prose. `.beads` has no rule-(g) argument written anywhere: the exclusion is
INHERITED rather than decided. That is the gap this bead names, and it is a documentation gap at
least, whichever way the ruling goes.

=== THE ARGUMENT AGAINST EXTENDING RULE (g) TO THE EXPORT ===

1. A GATE MUST BE DETERMINISTIC AT A COMMIT, AND THIS INPUT IS NOT. The export is a full-database
   dump that `bd` REWRITES in every checkout, so two worktrees at the same commit hold different
   bytes depending on when `bd` last ran. The gate reads the working tree.

2. IT WOULD GO RED WHERE NOBODY MAY FIX IT. Worker branches are forbidden from committing
   `.beads/issues.jsonl` (pre-commit hook plus `scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh`), so a local
   run in a worker worktree reports a file the worker must neither edit nor commit.

3. THE EXEMPTION DOES NOT FIT THE MECHANISM. Rule (g)'s exemptions are "a PATH plus a LINE
   CONSTRUCT — never a file exemption and never a line range". The favourable structural fact is
   that JSONL puts status and content on ONE line, so `"status":"closed"` IS expressible as a
   line regex. But such a regex exempts the whole record whatever else is on it, which is a
   file-class exemption wearing a line-regex costume — and a second one is needed for the 120
   memory records, which have no status at all.

4. THE CLASS IS ONCE-EVER, AND THE STANCE SAYS SO. This is the first product rename, and the
   rename's own window clause is "BEFORE first publish". A standing whole-repo gate for a
   once-ever class is gold plating.

=== THE NARROW ALTERNATIVE, WHICH MAY BE WORTH THE FIFTEEN LINES ===

Not a gate and not in `check_retired_spellings.py`: a mayor-side census that asks `bd` rather
than the export — `bd list --limit 0 --json`, which returns NON-TERMINAL beads only, so the
closed-history exemption is free and the memory records never appear. Scan title, description and
notes for rule (g)'s retired name. No CI wiring, no exemption roster, no per-status rule, and it
cannot fire in a worker worktree because nobody runs it there.

The honest home for it, though, may not be a script at all: the failure was a RENAME RUNBOOK that
swept the tree and not the tracker. A line in the rename procedure ("sweep non-terminal beads
too, and leave closed ones alone") costs nothing and would have prevented this entirely.

=== WHAT A RULING NEEDS TO DECIDE ===

  (a) Extend rule (g) to the export? The recommendation is NO, on 1-4 above.
  (b) Add the narrow `bd`-side census? Genuinely optional; cheap, and it detects the class
      without any of 1-4.
  (c) Either way, record WHY `.beads` is subtracted from rule (g), so the next reader does not
      have to re-derive it. That much is owed by rule (g)'s own stated standard.
close_reason:

DELIBERATELY NOT GIVEN ITS OWN BEAD. Trading this bead for a smaller bead would be the same

Correct, and it worked exactly as advertised on two of three branches.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY, AND THE GAP IS THE REASSURING KIND. A LIVE WORKER'S branch also returns ZERO from that check, because a dispatch in flight has not yet written its branch name into any bead.                                                                dispatched minutes earlier, mid-flight

Section 5's own reasoning about the `+` reading applies here with the sign flipped: the damage from a wrong ORPHAN reading is not a lost branch but an act taken against live work. title: RULING: ##NaN vs NaN stringification on non-presence attributes — spec/004B contradicts itself and the repair feeds the render-tree hash
description:
FOUND 2026-09-05 by the ssrhtml-a worker while landing rf2-u82a (PR #9286). Reported and deliberately NOT fixed, because the repair touches a hash input and 004B points two ways. This bead is the ruling that needs making.

THE OBSERVATION, measured against react-dom 19.2.0. On NON-presence attribute classes, re-frame2 emits `download="##NaN"` and `title="##NaN"` where react-dom emits `="NaN"`. Both re-frame2 hosts (JVM and CLJS) agree with each other, so the `##` prefix is self-consistent rather than a platform split — it is a deliberate spelling, not a bug in one host.

WHY IT IS A RULING AND NOT A REPAIR. spec/004B contains two passages that point opposite ways:
  - one says the emitter uses "JavaScript spellings", which argues for `NaN`;
  - one says "`##NaN` is not data ... rejected at the site that recorded them", which argues the `##` form is the deliberate canonical spelling and the value should never have reached the attribute at all.
Both are in the same document. Whichever way this is ruled, one of those passages needs amending, which is itself a spec edit on a hot-zone page.

AND THE BLAST RADIUS IS WHY A WORKER SHOULD NOT DECIDE IT. The repair touches `canonical-number`, WHICH FEEDS THE RENDER-TREE HASH. A change there is not a rendering tweak: it changes hash inputs, so it can move every recorded hash in the corpus and anything pinned against them. Establish that blast radius before proposing a fix — count what pins a render-tree hash today, with a control.

THE THREE OPTIONS, as I read them:
  (a) EMIT `NaN` on these classes, matching react-dom. Smallest visible change; but if `canonical-number` is the only place to do it, it is not small underneath.
  (b) KEEP `##NaN` and amend the "JavaScript spellings" passage to name this exception. Zero code change, and defensible if the `##` form is genuinely canonical — a deliberate divergence with precedent, exactly as 004B already records for `value`.
  (c) REFUSE THE VALUE AT THE RECORDING SITE, which is what the second passage literally says should already happen. Largest change, and the only one that makes the contradiction go away rather than choosing a side of it.

RELEVANT PRECEDENT, already settled and worth not re-litigating: spec/011-SSR.md rules byte-for-byte HTML equality explicitly OUT, permitting differences in "boolean-attribute spelling". So react-dom parity is NOT in itself a reason to prefer (a) — the project has already said it is not held to byte-parity. What decided the SIBLING case (rf2-u82a, PR #9286) was not parity but the 004B class contract: an attribute being PRESENT WHEN IT MUST BE ABSENT is not a spelling difference. `##NaN` versus `NaN` on a non-presence attribute IS a spelling difference, which is the strongest single argument for (b).

STANCE BEARING: "don't litigate the minutiae" and "trust the programmer" both point at (b) — a self-consistent spelling on both hosts, in a place no consumer has complained about, is a candidate for dying with its reasoning recorded. Against that, "fail closed, fail loudly" and the second 004B passage point at (c). What is NOT defensible is leaving the two passages contradicting each other, whichever code path stands.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING: every claim above is the reporting worker's or mine. Re-read both 004B passages at tip and quote them; confirm both hosts really do agree; confirm `canonical-number` really is the shared path and really does feed the hash.

FENCE if this is dispatched after a ruling: the code half is `implementation/ssr/**`. The spec half is `spec/004B` — HOT-ZONE and single-toucher, so sequence it against whoever holds that file, and do NOT bundle the two halves into one worker unless the ruling makes them one change.
notes:
--- TRIAGE PASS 2026-09-05 19:49 AUSEST (worker rulings-a; read-only classification pass; no status change, no code, no PR) ---
BUCKET (B) — and THE PREMISE AS FILED DOES NOT HOLD. I read both 004B passages at source rather than from this description.

AT TIP aa3c616e46, spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:
  :234  "`-0.0` renders `"0"`; `NaN` and the infinities take their JavaScript spellings."
  :318-324  "And `##NaN` is not data either, because the promise is that the tree prints and reads back **equal**: `##NaN` is the one value that survives print/read while never comparing equal to itself, so a tree carrying one is not equal to itself -- and the tree is an equality input ... Both are rejected exactly as any other non-data value is, at the site that recorded them."

NEITHER PASSAGE ENDORSES `##NaN`. :234 names the JavaScript spelling, which is `NaN`. :324 says a NaN never reaches the tree at all, because it is refused where it was recorded. This description reads :318-324 as arguing "the `##` form is the deliberate canonical spelling"; the passage says the opposite — that `##NaN` is NOT DATA. So option (b) — keep `##NaN` and amend the JavaScript-spellings passage — is the ONE option no 004B sentence supports.

Nor are the two passages actually in conflict. They govern different things: :324 governs whether a NaN may be a prop at all, :234 governs how a number that IS data renders. Read that way 004B is self-consistent and the implementation is what disagrees with it, by emitting a spelling neither passage sanctions.

THE ANSWER 004B ALREADY IMPLIES is option (c): refuse the value at the recording site. And spec/011-SSR.md's byte-parity-out ruling independently removes react-dom parity as a reason for (a) — which this description already says.

DISPATCH SHAPE, not a ruling: the FIRST task of whoever takes this is the blast-radius measurement this bead already specifies — count what pins a render-tree hash today, with a control. `canonical-number` is genuinely shared: verified at tip in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/{emit,hash,html_helpers,ui_tree}.cljc, so hash.cljc confirms it feeds the hash. If that measurement comes back large, bring it BACK as a cost question — but do not choose (b) merely to avoid it, because (b) leaves 004B reading as though `##NaN` is acceptable output, which no passage says.

Owed either way: 004B must stop being readable as endorsing `##NaN`.

GATING: zero open beads at tip aa3c616e46.

--- worker hicres-a, branch worker/hicres-a, 2026-09-05 ---
RULING (c) — AND THE PREMISE AS FILED IS REFUTED AT SOURCE, WHICH ALSO
DISSOLVES THE REASON THIS WAS FILED AS A RULING.

BOTH 004B PASSAGES RE-READ AT MY BASE 79d87e4ad3, not inherited from this
description or from the triage note:
  :233-234  "`-0.0` renders `\"0\"`; `NaN` and the infinities take their
            JavaScript spellings."
  :318-324  "And `##NaN` is not data either ... Both are rejected exactly as
            any other non-data value is, at the site that recorded them."
NEITHER ENDORSES `##NaN`. `##NaN` is EDN's spelling; the JavaScript one is
`NaN`. The triage's reading holds in full, and option (b) is the one option
no 004B sentence supports. Nor are the passages in conflict: :233-234 sits
inside "Attr value normalization (in-tree, semantic space)" and governs how a
number that IS data renders; :318-324 sits inside "The opaque marker" and
governs whether a NaN may be a prop at all.

THE BLAST-RADIUS MEASUREMENT THIS BEAD ASKED FOR, TAKEN FIRST AND IT IS ZERO.
What pins a render-tree hash today: 11 `:expect "<8-hex>"` literals in
spec/conformance/fixtures/ssr-render-tree-hash.edn; 24 8-hex literals in
implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/hash_parity_fixtures.cljc; 89 across
implementation/ssr/ + spec/conformance/ + bench/hicasso/ together. NOT ONE OF
THEM CARRIES A NaN — a `NaN` search returns 0 lines on each of the five
hash-pinning artefacts (hash_parity_fixtures.cljc, ssr-render-tree-hash.edn,
ssr_hash_test.clj, hash_parity_test.clj, hash_parity_cljs_test.cljs), against
controls of 31 and 30 `hash` lines on the two fixture files, so the zero is a

title: ci: wire skills/re-frame2-improver/tests/*_test.clj into the skills-structural job
description:
PR #9232 (rf2-1lv3) added skills/re-frame2-improver/tests/storage_materializer_test.clj, a bb structural fixture pinning the canonical storage materializer in references/schemaless-events.md. It runs locally (bb tests/storage_materializer_test.clj from skills/re-frame2-improver/) and discriminates — restoring the direct .getItem js/globalThis.localStorage form fails it with 2 assertions, removing the decode catch fails it with 1 — but NOTHING RUNS IT IN CI.

Two gaps, both outside PR #9232's fence:

1. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh has NO arm for skills/re-frame2-improver/*. Measured: grep for 'improver' in that script returns nothing. Only skills/re-frame2-setup/*, skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/* and skills/reagent-migration/* have arms. So a diff confined to the improver tree classifies to zero outputs and arms no job.
2. .github/workflows/test.yml's skills-structural job has steps for re-frame2-pair, re-frame2-setup and re-frame2-pair-retro, but none for re-frame2-improver.

This is the same local-only-then-wired path both siblings took: rf2-agi57x wired re-frame2-setup, rf2-qad4l wired re-frame2-pair-retro (the latter noting PR #8848 added the test with .github/workflows/** fenced out, leaving it local-only). Follow the pair-retro step shape — loop every tests/*_test.clj so a future improver test is gated automatically rather than waiting on another wiring PR.

HOT-ZONE / SEQUENCING: .github/workflows/* and .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh are hot-zone, and the classifier arm must land in ONE commit with its mirror pin in implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs (SKILLS_STRUCTURAL_ONLY_FILES) — the mirror test pins the classifier's outputs, so splitting them lands a tree where the suite contradicts the script. Sequence against any other worker touching those files.

Acceptance: a diff confined to skills/re-frame2-improver/ arms skills_structural; the skills-structural job runs bb over skills/re-frame2-improver/tests/*_test.clj; the mirror test pins the new arm from both sides.
notes:
MAYOR SEQUENCING NOTE 2026-09-05 — THIS BEAD LANDS IN THE ONE-TOUCHER PAIR, AND THAT IS A DISPATCH CONSTRAINT, NOT A WARNING.

The filing worker named the shape correctly: wiring a new skill test into CI needs the classifier arm in `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh`, a workflow step, AND the mirror in `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs`. Both files verified present at tip.

WHY THAT MATTERS. CLAUDE.md makes that pair ONE-TOUCHER BY CONSTRUCTION, not by convention, for exactly this kind of change: the test PINS what the classifier OUTPUTS, so adding a new surface arm lands a tree where the suite contradicts the script unless both halves move in ONE commit. This bead adds an arm, so it is squarely in that case — unlike PR #8664, which touched the mirror alone to correct a stale pin against the script's UNCHANGED behaviour and merged green at 88/88.

SO THE DISPATCH RULES ARE:
  * ONE worker, ONE commit, BOTH files. Never split across two PRs and never two workers in parallel — the concurrency half of that rule is unconditional even when one of the two diffs turns out to be a single file.
  * `.github/workflows/**` is HOT ZONE, so sequence it: verify no other live worker or open PR holds a workflow file before dispatching, by ENUMERATING the files each open PR touches rather than matching branch names (a name match misled me this session).
  * **ADDING A WORKFLOW STEP MOVES THE CHECK-COUNT BAND the merge criterion uses.** The band has read 87 all session. A worker that adds a job must say so loudly in its report, and the mayor must re-measure the band on the next tick rather than carrying 87 forward — clause 5 exists precisely for this and its job-key discriminator needs the TWO LEADING SPACES form.

AND THE PRECEDENT TO FOLLOW: the filing worker records that `re-frame2-setup` and `re-frame2-pair-retro` each took the same local-only-then-wired path. Read how their arms are spelled before inventing a third spelling.

NOT URGENT. The test exists and passes locally; what is missing is CI enforcement. P3 is right.

MAYOR NOTE 2026-09-05 — THIS GAP IS WIDER THAN ONE SKILL. Two workers hit it independently within the hour, from opposite directions, which is how I know it is structural rather than incidental.

MEASURED: `test.yml`'s `skills-structural` job loops `tests/*_test.clj` for **`re-frame2-pair`, `re-frame2-setup` and `re-frame2-pair-retro` ONLY** — three of the nine skill packages under `skills/`. The other six have no CI arm at all.

THE TWO INDEPENDENT HITS:
  * The `re-frame2-improver` worker wrote a `bb` structural fixture, proved it discriminating in both directions, and then found nothing in CI runs it. That is this bead.
  * The `re-frame2` (flagship) worker could not commit its behavioural check AT ALL: that package has **no test surface whatever** — 62 files, no `tests/` directory — and adding one would need the same `.github/workflows/` edit, which was outside its fence. It ran the witness as a scratch consumer project outside the repo instead, and leaned on an already-CI-wired lint rule as the durable guard.

SO THE HONEST SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM: a worker can write a genuine, discriminating test for a skill and have no way to make CI run it without a hot-zone workflow edit — which no single-skill fence permits. The result is that skill tests get written, proven locally, and then quietly not enforced. That is the same silent-coverage-hole family as everything else this session: a check that exists and inspects nothing, reached from the CI side rather than the test side.

WIDENING THIS BEAD'S SCOPE ACCORDINGLY: rather than wiring one package, consider whether the loop should enumerate skill packages that HAVE a `tests/` directory, so a package gains enforcement by adding tests rather than by also editing a workflow. **Whether that is right is a judgement — a derived loop is harder to read than three named packages, and this project prefers explicit over clever.** Establish which the maintainers want before building it; a reasoned "keep it explicit, add the fourth name" is a perfectly good outcome.

THE ONE-TOUCHER AND BAND CONSTRAINTS IN MY EARLIER NOTE STILL APPLY UNCHANGED, and matter more if the arm becomes derived.
close_reason:

Red-then-green: with the arm removed the mirror captured exit 1 with 4 failures (3 pins plus the declaration ratchet firing the OTHER way); with it, exit 0 and 366 passed, up from 362.

TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS FROM THE WORKER, both worth keeping:
(1) THE BEAD'S OWN NOTE WARNED THIS WOULD MOVE THE CHECK-COUNT BAND. IT DOES NOT — this adds a STEP to an existing job, not a job. Verified with the two-leading-spaces job-key discriminator: 0 on this diff, 1 on the 366e4fca79 control that genuinely added a job; 71 jobs before and after. That is the discriminator being exercised in both directions rather than only where the answer is zero, which is exactly how CLAUDE.md says to use it.
(2) THE BEAD FLOATED A DERIVED LOOP over packages with a tests/ directory. The worker kept it EXPLICIT AND NAMED, on measurement: re-frame2-pair keeps its tests in tests/prompts/ and tests/runtime/, so tests/*_test.clj matches NOTHING there, and reagent-migration's tests/ is a shadow-cljs fixture run by a different job. A derived loop would have run zero tests for the package with 13 of them — the same fail-open shape this whole cluster was about, reached through a convenience refactor. Adding the fourth name explicitly is the right outcome.

title: spec(conventions): RULED A — Lifecycle-verb roster gains register-* and install-* rows and a scope sentence
description:
RULED 2026-09-06 (delegated by Mike; option A, extend and scope, with the second reviewer's corrected semantics — the ruling, both reviewers' full analyses and the pre-ruling description are in the notes). This description is the implementation brief. Single-worker spec task; the 2026-09-05 hold is lifted.

## The work, in one sentence
One spec-only edit to spec/Conventions.md §Lifecycle-verb law (hot-zone) that gives the closed roster the two setup verbs the tree already uses — `register-*` (paired with the existing `unregister-*` row) and `install-*` (its OWN row, not a pair with `destroy-*`) — narrows `attach!`/`detach!` to host-surface listeners, adds a scope sentence saying what the roster governs, fixes two stale lines in the law's own §Naming section, and clears one manifest justification. Zero runtime code, zero renames on any facade.

## The problem (measured at tip 13884f326f, 2026-09-06)
- The roster (Conventions :1265-1275) names teardown verbs (`clear-*`, `unregister-*`, `destroy-*`, `reset-*`) but never the setup half of the two that most need one: the `unregister-*` row (:1268) cites `unregister-listener!` as its exemplar while `register-*` is unrostered; the `destroy-*` row (:1269) cites `destroy-adapter!` with "lifecycle symmetry with the creating call" while the creating call, `install-adapter!`, is unrostered.
- SELF-CONTRADICTION inside one file: the ladder at :1303 says "Is it a listener add/remove? → `attach!` / `detach!`", while §Naming bucket 2 at :1328-1337 teaches `register-listener!` / `unregister-listener!` as the canonical listener shape. An author following :1303 in good faith coins the first-ever facade `attach-x!` beside ~429 files of `register-`. `attach!`/`detach!` has ZERO facade instances on any facade (spec/api-manifest.edn is the authority); its one live use is Xray's non-facade `keybinding/attach!`/`detach!` (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs:507,530), a window keydown listener — a genuine HOST-surface listener, which is the discriminator worth keeping.
- Two stale lines in the law's own bang section: :1336-1337's examples are 2-arity (`(rf/register-listener! ::audit (fn …))`, `(rf/unregister-listener! ::audit)`) where the fns take `[stream id f]` / `[stream id]` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2201,2236; spec/009 §The listener API agrees) — they cannot be pasted into working code; :1344 lists `install-adapter!, dispose-adapter!` where the public teardown has been `destroy-adapter!` since M-53 (the same file says so at :1396: "There is no `dispose-*` verb on the public surface and no alias").
- Subtraction cannot close this (verified by both reviewers): rf2-kuky.33 (closed) removed the revalidation pair; rf2-kuky.4 item (a) may delete `rf/install-adapter!` from the core facade but keeps `re-frame.substrate.adapter/install-adapter!` and touches none of Story; rf2-kuky.22 shrinks `register-listener!`'s streams but keeps the verb under all three of its options. Story's `install-canonical-vocabulary!` (tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:648, 34 non-test files) and `register-substrate!` (story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs:198) are facade exports (`:facade? true`) that no open bead touches.
- The manifest carries the deferral: spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1193 (`install-adapter!`) reads "RECORDED UNCERTAINTY (naming, not placement): install-* is not in the closed roster…".

## Exact edits (line numbers at tip 13884f326f — re-anchor by TEXT, they drift with every Conventions PR)
spec/Conventions.md — the ONLY hot-zone file in this PR:
1. Roster table (:1265-1275; 3 columns `Verb | Owns | Mechanism (the discriminator)`):
   a. Turn the `unregister-*` row (:1268) into `register-*` / `unregister-*`. Owns: add or replace, and remove, ONE callback or implementation keyed by id in a runtime hook table. Mechanism: the framework invokes the fn from arbitrary call sites; re-registering the same id REPLACES in place (reload-safe); removal is by id. ### The law, as written

`spec/Conventions.md:1259-1306` (landed `61322e9bf1`, 2026-06-01, rf2-3nbl5.4) is a **closed** verb roster for "naming lifecycle and facade APIs": `clear-*`, `unregister-*`, `destroy-*`, `reset-*`, `unsubscribe`, `watch-*`, `attach!`/`detach!`, `mount!`/`unmount!`, `open!`/`close!`, `configure!` (+ the `describe-config`/`current-config` reads). Its naming ladder routes a listener surface unambiguously:

> 5. Is it a **listener** add/remove? → `attach!` / `detach!`. (`:1303`)

and closes with the sentence this bead exists to obey:

> The roster is **closed**: a surface that fits none of these is evidence the law is missing a verb — file a bead against this section rather than coining `dispose-` / `teardown-` / `shutdown-` / a fresh `un-*`. Adding a verb is a Spec change to this table, not a per-author call. (`:1306`)

Read the roster as a shape and the gap is structural, not incidental: it names **teardown** verbs (`clear-`, `unregister-`, `destroy-`, `reset-`) and a few symmetric **pairs**, but never the **setup half** of the two teardown verbs that most need one. `unregister-*` is rostered with `unregister-listener!` as its exemplar; `register-*` is not. `destroy-*` is rostered with `destroy-adapter!` as its exemplar — "lifecycle symmetry with the creating call" — but the creating call, `install-adapter!`, is not.

### The same file, seventy lines later, says the opposite

§Naming — bang suffix (`Conventions.md:1328-1351`) is the law's own "in-depth treatment" of the `!` axis, and it names the unrostered verbs as the canonical shapes:

```markdown
### 2. Listener registrations — bang                                         ;; :1328
- `register-listener!`, `unregister-listener!` (the epoch listener is the `:epoch` stream of this verb)
- `register-observability-sink!`, `unregister-observability-sink!` (…)
(rf/register-listener! ::audit  (fn [event] ...))           ;; bang — hooks a global   ;; :1336

### 3. Adapter / platform installation — bang                                ;; :1340
- `install-adapter!`, `dispose-adapter!`                                     ;; :1344
```

So an author adding, say, a navigation hook today gets two answers from one file: the ladder at `:1303` says `attach-nav-listener!`; bucket 2 at `:1332` says `register-nav-listener!`; and the tree says `register-` by 429 files to 0. (`:1344` is also stale — `dispose-adapter!` was renamed `destroy-adapter!` under M-53, and `:1336`'s example is 2-arity where the fn takes `[stream id f]` at `core.cljc:2228`. Both are fixed by whichever option lands.)

Facade roster = `spec/api-manifest.edn` (101 `re-frame.core` rows; the manifest is the authority, not a source grep). "Non-test files" = `rg -l` over `implementation tools examples testbeds skills bench`, excluding `*.md`, `test/`, `*_test.*`, `spec.cjs`, `docs/`; it **includes** the defining and framework-internal files, so it is an upper bound on consumers. ### The gap is wider than the bead's three, and subtraction cannot close it

The law binds "lifecycle and facade APIs" across all three facades, and the same two verbs are load-bearing outside `re-frame.core`:

|---|---|---|
| `install-machine-runtime!` (`machines.cljc:446`) | re-frame.machines | 2 |
| `install-render-to-string!` (`ssr.cljc:54`) | re-frame.ssr | 2 |
| `install-canonical-vocabulary!` (`story.cljc:648`) | re-frame.story | 34 |

| `register-substrate!` (`story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs:198`) | re-frame.story | 9 |

Against that, **`attach!`/`detach!` has zero facade instances on any of the three facades** — the manifest's only `watch-`/`attach`/`detach` hit is `re-frame.story/watch-variant`. The row's sole live use is Xray's non-facade `keybinding/attach!`/`detach!` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs:507,530`, a window keydown listener — a genuine host-surface listener, which is the discriminator worth keeping). The roster names the verb nobody exports and omits the one everybody does.

This is why the recorded hold ("rule after rf2-kuky.4 and rf2-kuky.33; the question may answer itself by subtraction") has run its course. rf2-kuky.33 is closed and did subtract two cases. rf2-kuky.4 item (a) would delete the **core facade alias** `rf/install-adapter!` (0 facade-qualified non-test callers — kuky.4's figure, re-verified here) but keeps `re-frame.substrate.adapter/install-adapter!` for its 32 test files and touches none of machines/ssr/story. rf2-kuky.22 shrinks `register-listener!` to `#{:trace :epoch}` under its option A and says in its own non-goals: "rf2-uimu (the verb law has no `register-*` row) is unaffected by the stream count — referenced, not resolved here." Under every outcome of both beads, `install-*` and `register-*` remain live facade verbs with no roster row.

### Who it hurts

- **The next author** (human or agent) who follows the ladder in good faith and names a listener surface `attach-x!` — creating the first-ever facade `attach!` beside 400+ files of `register-`. Regularity is lost at the moment the law is obeyed.
- **The manifest and its readers**: `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1193` (`install-adapter!`) and `:212-219` (`load-theme`) carry "RECORDED UNCERTAINTY" that every future sweep re-reads and re-defers.
- **The spec's own credibility**: a closed roster contradicted by its sibling section seventy lines down is not closed; it is unfinished.

### The strongest counter-evidence, honestly

1. The roster's closure is the whole point — rf2-3nbl5.4 chose `attach!`/`detach!` deliberately so that "two authors adding symmetric teardown surfaces a year apart reach the same verb". Extending on demand is how closed vocabularies stop being closed. (Answer: the extension records verbs that *already* have hundreds of consumers; it is the roster catching up with the tree, not the tree pulling the roster.)
2. rf2-kuky.4's triage calls (a) "already answered by the demand bar" — so `rf/install-adapter!` may be leaving the core facade anyway, and a row written around it could look stale within weeks. (Answer: the row is written around the *verb*, exemplified by the owning ns and by machines/ssr/story, and survives (a) either way.)
3. Nothing is broken today: every row is `:action :keep`, rf2-2hpxo closed, the tag is not held. (True — this is a consistency ruling, which is why the cost of A is one file.)
4. Codex on rf2-kuky.22 argued hard that raw listeners and projected sinks are different *operations*. (Also true, and orthogonal: both use `register-`; the verb question is the same whichever door survives.)

## The decision

**Which of the following amends `spec/Conventions.md` §Lifecycle-verb law?**

- **A.** Extend the roster with `install-*`/`destroy-*` and `register-*`/`unregister-*` as named pairs, narrow `attach!`/`detach!` to host-surface listeners, and add one sentence scoping the roster to lifecycle *pairs*. Rule rf2-7nk1 in the same edit (`load-theme!`, no `load-*` row).
- **B.** Keep the roster as written and rename the survivors onto it (`register-listener!` → `attach-listener!` etc.).
- **C.** Keep the roster as written; record `install-*`/`register-*` as standing exceptions in the manifest justifications.
- **D.** Keep the hold until rf2-kuky.4 and rf2-kuky.22 land, then re-derive.

## Options

### A. Extend and scope (recommended)

**What changes.** One edit to `spec/Conventions.md` §Lifecycle-verb law (hot-zone file; sequence per below):

```markdown
| `install-*` / `destroy-*` | Seat / tear down a process-level singleton subsystem. | The target has identity and a creation moment
  (adapter, machine runtime, render fn, vocabulary); `install-*` is the creating half of the `destroy-*` row. `!` per §Naming bucket 3.
  Exemplars: `re-frame.substrate.adapter/install-adapter!` / `destroy-adapter!`, `install-machine-runtime!`, `install-render-to-string!`. |
| `register-*` / `unregister-*` | Add / remove ONE fn under an id in a framework hook table. | Listener and sink tables the framework
  invokes from arbitrary call sites (`register-listener!`, `register-observability-sink!`); the add half of the `unregister-*` row.
  `!` per §Naming bucket 2. Distinct from `reg-*` (registrar entry, no bang) and from `attach!` (host surface). |
| `attach!` / `detach!` | Add / remove a listener to a HOST surface. | window/document/host-event listeners bound outside any
  framework table (`keybinding/attach!`). If the fn lands in a framework table keyed by id, it is `register-*`. |
```

plus a scope sentence after the table: *the roster governs lifecycle pairs — create/destroy, add/remove, in/out, show/hide, config write/read. Imperative verbs that are not lifecycle pairs (`set-*!`, `validate-*!`, `render!`, `hydrate!`, `flush-*!`, `load-*!`) take their `!` from §Naming and are outside this table.* That sentence is what makes "closed" true: today `set-schema-fns!`, `set-hiccup-emitter!`, `validate-event!`, `hydrate!` and a dozen more are nominal violations that nobody has filed because everybody reads the roster as narrower than it says. ## Recommendation

**A.** The posture is elegance and regularity, and `spec/Principles.md` §Regularity over cleverness says "there is one obvious way to do a thing" — today the spec gives a listener surface two names and the tree has voted 429–0 for one of them. §The demand bar cuts the same way, in the direction the counter-evidence misses: it refuses surfaces with no named consumer, and the verb with no consumer on any facade is `attach!`, not `register-`; extending the roster records consumers that already exist by the hundreds. The law's own escape clause prescribes exactly this repair ("adding a verb is a Spec change to this table"), so A is the law working as designed, not an erosion of it. The scope sentence is the part with lasting value — it turns a roster that is "closed" only because nobody reads it literally into one that is closed because it says what it covers.
