title: skill(re-frame2-implementor): description's trigger clause fires on the out-of-scope prompts evals 17-19 grade as non-triggers; evals are trigger-only (schema 1)
description:
IMPLEMENTOR-REVIEW-7f2c-B5

CLAIM
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:11-13 (frontmatter description) — "Trigger on phrasing like "port re-frame2", "implement re-frame2 in <language>", "second re-frame2 implementation", "implementor checklist", "conformance corpus", or any prompt about building re-frame2 itself."
- SKILL.md:14-17 — "**Do not use** for: writing apps on the CLJS reference (use `re-frame2`), greenfield bootstrap (use `re-frame2-setup`), v1→v2 migration (use `re-frame-migration`), or live-app inspection (use `re-frame2-pair`)." — no out-of-scope-host clause.
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/evals/evals.json:23-25 — ids 17-19 `should_trigger: false`: "Can I implement re-frame2 in Python for a terminal UI app?", "I'm thinking of porting re-frame2 to Rust for an egui frontend. What's the implementor checklist?", "How would I build re-frame2 against a Vue or Svelte substrate instead of React?" (rationale: out of scope per spec/000-Vision.md footnote).
- evals.json:3-4 — `"schema_version": "1"`, "trigger-only fixture"; every entry carries only `should_trigger` (+ `rationale` on negatives). README.md:50 — "Trigger-accuracy fixtures for the description".

TRUTH AT TIP
- Prompts 17-19 match the description's own trigger clause literally ("implement re-frame2 in <language>", "implementor checklist", "any prompt about building re-frame2 itself"), so the description as written scores three held-out negatives wrong under the skill-creator description-optimisation loop the evals exist for (evals.json:4).
- skills/README.md §Disqualifiers (the family's single routing source) and SKILL.md:42 both state the out-of-scope behaviour: "surface the scope footnote and stop … do not start Phase 1 / Phase 2 implementation work" — a disqualifier the description does not carry.
- Sibling skills already grade outcomes for their high-drift behaviours: skills/re-frame2-xray/evals/evals.json is `schema_version "2"` with `expected_output` + `expectations[]` on positives; skills/re-frame2-improver/evals/evals.json discriminates `kind: "trigger" | "behavioural"`. This skill's two highest-drift behaviours — the out-of-scope stop, and the no-interview minimum-port default (phase-1-decisions.md:7-12) — have no eval of any kind beyond "did it fire".

IMPACT
The trigger surface contradicts three of its own fixtures, and the behaviours the dispatch brief singled out (out-of-scope refusal; in-scope Phase 1 start) are evaluated only by whether the skill loads, never by what it then does — the description could be "optimised" into firing on Python and nothing would catch a Phase 1 kickoff for a terminal UI.

FIX SHAPE (one PR)
1. Description: append one clause to the Do-not-use list — "or implementing against a non-React substrate or a non-cross-compile-to-JS host (Vue / Solid / Svelte / vanilla DOM, Python / Ruby / Rust / Go / server-side JVM) — surface the `spec/000-Vision.md` scope footnote instead of starting Phase 1". Reconcile the `notes` string in evals.json if wording changes.
2. Graduate evals.json to the family's schema-2 shape with two behavioural entries: (a) prompt 17 or 19 with `expected_output` "names the scope footnote, lists the eight in-scope hosts, does not begin Phase 1/2" and matching `expectations[]`; (b) "build a minimum re-frame2 port in TypeScript" with `expected_output` "records a port profile with every optional capability defaulted to no, asks no per-decision question, and begins Step 0 / the first slice" — copying re-frame2-xray's entry shape. Keep the 19 trigger fixtures.

GATE

Trigger accuracy itself has no repo gate — verify by hand against the 19 prompts.

ACCEPTANCE
The description's Do-not-use list names out-of-scope substrates/hosts; evals 17-19 are consistent with the description by inspection; evals.json carries at least one behavioural entry for the out-of-scope stop and one for the minimum-port Phase 1 default.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): spec/ re-authoring triad still says shims are on disk, tests are smoke-only, and names hot-reload/wait + an unemitted connect reason
description:
## CLAIM

The re-authoring scaffolding under `skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/` is labelled "exists to re-author the skill from inputs" (each file's banner). Four statements in it no longer describe the skill as shipped, and one contradicts a sibling sentence in the same file:

1. `spec/inputs.md:42` — "**Bash shims** — `skills/re-frame2-pair/scripts/*.sh`. Retired from the skill's tool surface …; **on disk only for the project's own e2e harness and ad-hoc shell use**."
2. `spec/design.md:274` (OQ3) — "`tests/` exists but **only carries connection smoke tests**."
3. `spec/design.md:105` — "the skill returns `:missing :re-frame2-tool-pair` on connect."
4. `spec/design.md:156` (L4) and `spec/authoring-prompt.md:57` (cardinal rule 4) — "the AI **must** call `hot-reload/wait` before dispatching"; `design.md:251` "Skipping `hot-reload/wait`".
5. `spec/inputs.md:26` lists `register-epoch-listener!` among `re-frame.core`'s "public single-import API"; `authoring-prompt.md:51,55` and `design.md:138` use the same name as a facade surface.

## TRUTH AT TIP

1. `git ls-files skills/re-frame2-pair/scripts skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/e2e skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/shim` returns nothing — no `scripts/` dir exists; `tests/shim/` on disk is an untracked empty `target/` leftover. The same file says so eleven paragraphs later (`inputs.md:69` §7.5: "has been **removed**"), as do `design.md:161` (OQ1 "Resolved: yes, removed"), `docs/TESTING.md:5` and `docs/initial-spec.md:15-20`. §4 is the one surviving copy of the pre-removal wording.
2. `tests/` today: `fixture/` (a shadow-cljs counter app + the `:pure-test` node-test build with 27 deftests over the shipped `pure.cljc`), `runtime/` (12 Babashka AST pins), `prompts/` (prompt_regression_test.clj, ~25 deftests). `docs/TESTING.md` §1–3 describe all three. There are no "connection smoke tests".
3. `grep -rn 're-frame2-tool-pair' tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src skills/re-frame2-pair/preload` returns nothing. The connect verdicts the server actually emits are the `discover-app` ladder in `tools/discover_app.cljs:25-26,193,207` (`:debug-disabled`, `:no-frames-registered`, `:build-not-running`, `:no-runtime-connected`, `:nrepl-unreachable`, `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing`), catalogued in `references/errors.md`.
4. There is no op named `hot-reload/wait` in `references/ops.md`; the protocol is `tail-build` with a pre-edit `baseline` (`ops.md:249-275`, post rf2-1f60u). The name is a pre-MCP placeholder the shipped catalogue never used.
5. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` has no `defn register-epoch-listener!`; the facade is the stream-parameterised `(rf/register-listener! :epoch id cb)` (`core.cljc:2158` dispatches to `rf-epoch/register-epoch-listener!` on the epoch artefact). `SKILL.md:79` and `design.md:137` (L1) already state the facade form correctly — the `register-epoch-listener!` mentions are the older name surviving beside it.

`python scripts/check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py --verbose` is green on all of this (it scans for retired tool/transport *names*, and none of these five is on its list).

## IMPACT

authoring-prompt.md is a one-shot "drop into a fresh session and it produces the skill" prompt. A re-author following it would (1) go looking for `scripts/*.sh` to keep "on disk for the e2e harness", (2) treat `tests/` as smoke-only and not know the pure-core node-test and AST pins are the behaviour + wiring gates, (3) teach a connect reason the server never emits, (4) teach an op name that does not exist instead of `tail-build` + baseline, (5) cite a facade fn that does not exist. Each is a P3 "historical claim not labelled historical" — here it is worse than initial-spec.md because these files are NOT labelled historical; they are labelled as the current re-authoring inputs.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR, three files, prose only:
- `inputs.md:42` — replace the bullet with the §7.5 wording (removed; MCP is the one implementation; live coverage in `live-e2e-fixture.cjs`), or delete it and let §7.5 stand.
- `inputs.md:26` — move `register-epoch-listener!` off the core.cljc list; name `(rf/register-listener! :epoch …)` as the facade form (matching L1 in design.md:137).
- `design.md:105` — cite the real ladder (`references/errors.md`) instead of `:missing :re-frame2-tool-pair`.
- `design.md:156,251` + `authoring-prompt.md:57` — `hot-reload/wait` → "`tail-build` with the pre-edit `baseline` (ops.md §Hot-reload coordination)".
- `design.md:274` OQ3 — restate: `tests/` carries the fixture + pure-core node-test, the AST pins and prompt regression; AI-response evals remain deferred.
- `authoring-prompt.md:51,55` — `register-epoch-listener!` → `register-listener! :epoch`.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py --verbose` (must stay green — do not reintroduce a retired name while rewording) and `bb tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` (`gated-write-tools-stay-allow-listed-in-reauthoring-docs` and `catalogue-count-matches-live-manifest` read all three spec files and `docs/initial-spec.md`). Nothing checks the corrected claims themselves — verify by hand against the cited paths and say so.

## ACCEPTANCE

title: docs(claude): mkdocs --strict does not gate in-page anchors, so check_doc_slugs.py is the only anchor gate under docs/
description:
FOUND 2026-08-22 06:1x AUSEST by the rf2-n3uw worker during its sabotage run, and RE-VERIFIED AT
SOURCE by the mayor at tip 852abfc48a before filing.

THE MEASUREMENT. A broken in-page anchor was planted mid-line in a page under docs/. Two gates
were run on it:

  python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py    -> exit 1, naming the file, the line and the anchor
  python -m mkdocs build --strict      -> exit 0

THE REASON, read out of mkdocs.yml rather than inferred. The validation block sets exactly one
key:

  validation:
    links:
      unrecognized_links: warn

There is NO `anchors` key, so anchor validation sits at the MkDocs default, and `--strict`
promotes WARNING but not INFO. The file's own comment block already documents this promotion
mechanism for the two `links` levels — it is why `unrecognized_links` was raised to `warn` under
rf2-5exqc — but it stops at links and says nothing about anchors.

THIS IS REDUNDANCY MISSING, NOT COVERAGE MISSING, and the priority reflects that. In-page anchors
under docs/ ARE gated: check_doc_slugs.py catches them, and it runs in test.yml's
verify-readme-links job on every PR, which carries no surface guard. Nothing is currently
shipping unchecked.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH RECORDING: it is a FAIL-OPEN GATE NOMINATION waiting to happen, which is the
class this project already spends words on. CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section carries a careful pin
beginning "Link validation is split across two gates, and the split does not follow the job name",
and it nominates gates by path. A reader of that passage would reasonably take `mkdocs build
--strict` to cover anchors on a page inside docs_dir — it is the strict site build over exactly
that tree. It does not, and a brief nominating it alone for an anchor change gets a green that
inspected nothing. The method's own rule is "never nominate a gate that does not cover the surface
being edited", and this is a case where the non-coverage is invisible from the gate's name, its
scope and its output.

THE REPAIR, and it is one clause in prose that already exists — do NOT add a section:
in CLAUDE.md's link-validation paragraph, say that `mkdocs build --strict` does not gate in-page
ANCHORS at all (it reports them at INFO, which --strict does not promote), so check_doc_slugs.py
is the only anchor gate for pages under docs/. Optionally note the same asymmetry beside the
existing `unrecognized_links` comment in mkdocs.yml, which is where the mechanism is already
explained.

A SECOND OPTION EXISTS AND IS NOT BEING RECOMMENDED WITHOUT A RULING: setting
`validation.anchors: warn` in mkdocs.yml would make the strict build gate anchors too. That is a
behaviour change to a shared build rather than a documentation fix, it would red the build on any
pre-existing broken anchor across the whole site, and the coverage it adds is redundant with a
gate that already runs on every PR. It should not be done as a side effect of this bead.

CLAUDE.md is a high-traffic file read by every agent every session; sequence this against anything
else editing it.

title: Story feature-parity with Storybook — build /docs/Story tutorial mirroring Storybook React tutorials + identify gaps
description:
Mike directive 2026-05-20 — defer until most existing Story P2 work lands.

**Goal**: Story should achieve feature parity with Storybook. Use the construction of a /docs/Story tutorial set (mirroring https://storybook.js.org/docs/get-started/why-storybook React-tutorial tracks; ignore Vue/Svelte/etc sections) as a forcing function to discover gaps.

**Process**:

1. **Attempt to build the tutorial set** at /docs/Story — emulating the Storybook React tutorial structure, but leveraging re-frame2's strengths (immutable app-db, frames isolation, decorator-as-data, parallel-frames, machines, etc.) and idioms (no JSX, Reagent hiccup, EDN data shapes). Don't copy Storybook's surface — translate the *learning goals* into re-frame2-native shapes.

2. **As you attempt each tutorial section**, identify gaps:
   - **Capability gaps** — Story doesn't provide a feature Storybook does. File as P2/P3 feat bead with reproduction (the tutorial section that couldn't be written cleanly).
   - **Polish gaps** — Storybook is visually more polished. Use the **frontend design Skill** (or equivalent UI/UX review) to specify what's missing: animation timing, hover states, focus rings, typography hierarchy, spacing rhythm, dark-mode contrast, microcopy. File as P3 polish beads.
   - **DX gaps** — e2e tooling experience is rough. Story has Playwright-driven recording (rf2-l6jev work), but is the dev loop tight? Hot reload? Vite-equivalent fast feedback? File as P2/P3 DX beads.
   - **Insight gaps** — what does Storybook do conceptually that Story hasn't framed? Decorators as global/story/variant overlays already covered; what about: \"Args\" (typed prop tables with controls auto-derivation — rf2-b87h2 covered this), \"Play functions\" (rf2-wfizd open), Visual regression testing (Chromatic), Composition (linking multiple stories), Test runner ergonomics, Add-ons system, MDX-style documentation pages, Theming presets.

3. **Output**:
   - **Tutorial set** at /docs/Story (the docs are themselves a deliverable — they become Story's onboarding path)
   - **Manifest doc** at ai/findings/YYYY-MM-DD-story-vs-storybook-gap-audit.md (gitignored draft, then committed as tools/story/spec/Feature-Parity-Audit.md once stable)
   - **Per-gap beads** filed: capability/polish/DX/insight (use the frontend design Skill for polish reviews)

**Sequencing**:

- Phase A — Audit pass with the frontend design Skill (read-only; produce gap manifest)
- Phase B — Operator review of manifest (Mike decides which gaps to action; some may be deliberate divergence)
- Phase C — Per-bead implementations (parallel-dispatchable across distinct gaps)
- Phase D — Tutorial set written end-to-end (gates on most P2 gaps landing)

**Deferral condition**: defer this epic until the following Story P2 beads close:
- rf2-p1ai7 (Story modal ARIA)
- rf2-u01y5 (Story controls panel accessible names)
- rf2-wfizd (decision: :play vs :play-script — likely answered by Storybook tutorial parity)
- rf2-c2770 (Template :include-story? scaffolding)

**Why defer**: doing the parity audit now means the audit's gap list is polluted by gaps that are already in-flight or queued. Better to clear the ready Story backlog first, then audit against \"what's actually missing\".

Reference: Storybook React tutorial — https://storybook.js.org/docs/get-started/why-storybook
Frontend design Skill — TBD (review what's available; rf2-4w88j HCM/axe-core may be related).

Acceptance:
- /docs/Story tutorial set exists, structured as a learning ladder from \"hello world\" through advanced patterns
- Feature-Parity-Audit.md catalogues every Storybook capability + Story's coverage status (matches / divergent-by-design / gap)
- All gap beads filed and dispositioned (action / defer / reject) by Mike
close_reason: Substantially-done. Tutorial scope delivered by rf2-0pvm3 / PR #1799 (Yegge-voice refresh of /docs/story/ · 8 chapters · tutorial best-practices applied). The remaining 'Storybook gap audit' premise was explicitly de-scoped during rf2-0pvm3 (bead body: 'Dont constantly reference Storybook'); if useful later, file as its own scoped bead.

title: facade sweep follow-up: clear-flow sits off the facade while clear-event/clear-sub/clear-fx/clear-resource/clear-mutation sit on it (asymmetry recorded by rf2-2hpxo)
description:
Observed while classifying the 103 re-frame.core facade rows for rf2-2hpxo. Recorded, NOT acted on: acting would mean ADDING a facade export, which slice 1 explicitly does not do on its own initiative.

THE ASYMMETRY. The Conventions Lifecycle-verb law makes clear-* the symmetric inverse of reg-*. On re-frame.core today:

  reg-event      + clear-event       both on the facade
  reg-sub        + clear-sub         both on the facade
  reg-fx         + clear-fx          both on the facade
  reg-resource   + clear-resource    both on the facade
  reg-mutation   + clear-mutation    both on the facade
  reg-http-interceptor + clear-http-interceptor  both on the facade
  reg-resource-scope + clear-resource-scope      both on the facade
  reg-flow       + (no clear-flow)   registrar ONLY

rf2-wad2fl (the front-porch shrink) moved clear-flow to re-frame.flows and kept reg-flow on the facade. Every other registrar/clear pair kept both halves together. So either the flows pair should be reunited (add clear-flow back to the facade as a late-bind wrapper -- the wrapper already exists in implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_flows.cljc and is simply not re-exported), or the OTHER seven pairs are the anomaly and rf2-wad2fl's reasoning should extend to them.

EVIDENCE THE FIRST READING IS RIGHT: the defwrapper for clear-flow is already written and live -- it is one of the 51 wrappers in implementation/core/src/re_frame/*.cljc -- so restoring the export is a re-export line, not new machinery. But this is pre-alpha and the surface is deliberately small, so it is Mike's call which direction to make consistent, not a worker's.

title: CLAUDE.md trap (c) quotes rollup totals of 82/83/84 from 2026-09-01; the band has been 86 all session and the figures read as current
notes:
FILED 2026-09-03 05:3x AUSEST by the mayor, from the sentinel-a report. THIS IS A METHOD-DOC DRIFT ITEM AND THE MAYOR CHECKOUT HAS A COMMIT GUARD, SO THE FIX IS WRITTEN OUT HERE RATHER THAN APPLIED.

CLAUDE.md, in the "Three mechanical traps in the merge criterion" bullet, trap (c), reads: "Measured 2026-09-01 across five PRs at once: totals of 82, 83 and 84 all occurred". A worker read that as the recorded BAND and reported that the current total of 86 is "above the 82-84 band recorded in CLAUDE.md".

STRICTLY THE DOC IS NOT WRONG: the sentence is dated, it is presented as an observation about five specific PRs mid-build, and the surrounding paragraph says explicitly that "a raw count is not comparable across PRs mid-build". So it does not ENFORCE 82-84.

BUT IT READS AS A BAND TO A CAREFUL READER, and that is the defect. The band has been 86 across every merge this session - I have re-measured it on the last five merged PRs at the top of every merge tick, more than a dozen times, and it has not moved. A reader who takes 82-84 as current will either think the trunk has grown a job it should not have, or - worse in the fail-open direction this bullet exists to prevent - will treat a genuinely short rollup as normal.

THE FIX, minimal and in the doc own voice: keep the measurement and the reasoning, and make the figures visibly historical rather than nominal. Something of the shape "Measured 2026-09-01 across five PRs at once, when the band was in the low eighties: totals of 82, 83 and 84 all occurred" - the point being that the presence of the aggregator tracked NEITHER the total NOR settledness, which is what the trap is actually about and which does not depend on the numbers at all. Then add one sentence saying the band is re-measured every merge tick and the doc figures are illustrative, never the band.

DO NOT put a current number in CLAUDE.md. That is the trap one level up: a hardcoded band in a doc is a figure that goes stale silently, which is exactly the failure this bead is reporting. The band is measured, never quoted.
close_reason: Fixed by PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9059 (worker/ciarm-a, base 0cb5c43939). One line changed in CLAUDE.md (1 insertion, 1 deletion), trap (c) only; no other bullet, heading or paragraph touched. Applied the fix as written on this bead: the measurement now reads 'Measured 2026-09-01 across five PRs at once, WHEN THE BAND WAS IN THE LOW EIGHTIES: totals of 82, 83 and 84 all occurred ...', and one sentence follows it -- 'Those totals are a dated illustration, never the band: the band moves as jobs land, so it is re-measured at the top of every merge tick from the PRs actually in front of you, and no figure quoted in this file is the thing to compare a rollup against.' The measurement and the reasoning are kept intact, because the trap is that the aggregator's presence tracked NEITHER the total NOR settledness, which does not depend on the numbers. NO CURRENT NUMBER WAS PUT IN THE FILE, per this bead's own instruction -- a hardcoded band would be the same trap one level up. (Incidentally corroborating the bead's premise without recording it in the doc: PR #9057's rollup read 86 checks while this work was in flight.) Verified: file encoding and CRLF line endings unchanged, line count unchanged, exactly one line in the diff. check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0 -- and that gate is the surface for repo-root markdown, confirmed at source in its own docstring (rf2-znup0), not check_doc_slugs.py. Its green is silent, so it was exercised rather than trusted: a broken relative target plus a broken in-page anchor planted in CLAUDE.md gave exit 1 naming CLAUDE.md:141 and both faults, the restore was verified by git blob-hash equality, and the gate returned to exit 0. check_doc_slugs.py 0 as well. PR open, not yet merged.

title: scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py skips every ../ link, so an in-package reference to unshipped spec/ is invisible (improver references/README.md links ../spec/design.md)
description:
CLAIM. scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py ~L171-175 skips links beginning with ../. skills/re-frame2-improver/references/README.md links ../spec/design.md, which package.json files[] does not ship, with no monorepo-only marker (rf2-lzsrd item 3 on the skill side).
IMPACT. The gate's green says every intra-package link resolves; a shipped file pointing at an unshipped one passes.
FIX SHAPE. Resolve ../ links relative to the package root and apply the same shipped/unshipped test; keep the existing allow-list mechanism for deliberate monorepo-only pointers. Small; not a new gate.
GATE. the script's own --self-test.
Surfaced by the 2026-09-02 independent skills review (15 reviewers, tip 72df4dd915); routed out of the reviewing skill's scope. Re-verify line numbers at dispatch. Filed 2026-09-02 12:16:50 AUSEST. Reported by the improver reviewer.
acceptance_criteria: A ../ link from a shipped file to an unshipped path fails the gate unless carried with the monorepo-only marker; the improver case is either fixed or marked
close_reason:
Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9038.

PREMISE CONFIRMED AT SOURCE. _broken_package_links carried 'if target.startswith("../"): continue' at the line numbers this bead cites, with a docstring rationale that ../ links escape the package and belong to check_doc_slugs.py. The rationale is what fails: a ../ from a NESTED doc usually lands back INSIDE the package. references/README.md -> ../spec/design.md resolves to <package>/spec/design.md, which package.json files[] does not ship - an intra-package link that escaped the check purely on spelling.

FIX. Scope is now decided by where a link RESOLVES, never by how it is spelled. The two-line spelling skip is gone; the pre-existing 'resolves outside the package' branch keeps genuinely-escaping links out of scope, unchanged and for the reason the docstring already gave. This is the fix shape this bead specifies - resolve, then apply the same shipped/unshipped test, keeping the allow-list marker mechanism.

MEASURED across all nine published skills, every ../-shaped link: 398 resolve outside the package root (out of scope, unchanged), 52 resolve inside and are shipped (now checked, pass), 3 resolve inside at an unshipped path (now checked). 55 links moved from unexamined to examined; the tree stays green.

THE IMPROVER CASE IS ALREADY MARKED, which this bead's acceptance allows ('either fixed or marked'). All three ../spec/design.md links in references/README.md sit on lines reading 'not shipped in the package' / 'reach it from a monorepo clone' - existing entries in _MONOREPO_ONLY_MARKERS. The defect was that the gate never got far enough to consult the marker, not that the marker was missing. spec/design.md does exist and is genuinely absent from files[], as reported.

NOT AN EXISTENCE CHECKER, and now pinned as such. New self-test case ok_shipped_but_absent_is_not_our_question links ../docs/NEVER-CREATED.md where docs/ IS in files[]: the target does not exist and the gate stays green. Allow-list membership is the packaging question this gate owns; existence stays check_doc_slugs.py's. No filesystem existence test was added - Path.resolve() is non-strict.

GATE. --self-test exit 0, 11/11, four new cases. Proven to discriminate: re-inserting the old skip into a scratch copy fails bad_parent_reentry_unshipped (expected 1, got 0), exit 1. Live scan exit 0 over 9 packages.

FINDING RETURNED, NOT ACTIONED: the 398 outside-the-package links are real breakage in the published tarballs - each skill ships as its own npm package and plugin, so no sibling resolves. Deliberate documented behaviour, far larger than this bead, and a ruling rather than a worker's call. Filed as rf2-nvbz.

title: skill(reagent-migration): leaf size — catalog-judgment.md is 450 L / 25 KB (1.8x the ceiling) and fails the catalogue test; MIG-23's 110-line SSR recipe is a severable references/ssr-hydrate.md
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/README.md` §Leaf size discipline: "each leaf file SHOULD be <=250 lines AND <=16 KB (target ~150 lines / ~10 KB)"; catalogue-shaped leaves may exceed only if "splitting would multiply file-handle overhead without reducing tokens-per-session. Test: would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?"

Measured at tip (`wc -l` / `wc -c`):

| leaf | lines | bytes | vs ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `references/catalog-judgment.md` | 450 | 25,115 | 1.8x / 1.6x |
| `references/catalog-mechanical.md` | 356 | 16,221 | 1.4x / at ceiling |
| `references/procedure.md` | 230 | 12,082 | under |
| `references/gotchas.md` | 209 | 10,217 | under |
| `references/mental-model.md` | 183 | 9,252 | under |
| `references/catalog-reject.md` | 147 | 7,469 | under |

## TRUTH AT TIP

The catalogue test FAILS for the judgment leaf. MIG-23 SSR-then-hydrate (`catalog-judgment.md:327-435`, ~110 lines, ~6.5 KB: the decision, the cold two-process boot condition, the server code block, the client code block, the `:identifier-prefix` contract, the out-of-scope list) is a self-contained recipe that a client-only SPA migration — the common case; the reporter census has no SSR class — never needs, yet every D-tier load carries it. Splitting it out reduces tokens per common session by construction.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, skill files only)

1. Move MIG-23's body to `references/ssr-hydrate.md` (one level deep: routed from `SKILL.md`'s D-tier bullet and from MIG-15's SSR pointer at `catalog-mechanical.md:278-281`). Keep a 3-line MIG-23 stub in the catalogue (the decision sentence + the pointer) so the D-tier roster stays complete.
2. `spec/design.md:172-198` §4 locks "six reference leaves" — amend to seven in the same PR (nothing else in the folder forbids a new leaf; `inputs.md` §7 and `authoring-prompt.md` already say a surface move re-checks the leaves).
3. `tests/fixture/README.md:3-5` and `.github/workflows/test.yml:5868` cite MIG-23 "in `catalog-judgment.md`" — retarget the pointer.
4. `catalog-mechanical.md`: leave it. At the byte ceiling exactly and 1.4x lines, and every M-rule is loaded in every session; splitting would not reduce tokens. A light trim of MIG-11's prose (158-197) is optional.

Result: `catalog-judgment.md` ~340 L / ~18.5 KB; still over the line ceiling but now passing the catalogue test (the remaining rows are all loaded by any D-tier session). No SKILL -> A -> B chain is introduced.

## GATE

`wc -l` / `wc -c` on the leaves; `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`; `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --ci` (the new leaf lives under `references/`, which `package.json` `files[]` already ships, so no packaging edit).

## ACCEPTANCE

MIG-23 lives in `references/ssr-hydrate.md`, reachable one level from `SKILL.md`; `catalog-judgment.md` under 20 KB with a MIG-23 stub; `design.md` §4 says seven leaves; the fixture README and test.yml comment point at the new leaf; gates exit 0.

Reviewed at tip 72df4dd915 (HEAD d12181c4c3; no relevant diff) on 2026-09-02 12:00:31 AUSEST.
acceptance_criteria: MIG-23 body lives in references/ssr-hydrate.md one level from SKILL.md with a 3-line stub left in the catalogue; catalog-judgment.md under 20 KB; design.md §4 says seven leaves; fixture README + test.yml comment retargeted; doc_slugs + package_refs --ci exit 0

MIG-23's body moved to references/ssr-hydrate.md (117 L / 6,138 B), routed DIRECTLY from SKILL.md so no SKILL->A->B chain appears; an eight-line stub keeps the D-tier roster complete. Retargeted: MIG-15's SSR pointer, procedure.md's D-hit list, tests/fixture/README.md, README.md's tree, spec/design.md section 4 (now seven leaves, with the reason recorded) and spec/authoring-prompt.md. package.json ships references/ wholesale so no packaging edit was needed, as predicted. Re-measured rather than trusting the bead: catalog-judgment.md 450 L / 24,665 B at the merge base, 471 L after the two content commits, 370 L / 20,944 B final (git-object bytes). Still over the LINE ceiling and kept that way deliberately — every remaining row loads in any D-tier session, which is what the catalogue test asks. catalog-mechanical.md left alone on the same reasoning (392 L / 17,804 B). Also caught and fixed a violation this PR would otherwise have created: the content commits pushed gotchas.md to 264 L, trimmed back to exactly 250. ## The decision in one sentence

Whether the RealWorld-on-Resources flagship keeps what PR #10152 landed — a logged-out visit to `/?feed=following` renders an honest "nothing on this page was ever requested" panel with two recovery links — or ADDITIONALLY (B) replace-navigates to Global Feed when a saved token is rejected at boot, or (C) puts the following feed behind the library's `:can-enter` auth guard so the existing login / `:return-to` recipe handles it.

## The problem, carefully

**What is true today (trunk `155ff6871c`, every cite re-read there).** The following feed is not a route; it is a query ARM of the public home route. `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/routing.cljs:111-125` registers `:realworld/home` at `/` with `:query [:map [:feed {:optional true} :string] [:page {:optional true} :int]]` and no `:can-enter`. Its third route resource is the feed entry:

```clojure
;; routing.cljs:103-109
{:resource  :realworld/feed
 :when      (fn [route _ctx] (= "following" (get-in route [:query :feed])))
 :params    (fn [route] {:page (or (get-in route [:query :page]) 1)})
 :blocking? false
 :keep-previous? true}
```

It carries no `:scope`, so it inherits the registration's `:scope {:from-db :realworld/session}` (`resources.cljs:282-293`, the key at `:293`), and that resolver returns nil whenever nobody is signed in (`scope.cljs:136-144`). The library resolves scope at PLAN time and a nil `{:from-db …}` throws `:rf.error/resource-scope-unresolved-reference`, fail-closed, "never permission to read global" (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc:770-782`); the planner catches it and commits a failed activation — "empty next ownership, no ensures, prior owner released" (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:1134-1160`; spec `spec/016-Resources.md:1369`, and `:101-107` for the no-global-fallthrough rule). So on that arm the articles and tags reads are never ensured either: a plan is atomic.

**What #10152 landed (the floor).** `home-page` subscribes to `:rf.route/error` (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:422-425`), gates on `:rf.error/id = :rf.error/resource-route-plan` (`views.cljs:445-446`) and, only then, renders `home-plan-error` in place of the feed column and the tag sidebar (`views.cljs:463-469`; the panel at `:386-405`). The panel's two links are ordinary navigations: "Switch to Global Feed" dispatches `:home/show-global-feed` → `[:rf.route/navigate {:to :realworld/home :query {}}]` (`views.cljs:63-64`, `:399-401`); "sign in" is `[rf/route-link {:to :realworld.auth/login}]` (`:403`). The README states the exception at `README.md:166`, including that a cold bookmark with no token lands in the identical place.

**What the source bead held for Mike** (rf2-fn0kx.9 close reason, §HELD FOR MIKE — TWO, item 1): "Whether to ADDITIONALLY navigate away on `:abandon-restore`, plus the report's L-sized `:requires-auth`-route option. The floor (A) has landed; these are enhancements above it." The handler in question:

```clojure

:abandon-restore
(fn [_]
```

## Make it tangible

The sequence: a signed-in reader clicks "Your Feed" (URL becomes `/?feed=following`, `views.cljs:66-67`; under the base-path strategy at `routing.cljs:366-367` that is `/realworld-resources/?feed=following` on a prefixed host, `/?feed=following` under `npm run dev:example`, which serves at root — the prefix question is rf2-67vjf's, not this bead's), then presses F5.

**Today, after #10152 (option A):**

1. Boot runs `:initial-events [[:auth/classify-token] [:auth/initialise] [:app/initialise]]` and the frame's first URL→route sync (`core.cljs:406-416`). The token is in app-db, the user is not; `:realworld/viewer` returns nil while a token is present with no username (`scope.cljs:115-119`), so the FIRST plan already fails closed at the articles entry. The shell shows its "restoring session" state (README `:167`).
2. `GET /user` is refused → `:auth/restore-failed` → `:abandon-restore`: user and token cleared, replan under the anonymous viewer. Articles and tags would now resolve `[:rf.scope/viewer :anonymous]`, but the feed's `:when` admits the arm and the session resolver still returns nil, so the REPLAN fails closed too — "a COMMITTED FAILED REPLAN … no partial ensures" (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/replan.cljc:50-58`).
3. Render. URL unchanged: `/?feed=following`. Below the banner, one panel: *"Nothing on this page was ever requested, so there is nothing to show. This is not an empty feed. Your Feed is private to a signed-in reader. Switch to Global Feed or sign in."* followed by the framework's own `:reason` string. No tabs, no tag sidebar (`views.cljs:463-469`).
4. Click "Switch to Global Feed" → navigate `{:to :realworld/home :query {}}` → URL `/` (a push), the plan forms, articles + tags load; the feed is gated out by its `:when`.
5. Click "sign in" instead → `/login`. After a successful login `:auth/post-login-redirect` reads `[:auth :return-to]`, finds NOTHING — the only writer of that slot is the `:rf.route/entry-denied` handler (`routing.cljs:335-346`) and home has no guard — and navigates `{:to :realworld/home}` (`auth.cljs:306-324`): the reader lands on Global Feed at `/` and clicks "Your Feed" once more. Small friction, worth knowing; not a defect.
6. Back after step 4 returns to `/?feed=following`, still logged out → the same panel. Consistent.

Door 2 (cold bookmark, no token): step 1 enters with the viewer already `[:rf.scope/viewer :anonymous]` (blank token), the articles entry would resolve — and the feed entry throws, failing the whole plan atomically (spec 016 `:1369`). Same panel, reached from route entry directly; no restore ever runs.

**Under B — replace-navigate on `:abandon-restore` when the current route carries `?feed=following`:** step 2 dispatches `[:rf.route/navigate {:to :realworld/home :query {} :replace? true}]` in place of the replan; URL becomes `/`, Global Feed renders, the panel is never seen, the feed URL is not on the back stack. Door 2 is UNCHANGED — the handler never runs — so the same URL yields the panel for a reader with no token and a bounce for a reader with a stale one. A machine action receives `{:keys [data event state meta] cofx :rf.cofx}` (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:461`) and cannot read the route slice, so B is a small ordinary event that reads `[:rf.runtime/routing :current :query :feed]` off `:rf.db/runtime` — the exact shape `:home/go-to-page` already uses (`views.cljs:80-84`) — and either navigates or replans; `:abandon-restore` dispatches it instead of the bare replan. Roughly 15 lines, plus rewording the STAY-PUT comment (`auth.cljs:434-448`) and README `:166`, which currently argue the opposite of what B does.

**Under C — put the following feed behind the auth guard.** The library facility is already there and the app already uses it on three routes; nothing is hand-rolled:

- `:can-enter` is an accepted route-metadata key (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:168`; spec `spec/012-Routing.md:292`).
- The guard sub receives the RESOLVED TARGET appended as an argument — `[<guard-id> {:route-id :params :query :fragment :url}]` — precisely "so `:can-enter` can branch on WHERE the user is heading" (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/decisions.cljc:79-93`). The guard runs on every door that is not an exact no-op, initial load included (`decisions.cljc:28-31`; spec 012 `:1706`).
- Denial is TERMINAL: nothing commits, `:rf.route/entry-denied` fires once with the replayable `:destination` (`decisions.cljc:319-347`; spec 012 `:1639-1650`); the recipe is spelled at spec 012 `:1741-1762` and `docs/routing/how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md:65-77`.
- This app's handler already implements it, restore-aware: stash the destination, replace-navigate to login unless a restore is in flight, in which case stay put (`routing.cljs:335-346`); `:auth/settle-deferred-entry` resolves the stash once restore settles either way (`auth.cljs:346-374`); `:auth/post-login-redirect` returns to it wholesale (`auth.cljs:306-324`).
- There is no cheaper library spelling: a declarative `:redirect-to` key is recorded as post-v1 and deferred (spec 012 `:2027-2031`).

The report's spelling of C is a NEW route (`/feed`, `:tags #{:requires-auth}`, its own `:resources`); it retargets `:home/show-your-feed`, changes `your-feed?` from a query read (`views.cljs:94`) to a route read, branches `home-page`, and abandons the URL the code calls "the official-contract token" (`routing.cljs:112-114`, `views.cljs:51-54`) and that the HTTP twin shares (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/tags.cljs:225-226`, `:295`). L-sized, as the report said.

**C′ (mine — the cheap spelling of C, offered so C is priced against the API rather than against a new route).** Keep the URL; guard the ARM. Because the guard sub sees the target's `:query`, `:realworld/home` can carry:

```clojure
;; routing.cljs — ~8 lines
(rf/reg-sub :realworld-resources.routing/home-arm-ok?
  {:inputs [[:auth/user]]}
  (fn [[user] [_ target]]
    (or (not= "following" (get-in target [:query :feed]))
        (some? user))))
;; and on :realworld/home:   :can-enter [:realworld-resources.routing/home-arm-ok?]
```

Walk under C′, door 1: initial entry to `/?feed=following` is DENIED (user nil while the token is unresolved) → the handler stashes `{:to :realworld/home :query {:feed "following"}}` and DEFERS (`restoring-session?`) → restore fails → `:abandon-restore` → `:auth/settle-deferred-entry`'s `:else` arm replace-navigates to `/login`, stash kept → sign in → `:auth/post-login-redirect` returns to `/?feed=following`, whose plan now forms. Door 2: denied at once, `/login`, sign in, feed. Step 5's friction disappears for free. What it costs: the plan-error panel's recovery branch (`views.cljs:396-404`) becomes unreachable in the demo (keep it — it is still the honest render for a genuinely broken plan); the routing docstrings that say a nil session on that arm "is a whole-plan planning error, by design" (`routing.cljs:30-35`, `:92-102`) and README `:166` are reworded; and the example no longer shows a reader the fail-closed scope failing — it shows a login bounce.

## Options

### A. Keep the landed behaviour; record the ruling (the bead's "retain", recommended)
- What changes: nothing in the tree. The ruling is the close reason.
- Consequences: the reader on `/?feed=following` without a session sees the honest panel and two ordinary navigations; the URL is preserved (bookmark, Back, share all behave); the example keeps its live demonstration of "idle ≠ empty", of fail-closed scope as a planning error, and of `:when`. Known friction: "sign in" from the panel lands on Global Feed, not the feed (step 5). If Mike wants that closed without a guard, it is a five-line stash — an `:on-click` event writing `[:auth :return-to] {:to :realworld/home :query {:feed "following"}}` before navigating to login, reusing `:auth/post-login-redirect` unchanged — but it is hand-rolled state for a one-click cost and I would not spend it.
- Cost: zero worker time. No files. No spec sentences.
- Risk: none. The panel has not been seen in a browser (PR body); the merged-PR audit note records an isolated Babashka evaluation of the source forms passing (no count given), and the Codex section carried below reports its own probe at 22 checks, exit 0.

### B. Additionally replace-navigate to Global Feed on `:abandon-restore` when the route is the feed arm
- What changes: one new ordinary event reading the routing slice and branching navigate-vs-replan; `:abandon-restore` dispatches it; the STAY-PUT comment at `auth.cljs:434-448` and README `:166` rewritten.
- Consequences: door 1 readers never see the panel and lose the feed URL from history; door 2 readers still see the panel (B cannot reach them), so one URL now has two behaviours depending on whether a token was present at boot, and the action documented as "stay put so a public deep link remains readable" (`auth.cljs:434-438`) acquires an exception in the same handler. Nothing changes for the AI or the library; the example teaches a slightly muddier lesson.
- Cost: ~0.25 worker-morning; 2 files (`auth.cljs`, `README.md`), no hot-zone. No spec sentences.
- Risk: low mechanically; medium pedagogically — the panel still ships for door 2, so B buys no simplification, only an asymmetry.

### C. Give the following feed its own authenticated route (the report's L-sized option)
- What changes: `reg-route :realworld/feed` at a new path with `:can-enter [:realworld-resources.routing/authed?]` and the feed entry as its `:resources`; `:home/show-your-feed`, `your-feed?`, `home-page` and the README retargeted; the `:when` demonstration moves or is lost; docs that cite the example's route shape are swept (the reviewer counted 67 files naming the example under `docs/`, `spec/`, `skills/`; at least `docs/routing/examples.md`, `docs/resources/examples.md`, `skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md:52-62` describe the current design).
- Consequences: a logged-out reader is bounced to login and returned to the feed after sign-in — the standard protected-page UX, handled entirely by the guard + `:return-to` recipe already in the app. The Conduit URL `/?feed=following` is abandoned or redirected, diverging from the HTTP twin. The feed stops being the corpus's `:when` example.
- Cost: ~1 worker-morning; 4-6 example files plus a docs sweep; no hot-zone. Spec: none (the pattern is spec 012 `:1741-1762` as written).
- Risk: medium — URL contract divergence between twins; loses two teaching moments; docs drift if the sweep is incomplete.

### C′. Guard the ARM on the existing home route (mine; the cheap spelling of C)
- What changes: the ~8-line guard sub above plus `:can-enter` on `:realworld/home`; docstrings at `routing.cljs:30-35`, `:92-102` and README `:166` reworded; the panel's recovery branch left in place.
- Consequences: same UX as C (bounce, return after sign-in, step-5 friction gone) with the URL and the HTTP twin untouched, and no new route. A reader sees `:can-enter` on a PUBLIC route and must read the sub to learn it is per-arm — a small, real oddity. The fail-closed-scope failure becomes unreachable in the demo, so the example stops SHOWING the thing its README `:166` and `:118` explain.
- Cost: ~0.5 worker-morning; 2-3 files, no hot-zone. No spec sentences.
- Risk: low mechanically (every piece is an existing library contract and an existing app handler); the cost is pedagogical.

## Recommendation
DOSSIER (continued, part 2 of 2 - same canonical record, verbatim)

**A.** Argued from the stance, second half included: the floor is landed and honest — a reader on a private feed's URL with no session is told exactly what happened and handed two ordinary navigations, and the URL they typed is preserved. That is not a defect to litigate. B spends a morning-quarter to give one of three doors a different answer from the other two and to contradict the handler's own documented design. C and C′ are clean uses of an API the app already exercises on three routes, and C′ in particular is cheap — but both replace the example's one live demonstration of fail-closed scope, of "idle ≠ empty", and of `:when` deciding whether a read is planned at all, with a login bounce the settings and editor routes already demonstrate. The flagship's job is to show those distinctions; trading them for a smoother edge case on the demo backend's deliberately-always-rejected restore is gold plating.

What would change my mind: (1) if Mike wants the flagship to TEACH per-arm guarding — a query arm of a public route needing a session is a real shape and C′ is its eight-line spelling; then C′, not C, and the README gains a paragraph rather than losing one. (2) A real-backend deployment where expired tokens are the common case and the panel is judged too "error-y" for the landing page; then C′ again rather than B, because it closes the step-5 friction for free and keeps one behaviour per URL.

The example already demonstrates the important distinction between an unavailable private resource and an empty collection. THE QUESTION. rf2-fn0kx.9's close reason (§HELD FOR MIKE — TWO, item 1) held whether the RealWorld-on-Resources flagship should ADDITIONALLY navigate away on `:abandon-restore`, or give the following feed its own authenticated route, above the floor PR #10152 landed (merged 2026-09-21T18:56:38Z at 839a4fb2c5; 6 files, all under examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/).

THE FLOOR, AND WHY IT IS SUFFICIENT. The following feed is not a route; it is the `?feed=following` query ARM of the public home route (`:realworld/home` at `/`, no `:can-enter`, routing.cljs:111-125). Its route resource `:realworld/feed` (routing.cljs:103-109, `:when` on the query) inherits `:scope {:from-db :realworld/session}` (resources.cljs:293), whose resolver returns nil with no signed-in username (scope.cljs:136-144); a nil `{:from-db …}` scope is `:rf.error/resource-scope-unresolved-reference`, fail-closed and never a global read (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc:770-782; spec/016-Resources.md:101-107, :1369), and the planner commits a FAILED activation with no ensures — a plan is atomic, so the articles and tags reads are never requested either (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:1134-1160). PR #10152 made `home-page` gate on `:rf.error/id = :rf.error/resource-route-plan` (views.cljs:445-446) and render `home-plan-error` (views.cljs:386-405) in place of the feed column and tag sidebar (views.cljs:463-469): "Nothing on this page was ever requested, so there is nothing to show. This is not an empty feed.", the framework's own `:reason`, and two ORDINARY navigations — "Switch to Global Feed" dispatches `[:rf.route/navigate {:to :realworld/home :query {}}]` (views.cljs:63-64; the feed's `:when` then gates it out and the plan forms) and "sign in" is `[rf/route-link {:to :realworld.auth/login}]` (views.cljs:403). The URL `/?feed=following` is preserved, so bookmark, Back and share all behave, and README.md:166 states the exception. That is honest, and it is the example's one live demonstration of fail-closed scope as a planning error, of "idle is not empty", and of `:when` deciding whether a read is planned at all (routing.cljs:206-207: "The real `:when` demonstration is the home route's feed entry"). Nothing in implementation/ is involved under any option; examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm) and compile-swept.

THE THREE DOORS INTO THAT PAGE, AND WHICH ONES `:abandon-restore` REACHES. (1) F5 on `/?feed=following` with a saved JWT the server rejects — the shipped demo backend rejects `GET /user` on every cold boot by design (examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:408-416), so every reader of the demo meets this door; `:abandon-restore` RUNS (auth.cljs:432-453): clears user and token, persists nil, replans under the anonymous viewer, settles any deferred entry — and the REPLAN fails closed too, because the arm's `:when` still admits the feed and the session resolver still returns nil (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/replan.cljc:50-58: a committed failed replan, no partial ensures). (2) A cold bookmark with NO token — `:auth/initialise` dispatches `[:auth/flow [:auth/restore false]]` (auth.cljs:570-584), the `:has-token?` guard (auth.cljs:409) routes it to the no-op `{:target :idle}` arm (auth.cljs:475-476), so neither `:abandon-restore` nor `:auth/clear-session` ever runs; the plain route entry fails the plan and lands on the same panel by the same route. (3) An expired JWT against a real backend — identical to door 1. So `:abandon-restore` reaches doors 1 and 3 only; door 2 is unreachable by it, which is why the reviewer's original "B instead of A" was never a live choice and why B cannot replace the fallback. Interactive logout from the feed already goes home: `:clear-session` navigates `{:to :realworld/home}` (auth.cljs:461-470) and a `:to` destination takes `:query` literally as `{}` (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/navigate.cljc:329-334) — nothing to add there.

WHY NOT B (additionally replace-navigate to Global Feed on `:abandon-restore` when the route is the feed arm; ~0.25 worker-morning, auth.cljs + README.md). A machine action cannot read the route slice (spec/005-StateMachines.md:461), so B is a small ordinary event reading `[:rf.runtime/routing :current :query :feed]` off `:rf.db/runtime` and branching navigate-vs-replan — mechanically easy. But it reaches only doors 1 and 3, so one URL gets two behaviours depending on whether a token was present at boot (a bounce for a stale token, the panel for no token), the panel still ships, and the handler's own documented STAY-PUT design (auth.cljs:434-448: a cold-boot deep link should remain readable, "not get yanked home") acquires an exception in the same handler. B buys no simplification, only an asymmetry and a muddier lesson.

WHY NOT C (a new authenticated `/feed` route with `:tags #{:requires-auth}`, L, ~1 worker-morning plus a docs sweep — 67 files under docs/, spec/, skills/ name the example) or C-PRIME (the dossier's cheap spelling: a ~8-line `:can-enter` sub on `:realworld/home` that reads the guard target's `:query` and denies the following arm when `[:auth/user]` is nil; ~0.5 morning). Both are clean uses of a library contract the app already exercises on three routes — `:can-enter` receives the resolved target (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/decisions.cljc:79-93), denial is terminal and fires `:rf.route/entry-denied` with a replayable `:destination` (decisions.cljc:319-347; spec/012-Routing.md:1639-1650, :1741-1762), and this app's handler is already restore-aware (routing.cljs:335-346, auth.cljs:346-374, :306-324) — and C-prime would close the sign-in friction below for free and keep the URL and the HTTP twin untouched. But both replace the flagship's only live demonstration of fail-closed scope / "idle is not empty" / `:when` with a login bounce the settings and editor routes already demonstrate, C additionally abandons the Conduit URL `/?feed=following` that the HTTP twin shares (examples/real-apps/realworld_http/tags.cljs:225-226, :295) and moves or loses the corpus's `:when` example, and there is no cheaper library spelling (a declarative `:redirect-to` is post-v1 and deferred, spec/012-Routing.md:2027-2031). Trading those teaching moments for a smoother edge case on a restore the demo backend rejects on purpose is gold plating.

ACCEPTED BEHAVIOUR, STATED SO NOBODY REFILES IT. Clicking "sign in" from the panel lands the reader on Global Feed at `/` after login, NOT on Your Feed: `:auth/post-login-redirect` reads `[:auth :return-to]`, whose only writer is the `:rf.route/entry-denied` handler (routing.cljs:335-346), and home has no guard, so the slot is empty and the handler navigates `{:to :realworld/home}` (auth.cljs:306-324). The reader clicks "Your Feed" once more. Both reviewers priced this as a small ergonomic cost, not a defect; it is ACCEPTED. If it is ever wanted closed without a guard, it is a ~5-line stash — an `:on-click` event writing `[:auth :return-to] {:to :realworld/home :query {:feed "following"}}` before navigating to login, reusing `:auth/post-login-redirect` unchanged — hand-rolled state for a one-click cost, and not spent. Back after "Switch to Global Feed" returns to `/?feed=following` logged out and shows the same panel; consistent. README.md:166 ("switching to Global Feed, or signing in, replans cleanly") is true as written, so no docs bead is created.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION. Satisfied by A as-is: the cold-bookmark fallback (door 2) and public deep links (the article route stays public, routing.cljs:189-210) are untouched because nothing changes.

LIMITS OF THE EVIDENCE. Nobody has mounted `home-plan-error` in a browser: the PR body says so, and both the merged-PR audit and Codex's probe are isolated Babashka evaluations of the unmodified source forms (Codex: 22 checks, exit 0, controls both ways — following versus global/other queries, anonymous versus signed-in scope resolution, planning versus blocking errors, guard stash present versus absent; the planning branch omitted the article list and tags spinner while its panel carried both links, and the Global Feed handler produced a navigation with an empty query). The walk above is reasoned from the code. Recovery-link usability and browser-history behaviour remain the experiential uncertainties; neither is a reason to spend a worker on an example that is honest by inspection.

WHAT CHANGES THIS: (1) Mike wanting the flagship to TEACH per-arm guarding of a public route's query arm — then C-prime, never C, and README.md:166 gains a paragraph rather than losing one; (2) a real-backend deployment where expired tokens are the common case and the panel is judged too error-like for the landing page — then C-prime again rather than B, because it closes the sign-in friction for free and keeps one behaviour per URL.

title: method: §5's repeated-disposition bullet closes the truth half and leaves the cost half open — verifying a standing list is what licenses re-emitting it
description:
loops.md §5's "disposition reported more than once" bullet closes the TRUTH half and leaves the COST half open — re-deriving a standing list faithfully is what licenses re-emitting it, and the operator pays.

## The instance, 2026-09-22

The mayor closed seven or eight consecutive loop reports with a verbatim "Standing" block naming the
same eleven operator-owned items. Mike interrupted with "You have already reported that bug, I think."

Then the §5 bullet was applied exactly as written — **re-run the test rather than re-reading your own
report** — and the list came back **clean**: all eleven still open, `rf2-fn0kx.6` correctly `in_progress`
as the item behind the held PR #10184. Nothing was stale. The disposition was TRUE on every tick it was
reported.

## Why that is a gap rather than a success

The existing bullet (landed by rf2-prwqz, PR #9918) is aimed at a coordinator whose repeated conclusion
has gone WRONG, and its remedy is verification. That remedy is correct and it fired correctly here.

But it is silent on the case where verification PASSES. Re-deriving the list is precisely what makes a
coordinator confident enough to restate it, so the bullet's remedy, applied diligently, can INCREASE the
repetition it does not measure. The failure is not a wrong fact; it is a right fact delivered for the
eighth time to a reader who acted on it the first time or has deliberately not.

**The two failures need opposite corrections and share a trigger**, which is why one bullet covering
both is worth having: a carried disposition must be re-derived and then usually NOT re-emitted. Today
the method says the first half and stops, and "I checked it and it is still true" reads as a positive
reason to say it again.

## Suggested shape, for whoever takes it

A clause on the existing bullet rather than a new one — it is the same trigger and the same paragraph.
Roughly: *re-deriving a standing disposition licenses acting on it, never restating it; report the
DELTA against your last report and the fact that the rest re-derived unchanged, in one line. An
operator who has seen an item once does not need it re-listed to keep owning it.*

Do not turn this into a rule about report length in general; the defect is specifically a REPEATED
BLOCK, which is mechanically recognisable to its author and is what the operator objected to.

## What is NOT claimed

No claim that the standing list was wrong, that surfacing operator items is wrong, or that the existing
bullet should change its prescription — it is right and it worked. And n=1 on the operator objection,
though the repetition itself is measurable: the same block appeared in consecutive reports with no entry
changing.

## Provenance

Found by the mayor in a §5 pass, prompted by the operator's own interruption rather than by the loop —
which is itself the point, since §5 explicitly does not reread the mayor's own reports.
Sibling record: rf2-prwqz, which landed the bullet this would extend.
notes:
WORKER VERDICT, 2026-09-22, worker/methodbullet-kj507, PR #10199 (draft at time of writing).
DELIVERABLE: five lines appended to the EXISTING section 5 Gotchas bullet "A disposition you have
reported more than once" in docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md. No new bullet, no new section, nothing
removed or modified. Three-dot diff against the merge base is a pure 5-line insertion with 0 deletion
lines. Nothing else touched. Worktree guard ran and exited 0.

THE CALL: WRITE, not write-nothing. The item invited writing nothing and I weighed it as a real
option rather than a formality, having first read rf2-prwqz's close reason as the brief directed.
Three things decided it the other way.

## Recommendation

**C.** The stance's second half decides it. "Trust the programmer" here is trust the skill author (and the AI that re-authors it under `spec/authoring-prompt.md`) to keep a leaf as dense as its subject needs, given the two-leaf rule already bounds what a session loads — the worst legal pair is ~21k tokens, a tenth of a window. "Don't litigate the minutiae" is exactly what A does fourteen times (twenty-nine, family-wide): every reason will say "single arc, one trigger", and each number will be wrong within a month, as every figure in `design.md:115` and three in the README already are. B is the thorough option and is measured not to work — neither leaf reaches the target under any seam, and the one trigger that loads them wants the whole. C is cheaper than A, removes the recurring finding instead of paying it again, keeps the target as a prompt for the next authoring pass, and changes no number — the 2026-09-03 ruling on rf2-wh25 deliberately kept 16 KB and 250 L and reserved the policy question for the maintainer; this is that question, arriving.

If Mike prefers a record to exist, **A** is the honest fallback and is a morning; then record the sibling's two in the same PR and take every figure from this dossier's post-#10153 measurement. I would not do B.

What would change my mind: (1) Mike wants the ceiling to have teeth — adopting `setup_drift_test.clj`'s assertion across the family — in which case A is the precondition and B follows for the 2× leaves; (2) evidence that authoring sessions routinely load three-plus leaves (the two-leaf rule not being honoured), which would make per-leaf size the real bound again; (3) anything other than an auditor turning out to read the exemption list.

**One ruling settles both beads.** The rule lives in the family file, so whatever sentence lands at `README:263` binds `re-frame2-implementor` too; A or C each settle rf2-rker6 without further thought (its leaves are 1.02× and 1.04×, with a ~300 B / ~600 B trim available that becomes optional under C and unnecessary under A). B does not reach rf2-rker6 at all. Proposed single sentence Mike could rule with:
(DOSSIER continued)
> *The 16 KB / 250-line leaf figures are targets tried at a leaf's next authoring pass, not a per-leaf record: a leaf over them is not a review finding and owes no recorded exception; whoever proposes a split brings the tokens-per-session arithmetic, and the existing exempt list stands as history.*

## Codex Recommendation

**Recommendation, not a ruling: adopt a narrower version of C.** Keep the 250-line / 16,384-byte SHOULD targets, the one-level routing rule, and review of avoidable context cost. Remove the obligation to maintain an exhaustive exemption census. An overrun remains a useful review signal; it does not by itself require a split or another administrative entry. Preserve concise reasons for specifically considered exceptions so the next author can reuse the reasoning. I would not adopt C's categorical "not a review finding" language, nor declare all fourteen leaves indivisible.

**Independent evidence, inspected revision `28d588863bb2cada5f697f12613c37c6a7a4fcac`.** I enumerated tracked Markdown under this skill's `references/`, `patterns/`, and `decision-trees/`, normalized CRLF to LF, and compared every measured leaf's bytes with its Git blob at that revision. The result is 47 leaves, 16 above 16,384 bytes, and four above 250 lines. Boundary controls at 16,383/16,384/16,385 bytes and inclusion/exclusion controls for all three leaf directories and `SKILL.md` passed. The README's actual exemption roster names two of those sixteen (`skills/README.md:290-303`), leaving fourteen. The dossier's count survives, but `patterns/resources-mutations.md` is now 19,042 bytes / 208 lines. The two largest remain 38,760 and 34,674 bytes. The LF convention is independently documented in `skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj:194-205`; that test enumerates the setup skill's references, not the authoring skill's.

**The session-budget argument needs correction.** `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:120` and `:137` limit leaves per *task*. They do not cap a conversation containing several tasks, and `:140` also directs the agent to worked examples. The largest unrestricted pair of leaves is production-observability plus api-cheatsheet, giving **88,918 LF bytes including the 15,484-byte router**, rather than the dossier's 83,791. That is arithmetic, not an observed typical task. No tokenizer or representative session trace was run, so neither a precise token cap nor a fixed fraction of a context window is established. A two-file instruction also cannot protect the budget against future growth of either file.

**The claim that useful splits are impossible is also too strong.** The production leaf itself shows an errors-only configuration at `references/cross-cutting/production-observability.md:24` and `:119`, and an events-only configuration at `:54` and `:243`. This matches independent stream selection in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc:227-240`; `implementation/core/test/re_frame/observability_process_default_cljs_test.cljc:139-158` exercises errors-only configuration, and `:233-249` exercises per-stream inheritance. I read these tests; I did not execute them. The opening two-stream example therefore does not establish that every reader needs both record catalogues. Counting complete sections, including their newline bytes, gives 8,857 bytes for handled-events and 13,361 for errors. Avoiding the unneeded catalogue could materially reduce a stream-specific task's reading even if the remainder still exceeded 16 KB. A split need not cross the target to be useful: the README's test at `:271-284` asks about context saved. Conversely, those possible savings do not prove that a split is worth additional routing and shared setup text.

The API cheatsheet likewise has **14** `##` sections with explicit categories, including HTTP at `references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:76`, SSR at `:122`, and schemas at `:135`. Some lookups have a known category before reading. Its catalogue form is a reason to preserve convenient discovery, not proof that every lookup must read the whole file. I would leave both files intact in this policy cleanup, while allowing a later concrete routing proposal to demonstrate useful savings.

**Why this tradeoff fits the project.** `skills/README.md:263-288` already expresses the right author judgment. Exact census maintenance adds another source of drift without changing what the agent loads: `skills/re-frame2/spec/design.md:115` still records 20,599 / 19,236 bytes for leaves now measuring 20,982 / 20,787. Keeping reusable reasoning while dropping mandatory repeated inventory serves productivity without suppressing review of actual duplication or unnecessary reading. This explicitly changes the recording requirement in rf2-wh25's existing ruling; it needs Mike's policy decision, not an inferred implementation permission.

**Practical follow-up after that decision:** revise the family README's recording language and label retained measurements as historical; replace the authoring design's duplicate census with its central policy link and retain the useful named-exception reasoning. Align `design.md:120` with the revised recording rule. Keep the numeric targets, current leaf routing, and setup-specific test. Any ruling intended to cover rf2-rker6 must name the implementor scope explicitly; it does not automatically complete that bead's separate factual corrections. No family-wide split campaign or new size gate follows.

The main uncertainty is actual reading behavior. Frequent single-stream observability work, repeated whole-cheatsheet loading for one symbol, or demonstrated task degradation would justify targeted restructuring. Current file arithmetic supports investigating those seams; it does not establish their frequency or justify blanket exceptions. No runtime code, policy, or decision status was changed for this recommendation.

Decision: option B of the dossier, the PARSER mechanism — `scripts/check_skill_redirect_anchors.py` learns to read the WHOLE comma-separated label list an author writes after a `SKILL-REDIRECT.md → ` arrow (separators `,` `;` `and` `or`; an optional `§Section` qualifier and an optional `(gloss)` after each label; the list ends at the first thing that is not an emphasised label, so ordinary italic prose is never read as a label), replacing `REF_RE`'s one-label-per-arrow capture with an arrow match plus a bounded list walk (about 15 lines added, 4 removed, stdlib only, no new flag, no self-test, no fixture directory, no workflow edit). In the same PR, `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:162`'s arrowless cite is rewritten to the arrow form so its three labels are read; three further one-line normalisations (`patterns/async-effect.md:143`, `patterns/stale-detection.md:144`, `references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:199`) are conditional — their labels are already gated by first-position cites elsewhere.

Why (the numbers, measured at trunk d51a7f5a1c): 61 arrow cites in 171 `skills/**/*.md`; the trunk gate reads 59 label tokens (the first after each arrow); the list parse reads 80 (86 after the normalisations), 0 broken either way; 13 single-arrow lines carry 2-5 labels; 6 labels are cited ONLY in a later position and a rename of any of them today reds nothing. Plants: a broken first label reds both parsers; the exact pre-#10153 fourth label, a table rename of a later-only label and a normalised-but-wrong arrowless label red only the list parse, each naming file:line; the three prose-italic control lines yield exactly one real label each under both parsers. The Codex review's normalise-the-leaves alternative (27 references across 17 files, parser untouched) was declined: it bends the author to the tool and leaves the gate silently accepting the next comma list.

Not touched by this PR: `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` (three PRs are queued on it and its comment block stays true under B), `images.md` (rf2-zr1jy's two-arrow rewrite composes with the parser: 80/80 measured), `check_doc_slugs.py` / `check_readme_links.py` (rf2-dnx3r's), any workflow, any fixture tree.

Acceptance (the bead's original criterion, now concrete): missing first / later / normalised-arrowless labels FAIL naming file:line; the five ordinary italic tokens after an arrow are NOT flagged; the list-parse census at the worker's merge base equals 80 plus the labels it normalised (86 if all four edits land), and a green on a lower count is a parser regression, not a pass.

## Make it tangible

**What an author writes and what each reader sees.** Take `event-state-cycle.md:125` as it stands:

```
`SKILL-REDIRECT.md` → **EP — Frames (002)**, **EP — Instrumentation (009)**, **Runtime architecture**, **Tool-Pair contract (live inspection)**.
```

- Today's `REF_RE` captures `EP — Frames (002)` and stops. Three labels on the line are never compared with anything.
- A bounded list parse — arrow, then repeat `[separator] *label* [§Section] [(gloss)]` until the next thing is not one — captures all four, and stops at the full stop. On `flows.md:32`, where the arrow's one label is followed by prose italics later in the sentence, it captures the label and never reaches `*storage / durability / lifecycle*`.

**What "widening the gate" is, in code.** I prototyped it in the scratchpad (`gate_wide.py`, the trunk script with one block swapped; not for landing). The whole mechanism:

```python
ARROW_RE = re.compile(r"SKILL-REDIRECT\.md`?\s*(?:→|->)")
NEXT_LABEL_RE = re.compile(
    r"\s*(?:,\s*(?:and\s+|or\s+)?|and\s+|or\s+|;\s*)?"   # separator (absent for the first label)
    r"(?:\*\*|\*|__|_)([^*_\n`]+?)(?:\*\*|\*|__|_)"       # the emphasised label
    r"(?:\s*§[^,;\n]*?(?=[,;]|\s*\(|$))?"                 # optional §Section qualifier
    r"(?:\s*\([^)\n]*\))?"                                # optional (gloss)
)

def labels_on(line):
    for m in ARROW_RE.finditer(line):
        pos = m.end()
        while (n := NEXT_LABEL_RE.match(line, pos)):
            yield n.group(1).strip()
            pos = n.end()
```

and the walk's one line changes from `for m in REF_RE.finditer(line)` to `for raw in labels_on(line)`. About 15 lines added, 4 removed, plus the comment at `:37-41` and the table's `:19-21` saying "every label in the list". Measured at trunk through the prototype: **80 tokens, 80 OK, 0 broken**; the five prose italics after an arrow (`flows.md:32`, `frames.md:37` ×3, `spec/design.md:162` — exactly the five the reviewer's widest probe flagged) are read by nothing, because the list ends before them. No `--self-test` exists today (14 of the 15 `scripts/check_skill_*.py` carry one; this is the fifteenth) and none is needed: `check_ci_reproduce_commands.py:419-423` accepts the bare live-checker shape, so `test.yml` (hot-zone) is untouched.

## Options

### A. Keep the first-label gate; record the boundary; the rest is eye-checked (the bead's A)

- What changes: two sentences — in the gate's `REF_RE` comment (`:37-41`) and the table's comment block (`SKILL-REDIRECT.md:19-21`) — saying only the FIRST label after an arrow is validated, later labels and arrowless cites are the editor's. Optionally the one-line rewrite of `SKILL.md:162` to the arrow form so its first label is at least read (cheap; do it under either option).
- Consequences: programmer and AI — nothing at authoring time; 21 of 80 tokens (four labels exclusively) stay unguarded, and every careful worker who touches a cite re-implements the parse by hand, as #10153's did (90 tokens). Tools — none. Production, spec — none. The class recurs at the next label rename or the next abbreviated cite; measured base rate above.
- Cost: fifteen minutes; two files, neither hot-zone (`scripts/check_skill_redirect_anchors.py`, `SKILL-REDIRECT.md`; both `i/lf w/crlf`, so Edit tooling and the three-number check, no `sed -i`).
- Risk: the sentence documents a manual process that measured as failing — three born-short cites, four months, through a 5-stage review. Low severity when it fails.

### B. Bounded extension: the gate reads the whole label list after an arrow; the one arrowless cite is normalised to the arrow form (the bead's B, at its measured size)

- What changes: `REF_RE` replaced by the arrow + list parse above in `scripts/check_skill_redirect_anchors.py` (~15 lines added, 4 removed; comment `:37-41` rewritten to name the accepted shapes: `,` `;` `and` `or` separators, an optional `§Section`, an optional `(gloss)`); `SKILL-REDIRECT.md:19-21` says "every label in the list"; `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:162` rewritten to `` `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` → *Principles*, *Conventions*, *Construction prompts (AI-shaped templates)*, … `` (the `` `EP — …` `` backticked pattern stays as #10153 left it). No self-test, no fixture directory, no `test.yml` change. The PR body carries P0–P5 as the negative controls the bead's acceptance criterion asks for (missing first / later / normalised-arrowless labels fail; ordinary italic prose — the five tokens at trunk — does not).
- Consequences: programmer and AI — nothing at authoring time; an author keeps writing the list they already write, and a dead label anywhere in it reds the PR with `file:line label=…`, as a first-position one does today. Tools — the existing gate, same wiring, same silent-on-success contract. Production, spec — none. Siblings — rf2-dnx3r's A(3) would extend `BULLET_LABEL_RE` in the same file to capture the URL: different regex, no logical overlap, but the two PRs must sequence (same file). rf2-0s9l6's option A (implementor cites labels instead of 87 direct URLs) would put more later-position tokens in front of this gate, not fewer.
- Cost: half a worker-morning. Files: `scripts/check_skill_redirect_anchors.py`, `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` (comment only), `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md` (one line). No hot-zone file. All `i/lf w/crlf`.
- Risk: the list's separator vocabulary is enumerated from today's leaves; a future author's `·` or ` / ` between labels would end the list early and put the tail back in the blind spot, silently — the same class one notch wider. Bounded by construction (the list ends at the first non-label, so prose is never a label) and by the P0 control (80/80 at trunk). The worker should take the census in this dossier as the before number and require 80 after, not merely exit 0.

A leaves-only normalisation (each label under its own arrow, no gate change) is the other reading of the bead's B: 13 lines rewritten to a shape the leaves have never used, nothing stopping the next author from writing the list again, and the gate silently accepting it — which is the defect. Not recommended.

## Recommendation

**B.** The stance's second half is the argument. "Trust the programmer" is not engaged: this gate never nags an application author — it fires only on a dead label in the skills tree, exactly as it does today, and B changes which labels it can see, not when it speaks. "Excellent tools, low friction" is engaged directly: the gate exists so that "every leaf citation" stops going "stale silently" (its own docstring), it is doing that for 74% of them, and the missing 26% is the shape authors naturally write — a comma list — which B reads without asking anyone to change how they write. "Don't litigate the minutiae" cuts against A here: A's sentence buys nothing that was not already true, and it institutionalises the eye-check that a careful worker re-does by hand every time a cite is touched, which is more expensive than the fifteen lines. No new gate, no fixture tree, no `test.yml`, zero false positives measured, half a morning.

```python
# Reference syntax in leaf files (any *.md under skills/): the file name, an
# arrow, then ONE OR MORE emphasised labels. Authors write lists, e.g.
#   `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` -> **A**, **B** §Section, *C* (gloss), and *D*.
# Read after the arrow, repeatedly: [separator] <emphasised label> [§Section] [(gloss)]
# with separator one of `,` `;` `and` `or` (absent before the first label).
# The list ends at the first thing that is not an emphasised label, so italic
# prose later in the sentence is never read as a label. Arrow may be the
# Unicode -> (U+2192) or ASCII ->; the redirect name may be back-ticked.
ARROW_RE = re.compile(r"SKILL-REDIRECT\.md`?\s*(?:→|->)")
NEXT_LABEL_RE = re.compile(
    r"\s*(?:,\s*(?:and\s+|or\s+)?|and\s+|or\s+|;\s*)?"   # separator (absent for the first label)
    r"(?:\*\*|\*|__|_)([^*_\n`]+?)(?:\*\*|\*|__|_)"       # the emphasised label
    r"(?:\s*§[^,;\n]*?(?=[,;]|\s*\(|$))?"                 # optional §Section qualifier
    r"(?:\s*\([^)\n]*\))?"                                # optional (gloss)
)


def labels_on(line: str):
    """Yield every raw label cited on one line, in order: every arrow, every list."""
    for m in ARROW_RE.finditer(line):
        pos = m.end()
        while (n := NEXT_LABEL_RE.match(line, pos)):
            yield n.group(1).strip()
            pos = n.end()
```
