description:
Two corrections to `skills/re-frame2/patterns/`, one surface, both verified at source at
trunk `5c81c60be3`. The first is the substantive one.

## 1. The CSRF registration advice is in PROSE, so the copyable fence ships the leak

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/form-action.md` gives the registration-owned classification as a
sentence at **line 198**:

> Add `:sensitive [[:csrf-token]]` to the action's registration metadata to classify its event
> payload; the structural event schema's `:sensitive?` mark covers validation-failure traces
> only.

The leaf's own `reg-event :cart/add-item` fence (around lines 118-130) carries `:doc`,
`:schema` and `:rf.cofx/requires` and **no `:sensitive` key at all**. `:sensitive [[:csrf-token]]`
appears in a fence **nowhere** in that file — measured: every `csrf-token` site in the leaf is
at lines 37, 64, 70, 82, 126, 137, 150, 194, 196, 198, and the only registration-metadata
mention is the prose at 198.

The merged spec recipe has it in the fence. `spec/Pattern-FormAction.md:266` reads
`:sensitive        [[:csrf-token]]`, sitting between `:schema` and `:rf.cofx/requires` under a
ten-line comment that says exactly why it is not a duplicate of the schema prop.

**Why this is worth the edit rather than a tidy-up.** Nobody copies prose. An agent reading
this leaf copies the fence, and the fence is a registration that omits the one declaration
covering the always-on surface. The spec states the consequence at its line 408: the
`:sensitive?` schema prop redacts the schema-VALIDATION-FAILURE trace only, and a POST that
validates cleanly produces no such trace — so on every *successful* dispatch the event vector
rides `:rf.event/v` with the token verbatim, and `:rf/server-init` put the whole POST envelope
there. The registration's `:sensitive [[:csrf-token]]` is what redacts that, and it is
always-on: it survives into the release build where the tripwire is elided.

**Why it was in prose, and why that reason is now gone.** rf2-iro6x relayed it:

> the `skills/re-frame2` leaf still gives the `:sensitive [[:csrf-token]]` advice in PROSE,
> because the drift gate would have flagged it inside a fence. **rf2-zkpxu removes that
> constraint** — the advice can move into its own recipe fence whenever that leaf's owner
> wants.

rf2-zkpxu merged in PR #10243: rule 7b's `CSRF_SCHEMA_ENTRY_RE` now runs behind a bounded
parser that establishes the bracketed `:csrf-token` really is a Malli `:map` entry before
flagging, so a classification PATH in a fence is no longer read as a required schema entry.
Its `X5` fixture is this exact case, and it is GREEN.

Move the declaration into the fence, keeping the prose sentence's *reasoning* wherever it
serves the reader better. Match the spec's spelling — the two files are meant to agree.

## 2. A spurious leading slash in the managed-http leaf

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md:150` writes `GET /api/inc.json`. The example it
cites requests the **relative** path: `examples/core/managed_http_counter/core.cljs:147` reads
`{:method :get :url "api/inc.json"}`, served from the example's own tracked
`examples/core/managed_http_counter/api/inc.json`. The example's README writes it relative at
all five of its sites, and its line 42 says why — *"so `api/` is a runtime"* directory beside
the page. A leading slash points at the server root and would not resolve.

Flagged by rf2-jlx14 while fixing the same stale clause in `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`,
correctly left alone there as a different file outside that dispatch's fence. One character,
riding along here because it is the same surface.

## Fences

**`skills/re-frame2/patterns/` only.** Do not touch `spec/Pattern-FormAction.md` — it is
correct and merged; it is the model, not the target. Do not touch the example or
`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`. `spec/Conventions.md` and `spec/API.md` are hot-zone: read
them if you need to, never edit them.

## Gates, and the two that do NOT apply

* `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` is the gate that matters — it is the one
  whose rule 7b forced the prose in the first place. Run it over the repo AND run
  `--self-test`, and report both exit codes. A RED here means the bounded parser does not
  cover this spelling, which is a finding worth reporting rather than working around.
* `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` — `skills/` is inside its roots.
* **Neither link gate reads inside a fenced code block**, and your main change IS inside a
  fence. So a green from either says nothing about the line you moved. Say so plainly.
* Nothing validates this markdown's prose, tables or rendering. Check anchors and fence
  balance by hand and report the numbers.

Check `git ls-files --eol` before editing; take CR / CRLF / bare-LF with Python on the bytes
afterwards and require CR == CRLF and bare LF == 0; never `sed -i`.

## The direction test

The risk on a change that adds a key to a sample is that the sample stops being valid, and the
risk on a docs change generally is that it drifts from the thing it documents. So: quote the
skill fence and the spec fence side by side after the change and show they agree, and confirm
`:sensitive [[:csrf-token]]` now reads 1 in a fence in the leaf where it read 0.

title: core-instrumentation: elision walk-tree throws on a defrecord value (JVM) - every :db event fails on a classified frame, and a handler error with a record payload escapes dispatch-sync
description:
## Defect

The shared egress walk kernel `rf.elision/walk-tree` rebuilds every map it descends with `(reduce-kv … (empty v) v)`. On the JVM, `(empty <defrecord instance>)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException: Can't create empty: <Rec>`. Nothing in the walk short-circuits when no declarations exist, so ANY value containing a record anywhere makes `elide-wire-value` and `rf/project-egress` throw. The damage is in the event pipeline, not just a tool read:

- On a frame that declares any sensitive or large path, the dev `:rf.event/db-pending` projection walks the pending app-db. The throw rethrows out of `trace/emit!`, and every `:db`-returning event is rejected as `:rf.error/interceptor-exception` with nothing committed, for as long as a record sits in app-db.
- A handler exception whose event payload carries a record makes `dispatch-on-error!`'s elision throw out of the error path, so `dispatch-sync` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` instead of containing the handler's error. This path is always-on, so JVM SSR is affected in production too.

On CLJS, `empty` returns nil for a record, so the walk silently rebuilds it as a plain map — no crash (inspected).

## Where

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:806-834` — `walk-tree`, map arm at `:817-820`.
- Callers that run it on the pipeline: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:753-755` (`project-db-tags`, gated on `frame-has-declarations?`); `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:607-613` (`dispatch-on-error!`, always-on); `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:891-895` (`emit!` rethrows a projection throw while the continuation is live).
- Public entries: `rf/dispatch` / `rf/dispatch-sync`, `rf/project-egress`.

## Failure scenario

`(defrecord Money [amount currency])`, running on the JVM.
- (a) `(rf/project-egress {:price (->Money 10 "AUD")} {:frame F :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool})` throws, with no declarations at all.
- (b) Put `(->Money 2 "AUD")` into app-db, then have any event classify an unrelated path `:sensitive [[:secret]]`. Afterwards `(rf/dispatch-sync [:inc])`, where `:inc` returns `{:db (update db :n inc)}`, commits nothing: `:n` stays nil and one `:rf.error/interceptor-exception` "Can't create empty: user.Money" is emitted.
- (c) `(rf/reg-event :boom (fn [_ _] (throw (ex-info "boom" {}))))`, then `(rf/dispatch-sync [:boom {:m (->Money 1 "AUD")}])` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` to the caller. The same call with a plain map payload returns normally.

## Evidence

EXECUTED — bounded JVM probes from the reviewer scratch dir against the frozen tree at `034d0c8fc8` (nothing written to the tree):

- CONTROL `elide-wire-value {:a {:b 1}}` → `{:a {:b 1}}`.
- PROBE (a) → `[:THREW "java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException" "Can't create empty: user.Money"]`, both through `elide-wire-value` and through `project-egress`.
- PROBE (b) CONTROL on an unclassified frame: the record commits and 0 error traces are emitted. PROBE on the classified frame: `:n` after `[:inc]` is nil, and the errors are `[[:rf.error/interceptor-exception "Can't create empty: user.Money"]]`.
- PROBE (c) CONTROL plain payload → `dispatch-sync` returns. PROBE record payload → `[:THREW "java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException" "Can't create empty: user.Money"]`.

`spec/Conventions.md:1197-1201` says event payloads SHOULD be plain EDN. It forbids host handles, and records are not named. Nothing in the spec tells an author that a record in app-db breaks every event once anything is classified. A tracker full-text search for "create empty" / `walk-tree` finds no bead on this.

## Smallest fix

In `walk-tree`'s map arm, seed the rebuild with `{}` for a record (`(if (record? v) {} (empty v))`), or rebuild records through `into`, so the walk is total over map-shaped values. That matches what CLJS already does. Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc`, plus a record case in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_test.clj`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM core artefact: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/core`. The defect and the fix are JVM-observable, and `walk-tree` sits in no reader conditional. `npm run test:cljs` keeps the CLJS behaviour pinned.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fix — rf2-3x7nj.4.6 (2026-09-23, worker/instr-elision-3x7nj, PR #10279)

Reproduced at trunk 2c8b8847a3 with a bounded JVM probe (`(defrecord Money [amount currency])`), controls both ways: a plain map egressed fine; (a) `elide-wire-value` and `rf/project-egress` over `{:price (->Money 10 "AUD")}` both threw `UnsupportedOperationException: Can't create empty: probe.Money`; (b) with the record committed on an unclassified frame (control: `:n` incremented, 0 error traces), classifying `[[:secret]]` then dispatching `:inc` left `:n` unchanged with one `:rf.error/interceptor-exception` whose message was the same `Can't create empty`; (c) a throwing handler with a plain payload returned from `dispatch-sync`, the same handler with a record payload threw to the caller.

Fix, as the description prescribes: `walk-tree`'s map arm seeds the rebuild with `{}` for a record (`(if (record? v) {} (empty v))`), so the walk is total over map-shaped values and a record egresses as a plain map — what CLJS already did, since `cljs.core` records do not implement `IEmptyableCollection` (checked in the 1.12.145 jar: `emit-defrecord` lists no such protocol, and `empty` returns nil). The classification walker shares `walk-tree`, so the db-pending projection path is fixed by the same line. After the fix the probe egresses `{:price {:amount 10 :currency "AUD"}}`, (b) commits, (c) returns.

Regressions in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_test.clj`: `walk-rebuilds-a-record-as-a-plain-map` (a, plus a declaration inside a record still redacting), `a-record-in-app-db-does-not-reject-db-events-on-a-classified-frame` (b, seeding before classifying so the record is in app-db first), `a-handler-error-with-a-record-payload-is-contained` (c, with the plain-payload control). Control: with `(empty v)` restored the namespaces went 2 failures + 1 error, exactly those three deftests, their control assertions green; restored, blob hash equal to the committed object.
Merged-PR audit #10279 (950a0cba74f4ba056b1ae5b0a523cf4e7d6a702a; merged 2026-09-23T13:30:43Z). Completeness: All three implementation claims are addressed: ancestor and index-free classification governs offset reads; map traversal rebuilds records safely; all three trace-ring eviction/trim sites copy retained IDs. The existing open pagination-contract question rf2-ealv5 is reused with concrete measurement, not silently treated as resolved. Correctness: Independently ran exact merged core sources at 950a0cba74f4ba056b1ae5b0a523cf4e7d6a702a: elision and trace-buffer suites 113 tests/306 assertions, zero failures/errors, exit 0. Additional indexed-batch large-offset probe 1 test/3 assertions passes and records marker/default versus explicit-large behavior. Verified worker root and loaded source identities. CI 74 success/14 skipped. Ancestor sensitive dominance, large-shadow suppression, marker handles and opt-ins traced; no additional material defect found. Implementation quality: Reuses the existing walker decision and candidate forks; record handling is a one-arm correction; ring repair copies only on eviction or trim. No public API growth. Existing policy follow-up remains separately trackable and ready. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: rf2-ealv5.

Each control red with its fix removed, each restore blob-verified.

title: machines-lifecycle: a :spawn-all child finishing after its parent was destroyed resurrects the parent (join carrier bypasses the stale gate)
description:
## Defect

A `:spawn-all` join child that reaches `:final?` AFTER its parent was destroyed is not stale-suppressed. `finalize-machine`'s stale gate requires `invoke-id`, and a join child carries its coordinate only under `:rf/join-child` (never `:rf/invoke-id`), so the gate is always false for join children. The completion carrier is dispatched at the dead parent's address. Because the parent's explicit destroy leaves its join slot in place (children and their join survive an explicit destroy, by Spec 005:2654), the carrier folds into the orphaned join, and when the join resolves the resolution event `[<parent> [<on-*-complete> …]]` is dispatched too. For a `reg-machine` singleton parent, D5 lazy re-creation answers that framework-minted event: the destroyed parent is RESURRECTED from its initial snapshot, runs its initial `:entry` actions again, and receives the resolution event in its initial state. For a spawned parent, each carrier instead raises a spurious `:rf.error/no-such-handler`. This is the exact resurrection rf2-xjee fenced for single `:spawn` / `:on-error` (Spec 005:3381, 005:4002). rf2-xjee's own close reason (item 4) flagged this gap and left it without a bead: "`stale-spawn?` still requires `invoke-id`, so a `:spawn-all` join child … is outside this predicate … No bead filed."

## Where

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc:507`: `stale-spawn? (and parent-id invoke-id (not parent-live?))`. For a join child `invoke-id` (`(:rf/invoke-id child-data)`, :390) is always nil.
- `finalize.cljc:803-818`: `(when-not stale-spawn? … parent-id (when-let [target-invoke-id (or invoke-id (:invoke-id join-child))] (dispatch-spawn-done! …)))` dispatches at the dead parent.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:2502-2509`: the join child args carry `:rf/parent-id` and `:rf/spawn-all-id`, never `:rf/invoke-id`.
- `lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:993-1009` hands the carrier to `lifecycle_fx/join.cljc:589` `intercept-spawn-done-event`. The surviving join slot passes every fence, the fold runs (join.cljc:800), and `build-resolution-fx` (join.cljc:540-543) dispatches `[parent-id [resolution-event child-id result]]`.
- Public entry: `[:rf.machine/destroy <parent-id>]`, the keyword form in `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:762`, on a parent resting in a `:spawn-all` state, followed by any join child finishing.

## Failure scenario

1. `(rf/reg-machine :pa/parent {:initial :idle … :idle {:entry :count-boot :on {:start :hydrating}} :hydrating {:spawn-all {:children [{:id :a …} {:id :b …}] :join :any :on-some-complete [:hydrate/done]} …}})`. Start it, then dispatch `[:pa/parent [:start]]`.
2. `{:fx [[:rf.machine/destroy :pa/parent]]}`. The parent snapshot is gone, the join slot keeps `:children`, and both children are live.
3. `(rf/dispatch-sync [:pa/child#1 [:go]])`, where child :a reaches `:final?`.

What happens: the `:rf.machine/done` reply is `:ok`, not `:stale`. `:rf.machine/started {:cause :lazy}` fires for `:pa/parent`. Its snapshot is back at `{:state :idle, :data {:boots 1}}`, and its initial `:entry` ran a second time (count 1 → 2).

Variant where the parent's INITIAL state is the `:spawn-all` state (`:hydrating`, `:on {:hydrate/done :ready}`). After the destroy, only the two children exist. When child#1 finishes, the old join resolves, and the resolution event is answered by a lazily re-born parent. In one handler call that parent boots into `:hydrating` (spawning a fresh batch: 2 × `:rf.machine.spawn/spawned`, 1 × `:rf.machine.spawn-all/started`), consumes the OLD join's `[:hydrate/done :a :old-a]`, transitions to `:ready`, and tears the fresh batch straight back down (4 × `:rf.machine/destroyed` in all). The final runtime-db holds exactly one snapshot, `:pa3/parent` at `:ready`. The app destroyed that parent mid-hydration, and it is now alive and reports hydration complete.

## Evidence

Executed with a bounded JVM probe, `clojure -M -i probe_a.clj` from a scratch runner whose deps point at the frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:
- Singleton parent: `parent snapshot: {:state :idle, :data {:boots 1}}`, `parent entry action count: 2`, `:rf.machine/started count: 1 {:cause :lazy}`, done reply `:ok`.
- Spawned parent (`:fixed-actor-id :pa2/p1`): `p1 snapshot after child done: nil`, `{:rf.error/no-such-handler 1}`.
- Initial-state-is-`:spawn-all` variant (`probe_a3.clj`): after the parent destroy the snapshots are `{:child#1 :child#2}`; after child#1 finishes they are `{:pa3/parent [:ready nil]}`; the ops are `{:rf.machine/started 1, :rf.machine.spawn/spawned 2, :rf.machine.spawn-all/started 1, :rf.machine/destroyed 4, :rf.machine.spawn-all/some-completed 1}`.

Control: single-`:spawn` stale suppression is pinned and works (`implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_reply_lowering_test.clj:244`). No test pins the `:spawn-all` analogue. Tracker searched: rf2-xjee (closed) records the gap in its close reason as deliberately unfiled. No open bead covers it.

## Smallest fix

In `finalize-machine`, apply the stale gate to join children as well: derive the gate from `reply-parent-id` / `reply-invoke-id` (which already fall back to `:rf/join-child`), so that `(not parent-live?)` suppresses BOTH carriers and records the `:status :stale` reply. Optionally let the teardown projection prune the dead parent's orphaned join slot once no child remains. Fence: `lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc`, plus a test beside `machine_reply_lowering_test.clj`. No hot-zone file. The 005:4002 wording already covers it.

## Gates

`.cljc` shared code, outside any reader conditional, so both lanes compile it: `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` (`implementation/machines` `clojure -M:test`) and `npm run test:cljs`.

## Decision needed

no

title: ssr: hiccup emitters give no form-control special forms - [:textarea {:value v}] paints an empty textarea, select :value / :default-value / :default-checked print as attributes until hydration
description:
## Defect

The two hiccup BODY emitters, `re-frame.ssr/render-to-string` (`emit/emit-element`) and the streaming shell walk (`streaming/walk-dom-tag`), give no form-control special form to the props React treats specially. Each one reaches the markup as an ordinary attribute:

- `[:textarea {:value "abc"}]` renders `<textarea value="abc"></textarea>`. react-dom/server renders `<textarea>abc</textarea>`, so the server paints an EMPTY textarea.
- `[:select {:value "b"} [:option {:value "a"} …] [:option {:value "b"} …]]` carries `value="b"` on the `<select>`. react-dom marks `selected` on the matching `<option>`, so the server paints the FIRST option.
- `[:input {:default-value "x"}]` and `{:default-checked true}` (after rf2-3x7nj.13.1 lands, `defaultValue`/`defaultChecked`) are unknown attributes. react-dom writes `value="x"` and `checked`.

The first paint therefore shows the wrong control state until hydration. React writes these at hydration, so the impact is limited to the pre-hydration window: slow JS, JS failure, no-JS crawlers and screenshots. That is also why this is lower impact than rf2-3x7nj.13.1, whose attribute divergences React never repairs.

## Where (trunk f6bb999d6e)

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc`, the `emit-element` DOM-tag branch (about :804-851): its branches are void, raw-text and else. None is for form controls, and every prop goes through `attr-string`.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc` `walk-dom-tag` (about :368-412) has the same shape.
- **The rule already exists in the same artefact** for the structural-tree serialiser: `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/ui_tree.cljc` about :900-930. `:default-value`/`:default-checked` become `value`/`checked`, `:value` on `:textarea` becomes the text child, and `:value` on `:select` becomes `selected` on the matching option. The textarea content contract is at about :846-895 (`reject-textarea-content!`). 004B §Property-only and form-control special forms owns the grammar.

title: schemas: the never-evicted sensitive-walker memo grows without bound in production when managed-HTTP feeds it per-request :decode schemas
description:
## Defect

The memo behind `extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema` never evicts. It rests on the boot-once invariant: "schemas are registered once at app-boot, so steady-state cache size equals the registry size". The managed-HTTP artefact breaks that invariant in production. It feeds each request's `:decode` schema through the memoized hook, both at dispatch and again when the response is classified. A `:decode` schema that carries a `:sensitive?` or `:large?` mark and is built per request adds one permanent cache entry per distinct request, which is unbounded growth. A request-specific literal operand is enough to trigger it, for example `[:= id]` asserting that the response echoes the requested id.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/cache.cljc:23-45`: `clearable-memo` has no eviction by design.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc:371-402`: the `extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema` memo. Its docstring at 391-397 claims the bound.
- spec/010-Schemas.md:535 repeats the claim ("The only way to grow the cache without bound is ... which only a stress test does").
- Producer: `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy_body.cljc:180-218`. `decode-schema-marks` passes the request's `:decode` to the memoized `:schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema` hook (line 202).
- Callers: `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:274` calls it once per request in `normalise-args`, and `privacy_body.cljc:292` calls it again in `classify-decoded` per response.
- Public entry: any managed-HTTP request whose `:decode` is a marked inline schema. Every build is affected, because the memo is not dev-gated.

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(rf/reg-event-fx :user/load
  (fn [_ [_ id]]
    {:http {:url (str "/users/" id)
            :decode [:map [:id [:= id]]
                          [:ssn {:sensitive? true} :string]
                          [:name :string]]}}))
```

Each distinct `id` requested adds a cache entry holding its schema. The entries are only released by the test-support `clear-sensitive-paths-cache!`, which production never calls.

## Evidence

Executed: a bounded JVM probe (probe4.clj, schemas `:test` classpath plus `../http/src`, run from the frozen tree's `implementation/schemas`, `-Xmx2g`). It called the real `re-frame.http.privacy-body/decode-schema-marks` with 200,000 such per-request schemas:

- Retained heap went from 15.3 MB to 108.7 MB, about 470 bytes per request, never released.
- `clear-sensitive-paths-cache!` dropped it back to 14.8 MB.
- Control: the same schema value called 200,000 times stayed flat at 14.8 MB.

The other `:schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema` / `redact-validation-tags` consumers (resources, routing, machines, flows, cofx, sub-override, the boundary interceptor) pass registered, static schemas, so HTTP `:decode` is the one per-call producer. `extract-large-paths-from-schema` is not memoized and is unaffected. No tracker bead covers this: the export was searched for `boot-once` and `clearable-memo` (neither hit a schemas bead) and `decode-schema-marks` (5 hits: rf2-1eng8 and review/cleanup beads, none about cache growth).

## Smallest fix

Route per-request `:decode` extraction through an UNMEMOIZED walk. Either http calls a non-memo extractor, which schemas would publish beside the memoized one, or `privacy_body.cljc` walks once per request and threads the result from `normalise-args` to `classify-decoded`. Keep the memo for registered schemas, per the deliberate no-LRU stance. Also correct spec/010-Schemas.md:535 and the walker docstring so they no longer claim that only a stress test can grow the cache.

Fence: `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy_body.cljc` (and `handlers.cljc` if the result is threaded), plus possibly `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc` / `walker.cljc` and a late-bind directory row in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc` if a new hook is published. No hot-zone file, unless a public name is added (then spec/API.md and the two api-manifest sidecars).

## Gates

- JVM: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/http` and `implementation/schemas`.
- CLJS: `npm run test:cljs`. The http privacy body is `.cljc`.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## FIXED — PR #10303 (worker/schemas-3x7nj), 2026-09-24

Route taken: the bead's first route ("http calls a non-memo extractor, which schemas would publish"), done by REBINDING the existing hook rather than minting a second key.

- `re-frame.schemas.walker/walk-sensitive-paths-from-schema` is a new unmemoised walk. It is in the walker namespace, which is not in the api-manifest.
- The memo is now built over it.
- `:schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema` now publishes this walk.
- The public `re-frame.schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema` stays memoised, as docs/api documents it, and so do the internal `schema-has-sensitive?` / `schema-sensitive-at?` decisions over registered schemas.

Why this form (smaller diff, no new surfaces):
- No new hook key, no late-bind directory row and no facade var. The directory description stays accurate.
- `privacy_body.cljc` changes only in a docstring.
- Threading the result instead would have had to reach transport.cljc, where `classify-decoded` is called, which is outside the fence, and it would still have needed an unmemoised walk.
- The hook's one other consumer, the resources invalid-params redaction (`validation-failure-params-marks`), passes a registered `:params-schema` and now walks once per failure. Its docstring's "modulo the memoised walker" is now merely redundant; that file is outside this fence.
- handlers.cljc:~270's comment ("the walker is memoised") is now stale, and is also outside this fence. Leave it for the rf2-3x7nj.16.x http worker.

Spec 010 §Schema digest (the boot-once paragraph), the walker memo docstrings and the cache.cljc ns docstring no longer claim only a stress test can grow the cache.

Measured with a JVM heap probe, 200,000 distinct per-request `:decode` schemas (`[:= i]` operand) through the real `decode-schema-marks`:
- fix removed: 15.3 MB -> 109.2 MB (clear -> 14.8 MB);
- with the fix: 15.3 MB -> 14.8 MB, flat.

Regressions:
- http: `decode-schema-marks-leaves-the-walker-memo-untouched`. After a per-request extraction, a memo lookup of the same schema value must NOT return the identical result object (it did at trunk).
- schemas: `sensitive-extractor-hook-is-unmemoized-public-memo-kept`. The hook retains nothing, and the public extractor still memoises.

Control: both were red at trunk. Planting the memo back onto the hook turned them red (1 assertion each), and the restore was verified by blob hash.
Merged-PR audit #10303 (2ec17584d2d39d232abf709d2ecf45a98d23a109; merged 2026-09-23T20:38:43Z). Completeness: All four findings addressed: whole-schema path sanitization, slot-specific large-value elision without overwriting query identity, explainer-owned failing values and nonmemoized per-request schema extraction. Correctness: Reviewed source changes and regression coverage including sensitive siblings, map-of keys versus values, absent explainer values, multi-error fallback and hook/public memo distinction. Accepted reported 21-artifact JVM run, schemas 416/19473, HTTP 524/4125, measured heap probe and targeted negative controls; CI 62 successful checks. Implementation quality: Keeps existing late-bind key and registered-schema memo, avoids an LRU or another public API, and distinguishes lookup identity from payload. No material additional finding. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

The node-test lane read exactly +1 assertion (the new fixture case), as predicted. Every defect reproduced at trunk; controls were restored and blob-verified.

rf2-3x7nj.19.4 — FIXED (route 1, made smaller). The existing :schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema hook is rebound to a new unmemoised walk (walker/walk-sensitive-paths-from-schema): no new hook key, no directory row, no public facade var. privacy_body.cljc gets only a docstring fix. The memo stays for the public extractor and for registered-schema validation. MEASURED heap over 200,000 distinct request schemas: 15.3 -> 109.2 MB with the fix removed, 15.3 -> 14.8 MB with it. spec/010 and the walker/cache docstrings no longer claim only a stress test can grow the cache. Residues outside the fence are carried on rf2-uoeyl: an http handlers.cljc comment ('the walker is memoised') and the resources validation-failure-params-marks docstring ('modulo the memoised walker').

title: machines-core: single-:spawn failure carrier has no attempt identity - a stale spawn/error queued behind a re-entry fires :on-error against the new attempt and destroys its child
description:
## Defect

A single-`:spawn` child's failure carrier `[:rf.machine.spawn/error <invoke-id> <err>]` carries no attempt identity. The parent-side resolver accepts it whenever the spawning state is still on the active path. So a carrier from attempt #1 that is queued FIFO behind a parent event which RE-ENTERS the spawning state (spawning attempt #2) fires the parent's `:spawn :on-error` against attempt #2. The parent leaves the state it just re-entered, and the healthy attempt-#2 child is destroyed by the exit cascade.

Spec 005 forbids this in terms: a late completion whose "spawn correlation no longer names a live actor (the actor was already destroyed, **or the spawn slot was reused**) is `:status :stale` … its app target (the `:on-done` / `:on-error` routing) MUST NOT run". `:spawn-all` has exactly this fencing (attempt coordinates on its done carrier). Single `:spawn` does not.

## Where

All citations are at `034d0c8fc8`.

- In scope. `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:1420-1429`: `pick-spawn-error-transition` resolves `spawn-node` on `(prefix-of? invoke-id path)` alone. Its comment at `:1424` says it "mirrors the `:after` staleness check", but the `:after` check (`pick-after-transition`, `:960`) also compares a per-path EPOCH, and this one has no equivalent.
- The carrier sites, in lifecycle_fx:
  - `lifecycle_fx/spawn_error.cljc:141-154` (`dispatch-spawn-error!`: payload is `invoke-id` + `error`, no generation / actor id)
  - `spawn_error.cljc:113-139` (`dispatch-carrier!`: FIFO, `:rf.machine/internal?` dropped)
  - `lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc:507` (`stale-spawn?` is `(and parent-id invoke-id (not parent-live?))`: parent liveness only, even though `:517-520` already reads the slot's CURRENT generation and uses it only for trace correlation)
  - `lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:224-226` (the action-exception trigger: same shape)
- Public entry point: any machine with `:spawn {… :on-error …}` driven through `rf/dispatch`.

## Failure scenario

Parent `:working {:spawn {:machine-id :pd/child :on-error {:target :errored}} :on {:retry {:target :working :reenter? true}}}`. In one drain:

1. child#1 receives `[:boom]` and reaches its `:error? :final?` leaf. The `spawn/error` carrier is queued BEHIND an already-queued parent `[:retry]`.
2. `[:retry]` re-enters `:working`: child#1's slot is torn down and child#2 is spawned.
3. The stale carrier arrives. `[:working]` is still a prefix of the active path, so `:on-error` fires. The parent goes to `:errored` and child#2 is destroyed.

The user's retry is silently undone by the failure it was retrying.

## Evidence

EXECUTED. A scratch JVM probe through the real router (`make-reset-runtime-fixture`, plain-atom adapter, trace listener), with no writes to the frozen tree:

- CASE (retry queued behind the failure). Traces:
  - `child#1 :running→:failed`
  - `destroyed :pd/child#1`
  - parent `:working→:working` with `:rf/spawned {[:working] :pd/child#2}`
  - `:rf.machine.spawn/spawned`
  - parent `:working→:errored`
  - `destroyed :pd/child#2`

  `:working` entered 2 times, final state `:errored`, spawn slot nil.
- CONTROL (no retry): parent `:working→:errored`, `:working` entered 1 time. The on-error route itself is healthy.

Spec: `spec/005-StateMachines.md:4002` (stale suppression: "or the spawn slot was reused … MUST NOT run") and `:3381` (delivery requires a live parent).

INSPECTED, not executed. The `spawn/done` twin has the same gap. `registration.cljc:656-688` `apply-spawn-on-done` folds `:on-done` "whether or not the parent still rests on the spawning state". So a done carrier from a superseded attempt, or one queued behind an event that EXITED the spawning state, mutates `:data`. The same spec line forbids that ("it produces no `:data` / snapshot mutation").

Tracker: no existing bead covers this. `bd search` found nothing for "spawn slot", "pick-spawn-error", "stale carrier" or "spawn/error", and a scan of the export for "slot was reused" found nothing. rf2-gbzv9 (run propagation through the carriers) is unrelated.

## Smallest fix

Carry the attempt identity on the single-`:spawn` carriers, just as `:spawn-all` already does: the finishing child's actor id, or its generation (`reply/actor-generation`, already computed in finalize). The parent side then drops the carrier as stale, and emits the existing stale trace vocabulary with `:rf.reply/stale-reason`, when `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned parent invoke-id]` no longer names that child. Apply this in `pick-spawn-error-transition`, or ahead of it at the handler boundary, and in `apply-spawn-on-done`.

Fence:

- `transition.cljc` (resolver)
- `lifecycle_fx/{spawn_error,finalize,registration}.cljc` (carrier payload + done fold)
- a JVM test pinning the probe's CASE/CONTROL pair

The carrier shape is internal; the public `(nth ev 2)` error payload is unchanged. No hot-zone file, unless spec 005 wants a sentence naming the carrier's new slot.

OVERLAP NOTE: the carrier and done-fold halves live in lifecycle_fx, which is the machines-lifecycle slice (rf2-3x7nj.9). At filing time that slice had no child beads, so this is filed once here. Fold it together if that reviewer files the same root cause.

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines` (JVM; shared `.cljc` code, not a `#?(:cljs …)` branch).
- `npm run test:cljs` for `machines_on_error_cljs_test.cljc` / `final_state_cljs_test.cljc`, which exercise both carriers.

## Decision needed

None on direction; the spec already rules it. Implementer's choice: carry the actor id or the generation (the actor id is simpler and also covers `:fixed-actor-id` spawns). Also decide whether the done half ships in the same PR (recommended: one root cause, one fix).
notes:
== NOTE FROM THE rf2-3x7nj.9.3 RULING (mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-23 23:46:00 AUSEST) ==

rf2-3x7nj.9.3 was ruled today, and the ruling widens and corrects this bead's scope. Read 9.3's ruling note for the full implementer package, tests and spec edits.

1. SAME PR. This bead and 9.3 share one root cause: single-:spawn completion carriers carry no attempt identity. They are one fix. Ship them together, as 9.3's ruling says.

2. THE EXIT HALF IS NOW IN SCOPE, for the error carrier as well as the done carrier. A single-:spawn carrier is delivered only while the same spawn attempt is current, meaning the :spawn-bearing node at invoke-id is still on the parent's active path AND the parent has not re-entered it since that child was spawned. A stale ERROR carrier must skip the WHOLE pick. That covers both the :spawn :on-error arm and the escape-hatch walk that pick-spawn-error-transition falls through to: the leaf->root walk, then the root :on (transition.cljc:1438-1447 at trunk 950a0cba74). Codex measured that walk firing after exit: a late failure after :cancel reached :caught through a root :on {:rf.machine.spawn/error :caught}. Both triggers are covered, the error-leaf trigger in finalize and the action-exception trigger in registration.cljc.

3. CORRECTION to "carry the actor id — simpler and also covers :fixed-actor-id spawns": it does NOT cover them. reply/actor-generation (reply.cljc:132-140) returns 1 for every fixed id, and a :fixed-actor-id re-entry reuses the same actor id. Nor can the currency test read the registry slot or the :rf/spawned mirror. Per D8 (spec 005:3329), finality clears both on EVERY completion, and rf2-3x7nj.9.4 records the mirror being wiped by an exit plus re-entry in one macrostep. The identity must be a per-entry attempt token in the parent snapshot, modelled on :spawn-all's :rf/attempt exact-attempt fence (spec 005:4027-4030). It must survive the child's finality, and it must hold even when the replacement child has also finished before the old carrier arrives.

4. SPEC: this is no longer "no hot-zone file". 9.3's ruling requires a spec/005:4002 clarification. A new snapshot key or a new trace op would add rows in spec/005, spec/Spec-Schemas and spec/009, all of which are hot-zone.

This bead's own direction is unchanged, and "Decision needed: None" still holds. This note changes only its scope.
== STOPPED FOR HOT-ZONE GRANTS — design ready for re-dispatch (machines-tail worker, 2026-09-24 04:21 AUSEST) ==

Mayor ruling: option (c). rf2-3x7nj.8.2 and rf2-3x7nj.9.3 were left OUT of PR #10296, which ships 9.6, 8.4 and gdne8. The reason is that the ruled fix needs rows in three hot-zone files that were not granted and are held elsewhere: spec/Conventions.md (rf2-3x7nj.5.2) and spec/009 (rf2-3x7nj.13.3). Shipping a reserved key without its catalogue rows is the drift those tables exist to stop. Both beads stay in_progress for re-dispatch with all three grants. No code for 8.2/9.3 was written or committed.

PREMISE HOLDS AT TRUNK 27bc54ef87 (implementation/machines unchanged by my branch for these paths). Measured with a JVM probe through the real router (plain-atom adapter, make-reset-runtime-fixture). The base parent is :idle {:on {:start :loading}}; :loading {:spawn {:machine-id :pc/child :on-done (fn [{:keys [data result]}] (update data :results conj result))} :on {:cancel :idle :retry {:target :loading :reenter? true}}}. The child is :running {:on {:go :done :boom :failed}}, :done {:final? true :output-key :id}, :failed {:final? true :error? true}, with :data {:id "first"}. After [:start], one handler queues the listed events with :dispatch fx:
- CONTROL, [child :go] only: state :loading, :results ["first"], slot nil (the legitimate D8 fold).
- EXIT done, [child :go] [:cancel]: state :idle, :results ["first"]. DEFECT.
- RE-ENTRY done, [child :go] [:cancel] [:start]: state :loading, :results ["first"], slot :pc/child#2 (live replacement). DEFECT.
- FIXED-ID re-entry, same queue with :fixed-actor-id :pc/kid: :results ["first"], slot :pc/kid. DEFECT; the actor id cannot discriminate this case.
- CONTROL error, :on-error :errored with [child :boom]: state :errored.
- 8.2 retry behind the failure, :on-error :errored with [child :boom] [:retry]: state :errored, slot nil (child#2 destroyed). DEFECT.
- One side observation, not re-measured further: with :on-done declared and NO :on-error, an :error? final child delivered after [:cancel] folded :on-done with result nil (:results [nil]) and the root :on {:rf.machine.spawn/error :caught} did not fire. So Codex's "root :on catches a late failure" row needs a parent shaped without :on-done. Re-derive that row's fixture before pinning it.

WHY NO EXISTING SLOT CARRIES THE ATTEMPT IDENTITY (hence a new reserved key):
- :rf/spawn-counter is [:map-of :keyword :int] keyed by ID-PREFIX, not by invoke-id. Two invoke-ids spawning the same prefix bump one counter, so its value is not "the current attempt at invoke-id". A :fixed-actor-id spawn does not bump it at all.
- [:data :rf/spawned <invoke-id>] and the runtime-db slot [:rf.runtime/machines :spawned P invoke-id] are both cleared at D8 finality on EVERY completion. So "slot still names the carried actor" rejects every legitimate fold, and "slot is nil" cannot tell "current child finished" from "re-entered, and the replacement also finished".
- :rf/after-epoch is bumped only for :after-bearing nodes, and the ruling rules it out.
- reply/actor-generation reads 1 for every fixed id.

PROPOSED DESIGN (key names are proposals; the next worker may rename):
1. PARENT TOKEN — a new snapshot-ROOT key :rf/spawn-attempts, shape {<invoke-id-vector> <pos-int>}, sibling of :rf/spawn-counter.
   - Bump it in transition.cljc handle-spawn-decl on every entry of the :spawn-bearing node, threaded through the snapshot like allocate-spawned-id: (update-in s [:rf/spawn-attempts invoke-id] (fnil inc 0)).
   - It is runtime-owned and survives finality, because finality touches neither snapshot-root counter.
   - PARALLEL CAVEAT: handle-spawn-decl's invoke-id is region-RELATIVE, and the parallel snapshot is shared, so two regions with the same in-region prefix would collide. Key it REGION-QUALIFIED, matching prefix-region-invoke-id's [region & path]. run-spawn-phase has `machine`, so it can pass (:rf/region machine) down.
2. CHILD STAMP — carry the token on the spawn args (:rf/invoke-attempt n). spawn-fx* stamps it into the child's identity envelope in :data beside :rf/invoke-id (proposed [:data :rf/invoke-attempt]), just as :rf/join-child carries :rf/attempt for :spawn-all.
3. CARRIERS — both carry the token:
   - done: the completion map built in finalize.cljc (currently {:result :error? :completed-at}) gains :rf/invoke-attempt.
   - error: dispatch-spawn-error! (spawn_error.cljc) appends it as a 4th element, [:rf.machine.spawn/error invoke-id err attempt], from BOTH triggers: the error-leaf one in finalize and the action-exception one in registration.cljc.
   - The public (nth ev 2) payload and the callback signatures stay unchanged.
4. GATE — at the parent handler boundary in registration.cljc, BEFORE apply-spawn-on-done and BEFORE the engine step, for non-join done carriers and for error carriers.
   - A carrier is current iff the :spawn-bearing node at invoke-id is on the active path (region head stripped as pick-spawn-error-transition does) AND carried = (get-in snapshot [:rf/spawn-attempts <qualified-invoke-id>]).

   - A carrier with NO token is not runtime-minted. The documented hand-dispatched escape hatch is one such case, and it keeps today's behaviour.
   - finalize's existing parent-liveness gate still runs first.
5. TRACE — a new op, :rf.machine.spawn/stale-completion. Tags: :actor-id (parent), :invoke-id, :kind (:done | :error), :rf.reply/status :stale, :rf.reply/work-status :suppressed, :frame, and :rf.reply/stale-reason, which is one of:
   - :rf.machine.spawn/state-exited (the node is not active);
   - :rf.machine.spawn/attempt-superseded (the token differs).
   The carried/current attempt pair rides :rf.reply/correlation, per Managed-Effects §Stale suppression step 4.
6. Rewrite apply-spawn-on-done's docstring. The sentence "whether or not the parent still rests on the spawning state" goes; the fold now runs only for a current carrier.

CATALOGUE ROWS THE FIX NEEDS (the three grants):
- spec/Conventions.md, reserved-keys table (about :640-653): a row for :rf/spawn-attempts (snapshot root) and one for :rf/invoke-attempt (child :data). Add both to the "Persistence posture" sentence's list of persisting slots.
- spec/Spec-Schemas.md, :rf/machine-snapshot (about :2836-2847): [:rf/spawn-attempts {:optional true} [:map-of [:vector :keyword] :int]] with a comment. Add the key to the round-trip / read-only invariants (about :2881-2888).
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md: a row for :rf.machine.spawn/stale-completion beside the :rf.machine.spawn-all/* ops (about :189 / :231).
- Also spec/005 (it was granted to this worker and would be again): the reserved snapshot-internal keys table (:77), the :4002 clarification the ruling requires, and :on-error arm 2 (about :3386), which applies only to a current carrier.

TESTS: take the ruling's list verbatim. The probe rows above are its RED half at trunk and are ready to become JVM tests. CLJS (final_state_cljs_test.cljc, machines_on_error_cljs_test.cljc) is graded by CI.
== ADDENDUM to the machines-tail design note above (2026-09-24 04:47 AUSEST) — :on-error "resolution arm 2" does not fire today ==

This comes from the review session, relayed by the mayor. A failed single-:spawn child whose parent declares NO :on-error arrives as an ordinary completion and is folded into :on-done (registration.cljc apply-spawn-on-done, about :656-688). finalize.cljc skips the done carrier (about :452-454) only when :on-error IS declared. So spec 005 §:on-error "resolution arm 2" (an explicit :on {:rf.machine.spawn/error …} catching a failure that has no :on-error) never fires today. That was measured at a7913dfad9 for rf2-3x7nj.41.1, which is pending a decision.

My own probe agrees. With :on-done declared and no :on-error, a late failure folded :on-done with result nil (:results [nil]), and a root :on {:rf.machine.spawn/error :caught} did not fire.

Consequences for the design above:
- Item 5 of "CATALOGUE ROWS", which clarifies arm 2 as applying only to a current carrier, must NOT word arm 2 as though it works. Coordinate it with whatever rf2-3x7nj.41.1 rules.
- The ruling's "EXIT error with a root :on {:rf.machine.spawn/error :caught}" test row is reachable only through a parent that DECLARES :on-error. After the exit, that local arm declines because the spawning node is no longer active, and the leaf->root walk then reaches the root :on. A parent with no :on-error never mints the error carrier at all.
- PR #10296's spec/005 edits do not touch arm 2.
== IMPLEMENTED (worker machines2-3x7nj, PR #10311, one PR with rf2-3x7nj.9.3 per its ruling) ==

VERDICT: fixed. The design proposed in this bead's notes was built exactly as proposed, with the key and op names unchanged:

title: story-ui-workspace: the multi-substrate grid and every workspace cell never apply a variant's :sub-overrides, so pinned design states paint from the real app-db while the single canvas paints the pinned value
description:
## Defect

A variant's pinned subscription overrides (`:sub-overrides`) are applied by only two render paths:
- the canvas's single-pane path, which wraps the view in `sub-overrides-scope`;
- the `render-variant` host (`render-host-scope`).

The other two paths that render a variant never wrap the view in the override-context Provider:
- the canvas's **multi-substrate grid branch**, used when a variant declares more than one substrate;
- **every workspace cell** (`:grid`, `:variants-grid`, `:tabs`, `:prose`).

On those paths a view's `@(rf/subscribe [:q])` reads the real subscription against the variant frame's app-db instead of the pinned value.

A design or view-state variant is the case this hurts most: its fidelity is `#{:sub-overrides}`, with no setup and no seed. It paints the pinned state on the single canvas, but in a side-by-side substrate comparison or a devcards-style `:variants-grid` gallery it paints whatever an empty app-db yields. The gallery is exactly where a set of design states is meant to be viewed together.

Nothing on screen says the overrides were dropped. The sidebar chip and the plan's `[:world :fidelity]` still say the picture rests on sub overrides.

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs:596`: `canvas-inner` resolves `sub-ovr` off the compiled plan for every render.
- `canvas.cljs:700-708`: the grid branch. `multi?` leads to `[rf/frame-provider {:frame variant-id} [rf.story.ui.multi-substrate/multi-substrate-grid variant-id]]`, and `sub-ovr` is never used.
- `canvas.cljs:764-775`: the single-pane branch. It wraps the render in `[sub-overrides-scope sub-ovr ...]` at `:770`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs:510-548`: `multi-substrate-grid` and its cells. This file is outside this slice (story-ui-evidence scope). It contains no sub-override reference at all.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/workspace.cljc:332-477`: `variant-cell-inner`, inside `#?(:cljs ...)`. It renders `[rf/frame-provider {:frame variant-id} [:div ... (safe-decorated-view (render-view ...) ...)]]` at `:451-458`, with no override scope and no plan read for overrides. This file is in this slice.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/canonical.cljc:110-147`: `render-host-scope`, the `render-variant` host, wraps the view in `override-provider` — the path that agrees with the single canvas.
- Public entry:
  - select a variant declaring `:substrates #{:reagent :uix}` together with `:sub-overrides`;
  - or open any workspace listing a variant with `:sub-overrides`, for example the `:variants-grid` of a story whose variants are view states.

Contract: `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` §View-state subscription overrides, `:642-752`.
- "Story MUST support a deliberate lower-fidelity path for view-state/design variants" (`:644-645`).
- "overrides are for rendering/view-state exploration" (`:663`).
- "**Render-path read + the honesty rule (rf2-7pgiz — wired).** Overrides feed the RENDER PATH only, and they now **surface at render**: a normally-authored view's `@(rf/subscribe [:q])` paints the pinned value with no events, no app-db seed." (`:729-732`)

The spec does not list each render surface by name. It names the canvas's `sub-overrides-scope` and the host's `render-host-scope` as "the render path" (`:738-739`). No passage exempts the grid or workspace cells, and no bead rules them out (a tracker search for `sub-overrides-scope`, `override-provider` and `multi-substrate-grid` finds no ruling). So two render paths honour the contract and two silently do not.

## Failure scenario

1. `(rf/reg-sub :probe/n (fn [db _] (:n db)))`, with a view that paints `@(rf/subscribe [:probe/n])`.
2. Story `:story.vs {:component :app.ui/counter}`.
3. `:story.vs/pinned-multi {:substrates #{:reagent :uix} :sub-overrides {[:probe/n] 5}}`.

Selecting `pinned-multi` takes the grid branch. Both cells paint the view with `:probe/n` read from the variant's empty app-db (nil), not 5.

The same override on a single-substrate variant paints 5 on the canvas. Placed in a `:variants-grid` workspace, that single-substrate variant again paints nil in its cell.

`render-variant` on either variant renders with 5.

## Evidence

**Render half: INSPECTED only.** `canvas.cljs`, `multi_substrate.cljs` and the workspace cell are CLJS, so no JVM or browser run is possible in this wave.
- Read side by side: the single-pane branch applies `sub-overrides-scope` (`canvas.cljs:770`) and the grid branch does not (`:700-708`).
- A search of `multi_substrate.cljs`, `workspace.cljc`, `canvas.cljs`, `canonical.cljc`, `render.cljc` and `sub_overrides.cljc` for `sub-overrides-scope|override-provider|sub-override|sub-ovr` finds override use only in `canvas.cljs` (`:596`, `:770`) and `canonical.cljc` (`:143`). It finds zero hits in `multi_substrate.cljs` and `workspace.cljc`. The search is positive in the files that do carry it, so the zeros are real.

**Plan half: EXECUTED** as a bounded JVM probe from `tools/story` at `034d0c8fc8`, using the `story_ui_test.clj` reset-fixture boot. The frozen tree's `git status` was clean afterwards.

| variant | `[:world :substrates]` | canvas branch | overrides resolved | `[:world :fidelity]` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `:story.vs/pinned-multi` | `#{:uix :reagent}` | GRID | `{[:probe/n] 5}` | `#{:sub-overrides}` |
| `:story.vs/pinned-single` (control) | nil | single pane | `{[:probe/n] 5}` | `#{:sub-overrides}` |
| `:story.vs/plain-multi` (control) | `#{:uix :reagent}` | GRID | nil | nil |

"Overrides resolved" is `rf.story.render/resolve-render-sub-overrides`, the same resolver `canvas-inner` calls at `:596`. So the plan hands the grid-bound variant exactly the override map the single pane applies. The grid branch then discards it.

Reported first by the story-ui-evidence reviewer as an out-of-scope observation in rf2-3x7nj.29's notes; verified here independently.

## Smallest fix

Wrap the grid branch in the same scope:
`[rf/frame-provider {:frame variant-id} [sub-overrides-scope sub-ovr [multi-substrate-grid variant-id]]]` at `canvas.cljs:707-708`. The Provider is a React context, so it covers every cell.

In `workspace.cljc` `variant-cell-inner`, resolve the overrides off the compiled plan with the cell's `run-opts` (`rf.story.render/resolve-render-sub-overrides`), and wrap the `safe-decorated-view` in `rf.story.ui.canvas/sub-overrides-scope`.

**Related: rf2-3x7nj.28.2.** It moves the same three sites (canvas grid branch, `multi-substrate-grid`, workspace `variant-cell-inner`) onto the compiled plan for `:component`/`:substrates`. A single change that has each of these renderers read one compiled plan closes both findings.

Fence: `ui/canvas.cljs`, `ui/workspace.cljc`. No hot-zone files.

## Gates

Every change sits in `.cljs` or the `#?(:cljs ...)` branch of `workspace.cljc`. Only the CLJS lane compiles and grades it: `npm run test:cljs`, plus the browser lane for a DOM pin that a grid or workspace cell paints the pinned value. A JVM green says nothing about these forms.

## Decision needed

No.

Merged-PR audit #10317 (63e118215cb01387943edb775501b714367f58e3; merged 2026-09-23T23:38:52Z). Completeness: All four workspace findings are covered across canvas, grid, workspace, switchers and Run all. The run-owner listener also addresses open audit finding rf2-iftxj, annotated without status change. Correctness: Read every production diff and the actual rerun regression. title: story-ui-evidence: dispatch console's JSON heuristic matches ordinary EDN payloads with a string value before a keyword ({:email "a@b.c" :password "x"}), so on CLJS they go to JSON.parse and dispatch is refused
description:
## Defect

The dispatch console decides whether a payload is JSON with the heuristic `looks-like-json?`: the payload starts with `{` or `[` and contains a match for the regex `#"\"[^\"]+\"\s*:"`, meaning "a quoted key followed by a colon". The docstring calls this "the cheap unambiguous discriminator". It is not unambiguous: in EDN, a STRING VALUE followed by a KEYWORD matches exactly the same text (`"a@b.c" :password`).

On CLJS those payloads go to `js/JSON.parse`, which throws, and the console refuses to dispatch with "payload parse error: SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON...". Ordinary EDN maps where a string value precedes another key are the normal shape of form payloads, for example `{:email "a@b.c" :password "hunter2"}` or `{:name "Bob" :id 7}`. The user has to reorder the keys to get a dispatch through.

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/dispatch_console.cljc:100-114`: `looks-like-json?`.
- `:116-121` (`#?(:cljs ...)`): `parse-json-cljs` calls `js/JSON.parse`.
- `:123-150`: `parse-payload`. The CLJS arm takes JSON whenever the heuristic matches; the JVM arm always reads EDN.
- Entry point: the Dispatch console panel's dispatch button. `dispatch-from-inputs!` at `:510-548` calls `(parse-payload pl-raw)` at `:532` and sets "payload parse error: ..." on `:error`.

## Failure scenario

In the dispatch console, event `:login/submit`, payload `{:email "a@b.c" :password "hunter2"}`, click dispatch.

- Actual (CLJS): no dispatch, error "payload parse error: SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1".
- The same payload with the keys swapped, `{:password "hunter2" :email "a@b.c"}`, also matches (`"hunter2" :email`). Only payloads whose strings are all LAST, like `{:id 7 :name "Bob"}`, get through.

## Evidence

EXECUTED on the JVM, bounded, against the real `looks-like-json?`:

- returns `true` for `{:email "a@b.c" :password "hunter2"}`, `{:name "Bob" :id 7}` and `["a" :b]`;
- returns `false` for `{:id 7 :name "Bob"}` and `{:a 1}`.

The JVM `parse-payload` still reads all three as EDN, because its JSON arm is EDN.

EXECUTED in node, mirroring the CLJS arm (the same regex, then `JSON.parse`): the three matched EDN payloads throw `SyntaxError` ("Expected property name or '}'" and "Expected ',' or ']' after array element"). The control is real JSON `{"a":1,"b":"two"}`, which parses.

The CLJS branch itself was not compiled here; its behaviour is inspected plus mirrored. The existing tests (`test/re_frame/story/ui/dispatch_console_cljs_test.cljc:47-73`) cover `{:a 1}` and `[1 2 3]` only.

Dedup: there is no open or closed bead on the payload heuristic.

## Smallest fix

Try EDN first and fall back to JSON only when EDN reading fails (CLJS only). Or tighten the heuristic so that the quoted token must directly follow `{` or `,` and be followed by a colon with no space before a keyword. EDN-first is the simplest and cannot misroute valid EDN.

Fence: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/dispatch_console.cljc` (plus its test). No hot-zone file.

## Gates

The behaviour change sits in the `#?(:cljs ...)` arm (`parse-json-cljs` and its use in `parse-payload`), which is compiled only by the CLJS lane (`npm run test:cljs`). A JVM green says nothing about it. `looks-like-json?` itself is common code and JVM-testable via `clojure -M:test` in `tools/story`.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fix — PR #10326 (worker story-ev-3x7nj, 2026-09-24)

Re-verified at trunk 63e118215c. On the JVM, `looks-like-json?` returns true for `{:email "a@b.c" :password "hunter2"}`, `{:name "Bob" :id 7}` and `["a" :b]`, and false for `{:id 7 :name "Bob"}`.

Fix, in the CLJS arm only: `parse-json-cljs` now reads EDN when `JSON.parse` refuses the payload. The `looks-like-json?` docstring now calls it a pre-filter rather than an unambiguous discriminator.

The item's suggested EDN-FIRST order was NOT taken. Compact JSON is often readable EDN, so EDN-first misroutes it silently:
- measured on the JVM, `clojure.edn` reads `{"id":7}` as `{"id" :7}` and `{"id":7,"ok":true,"none":null}` as `{"id" :7, "ok" :true, "none" :null}`;
- CLJS `clojure.edn` is tools.reader, whose `parse-symbol` returns `[nil "7"]` for the token `7`, so `:7` is a keyword there too;
- JSON-first is kept, and a CLJS row pins `{"id":7,"ok":true,"none":null}` → `{:id 7 :ok true :none nil}`.

The trade-off is that only EDN that is ALSO valid JSON (e.g. a string key followed by `:1`) now reads as JSON.

Regression (in `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/dispatch_console_cljs_test.cljc`): `parse-payload-edn-with-a-string-before-a-keyword` (both runtimes) and `parse-payload-compact-json-stays-json-cljs`. Control: CI's node lane ran them WITHOUT the fix (first push of #10326) and read 3 failures, all in the new EDN row, each `[:error "SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON ..."]` (or `Expected ',' or ']'` for the vector). With the fix the node lane read 12703 tests / 64011 assertions, 0 failures.
Merged-PR audit #10326 (ed48977d96e1d92e1642f4a1fc88c3455e1c20e5; merged 2026-09-24T00:45:32Z). Completeness: All four evidence-surface claims addressed: generated expectation variants redeclare child-only script/plays; a stable per-cell boundary renders captured failure and resets for changed inputs; EDN false positives recover after JSON refusal; only the top mounted trap handles Escape. The source explicitly permitted dropping the optional substrate assertion clause; both corresponding spec claims are removed. Correctness: Accepted author final Story 2077 tests/7801 assertions and successful CI, including real browser boundary/isolation/remount/recovery and stacked-Escape regressions. Negative controls recorded 10 browser failures, 3 node payload failures, and 4 snippet replay failures. Read all production changes and affected spec hunks. No concrete remaining defect; no reruns. Implementation quality: Small boundary-local fixes reuse existing rendering, parsing and snippet helpers. JSON-first fallback preserves compact JSON semantics; the dialog stack is minimal and unmount cleanup removes the exact handler. No unnecessary framework or API expansion. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

title: xray/http: a by-design :request-id supersession paints the superseding event ERROR — :rf.http/aborted :reason :request-id-superseded is catalogued :error, so the event reads ✗, washes, and counts as a ribbon issue
description:
## Defect

A by-design managed-HTTP SUPERSESSION paints the superseding event as an ERROR in Xray. When a request reuses a `:request-id` whose earlier request is still in flight — the ordinary typeahead / search-as-you-type idiom — the runtime aborts the superseded request from inside the NEW request's issuing handler, and the abort choke emits `:rf.http/aborted` at `:error` with `:reason :request-id-superseded`. That row lands in the superseding event's bundle, so every superseding event gets:

- the Epoch / event status `✗` ERROR (`event-status-colour/event-bundle-outcome` reads `:error`);
- the L2 row's pink issue wash;
- an `:error` entry in `:rf.xray/issues-ribbon`, and so the auto-open-on-error trigger when that setting is on (default OFF) and Xray is hidden.

Nothing failed: supersession is Spec 014's designed replacement ("the new request replaces the old"), the superseded request's reply is deliberately suppressed, and the runtime ALSO emits the canonical `:rf.http/stale-suppressed` `:info` row recording exactly that (spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2296, which describes it as complementing the aborted trace).

Discovered while ruling rf2-3x7nj.24.1 (`:info` traces are not issues). That ruling makes Xray read the producer's severity verbatim — `:warning`/`:error` are issues, `:info` is not — and deliberately leaves this alone, because here the producer itself says `:error`. After it lands, this is the remaining healthy-path source of red in an HTTP-heavy app. Both the rf2-3x7nj.24.1 dossier and its independent Codex review named it as a separate question; neither filed it.

## Evidence

EXECUTED at trunk a61f903c5c (bounded JVM probe, real runtime on the plain-atom substrate, core + http from the mayor checkout, a local HttpServer that holds each request until released; two `dispatch-sync`s of `[:probe/search q]`, whose handler returns `{:fx [[:rf.http/managed {:request {...} :request-id :probe/search :reply-to [:probe/reply]}]]}`; traces grouped by `re-frame.trace.projection/group-by-event`, then the real Xray helpers; exit 0):

    [:probe/search "a"]   :other [[:rf.http/issued :info]]                                      issues [:advisory]               wash true  outcome :ok
    [:probe/search "ab"]  :other [[:rf.http/issued :info]
                                  [:rf.http/aborted :error :request-id-superseded]
                                  [:rf.http/stale-suppressed :info]]                            issues [:advisory :error :advisory]  wash true  outcome :error
    [:probe/reply ...]    :other []                                                             issues []                         wash false outcome :ok

(The `:advisory` entries go away under the rf2-3x7nj.24.1 ruling; the `:error` entry and the `:error` outcome do not.)

Where, at a61f903c5c:
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:517-518`: inside the issuing handler, `(rf.http.registry/supersede! frame-id request-id)`.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:643`: `((:abort-fn superseded-handle) :request-id-superseded)`.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc` abort choke (docstring :740-758, emit `(rf.trace/emit-error! :rf.http/aborted redacted)` a few lines below): one emit for every abort reason, including the reply-suppressing ones (`reply-suppressing-abort-reasons`, :105: `#{:request-id-superseded :epoch-restored :frame-destroyed}`).
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2295 catalogues `:rf.http/aborted` as `:error` for all six reasons.
- Consumers: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/issues_ribbon_helpers.cljc` `op-type->severity` / `issue-event?`; `panels/l2_timeline.cljc` `event-bundle-has-issue?`; `panels/event/event_status_colour.cljc` `event-bundle-outcome`.

Inspected, not executed: whether `:epoch-restored` and `:frame-destroyed` aborts land in a user-visible bundle the same way (they are emitted from `re-frame.http.registry`'s restore / frame-destroy walks), and whether an `:actor-destroyed` abort whose target is obsolete reads the same (it fires `:rf.http/aborted` beside `:rf.http/stale-suppressed`, 009:2295-2296).

## Decision needed

Yes. Which side moves — or neither:

- **(1) Producer.** The reply-suppressing, by-design abort reasons (`:request-id-superseded`, and perhaps `:epoch-restored` / `:frame-destroyed`) stop emitting `:rf.http/aborted` at `:error`: emit it at `:info`, or drop it for those reasons since `:rf.http/stale-suppressed` already records the suppression. Touches HOT-ZONE `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (the `:rf.http/aborted` catalogue row) and `implementation/http`; changes what pair-MCP's `:severity :error` filter returns.
- **(2) Xray.** Classify `:rf.http/aborted` by `:reason` and exclude the by-design reasons from the issue set. No hot zone, but it is a per-reason allowlist beside the producer's severity — the shape rf2-3x7nj.24.1 rejected as a standing classification burden.
- **(3) Accept.** A supersession is an abort and the row says why; the programmer reads `:reason`. No change.

Priority is low: it affects only apps that reuse a `:request-id` while a request is in flight, and it fails loud (a spurious red), never silent.

title: INCOMPLETE: artifact replay still skips schema and causal assertion verdicts
description: PR #10321 claims every artifact event-program assertion is evaluated. At merge 982fb2ce41a7163eab03e24255f5ac7967aa6f6a, artifact.cljc:301-315 delegates non-dispatch steps to exec-step!, but runner_events.cljc:955-959 intentionally returns step-skip for schema-error and causal/cascade assertions because the live result boundary owns their verdict. artifact/replay-result:420-448 only normalizes accumulator/step-failure records and checks the raw tape floor; project-evidence projects evidence without evaluating declarations. It never collects the event-program tape assertions or calls the existing schema/causal matchers. Therefore an expected schema violation that never occurs (empty tape) still yields :pass with no assertion record, and an unproven causal checkpoint also disappears. A matching expected schema violation instead remains unconsumed and can falsely fail. This is a source-traced residual of .31.1, not a claim that the reported 2075/7792 Story tests failed; those added cases exercise path-equals, wait-until and click. Correction: feed the artifact program tape-evaluated assertions through the existing result matchers, including consumed schema selectors and honest causal evidence refusals; preserve unified assertion/status behavior without a second assertion engine. Add focused replay coverage for missing/matching expected schema violations and a causal checkpoint with unavailable evidence.

title: INCOMPLETE: flow validation explanations bypass registry size elision
description: PR #10328 correctly fixes sensitive flow-output explanations, but explicitly leaves the size axis from the source finding unimplemented. At merge 10a499c3a61e13bce5e6913b59dfce067ff114db, flows.cljc:158-162 elides :value at the registered :output-path while inserting the explainer result unchanged. The added sensitive-output? deliberately uses :rf.egress/include-large? true and changes only sensitive outputs. Thus a non-sensitive output with a registry :large declaration and a failing walkable schema has an elided :value beside an :explain that re-ships the large value in Malli :value / :errors[*].:value. The schema seam sees schema props rather than the frame registry. Repeated invalid large derived values can therefore bloat trace buffers and tool responses despite the author opting into size elision. This residual is acknowledged in the PR and closed source Bead; no exact OPEN Bead found. The privacy correction itself is accepted. Correction: apply existing size-elision policy to the explanation when the output is registry-size-classified, using an honest existing marker/path/handle convention; preserve sensitive-wins precedence and ordinary unclassified explanations. Keep the fix local, with a focused registry-large failing-output regression and an unclassified control. Evidence is source inspection plus the implementer's explicit scope statement; no additional test suite rerun.
notes:
WORKER (flowsize-3x7nj, 2026-09-24): FIXED in PR #10346 (commit "fix(flows): a registry-large flow output's failure :explain carries a size marker, not the value (rf2-srvio)"), fenced to implementation/flows plus one clause in spec/013-Flows.md. No core change.

REPRODUCED at trunk ca56aeab4d, with the regression test written first. The JVM run gave 10 failures, all in the new regression. A flow with :large [[]] and a failing vector Malli schema emitted a :value that was the walker's :rf.size/large-elided marker, while :explain carried {:schema [:map [:n :int]], :value {:blob "BLOB-BLOB-...", :n "not-an-int"}, :errors (...)} raw, and the trace had no :large? stamp.

FIX, in validate-output! in implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc. This applies the existing validation size-safety policy (Spec 010 §:large?), with the frame's registry as the classifier instead of the schema.
- When it fires: the elide-wire-value walk that produces :value placed a :rf.size/large-elided marker in the output. The walker decides, so every declaration it honours counts, just as sensitive-output? does for the other axis.
- What happens: :explain is replaced whole by a marker, and the trace is stamped :large? true.
- A declaration covering the whole output (at :output-path or above it) reuses the walker's own marker, identical to :value.
- A narrower declaration gets rf.elision/->marker for the whole output. Its :path is :output-path and its :handle is [:rf.elision/at <output-path>]. Its :reason is the declaring source the walker's markers carry, chosen by rf.elision/owners->provenance. Its :hint is nil, as Spec 010's arm does.
- No new marker shape.
- Precedence: sensitive wins. The existing registry-sensitive arm still runs first. The size arm is also skipped when the schemas seam already stamped :sensitive? (a schema :sensitive? prop, or the opaque-schema fail-closed arm).
- An unclassified output keeps its raw :explain.

TESTS, in implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_schema_validation_test.clj:

title: machines: spawn-done-event-id docstring still says an error leaf routes as a failure only when the parent declares :on-error
description:
## Defect

PR #10351 (rf2-3x7nj.41.1, merged at trunk 089680d239) made every single-`:spawn` failure go out as `[:rf.machine.spawn/error …]`, whether or not the parent declares `:on-error`. The docstring of `spawn-done-event-id` in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` (around line 154) was outside that worker's fence, and it still says the old rule: an error leaf becomes a failure event only when the parent declares `:on-error`. It now contradicts the code and spec/005.

## Correction

Re-word that docstring to the rule as landed: a single-`:spawn` child's error leaf, or a thrown action, always routes as `:rf.machine.spawn/error`. A join child's failure stays on the done carrier with `:error? true` for the join's bookkeeping, and its per-child `:on-done` does not run. This is a docstring change only.

Search `implementation/machines` for any other docstring or comment still stating the `:on-error`-conditional rule, and fix each one the same way. Use a discriminator: comments that describe the historical rule as history are left alone. List each hit and its verdict.

## Decision needed

No.

title: xstate-parity dim E: tooling, serialization, testing, inspection and validation parity
description:

title: machines-viz: grammar mirror accepts bad :spawn :on-error / :on-done VALUES the engine refuses (nil, number, string, fn :on-error)
description:
## What

Worker mviz3-4v2t6 reported this while projecting the transition-shaped `:spawn :on-done` (rf2-4v2t6, PR #10409). The machines-viz grammar mirror does not copy the engine's refusal of a bad VALUE for `:spawn :on-error` or `:spawn :on-done`:
- for `nil`, a plain number or a plain string, the engine refuses and the viz accepts;
- the viz also accepts a fn `:on-error`, which the engine refuses.

The `:on-error` half predates PR #10409. That PR added only the TARGET check and the transition-map key check for a non-fn `:spawn :on-done`, which is what its bead asked for.

- Red-first.

title: spec/009: fresco-revision-not-controlled row should say a nil :value on a text field is the empty field (accepted)
description:
## What

`spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, the `:rf.error/fresco-revision-not-controlled` row of the error catalogue, says the element "is then refused unless it is an `input` or `textarea` carrying a non-nil `:value` to re-baseline TO". Since rf2-3x7nj.7.1 that sentence mis-predicts one case. An author writing `[:input {:value nil ::h/revision r}]` on a text field (for example `forms/buffered-field` for a todo with no title) is now ACCEPTED, because `re-frame.fresco.impl.controlled/install!` first makes a nil `:value` on a content-valued field the empty string `""` (`empty-when-nil!`).

## The correction

Add one clause to that row, for example: "a nil `:value` on a text field (a `<textarea>`, or an `<input>` whose type is not a token, label or filename type) is the empty field `""` and is accepted; a nil `:value` on a checkbox, radio, hidden, submit, reset, button, image or file input stays no value and is refused like a value-less one."

The rest of the row still holds as written: the acceptance predicate is still the one that selects the shadow component, and it still requires a non-nil EMITTED `value`. `docs/design/fresco/studio/revision-prop-spec.md` section 3.5 already says "non-nil emitted `value`" and needs no edit.

## Why it was not in the fixing PR

`spec/009-Instrumentation.md` is a hot-zone file, and the fixing dispatch was fenced to `implementation/fresco/` source and tests. Sequence this with any other spec/009 edit in flight.

## Gate

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py --verbose`, plus `mkdocs build --strict` (spec/ is staged into the site by `mkdocs_hooks.py`). The row is inside a table, so check its column count by hand.

title: INCOMPLETE: misplaced :regions still bypasses registration and can throw host errors
description:
Audit of PR #10464 at 62b75475c066d5be1d09e684dc5547c4f60d7b29. The scoped structure checks, transition-value checks and error-catalogue corrections fix rf2-uohfb, rf2-sbtv3 and rf2-ehitw. Evidence: a flat definition such as {:initial :a :regions {:r 42} :states {:a {}}} still escapes with a raw host exception in validate-timeouts!, as reported and ruled actionable on rf2-0br7z. The new lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc validate-definition-shape! accepts :regions whenever its outer value is a map, but checks and descends through the region bodies only when parallel/parallel? recognizes the root. It therefore passes this misplaced map to timeout.cljc:445-474, whose root/region validation and traversal consume :regions without requiring :type :parallel. A well-shaped :regions map on a non-parallel node can instead register silently while the runtime ignores it. Forgetting :type :parallel thus produces either lost declaration intent or a host stack trace rather than the named registration refusal the new boundary promises.

Required correction: follow rf2-0br7z's narrow ruling: refuse :regions at unsupported non-parallel positions before any consuming walker, reuse the existing unread-slot registration category appropriate to that position, and include the :type :parallel hint in the existing diagnostic message/payload. Preserve currently supported parallel definitions and flat definitions without :regions. Add focused public-registration regressions for both a well-shaped misplaced map and the demonstrated malformed body, with valid-position controls and a fix-removed check. No new category, general validation framework, or viz grammar expansion is requested. The implementer's measurements and original tests are accepted; no tests were rerun during this audit.

4. So `(assert-path-equals path v)` compares against nil and raises no error. A test assertion passes or fails against the wrong value, silently.

## Fix

- Normalise through `frame-target->id` in `resolve-frame`.
- Check every other helper that shares `resolve-frame`, and any that resolve a frame some other way, for the same object-vs-id gap.
- Add a regression: inside `with-new-frame`, `assert-path-equals` sees the frame's real app-db, both matching and mismatching. It must fail on trunk.
- Then `docs/api/re-frame.test-support.md` should say that `{:frame …}` accepts either form, a frame id or a frame object.
- The Core guide currently works around the bug by passing an explicit `{:frame :id}`. Once fixed, that workaround can stay or be simplified; say which.

Re-derive every file:line at your trunk.
