Commit 42da696b15 ("fix(ssr): SSR derived values release their inputs when disposed"). The smallest shape, as briefed. Folding ssr/adapter into plain-atom is untouched and stays Mike's call.

FIX. implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/substrate.cljc drops its IDeref-only `ssr-make-derived-value`. It uses `re-frame.substrate.plain-atom/make-derived-value` (now public, with a docstring), which is a JVM Reaction and a CLJS IDisposable reify, and on CLJS it calls the new `plain-atom/route-disposal-hooks!` for its own adapter map. That fn is the routing plain-atom already did for itself, extracted so both adapters share it. A routed hook answers only for the installed adapter, which is why SSR has to route the hooks itself. Spec 006 §make-derived-value "Disposable result" now says the plain-atom value "which the SSR adapter reuses" reifies IDisposable. The three docs pages that install ssr/adapter needed no change.

title: Make the stale timer the freshness wake: held :rf.resource/stale? flips at :stale-at (wake marker, no :revision bump; hydration, revival and still-fresh re-arm for the remaining window)
description:
## Bug

A held `[:rf.resource/stale? q]` (and the `:stale?` field of `[:rf/resource q]`) keeps reading `false` after the entry's `:stale-at` deadline passes. The stale timer fires on time, but its handler writes nothing, so nothing the sub depends on changes. The value flips only when some unrelated event commits a change to app-db. A component that mounts after the deadline reads `false` too, because `subscribe` returns the cached reaction. Users see a "fresh" badge on stale data for as long as the app stays quiet.

## Evidence

Code at 475bdcaacf:
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:3455-3505`: `stale-fired-handler` re-checks the entry, emits the `:rf.resource/stale-fired` trace, and returns `{:rf.db/runtime runtime-db}` unchanged. Its docstring (`:3472-3473`) claims "the durable `:stale-at` already makes the `:stale?` sub true (no write needed)". The probe below refutes that.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:143-154`: the sub compares `:stale-at` against the wall clock (`rf.interop/epoch-now-ms`) inside its body.
- `subs.cljc:476-493`: every resource sub is a `reg-frame-state-sub`. Its only input is the frame-state value.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc:608-619`: the body does not re-run when its input is `=` to the last one seen. So the clock is a hidden input the memo cannot see.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1926`: a commit that leaves both partitions `identical?` installs nothing. The stale timer's event is exactly that kind of commit.
- `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_invalidation_gc_cljs_test.cljc:356-365` (`stale-fired-rechecks-durable-fact-no-write`) pins the no-write behaviour.

Repro (*probed*: JVM, plain-atom substrate, run at 989a1c6d53, whose core and resources trees are identical to 475bdcaacf):

```clojure
(rf/reg-resource :probe/article
  {:scope :rf.scope/global :params-schema [:map [:slug :string]] :stale-after-ms 300}
  (fn [{:keys [slug]} _] {:request {:method :get :url (str "/a/" slug)}}))
;; ensure under an owner, then dispatch :rf.resource.internal/succeeded for the current work
(def held (rf/subscribe [:rf.resource/stale? q]))
@held                                                          ;; t0
(Thread/sleep 600)
@held                                                          ;; past the deadline
(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.resource.internal/stale-fired {:resource/key k}])
@held  @(rf/subscribe [:rf.resource/stale? q])
(rf/dispatch-sync [:probe/unrelated])                          ;; writes an unrelated app-db key

```

Observed:

```
A t0: held stale?= false  model :stale?= false  stale-at - now = 274
B after deadline, no event: held stale?= false  truth(entry-stale? now)= true
C after stale-fired: held stale?= false  model :stale?= false  fresh-subscribe= false  frame-state identical? to t0: true
D after unrelated app-db event: held stale?= true  model :stale?= true
```

Contract:
- Spec 016 §Freshness clock contract (`spec/016-Resources.md:1230`) declares this behaviour **by design**: "the sub re-runs on frame commits, not on wall-clock boundaries … a view that needs a live badge arms `:poll-interval-ms` or an app timer".
- That sentence does not cover a component that mounts after the deadline, which also reads `false` (row C). Its remedy works only if the app timer writes state, because an event that changes nothing installs nothing.
- The stale timer's own docstring states the opposite of the observed behaviour.

## Expected

Once a stale timer's re-check finds the entry stale, every held or newly created freshness read of that entry returns `true`, without a fetch and without a status change.

## Fix direction

This is Mike's decision, because spec 016:1230 currently rules the behaviour by design.
- **Recommended (both reviews):** make the stale timer the freshness wake. On a `:now-stale` re-check, write one entry fact so the frame-state changes and freshness subs recompute. For example, stamp the entry with the time the stale boundary was crossed.
  - The write must not bump `:revision`.
  - An obsolete wake (the entry was reloaded or removed) keeps its no-op.
  - Keep `:stale-at` as the authoritative deadline, and keep `entry-stale?` as the one derivation.
  - Replace the `stale-fired-rechecks-durable-fact-no-write` test, and rewrite consequence (1) at 016:1230 plus the handler docstring.
- **Alternative:** keep the spec. Then correct the handler docstring, and correct the spec's "app timer" remedy to say the timer must write app-db.

## Acceptance

  2. Hold `[:rf.resource/stale? q]` and `[:rf/resource q]`, and advance the clock past `:stale-at`.

- A wake for an entry reloaded since the timer armed leaves freshness `false` and writes nothing.

Frame-state therefore changes, so every held OR newly mounted `[:rf.resource/stale? q]` / `[:rf/resource q]` read flips at the deadline (to timer accuracy) — with no `:revision` bump, no `:status` change, no fetch. Three scheduling completions make the wake reach the ordinary paths, each arming for the REMAINING window (`:stale-at` minus now), not the full `:stale-after-ms`: (1) client hydration arms a stale timer; (2) a fresh-skip that revives an owner-free entry re-arms for the remaining window; (3) a still-fresh re-check re-arms itself for the remaining window, so the timer chases a deadline that moved later without a re-arm (an optimistic patch, or wall-clock drift). Spec 016's "by design" consequence (1) at 016:1231 is rewritten to match.

WHY:

It bites in the quiet case — a dashboard left alone, a second monitor. Returning to the tab hides most of it, because the focus scan refetches active-owner stale entries and that commit re-runs the subs.
- Prior art: TanStack Query `queryObserver.ts` `#updateStaleTimeout` arms `setTimeout(() => { if (!this.#currentResult.isStale) { this.updateResult() } }, timeUntilStale(...))` — scheduled against the REMAINING deadline (`timeUntilStale`, `utils.ts`); its stale timeout updates the observer result while a separate interval path refetches. Spec 016's stated TanStack divergence (016:1229) is about the default `staleTime`, not this.
- Behavioural consequence: an app that reacts to `:stale?` changing (a flow, a view that dispatches a refetch) now reacts at the deadline rather than at the next unrelated commit — which is what such an app meant. Stale-while-revalidate is unchanged: stale data stays on screen and the timer still fetches nothing. Polling is independent and unchanged.
- Each crossing adds one commit and one dev-history epoch per entry. A hidden tab may throttle the timer; the focus scan on return covers it.
- Rollback needs no timer arming once (3) exists: an optimistic apply touches no timers, so the entry's original timer survives. If it fires before the rollback, it finds the patched deadline still future and re-arms for it, and the restored earlier deadline is by then already past, so the rollback's own commit shows stale. If the rollback comes first, the original timer fires at the restored deadline and wakes. A rollback that restores a snapshot without the marker loses nothing.
- ACCEPTED RESIDUAL (best-effort; not filed): an optimistic `:patch` onto an entry whose deadline had ALREADY passed (so no live stale timer) moves the deadline into the future; if the mutation's success neither patches / populates / removes nor invalidates that key, no timer covers the new deadline and the badge reads fresh past it until the next commit. Narrow — an optimistic mutation that trusts its guess with no success reconciliation, applied to stale data — and closing it needs a conditional apply-time arm the stance does not justify. Likewise an optimistic seed pending longer than its window is covered late, at settle.
- Restore: 016:1744 clears host timers without rebuilding them (an accepted dev-tool limitation), so a restored entry crossing its deadline gets no wake until a later operation re-arms. Expanding restore's timer policy is a separate decision; not part of this work.
- Server: a `:server` frame arms no timers (schedule-timers' `:server?` flag, and `rearm-timers-after-hydration!` refuses a server frame), so the marker is never set on the server and never rides the SSR wire.
- If Option C is ever reopened it needs its own bead covering the timer-trust MUST at 016:1236, hydration and restore arming, and the Xray panel's `derive-stale?` copy.
- Effect on beads: this bead stays open for one worker / one PR; it unblocks nothing else.

Implemented as ruled. No deviation from the ruling's guidance.

title: Pair build can stamp a running shadow daemon's old commit instead of the compiled source
description:
Merged-PR audit #11052; follow-up to rf2-hxwy0.10. The new :built-from value is not reliably the source commit on the supported persistent shadow-cljs path.

Evidence: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/scripts/build.cjs obtains current HEAD, then only sets RF2_PAIR_MCP_BUILT_FROM on the new Node CLI child. shadow-cljs.edn reads it with #shadow/env. An existing shadow server evaluates that reader in its own JVM environment, which cannot inherit the later CLI child's environment. The pinned shadow-cljs 3.4.10 jar's shadow/cljs/config_env.cljc uses System/getenv, and config.clj re-reads the build in that process. The official guide explicitly documents that an existing server's environment wins and that --config-merge avoids this limitation: https://shadow-cljs.github.io/docs/UsersGuide.html#_using_environment_variables . Both wrapper and env reader remain unchanged on current origin/main. Live tracker search found only the closed source owner for this fingerprint, no open fix owner.

Concrete failure: start the package's shadow server/watch before this wrapper supplies the variable, then run npm run build at commit B. The wrapper logs B but the server build receives unknown. Or start the daemon with commit A, advance to B and rebuild: newly compiled B code can still report A. The skill then mistakes a freshly rebuilt server for a stale one and repeats the rebuild/session restart instruction. The stub test observes the new child's environment and cannot catch this, while CI compiles only the unknown/default path; the PR explicitly reports no real stamped build verification.

Proposed action: pass the SHA as a per-invocation compiler configuration override (for example shadow-cljs --config-merge), preserving the deliberate unknown fallback when git is unavailable. Do not require stopping a shared daemon or change tool-contract semantics. With the build lane granted, verify the returned instructions fingerprint from an actual compiled server while reusing one daemon across two distinct source commits; the second build must report the second commit. Keep any regression coverage focused on this path, with no general build-metadata framework.

Validation here: source inspection, pinned dependency reader and primary documentation; no local shadow-cljs run was started because this worker has no lane grant.

title: Production error :source-coord names whichever namespace registered the id last, not the implementation that threw
description:
## Bug

A production error record's `:source-coord` comes from a process-global `[kind id]` table that whichever `reg-*` macro ran last overwrites. It does not come from the implementation that executed and failed. Two cases follow:
- When two namespaces register one id (explicit images selecting different namespaces, or a frame frozen by a cross-namespace move), errors from one implementation point at the other's file and line.
- A programmatic re-registration keeps the previous macro registration's location.

The people affected are those who follow the error: Sentry-style shippers, Xray's jump-to-source, and AI pairs.

## Evidence

**Where (trunk 475bdcaacf):**
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:629-630`: `register!` calls `remember-error-coords!` only when `*pending-coords*` is bound (the macro path). A programmatic registration leaves the old entry in place.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc:486-515`: `error-coords-by-id` is a single `kind → id → coords` atom. `remember-error-coords!` does `assoc-in [kind id]`, and `error-coords-for` reads it back.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:419-436`: the error record's coordinate is looked up by category, id and op through `error-coords-for`. It never consults the executing descriptor or the frame's generation.

**Repro (*probed*):** JVM, `clojure -M` from `implementation/core`, plain-atom adapter, one error listener. Run at HEAD 9b20bf0093, whose `implementation/core` is byte-identical to 475bdcaacf.

```clojure
(ns probe.ca) (rf/reg-event :c/ev (fn [_ _] (throw (ex-info "thrown by probe.ca's handler" {}))))
(ns probe.cb) (rf/reg-event :c/ev (fn [_ _] (throw (ex-info "thrown by probe.cb's handler" {}))))
(rf/make-frame {:id :frame/a :images [(rf/image {:id :img/a :select-ns {:include ["probe.ca"]}})]})
(rf/make-frame {:id :frame/b :images [(rf/image {:id :img/b :select-ns {:include ["probe.cb"]}})]})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:c/ev] {:frame :frame/a})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:c/ev] {:frame :frame/b})
```

Observed error records:

```
{:frame :frame/a, :error :rf.error/handler-exception, :msg "thrown by probe.ca's handler", :coord-ns probe.cb, :coord-line 17}
{:frame :frame/b, :error :rf.error/handler-exception, :msg "thrown by probe.cb's handler", :coord-ns probe.cb, :coord-line 17}
```

`:frame/a` ran `probe.ca`'s handler, but its record points at `probe.cb` line 17.

The same happens after a cross-namespace move (*probed* with rf2-mn2ht.16's repro). The frozen frame still executes `probe.a`'s handler, while `(sc/error-coords-for :event :probe/ev)` returns `:ns probe.b`.

**Contract:** `spec/001-Registration.md:198-204` (Policy B) requires source coordinates to survive production elision for error emission. That requirement is sound. It prescribes a parallel registry keyed `[kind id]`, and that key is the defect: the spec also lets one `[kind id]` have several live implementations, chosen per frame by images (`spec/002-Frames.md` §Image resolution and composition).

## Expected

An error record's `:source-coord` names the file and line of the implementation that actually ran, in every build.

## Fix direction

- Carry a slim, private coordinate payload (`{:ns :file :line}`) on the retained descriptor: the source-store slot, and inline descriptors. It then rides into the sealed generation with the implementation.
- Have error-emit take the coordinate from the descriptor that executed (the lookup the failing frame performed), not from the global table.
- A programmatic registration carries no coordinate, so it reports none rather than a stale one.
- Keep public production metadata elision as it is.
- Rewrite `spec/001-Registration.md` §198-204 so the coordinate belongs to the descriptor. The global table can then go, unless another reader needs it.

## Acceptance

- New test using the two-image repro above, in either registration order. Each frame's error record names its own namespace and line. It fails at trunk.
- After a cross-namespace move (rf2-mn2ht.16's repro), an error thrown by the frozen frame names `probe.a`.
- A programmatic re-registration of a macro-registered id produces a record with no stale `:source-coord`.
- The core production-gate lane still sees `{:ns :file :line}` on the tight error record (no `:column`), as `spec/001-Registration.md:234` requires.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (sol/02 §5); probed during the cross-review.
- Related: rf2-mn2ht.16 (same move scenario). Sol 09 §2 covers a separate realm ambiguity in the same lookup (an event and a sub sharing an id), which is not part of this bead.
- Hot zones: none. `spec/001-Registration.md` is not on the hot-zone list.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/core-frames-registration.md` Insight 9, D3 and A2; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/02-core-registration-images.md` §5.

== DISPATCHED (mayor, 2026-10-10 18:29:23 AUSEST) == Clustered with rf2-mn2ht.18, .19 and .17 for one worker on worktree core-images-review, branch worker/core-images-review, one PR. That worker is the only toucher of spec/002-Frames.md for now. Do not dispatch a second worker onto it until that worker reports.
== FIXED (worker core-images-review, 2026-10-10) == PR #11057 (branch worker/core-images-review), commit b8ecdb1d6f.
Premise held at base 02018bf667: with probe.ca and probe.cb both registering one event id, frames selecting each namespace both reported the last registrant's coord; a frame frozen by a cross-namespace move reported the namespace it no longer runs; a programmatic re-registration kept the replaced macro registration's coord.
Fix: registrar/register! attaches the bound *pending-coords* to the stored descriptor via source-coords/with-registration-coords, as Clojure metadata on the descriptor map (a key would surface through rf/handler-meta in production, against Policy A). The descriptor carries it into the source store and every sealed generation. error-emit reads it with source-coords/registration-coords off rf.registrar/lookup run inside the failing frame's call-with-frame-resolution, with the existing event/sub realm pivot unchanged. No macro on the stack means no coordinate (a re-registration does not inherit one).
The process-wide [kind id] table (error-coords-for) STAYS: tools/story element_inspector reads it for a view's :file fallback, outside this worker's fence. Error emission no longer reads it. Inline image descriptors carry no coordinate (rf/image captures none per entry), so an inline implementation's error reports none rather than another registration's.
Tests: new error_record_source_coord_cljs_test (two images in both registration orders, frozen-by-move frame names coord.move-a, programmatic re-registration reports no coord, real reg-* macro reports {:ns :file :line} plus :column only in dev; it is on the prod-gate roster). on_error_cljs_test and observability_routing_cljs_test planted coords by seeding the table; they now plant them on the registration (the macro's *pending-coords* binding around the fn form).
Red before (fix absent): exit 1, 4 failures. Green: exit 0. Red again (registrar, source_coords, error_emit reverted): exit 1, 4 failures; restores verified by blob hash.
Spec: 001 Production elision contract item 2 and the classification-table row now put the coordinate on the descriptor and name the table as a tooling index; 009 line on production-surviving coordinates (hot file) now says the record reads the descriptor the failing frame resolved.
Out of scope, untouched: the event/sub realm ambiguity, and the default-projection architecture.
Not this worker's to change, for follow-up: router.cljc comment near the frame-destroyed emit still says the record reads its coords off the parallel error-coord registry (router.cljc fenced to the routing worker); skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/event-state-cycle.md says the record's coord comes from the error-coords-by-id registry; spec/015 :source-coord row, spec/Privacy.md item 1 and spec/Spec-Schemas.md trigger-handler paragraph call sink 2 the always-on error-coord registry (still true that it is retained, but the name now means the descriptor's coordinate).
Merged-PR audit #11057: follow-up rf2-0vp6s — Error source-coord can name a replacement registered while the throwing implementation is still running. This is a separate open finding; the source status and ruling are preserved.
close_reason: Merged as PR #11057 at 102b518249 (commit b8ecdb1d6f). Each registration carries its own source coordinate, and the error record reads it from the implementation the failing frame actually ran; a programmatic re-registration reports no coordinate. The global [kind id] table stays (Story's element inspector reads it) but error emission no longer uses it. Spec 001 Policy B rewritten; Spec 009's production source-coordinate sentence updated. Red at base exit 1, green exit 0, red again exit 1. Core JVM lane 1219/3606 -> 1227/3626; CI :node-test +8/+20 as predicted. Stale "error-coord registry" wording elsewhere filed as a follow-up.

title: Spec 002 L15 says all frames share one global handler registrar; frames resolve through their own sealed image generation
description:
Filed 2026-10-11 16:27:57 AUSEST at HEAD 82e4037dc7, as a follow-up to the Opus adversarial review (core-frames-registration report, insight 2 / action A3). It is residue of rf2-yiozf. Evidence below was read at HEAD.

## Problem

`spec/002-Frames.md:15` says:

> All frames share **one global handler registrar**. Multi-frame means "multiple instances of the same app's handlers" … not "multiple different apps with different handler sets on one page." The latter use case … is out of scope

That contradicts 002 §Image resolution and composition as rf2-yiozf rewrote it (PR #11119). Registrations go into one process-global SOURCE STORE, and each frame resolves through its own sealed resolved image generation. Frames built with different `:images` therefore can run different handler sets, and composing different handler sets is what explicit images are for. An AI pair reading line 15 predicts the wrong model.

## Fix

Rewrite line 15 to agree with §Image resolution: one source store, per-frame resolution, explicit `:images` for distinct handler sets. Restate the scope line accordingly. Micro-frontends embedded in iframes can stay out of scope, but "different handler sets on one page" no longer can.

## Related, not verified at HEAD

The same review action names a second sentence. `spec/Conventions.md` (about line 1495) says the CLJS value-alias registration path loses only the call-site stamp. Per the review it also loses provenance (`source_store.cljc` about 266-283), so a value-alias registration is invisible to `:select-ns` images (`core.cljc` about 935-945). Check this at HEAD and fix it in the same PR if it holds.

## Notes

- `spec/002-Frames.md` and `spec/Conventions.md` are both HOT-ZONE files, so sequence this against any other bead touching them.
- If Mike takes the open "live default path" decision (filed alongside this bead), this region of 002 changes again. This bead only makes today's text true.
- Gates: `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.

title: Fresco reg-state rejects UUID instance keys, though the codec and the guide treat a UUID as the canonical entity id
description:
Filed 2026-10-12 22:50:01 AUSEST at HEAD 5162360cf2, from the Opus adversarial review (fresco, decision 7 / action 6) and cross-checked against Sol 22. Evidence below was read at HEAD.

## Problem

`re-frame.fresco.impl.state/instance-key?` (`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/state.cljc:114-128`) admits keywords, strings, numbers and recursive vectors of those, but not UUIDs:

    (boolean (or (keyword? k) (string? k) (number? k)
                 (and (vector? k) (every? instance-key? k))))

The same file teaches "domain ids first", and says a good React `:key` is a good instance key (about :56-67). The codec calls a UUID "the canonical entity id" and accepts it as a key (`impl/codec.cljs`, about :1111-1119). So an existing UUID can key a row but not that row's open flag, and `[:order/id uuid]` fails recursively too. Authors have to stringify an id just to use `h/reg-state`.

## Sol cross-check

Sol 22 found this independently and marks it "Act now" in its current-state audit (baseline 7ddb511367): "Admit UUID values in `state/instance-key?` and recursive composite keys; update the public guide's accepted-key sentence… Keep nil and map rejection." Opus agrees. Whether `reg-state` later moves off the view door (Opus action 6's second half, and Fresco open question 6) is a separate question, and the UUID fix lands either way.

## Fix direction

- Add `uuid?` to `instance-key?`, so it is admitted at the top level and inside vectors. Keep rejecting nil and maps.
- Update the docstring, the public guide's accepted-key sentence, and the `:rf.error/fresco-state-bad-argument` row's wording if it enumerates the shapes. That row is in spec/009, a hot-zone file.

## Verification

- Read, write and clear under two distinct UUIDs and under `[:order/id uuid]` stay independent and restore their defaults. This is red before the fix (bad-argument refusal) and green after.
- nil and map keys are still refused.
- Lane: `npm run test:cljs` for the `.cljc` CLJS branch, plus the JVM side if `state.cljc` has JVM tests.

## F3 — P2: M-0 describes Shadow's mutually selected dependency modes as additive

Owned sites: references/setup.md:86 and :193. :86 says deps.edn is the default when :deps is unspecified, then tells the migrator to edit deps.edn only. :193 says Shadow reads both files and :dependencies is additive.

Avoid instructing two independent edits as a substitute for knowing which classpath is active.

Acceptance: the two paragraphs agree with Shadow's mode switch; one focused migration fixture with both files and no :deps edits the standalone list (or performs an explicit, complete mode conversion), and a :deps true/map fixture edits the active deps.edn aliases while recognizing ignored Shadow lists. title: False continuation-coverage claim: flattened-list gate ignores escaped paragraphs
description:
Merged-PR audit #9615, landing 6c53bf433734f952bd10fa36ce248f7f7fd3a3cd. The new nested-LIST-ITEM detector and four repairs work. A distinct, consequential coverage claim does not: closed rf2-luch says the remaining continuation corpus is now gate-enforced and cannot grow; in-progress rf2-6ml6 says to run scripts/check_flattened_lists.py, fix the ESCAPED paragraphs it names and watch their count fall to zero.

The shipped gate does not enumerate continuation paragraphs. collect_items (line 202) matches only list markers, inject marks those items, and analyse (line 467) grades consecutive ITEM pairs. ESCAPED at lines 419-431 means a marked list-item line became code or left its li; it is not an escaped-continuation detector.

Independent evidence with the exact landed gate, shared fence scanner and MkDocs config verified by Git blob hash: a file containing '- parent', blank line, two-space 'escaped continuation paragraph', blank line, '- sibling' exits 0 while the real Markdown render puts that paragraph OUTSIDE every li. At four spaces it moves inside li and still exits 0. Control '- parent / two-space - child' exits 1; its four-space repair exits 0, so the instrument demonstrably runs and detects its actual class. On the real landed docs/api/re-frame.core.md:76, 'Declared inputs always arrive as a vector' renders outside li while the gate reports zero defects for the entire file. Full CI likewise says 291 scanned, 0 flattened, 1 unmeasurable while the PR explicitly leaves the continuation corpus unrepaired.

Provide a working continuation measurement for the existing rf2-6ml6 repair and explicitly correct the coverage guidance by follow-up, preserving its original record. A focused reusable detector or appropriate extension is sufficient; it must associate continuation blocks with source parents and rendered li ownership rather than rename this item-only count. Keep the already-dispatched corpus repair separate. The reported 450/438/12 counts were not independently recounted by this audit; do not treat them as a current gate result. Fresh 21-open-owner census found no exact coverage-defect owner. rf2-6ml6 is the document repair, not this missing instrument, and is in_progress; rf2-luch is closed. Neither is reopened or rewritten.
acceptance_criteria: A documented runnable check detects the escaped two-space continuation and the real re-frame.core.md:76 example, and passes their correctly nested versions. Retain a flattened-item positive control and fence/comment controls. Make the actual continuation scope and any unmeasurable files explicit so the corpus repair has a meaningful nonzero baseline and a defensible completion check. Append corrected coverage guidance/forward pointers without changing existing source statuses or normative closure records. No general Markdown framework or bulk document repair is required in this finding.
notes: == CORPUS CENSUS FOLDED IN FROM rf2-2rn3, 2026-09-10 (mayor) == rf2-2rn3 was filed independently by the mayor, minutes before this bead, on the SAME finding -- that `check_flattened_lists.py` does not detect the escaped-continuation class. This bead has the better evidence (blob-hash-verified fixture, both directions), so rf2-2rn3 is closed as a duplicate and its distinct content is carried here rather than lost. WHAT rf2-2rn3 ADDS -- THE CORPUS SIZE, measured by the rf2-6ml6 worker with the continuation probe (sentinel into each candidate continuation line, pipe-bearing lines excluded from injection so indented TABLE ROWS are measurable rather than refused): 458 escaped continuation lines remain corpus-wide, after #9620 took docs/api from 84 to 0 (542 at that base). Largest carriers: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md 166 docs/EP/EP-0012 81 docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md 75 spec/, 8 files 31 plus 19 further indented TABLE blocks under list items outside docs/api MAYOR-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, with a control both ways, at trunk 8cb22c0de5: gate on trunk with the class present -> exit 0 flattened list planted in a TRACKED file -> exit 1 (the gate is live) restored to a byte-identical hash -> exit 0 A FIRST CONTROL OF MINE WAS INVALID and the failure is reusable: I planted into an UNTRACKED file and read exit 0, briefly concluding the gate was dead. `_tracked_markdown` enumerates with `git ls-files`, so an untracked probe file is invisible to the instrument. TWO DECISIONS, AND THEY ARE SEPARATE -- carried over from rf2-2rn3: 1. THE REPAIR. `docs/api` proved it mechanical and safe (211/211, `git diff -w` EMPTY, no prose touched). But the two largest carriers are `docs/the-mayor-method/` pages, held to a STRICTER rule than the rest of the corpus -- their fences are pasteable deliverables and a doc link inside a fence is itself reported -- so that tree wants its own pass, not a corpus-wide sweep. 2. WHETHER TO EXTEND THE GATE to this class. A new permanent obligation, so it gets its own decision rather than riding on a repair, exactly as rf2-7ntc reasons about the SSR roster. The argument is stronger than usual here: the defect is the most reader-facing markdown fault in this corpus (the bullet list VISIBLY splits, with body prose stranded between the halves), it is silent, and the instrument exists and is proven. The cost is that the probe is a renderer round-trip, slower than the current gate's line walk. Do not treat 2 as settled by 1. title: False same-frame isolation claim: Reagent bridge collapses namespaced instance IDs
description:
Merged-PR audit of #9605 (7886452fd0f99381665096182fa669755d89ba6b). Two callers supply distinct, accepted keyword :instance-id values through Panel-bridge, but the Reagent prop crossing erases their namespaces and restores the same-frame collision this PR repairs.

Concrete trigger under one frame-provider:
  [Panel-bridge {:instance-id :left/panel}]
  [Panel-bridge {:instance-id :right/panel}]
Panel-bridge forwards the keyword unchanged into [:> Panel-component {:instance-id instance-id}]. Pinned Reagent 2.0.1 convert-prop-value converts a named value with cljs.core/name, so BOTH component props are the string "panel". By the landed value-body composition both then use app-db-state/panel/top and [:rf.xray/app-db "panel" "top"], sharing lifecycle state, width slot and expansion/zoom identity. Detaching either can release the other's state, exactly the already demonstrated shared-key mechanism.

The direct Fresco path behaves differently: instance-token uses (subs (str instance-id) 1), preserving left/panel and right/panel. Plain strings "left/panel" and "right/panel" also survive Reagent distinctly. The contract accepts keywords without excluding namespaces and expressly promises the two component entry paths work alike.

Independent evidence: invoked actual reagent.core/as-element on the bridge's [:> component {:instance-id ...}] shape and read the resulting React props. :left/panel -> "panel"; :right/panel -> "panel"; strings "left/panel" and "right/panel" retained. The loaded reagent.impl.template source map was verified byte-equal after EOL normalization to the project's pinned reagent-2.0.1.jar source. Probe exit 0. This is a real Reagent prop-conversion probe plus source tracing of the landed panel, not a claim of a full mounted Panel integration run.

The existing bridge row only inspects the returned hiccup map before conversion, using the string "left". The keyword row only calls state-body directly with unqualified :left. Neither reaches this failure.

Normalize accepted keyword IDs to the same stable, namespace-preserving string token BEFORE the Reagent crossing. Keep omitted IDs and existing string IDs working. No general identity framework is needed. Exact-owner search found no open Bead for this defect: rf2-2n8q owns missing opts threading on mount-app-db-diff!, a different entry point; this issue occurs on the newly implemented Panel-bridge itself. Preserve the closed rf2-t3fz ruling and the working string/cross-frame repair.
acceptance_criteria: Two namespaced keywords with the same local name, such as :left/panel and :right/panel, passed through the actual Reagent prop-conversion path yield distinct, namespace-preserving identities that agree with the direct Fresco path. Verify the downstream inspector mount IDs and site IDs remain distinct, while string IDs, unqualified keyword/string aliases and omitted IDs retain the intended behavior. The regression must exercise conversion, not merely inspect the pre-conversion hiccup returned by Panel-bridge, and must fail with the currently landed forwarding behavior.
notes: Merged-PR audit #9613 (8e8f39bdd52403a6e47b3c186bbcc0c73ad397bc): the same exact bridge defect now has a public standalone entry point. mount-app-db-diff! forwards :instance-id opts through render-panel! to Panel-bridge unchanged; :left/panel and :right/panel therefore both become panel at the Reagent prop crossing. The bridge and instance-token/composition files are byte-identical to the independently probed #9605 landing. New DOM W1-W3 cover distinct string IDs, not namespaced keywords. panels_mount_cljs_test/crossed invokes Panel-bridge but stops at its pre-conversion hiccup map; its keyword assertion expects :left and will need to follow the normalized token when this existing repair lands. Extend this exact existing correction to cover the standalone facade; preserve its current criteria. No duplicate defect or status transition; discovered-from source rf2-2n8q.
close_reason:
Delivered by PR #9621, merged to trunk at 89cdb416f4 (rebase). Five files, +233/-34.

=== THE DEFECT ===

Reagent 2.0.1's `convert-prop-value` names a keyword prop with `cljs.core/name`, which DROPS the
namespace. `Panel-bridge` passed `:instance-id` across `[:>]` raw, so `:left/panel` and
`:right/panel` BOTH arrived as `"panel"` -- both instances composing `app-db-state/panel/top` and
`[:rf.xray/app-db "panel" "top"]`, sharing lifecycle state, width slot and zoom identity. That
restored exactly the collision #9605 had repaired, through a different door.

ASYMMETRIC, which is what made it invisible: the direct Fresco path's `(subs (str id) 1)` kept
`left/panel` intact, and plain STRING ids crossed distinctly on both paths. Only a NAMESPACED
KEYWORD through the Reagent door collapsed.

=== THE REPAIR, AND WHAT WAS REJECTED ===

Tokenise IN THE BRIDGE, BEFORE the crossing, through the same `instance-token` the boundary
already uses -- now public and idempotent, so the far-side call is a no-op. Rejected, each argued
in the PR body: narrowing the contract to exclude namespaced keywords (idiomatic value, already
works through one door, and the contract promises both doors behave alike); changing
`instance-token`'s keyword branch (already correct); tokenising only namespaced keywords (builds
the NEXT asymmetry); crossing by identity (over-engineering).

=== MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED ===

Reproduced through a real `reagent.core/as-element` crossing, reading React props.
  before: `:left/panel` -> "panel", `:right/panel` -> "panel"; the Reagent door composed
          ["app-db-state/panel/top"] for BOTH while the Fresco door composed distinct variants
  after : distinct, and the two doors agree
The plain-string control passed throughout, so the instrument reads the CROSSING rather than
echoing its input.

deftest. Restored and verified by blob hash (`i/lf` -> default form, 9c4aecdf4165... both sides,

1276/6118 exit 0; browser compile exit 0 with the browser run inside an `if [ "$C" -ne 0 ]` guard
so a failed compile could not serve a stale bundle; test:browser 900/4973 exit 0. clj-kondo and
Splint findings all confirmed pre-existing by linting the same files extracted at base.

=== THE FIFTH FILE, MAYOR-VERIFIED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED ===

The worker touched `panels_mount_cljs_test.cljs` beyond its brief and flagged it prominently in a
separately revertable commit. I checked it rather than taking the flag: that file carries
`mount-app-db-diff-instance-id-reaches-the-boundary` (:398) under a section headed "contract --
instance-id opt (rf2-2n8q)" (:361), i.e. a test asserting EXACTLY what this repair changes. Its

=== A GAP WORTH KNOWING ===

NO DOC OR SPEC ANYWHERE STATES THIS PROP'S ACCEPTED TYPE -- swept four ways with live controls,

and that is where the worker stated it. Not filed as its own bead: the stance's restraining half

de9312afa3da492cb4d442b49c9e0d2bb0d65a33 all completed/success; merge-tree clean; 0 job keys added;
five files disjoint from all four other open PRs.

Merged on the worker's own completion report, which explicitly named marking-ready as the one

title: api(resources): fold install-/remove-revalidation-listeners! into a :revalidate-on frame-config key owned by the frame lifecycle
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from resources.md (ref resources.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Focus/reconnect revalidation is spelled as an imperative pair the app must sequence by hand: `(rf/install-revalidation-listeners! frame-id)` AFTER the render that created the frame, and `(rf/remove-revalidation-listeners! frame-id)` to stop. Routing already folded the identical shape (`install-url-listener!` / `remove-url-listener!` / `install-history-listener!`) into a frame-config key, `:url-bound? true`, with no shim (commit `5b9bab33fa`, "API-shrink #6"): creation installs, re-registration reconciles, destroy removes, and no function exists to call. Resources uses only the destroy half of that lifecycle (`:resources/on-frame-destroyed!`) and leaves install/remove to the app.

The cost is visible in the ONLY consumer: `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/core.cljs` carries a 12-line comment (`:295–296`, `:326–334`) explaining that the call at `:335` "has to run AFTER the render that created it, never before" and that re-running on hot reload "never stacks" — ordering knowledge the `:url-bound? true` key on the SAME opts map (`:319–325`) already carries for free. `remove-revalidation-listeners!` has zero consumers outside its own test file. The manifest sidecar records the verb pair as unresolved against the Lifecycle-verb law (`spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1031–1036`; rf2-uimu); the fold dissolves the question — the answer to "which verb" is "no verb".

## Evidence (HEAD `6445d0611b`)

Census, one `git grep -n -E "(install|remove)-revalidation-listeners!"` over `examples tools testbeds docs skills spec migration implementation`, 62 lines:

| Root | Lines | Where |
|---|---|---|
| examples | 2 | `realworld_resources/core.cljs:295` (comment), `:335` (the one call) |
| tools / testbeds | 0 | — |
| implementation src | 25 | `core.cljc:1529,1532,1535`; `core_resources.cljc:75–99`; `late_bind/directory.cljc:640–648`; `resources.cljc:141–148,708–709`; `resources/revalidate_listeners.cljc:32,144,199–222,241`; `scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj:559` (comment) |
| implementation test | 4 | `resources/test/re_frame/resources_revalidation_cljs_test.cljc:368,436,460,485` |
| docs | 16 | `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1631–1641`; `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:16,308–343`; `docs/resources/coming-from-tanstack-query.md:27,191`; `docs/resources/concepts.md:248` |
| skills | 1 | `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:101` |
| spec | 14 | `spec/API.md:472–473` (rows); `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2271` (the `:rf.error/resources-artefact-missing` row lists the fn names); `spec/016-Resources.md:1196,1833` (prose); `spec/api-manifest.edn:133,163,290,298`; `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1031–1036,1846–1847` |

`:revalidate-on` occurs nowhere in the tree (0 hits) — the name is free.

The precedent's mechanism, verified: the frame engine fires `fire-frame-registered-hook!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:2926–2950`, called at the end of BOTH `upsert-frame!` branches, `:3392` first registration and `:3480` re-registration) after the container is live and `:initial-events` ran — but it consults exactly ONE late-bind key, `:routing/on-frame-registered!` (`:2949`). Routing's hook body (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:379–385`) reads `(:url-bound? (rf.frame/frame-meta id))` (`routing/url_bound.cljc:95`), records/drops the claim, reconciles the listener. The registration-time PREFLIGHT is likewise single-key: `:routing/preflight-frame-config!` at `frame.cljc:3235–3247`, with a fail-loud `:rf.error/routing-artefact-missing` when the config declares `:url-strategy` and routing is not loaded. The destroy path is already an ordered ROSTER of keys (`frame.cljc:4563–4682`; resources at `:4619` → `resources.cljc:670–681` `release-resources-host-caches!` → `revalidate_listeners.cljc` `on-frame-destroyed!`). `re-frame.resources` already requires `re-frame.frame` (`resources.cljc:6`). Today's installer (`revalidate_listeners.cljc:144–197`) always installs all three host listeners (`window focus`, `document visibilitychange`→visible, `window online`); the JVM arm is `nil`.

## Target API

```clojure
;; revalidation is a FRAME property, like URL ownership. No fns.
(rf/make-frame {:id :app :url-bound? true :revalidate-on #{:focus :reconnect}})
[rf/frame-root {:id app-frame :url-bound? true :revalidate-on #{:focus :reconnect}} [root-view]]
```

Contract:
- `:revalidate-on` is an optional frame-config key: a SET drawn from the closed enum `#{:focus :reconnect}`. `:focus` = window `focus` AND document `visibilitychange`→visible (ONE setting — codex: not two public settings); `:reconnect` = window `online`.
- Absent key, or `#{}` → no host listeners. An explicit empty set is a legitimate "none".
- First registration: after the container is live (the same hook point routing uses), install exactly the selected subset. The installer must honour the subset (today it installs all three).
- Re-registration (a deliberate `make-frame` / `frame-root` against an existing id — the surgical update, `spec/002-Frames.md:824`): reconcile, replace-don't-stack. A re-registration WITHOUT the key removes the listeners (the `:url-bound? false` relinquish rule, `url_bound.cljc:100–108`). Repeated `frame-root` renders with identical opts cause no listener churn. An incidental ensure/dispatch is never a configuration update (codex).
- Destroy: unchanged — `:resources/on-frame-destroyed!` removes.
- JVM / SSR / no-DOM hosts: inert (the CLJS arm is the only installer; a JVM `:revalidate-on` config registers with no listener-table entry).
- Validation: a non-set value or an unknown member fails LOUD at registration with zero residue (no frame registered; a failed re-registration preserves every committed value), via the same preflight seam routing uses. A config declaring `:revalidate-on` while `re-frame.resources` is not loaded fails loud with the existing `:rf.error/resources-artefact-missing` (mirror of the `:url-strategy`-without-routing rule at `frame.cljc:3238–3247`). Name the malformed-value id `:rf.error/invalid-revalidate-on` (sibling of `:rf.error/invalid-url-strategy`) and add its 009 catalogue row.

Mechanism (smallest change, no lifecycle framework):
1. `frame.cljc:2926` `fire-frame-registered-hook!`: consult an ORDERED roster `[:routing/on-frame-registered! :resources/on-frame-registered!]` (each `when-let`, routing first) instead of the one hardwired key; keep the not-`safe-call-hook!` loud-failure posture and update the docstring. `frame.cljc:3235`: consult `:resources/preflight-frame-config!` beside `:routing/preflight-frame-config!`, with the artefact-missing fallback for `:revalidate-on`.
2. `late_bind/directory.cljc`: add `:resources/on-frame-registered!` and `:resources/preflight-frame-config!` entries (`:producer-ns 're-frame.resources`, design-bead = this id); delete the `:resources/install-revalidation-listeners!` / `:resources/remove-revalidation-listeners!` entries (`:640–648`).
3. `revalidate_listeners.cljc`: replace the two public fns with a private `reconcile-listeners! [frame-id triggers]` that installs exactly the selected subset (replace-don't-stack) and removes when `triggers` is empty/nil; keep `dispatch-revalidation!`, the two event ids, `release-frame!`, `on-frame-destroyed!`, `reset-cache!` (the test-support reset hook stays). Rewrite the ns docstring paragraph "an app calls `install-revalidation-listeners!`" (`:30–40`).
4. `resources.cljc`: delete the comment + two defs (`:141–148`) and the two `set-fns!` rows (`:708–709`); add `on-frame-registered!` (reads `(:revalidate-on (rf.frame/frame-meta frame-id))` → reconcile) and `preflight-frame-config!` (set ⊆ `#{:focus :reconnect}`); publish both by key beside `:resources/on-frame-destroyed!` (`:681`).
5. `core.cljc:1525–1536` and `core_resources.cljc:75–99`: delete both facade wrappers. Add `:revalidate-on` to the `make-frame` docstring's config-key list.

Two production doors for one job, both with zero application consumers (`examples/`, 22 apps: zero registrations of any kind, zero `sentry|datadog|honeycomb`). The spec calls the sink normal and the streams advanced (`API.md:585`, `009:1258-1262`, `015:270`); the how-to teaches the advanced one first (observability.5 fixes the ORDER, not the count). The "raw `:exception`" discriminator is not one (`projection.cljc:352-363` drops it only under `:rf.egress/public-error`). What door (a) genuinely carries that the sink does not: (i) FRAMELESS records (`:frame nil`) — `:rf.error/no-frame-context` (`frame.cljc:804-808`, `error_emit.cljc:810`), the pre-frame SSR hydration-parse path of `:rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload` (`late_bind/directory.cljc:906`), hicasso's `compute-sub` errors (`server.cljs:259-267`); `route-error-record!` documents them as "carry no frame-owned sink policy by definition" (`observability.cljc:321-325`); and (ii) declaring once per process rather than per frame — `:observability` is accepted on `make-frame` / `frame-root` only; `configure!` (`core.cljc:2554-2605`) has no such key.

Test breadth is where the corpus-wide streams live: `:errors` facade 61 test files, `:events` facade 16 (`git grep -lE "register-listener! :<s>" -- 'implementation/*test*' 'tools/*test*' 'skills/*test*' 'examples/*test*'`); `:errors` home verb 22, `:events` home verb 1. Teaching sites for the two streams: docs 4 files, spec 2, skills 9, migration README 1 (list below).

## Options

**A — one production door (fable, Grok; RECOMMENDED).** `register-listener!` keeps only the raw dev streams: `#{:trace :epoch}` (`core.cljc:2107-2109`). Production observation is ONE door: frame `:observability` policy (today) PLUS a new process default `(rf/configure! {:observability {:handled-events […] :errors […]}})` with the same closed entry grammar (observability.1), wired by `register-observability-sink!`. `re-frame.error-emit` / `re-frame.event-emit` stay as IMPLEMENTATION namespaces (`^:no-doc`, not rowed as public) for the four framework capture sites and for tests; `:events` / `:errors` leave the public vocabulary. Rules that make it one door: a record routes to the owning frame's policy when the frame resolves and declares the stream, else to the process default, else nowhere (fail-closed, unchanged); a frameless record routes to the process default and projects under NO frame — `015:251` case 3: tree slots → `:rf/redacted`, summary ids intact; the raw cross-frame hook becomes an explicit entry `{:sink … :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/local-raw}` on the process default (profile already in the closed enum, `015:258`) instead of an ambient unprojected fan-out.

**B — keep the corpus-wide door as the documented advanced hook (codex).** Everything in observability.1-5 lands; `:events` / `:errors` stay public; no process default; the one missing sentence (observability.5) states the two unique carries. Codex: "Raw synchronous capture and projected delivery are different operations, even if both ultimately register callbacks in maps. Two empty application consumer lists do not establish equivalence… Trusting programmers supports an explicitly advanced raw hook beside the normal projected path… Do not add a process default merely to make deletion of an existing door possible."

**C — the process default now, retirement later (Grok's "third, cheaper path").** Add `configure! {:observability …}` (the declare-once and frameless home) without retiring the streams; revisit retirement once a real Sentry bridge exists in the corpus. Grok: "Zero in-repo app consumers of either door means we do not yet know how a Sentry bridge will actually be written. Deleting the advanced door before the replacement exists is the one way this can fail closed on frameless records."

## Recommendation

A, shipped as two implementation beads in order (the process default FIRST, the retirement SECOND — never the reverse), because: the spec already ruled which door is normal and the surface should say what the spec says; door (a) is fail-open by design (unprojected, no policy, raw throwable) and is the one the how-to hands a first-time reader; `register-listener!` then means one thing (raw dev stream, both members DCE'd) and `register-observability-sink!` one thing (projected production egress) — today the vocabulary mixes two DCE'd streams with two always-on ones and the reader consults a table (`API.md:596-606`) to learn which is which; and the four framework capture sites keep the implementation registry they already use. Codex's caution is carried as the HARD CONSTRAINT below and as the questions the ruling must settle; if Mike prefers to see a real bridge first, C is A1 alone.

## The hard constraint

The `configure!` process default MUST land in the SAME change as (before) the stream retirement, or frameless records reach nobody — the one real gap door (a) closes today (`observability.cljc:321-325`). Frameless projection additionally depends on the egress explicit-nil fix (`@egress.1`): today `project-egress` seeds the governing frame by truthiness and `elide-wire-value` falls through to the AMBIENT frame on `:frame nil` (`elision.cljc:1128` per the egress dossier), so "project under no frame" is not expressible until explicit nil fails closed. A1 is blocked on that bead.

## Questions the ruling must settle (codex's list), with recommended answers

1. **Precedence** — per STREAM: a frame that declares a stream (even `[]`) uses its own entries for that stream; a frame that omits the stream inherits the process default's entries for it; explicit `[]` is the opt-out. (Whole-map replacement rejected: it forces every frame wanting one custom sink to restate the default.)
2. **Absent vs explicit empty** — as in 1; `configure!` with `{:observability nil}` clears the default; validation reuses `frame_classification.cljc`'s `validate-observability!` at call time, fail-loud. Whether to reuse `:rf.error/bad-frame-classification` (with `:where 'rf/configure!`) or mint a category is the ruling's; recommend reuse, no new category. The check must not be an `assert` (rf2-xn13).
3. **Frameless records** — process default only; projected with `{:frame nil}` → fail-closed per `015:251` case 3. Blocked on `@egress.1`.
4. **Records whose `:frame` no longer resolves** (destroyed / dissociated incarnation — `capture_frame_reincarnation_sink_route_cljs_test.cljc` pins that a dissociated id must not resolve to a same-id successor's policy) — today a fail-closed no-op. Recommend: route to the process default under fail-closed projection — `015`'s rule forbids borrowing ANOTHER FRAME's policy; the process default is not a frame's. Ruling needed.
5. **Duplicate delivery** — exactly one policy source per record (frame policy if the frame resolves and declares the stream, else process default); a sink id present in both is invoked once.
6. **Raw cross-frame hook** — `:rf.egress/local-raw` on a process-default entry; coordinate the profile name with `@egress.1`.
7. **Console fallback** — composes with observability.2: a process-default delivery to a registered sink owns the record.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer, High. Codex prefers B ("prefer the narrower Target B… Fix swallowed options and teach projected sinks first; do not require process policy inheritance to delete raw hooks"; "sinks construct a bounded `:rf.observe/*` shape and project payloads, whereas the always-on stream exposes the error/event substrate's record for synchronous integration and capture. Hicasso's shipped capture-intents helper is evidence for the latter"). Grok: A in two steps, sequenced behind the egress profile enum. Fable's own "honest costs": (i) the default must land in the same change; (ii) ~77 test files migrate; (iii) rf2-xpd8's ruling names the listener and needs one sentence; (iv) a library wanting a cross-frame hook without frame config uses the one-line `configure!` default.

**Status:** High (the spec names the frame sink the *normal* production door and the corpus-wide `:errors` stream the *advanced* one, yet the how-to teaches the advanced door for seven sections and both doors have zero non-test consumers; the home-namespace verbs are justified by a DCE rationale that `trace.cljc:48` and `install.cljs:13` disprove; the sink's `:opts` bag is validated and then dropped; wave 3, 2026-09-05 09:09:26 AUSEST, tip 7d7ec09bd7 — main advanced to 90bdedcc17 during the read, see Provenance)
**Surfaces:** `rf/register-listener!` / `unregister-listener!` over `:trace` `:events` `:errors` `:epoch` (`core.cljc:2135-2182`); home verbs `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!` (`tooling.cljc:81`), `re-frame.event-emit/register-event-listener!` (`event_emit.cljc:95`), `re-frame.error-emit/register-error-listener!` (`error_emit.cljc:75`), `re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!` (`epoch.cljc:151`); the aliases `re-frame.trace/register-listener!` (`trace.cljc:951`) and the whole `re-frame.emit` namespace (`emit.cljc`); the late-bind hooks `:trace.tooling/register-listener!` (`directory.cljc:1114`) and `:error-emit/register-error-listener!` (`directory.cljc:907`); `rf/register-observability-sink!` / `unregister-observability-sink!` + frame `:observability` policy (`observability.cljc:111-135`, `frame_classification.cljc:145-256`); the dev console fallback (`error_emit.cljc:90-231`); `reg-error-projector` / `project-error` / `:ssr {:public-error-id}` (`error_projector.cljc:240,314`); `:rf.trace/no-emit?` / `:rf.trace/frame-no-emit?` (`trace.cljc:238,370`, `frame.cljc:3282`).

Three facts the table surfaces:

1. **Two production doors, one job, both empty.** The spec calls the frame sink "the NORMAL production observation surface" and the `:errors` stream an "advanced corpus-wide hook" (`spec/API.md:585`, `009:1258-1262`). Neither has a consumer outside tests. `examples/` (22 apps) contains zero registrations of any kind and zero occurrences of `sentry|datadog|honeycomb`. The teaching corpus disagrees with the spec: `docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md` builds the Sentry bridge on `register-listener! :errors` across §1–§7 (lines 19–272) and reaches the sink only at §8 (line 273, "Prefer the frame sink…"); `configure-dev-and-prod.md:33` names the streams first, then "or — the normal off-box path — declare a frame sink"; the Conduit tutorial (`05-test-and-ship.md:300-308`), `observability.md:481`, and the skill (`production-observability.md:3`) teach the sink first. Three orderings for one question.

2. **The "raw exception" discriminator is not one.** The corpus-wide door is justified as the post-mortem route because "`:exception` rides RAW" (`API.md:585`). But the sink also delivers the exception under its default profile: `projection.cljc:356-360` drops `:exception` only under `:rf.egress/public-error` and otherwise passes an opaque host object through the walker unchanged; the how-to says so itself (`report-errors-in-production.md:298`, "leaving the profile off keeps the exception"). What genuinely distinguishes door (a) is only (i) frameless records (`:frame nil` — no-frame-context, pre-frame SSR parse) which no frame policy can route, and (ii) not having to declare a policy on every frame — because `:observability` is accepted on `make-frame` / `frame-root` only, never on `configure!` (0 hits for a process-level default).

3. **The DCE tier rule's premise is false at tip.** `spec/Tool-Pair.md:635` (landed by rf2-rfid2x, `eba72089b0`): "canonical devtools attach via the per-stream home-namespace verbs … because a tool preload MUST NOT require `re-frame.core` into a production build". Measured: `re-frame.trace` requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` **unconditionally on both platforms** (`trace.cljc:48-49`; the facade's `:trace` arm and the home verb are literally one var, `trace.cljc:951`), and `re-frame.core` requires `re-frame.trace` (`core.cljc:52`) — so every bundle that has the facade already has the tooling registry, and the only DCE lever is the `goog.DEBUG` gate around the *call site*, which both spellings need equally (`trace.cljc:28-33` says exactly this). The exemplar the rule was lifted from, `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs`, requires `re-frame.core` at line 13 (for `rf/with-frame` + `rf/dispatch` at 75-76) two lines above the comment saying it uses the home namespace "so the dev-only tooling surface remains independently elidable". Seven of the ten home-verb `:trace` call sites also require `re-frame.core` (measured below). And `:events` / `:errors` are always-on — there is nothing to elide. The rule protects nothing; it only licenses a second spelling.

4. **`:opts` is swallowed.** A sink entry's `:opts` map is validated for shape at `make-frame` (`frame_classification.cljc:240-251`, fails loud on a non-map; tested at `frame_classification_cljs_test.cljc:190-203`) and appears in every teaching sample (`observability.cljc:22`, `015:281`, `API.md:701`). `route-stream!` reads only `:sink` and `:rf.egress/profile` (`observability.cljc:161-171`); `deliver-to-sink!` calls `(f projected)` (`:149`). The bag reaches nobody. Spec-Schemas rows it as "vendor-specific, framework does not own the vocabulary" (`Spec-Schemas.md:4332`) — a slot designed as a pass-through that does not pass through. This is the exact shape Principles §No silent swallow forbids ("an unknown opts key … a callback whose return it drops").

5. **Ownership is a side effect.** The dev console fallback goes quiet when *any* `:errors` listener exists, "even if that listener ignores this category" (`error_emit.cljc:120-128`). Story therefore registers `(fn [_record] nil)` purely to claim the stream (`shell.cljs:1153`, rf2-8yyd — 227 console lines per feature-load run otherwise). A tool with its own error surface has no honest way to say "I own errors" except a fake registration on a door it does not read.

## Simpler elegant target

**One dev verb over raw streams; one production door with a policy; nothing in between.**

```clojure
;; DEV — raw streams, DCE'd. The closed vocabulary shrinks to the two streams
;; that are actually raw-and-dev: :trace and :epoch.
(rf/register-listener!   stream id f)        ; stream ∈ #{:trace :epoch}
(rf/unregister-listener! stream id)

;; PRODUCTION — declared policy, projected delivery, always-on.
;; The policy is data on the frame (today) AND, new, a process default on
;; configure! — the same knob/frame precedence ladder :fx-overrides already
;; uses, so multi-frame apps declare once and frameless records have a home.
(rf/configure! {:observability {:errors [{:sink :app/sentry
                                          :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-observability}]}})
(rf/make-frame {:id :admin :observability {:errors [{:sink :app/sentry
                                                     :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/public-error}]}})
(rf/register-observability-sink! :app/sentry (fn [projected-record] …))
```


Rules that make it one door: a record routes to the owning frame's policy when it has one, else to the process default, else nowhere (fail-closed, unchanged). A frameless record routes to the process default and projects under *no* frame — which `015:251` case 3 already defines as whole-tree `:rf/redacted`, summary ids intact. The raw cross-frame case that door (a) served becomes an explicit opt-in on the sink entry (`:rf.egress/local-raw`, `015` case 4) instead of an ambient unprojected fan-out. The console fallback keys on "no entry routed this record" rather than "the listener atom is empty" — so Story's frames declare `{:observability {:errors [{:sink :rf.story/errors}]}}` and own their errors honestly.

## Why this is better (ethos)

**One way for the common case; power available, not ambient** (README ethos bar). The spec has already ruled which door is normal (`API.md:575,585`, `009:1258`, `015:270`). The surface disagrees with the ruling: the normal door has zero consumers and is taught last; the advanced door has the how-to. Deleting the advanced door from the app-facing vocabulary makes the surface say what the spec says.

**Privacy by default, honestly.** Door (a) is fail-open by design — unprojected, no frame policy, raw throwable — and it is the door the how-to hands a first-time reader at line 30. `015:321` distinguishes classification's fail-open from the projector's fail-closed carefully; a public verb that bypasses the projector entirely is a third posture the spec never names. Trust the programmer means giving them the projected record and an explicit `:rf.egress/local-raw` opt-in, not an ambient raw fan-out they must remember not to reach for.

**No silent swallow.** `:opts` is recognised, validated, documented, and dropped. Conventions §No silent swallow is the normative rule; this is its textbook violation, on the very door the spec calls normal.

**Low hidden context.** Registering any `:errors` listener silences the console for every category (`error_emit.cljc:120-128`). Story's `(fn [_record] nil)` is the corpus telling us the off-switch is in the wrong place — a registration on a door nobody reads, to change behaviour on a door nobody registered. Keying the fallback on routing makes "who owns this record" a fact of the policy data, readable by anyone.

**Regularity over cleverness.** After the change `register-listener!` means one thing (raw dev stream; both members DCE'd) and `register-observability-sink!` means one thing (projected production egress). Today the stream vocabulary mixes two DCE'd streams with two always-on ones and the reader must consult a table (`API.md:596-603`) to learn which is which.

**Clojure ethos.** The sink registry and the four listener registries are the *same data structure* — `(defonce ^:private … (atom {}))`, `swap! assoc`, return the id, `try/catch` per callback (`observability.cljc:109-135` vs `error_emit.cljc:66-85`, `tooling.cljc:79-99`). Two registries for one shape is not the smell; the smell is that the framework exposes the raw registry *and* the routed one as peers. Registration should be one plain map; routing should be declared as data on the frame. Data over imperative wiring. And a rule that exists "because of DCE" must be true of the dependency graph — measured, not remembered — or it is folklore wearing a contract's clothes.

**Honest costs.** (i) The process-level default must land in the same change as the stream retirement, or frameless records reach nobody — the one real gap door (a) closes today. (ii) Breadth: ~77 test files on the two production streams migrate to the implementation namespaces or a `test-support` helper; mechanical, but wide, and `hicasso` test-kit's `capture-intents` is a shipped surface. (iii) The rf2-xpd8 ruling (2026-09-04) reasons in terms of "listener, sink, console"; its producer routes through `dispatch-error-record!`, which feeds the sink route and the console identically, so nothing there moves — but the ruling text names the listener and will need one sentence. (iv) A library that wants a cross-frame hook without touching frame config loses the ambient route; the answer is the `configure!` default, which is also one line.

## Grok Thoughts

**Bother handling?** Yes. Two production doors for one job, the how-to teaching the fail-open one first, a DCE tier rule whose require-graph premise is false, and a sink `:opts` bag that is validated then dropped. That last one is a textbook No-silent-swallow violation on the door the spec calls *normal*.

**Diagnosis.** Correct and unusually complete. I re-read `deliver-to-sink!` — it calls `(f projected)` and never looks at `:opts`. `route-stream!` reads only `:sink` and `:rf.egress/profile`. The DCE claim is also right: `core.cljc` requires `re-frame.trace` unconditionally and `trace.cljc` requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` on both platforms, so the home-ns verbs do not buy elision the facade verb would lose. What genuinely distinguishes the corpus-wide `:errors` stream is frameless records plus “declare once, not per frame.” Target A’s process default is the replacement for that second unique carry; without it, stream retirement drops a real capability.

**Options.** Target A vs Target B is the right fork. Missing a third, cheaper path: fix honesty *without* retiring streams yet (delete or pass `:opts`, add the `configure!` default, rekey the console fallback, rewrite the how-to so the sink is §1). Zero in-repo app consumers of *either* door means we do not yet know how a Sentry bridge will actually be written. Deleting the advanced door before the replacement exists is the one way this can fail closed on frameless records.

**Recommendation.** Ship Target A, but as two beads, not one.

1. **Honesty bead (do now).** Delete `:opts` (the sink fn closes over its own config; if per-frame vendor tags are wanted later, pass them as a second argument — never accept-and-drop). Add `(rf/configure! {:observability …})` with the same knob/frame precedence `:fx-overrides` already uses. Key the console fallback on “no policy routed this record.” Rewrite `report-errors-in-production.md` so the sink is the first recipe. Fix the Tool-Pair DCE sentence to the preload truth: tools stay out of production via `:devtools/preloads`, not via which namespace they require.
2. **Retirement bead (after 1 is in).** Remove `:events`/`:errors` from the *public* stream vocabulary. Keep `re-frame.error-emit` / `re-frame.event-emit` as implementation registries for the four framework window-capture sites and for tests. Delete `re-frame.emit`, the `re-frame.trace/register-listener!` aliases, and the unused late-bind listener hooks.

Do not merge the sink with the raw streams. `reg-error-projector` is a different job; leave it. Do not implement this until the egress profile enum (including `:rf.egress/local-raw` as the explicit opt-in that replaces ambient raw fan-out) is stable — this design leans on that hatch.

**Implement.** One process default, one routing fallback branch, a wide but mechanical test migration (~77 files). Sequence behind `egress-and-redaction.md` for the profile names, and share the `register-listener!` vocabulary change with `trace-and-epoch-read-surface.md` so those two docs do not fork the stream set. `current-config` belongs in the boot/config bead, not here.

## Codex Thoughts

### Verdict: worthwhile diagnosis, but prefer the narrower Target B


The ignored sink `:opts` and conflicting teaching paths deserve action. Retiring public `:errors`/`:events` listeners and adding process-wide policy inheritance is a larger redesign than the evidence presently earns. Raw synchronous capture and projected delivery are different operations, even if both ultimately register callbacks in maps. Two empty application consumer lists do not establish equivalence.

The source confirms the concrete defect: [frame validation](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame_classification.cljc) accepts an `:opts` map, while [sink routing](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc) passes only the projected record. Choose explicitly between removing the unused slot and passing it as a documented second callback argument. For today's measured consumers I favor removal, with configuration captured in the registered function and existing `:frame` attribution available for lookups. If one shared vendor sink genuinely needs different per-frame configuration, the second argument is a small legitimate alternative, not necessarily over-engineering. Either choice must remove the accept-and-drop contract from code and examples.

### Correct the diagnosis before choosing the door

The sink does preserve opaque host exceptions under its default profile; raw exception presence is therefore not a sufficient discriminator. However the distinction is broader than frameless records: sinks construct a bounded `:rf.observe/*` shape and project payloads, whereas the always-on stream exposes the error/event substrate's record for synchronous integration and capture. [Hicasso's shipped capture-intents helper](../../../../implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs) is evidence for the latter, not merely an implementation detail to move out of sight. Trusting programmers supports an explicitly advanced raw hook beside the normal projected path.

The DCE criticism usefully invalidates an unsupported blanket teaching rule. A namespace dependency graph alone does not prove the size or contents of an advanced compiled bundle: reachable exports and gated call sites still matter. Prefer one documented registration facade and preserve genuinely necessary implementation namespaces, load-cycle hooks, and optional epoch loading. Verify any claimed bundle improvement with the existing positive-control build, not source greps alone.

### Recommended implementation

Lead the production how-to with a frame-owned projected sink. State plainly what is projected, what happens to exceptions, and when the advanced corpus-wide listener is appropriate. Reconcile the manifest, tool guidance, and examples around that distinction. Remove proven unused aliases independently; internal fan-out and late binding need not become public synonyms.

Do not add a process default merely to make deletion of an existing door possible. If a real multi-frame integration later needs it, specify absent policy versus explicit empty policy, per-stream inheritance versus whole-map replacement, frameless records, teardown records whose owner no longer resolves, and prevention of duplicate delivery. These are semantic choices, not simply one fallback branch. Frameless projection also depends on fixing the explicit-nil ownership defect discussed in [egress and redaction](egress-and-redaction.md).

The console issue is real but should remain small. [The current fallback](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc) deliberately treats any listener as corpus-wide ownership. Changing that to “an entry routed” can hide an error when a named sink is missing or throws; Story also suppresses errors outside a single variant frame. Keep today's behavior documented while evaluating an explicit host-level ownership choice, or define successful handoff precisely before changing it. Do not invent per-category routing, acknowledgements, or a suppression framework for this cleanup.

Acceptance should cover sink option handling, normal projected delivery, raw temporary capture, frameless errors, listener removal, missing/throwing sinks, and whichever console rule is actually chosen. The elegant result is clear defaults and honest escape hatches—not a smaller verb count purchased with more ambient configuration.

# Listener registration — one verb in the spec, two forms per stream in practice

**Status:** medium (the dual is tiered, but the tier rule is folklore; wave 2, 2026-07-10 14:30 AUSEST, Fable-authored)
**Surfaces:** `rf/register-listener!` (facade; closed streams `:trace` `:events` `:errors` `:epoch`), the four home-namespace verbs (`trace.tooling/register-listener!`, `event-emit/register-event-listener!`, `error-emit/register-error-listener!`, `epoch/register-epoch-listener!`), plus the distinct-job pair `register-observability-sink!` and `reg-error-projector`

---

## The problem

The spec's design is genuinely elegant: **one stream-parameterized verb over a closed four-stream
vocabulary** (API-shrink #4 already deleted the per-channel facade twins). But every stream remains
reachable **two ways** — facade or home namespace — and the corpus's own canonical tools straddle the
two *inconsistently*:

| Consumer | `:trace` | `:epoch` |
|---|---|---|
| Xray (`install.cljs:79,112`) | home ns | **facade** |
| Story (`frames.cljc:212`, `invariants.cljc:395`) | home ns | **facade** |
| pair preload (`runtime.cljs:1474,1330`) | home ns | **facade** |

Same tools, two same-axis dev streams, two call-site conventions. The reason for the home-ns form is
real and important — keeping `re-frame.core` out of production bundles so DCE holds — but it lives in
one Xray comment (`install.cljs:42-49`), not in any contract.

---

## Empirical use cases

### 1. Canonical tool attaches a trace collector

Xray, Story (5 sites incl. its own `trace-buffer` wrapper), pair preload — all via
`re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!`, all for the bundle-DCE reason.

### 2. Canonical tool attaches an epoch collector

Same three tools — all via the **facade** `rf/register-listener! :epoch`, despite
`re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!` existing (`docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md:113` explicitly names
both routes as the same registry).

### 3. Framework-internal error listeners

SSR error projection registers on `:errors` (always-on) *and* `:trace` (dev) under one logical id
(`ssr.cljc:459,475`) — deliberate cross-axis coverage; the router uses the home error verb likewise.
