title: Unit-test pruning: playground
description:
Apply the exact requested pruning prompt recursively to docs/tools/playground/test. This is a distinct worker cluster under rf2-0wcq5. Production code remains unchanged except temporary hash-verified fault plants. Push a draft test-only PR, babysit all latest-head checks to green, then mark ready. A measured no-op or unexecuted-file report is valid; do not manufacture changes.

Simplify the unit tests under docs/tools/playground/test. Do not change the code under test. LLMs tend to
write too many low-value unit tests, and this suite was largely written by them.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs, and that many of its tests are longer
than they need to be. Every test costs CI time, reading time and refactoring friction,
and the low-value ones hide the tests that matter. I want a lean suite: each test earns
its place by guarding a behaviour a caller relies on, against a regression that could
plausibly happen and would matter. Each surviving test should be as short as the thing
it proves.

Stay inside docs/tools/playground/test. Do not edit tests elsewhere. If a deletion relies on a test outside
docs/tools/playground/test to keep covering something, name that test in your report.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures, lines. Confirm a
   runner actually executes each file in docs/tools/playground/test; a file nothing runs cannot be pruned on
   evidence, so report it.
2. Read the code under test and list what it promises its callers: normal results, each
   boundary that takes its own path, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests
   refer to.
3. Map every test to the promise it checks. Most of the work shows up in this map:
   promises with five tests, tests with no promise, and tests of something no caller
   relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise.

Work in small batches by contract group, and commit as you go. Before each batch,
predict the change in test and assertion counts; after it, confirm the counts moved by
exactly that much. If helper agents are available, use read-only ones for the mapping
step. If docs/tools/playground/test plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a group boundary,
ship what is done, and list the files you did not reach.

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch?
  If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it,
  and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time
  validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or
  loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists, a var resolves, something "is
  registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test
  exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a
  roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended
  change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as
  a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no
  caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take
  one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a
  getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already
  exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the
  implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the
  contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return, and tests whose mock setup
  is most of the test while the assertion checks the mock.
- Separate per-platform test files asserting the same thing about platform-neutral code.
  A single shared test that runs on both platforms is one test, not two: keep it.
- Tests of test helpers and fixtures.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it, and tests whose only subject is production code
  that no production caller uses.

Simplify every test you keep:
- Assert the whole result with one equality instead of one assertion per field. Drop an
  assertion that a later one in the same test implies.
- Cut setup, fixtures and data to what the assertion needs. Remove unused bindings,
  requires, helpers and fixtures.
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and
  drop the mid-range ones.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.
- Delete comments and docstrings that restate the code or narrate history. Keep a
  one-line why where a test's purpose is not obvious from its name and body.
- Rename a test only when its name no longer says what it asserts, and first check that
  nothing matches on the name, such as a CI filter, a skip list or a doc that cites it.

Keep, however small:
- The only test of a promise a caller relies on: a normal result, a boundary that takes
  a different path (empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it), a promised
  failure.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened, unless a stronger test now covers
  it.
- The last guard of a security, privacy or redaction promise.
- The last test that keeps a gate able to fail, and the last test holding a published
  doc or spec claim to the code.
When a weak test and a strong test overlap, keep the strong one: the one that would fail
on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion, or swap an exact check for a looser one, to make a merge or a
  simplification easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Leave unused helpers, fixtures or requires behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a promise with no test, report it.
- Change production code. Dead code and stale docs or spec text go in your report as a
  list, not into your change.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in
the same change. Commit one file or module at a time.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions that rests on a surviving cover, break the code in a place
  the deleted tests guarded and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code and
  confirm it matches the committed file. One plant per group sharing a cover is enough.
  If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the tests back.
- A cover must actually run. A skipped test, a fixture the runner never loads, or a test
  on a lane nothing executes covers nothing. Confirm the runner executes a cover before
  resting a deletion on it.
- Run each test file you touched on its own at least once. Deleting a file can break a
  sibling that relied on it loading something first; give such a file its own require.
- A deletion made under the second question needs no plant. Give its one-line reason in
  the report instead.
- A simplification must not change what a test can catch. Where you removed an
  assertion, name the assertion that implies it.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, the surviving cover, or the one-line
  reason it was not worth keeping.
- Merges and simplifications: what went into what, and the lines each file lost.
- Notable keeps: tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Plants, and which test caught each.
- Tests outside docs/tools/playground/test that your deletions rely on.
- Dead code, stale docs or spec text, and gaps (promises with no test). One line each.

If you are unsure whether a promise a caller relies on is still covered, keep the test
and say so. Losing the only guard of a real promise is still the one mistake that matters
more than leaving an extra test in. But being unsure whether a test is worth keeping is
not a reason to keep it. If you cannot say in one line what plausible regression it
catches that a caller would notice, delete it.

title: Resource identity off-box: tokenise every non-global scope on every carrier, let params ride unless the resource claims :sensitive?, and retire :params/:scope key declarations
description:
## Ruling

Resource identity off-box follows one coarse rule (option B of README Q4):

- **Scope is always tokenised off-box.** Every non-global scope value becomes the existing content-free sensitive token on trace, tool, MCP and observability egress, for every owner and on every carrier: the free `:scope` tag, the scope component inside `:resource/key`, `:matched`, `:identities`, `:affected-keys`, `:previous-key` and a reply's `:correlation`. `:rf.scope/global` rides verbatim. A `[tier {identity}]` tuple may keep its tier keyword (a tool still shows "session scope"); any other non-global scope shape - a map, a string, any scalar or other EDN that scope validation admits - tokenises whole. It is the framework's standing rule, so it needs no owner lookup.
- **Params ride off-box** unless the resource makes the whole-resource `:sensitive?` (or `:large?`) claim, which tokenises scope, params and data exactly as today.
- **Per-slot identity declarations retire.** A `:params`- or `:scope`-rooted path in a `reg-resource` `:sensitive` / `:large` vector is a loud registration error (`:rf.error/resource-bad-spec`) whose message points at `:sensitive?`. `[:data ...]` paths stay. Mutation `[:params ...]` declarations stay, because mutation params are an event payload, not an identity.
- **"Off-box" means trace, tool, MCP and observability egress - not SSR hydration and not on-box inspection.** Scope keeps riding hydration (it goes to the principal's own browser), and SSR withholds only coarse-claim entries.
- **The rule protects resource-owned carriers, and the spec says exactly which.** It does not cover the read sub's query vector (Spec 015 ships query vectors raw by design), an explicit concrete scope passed in a `subscribe` payload, or the HTTP request URL and body (governed by the request's own `:sensitive?`). The contract is not "the principal never leaves the box"; it is "resource-owned carriers never ship the scope off-box, and params are yours to keep clean, or claim the read `:sensitive?`" - the same "pass identifiers, not secrets" guidance Spec 015 gives for cache keys.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both the dossier (`resource-identity-privacy-and-correlation`) and the Codex review chose B. Codex's three corrections are folded in above: name the protected carriers instead of claiming the principal never leaves the box; tokenise every non-global scope, not only tier/map tuples; keep app-facing continuation facts (that last one bears on the sibling correlation bead, not this one).

Decisive facts, read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. **The same scope gets two rules on one row.** `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj:359-374` pins a plain owner's `:rf.resource/invalidated` row whose free `:scope` identity map is tokenised while the same scope inside `:resource/key` and `:matched` rides raw (`(is (= [k [k]] [(:resource/key tags) (:matched tags)]))`). That contradicts the code's own principle, "the carriers of one scope must agree" (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/trace_egress.cljc:523`).
2. **Per-slot params grain promises more than it delivers, and nobody uses it.** The same param rides raw in the read sub's `:rf.sub/query-v` - "A value used as a cache key is structurally public to every layer that touches the cache ... So pass identifiers, not secrets" (`spec/015-Data-Classification.md:120`, `:130`) - and in the request URL. No example or guide declares a resource `[:params ...]` or `[:scope ...]` path; only tests do. The docs teach `:sensitive [[:params :password]]` for mutations only (`docs/resources/how-to/invalidate-after-a-mutation.md:68`).
3. **Scope is not always a tuple.** Scope validation admits "a `[:rf.scope/session ...]` tuple, a map, a string" (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:475`), while today's free-scope shape walk rides a scalar verbatim (`trace_egress.cljc:400-405`). The standing rule must therefore tokenise by "non-global", not by tuple shape.

Rejected options:

- **A, keep today's per-slot `:params` / `:scope` declarations:** keeps the same-row disagreement and the per-carrier projector chase, for a grain that is partial anyway (query vector, URL) and has no non-test consumer.
- **C, B's scope rule but keep per-slot params:** keeps most of the per-slot machinery for that same partial, unused grain. Revisit only if an app needs one secret param with otherwise-visible data and cannot split the resource.
- **D, always-opaque scope and params on every boundary (Xray's graph rule):** costs AI-pair readability of public params such as `{:page 2}` and `{:slug "welcome"}`, and would move the HMAC key out of its tooling-only namespace (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc:27-39`) into production-reachable code.

Supersedes: the per-slot `:params` / `:scope` key-declaration contract of `spec/016-Resources.md` §Resource registration (`:798-817`, "a `:params`-rooted (or `:scope`-rooted) path classifies the scoped key") and the per-slot re-key arm of §SSR and hydration (`:1662`, `:1672-1674`); and, as applied to resource identity, EP-0025 §subsystems' `reg-resource` row (`spec/015-Data-Classification.md:184`, "entry's `:params` / `:data`"). No earlier bead ruled on this; README Q4 of the adversarial review has been open since 2026-10-09.

## Work

Spec and tool spec:

- `spec/016-Resources.md` §Resource registration (`:798-817`): drop the `[:params :account-id]` example and the `:params`/`:scope`-rooted text; state the registration error; classification is `[:data ...]` per-slot paths plus the coarse claim.
- `spec/016-Resources.md` §SSR and hydration (`:1654-1690`): only coarse entries re-key and are withheld; delete the per-slot sentinel re-key text. Keep the redaction-token contract and the client-side reconcile drop of rows carrying a substitution.
- `spec/016-Resources.md` §Xray and AI tooling: state the standing scope rule, the carriers it covers, and what lies outside it (query vector, explicit `subscribe` scope, HTTP URL and body).
- `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:184`: the `reg-resource` matrix row's per-slot root becomes the entry's `:data`; params and scope are covered by the standing scope rule and the coarse claim.
- `tools/xray/spec/024-Resources-Panel.md:143-153`: drop per-slot key matching at `[... :resource/key 2 ...]` / `[... :resource/key 0 ...]`.

Code, under `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/` unless named:

- `registry.cljc`: reject `:params`/`:scope` roots in `reg-resource` `:sensitive` / `:large` with `:rf.error/resource-bad-spec`, message naming `:sensitive?`.
- `trace_egress.cljc`: one standing scope arm in `project-trace-scoped-key` (`:285`), and the free `:scope` tag projected by the same rule so a scalar non-global scope tokenises. Delete `key-slot-declarations` (`:135`), `redact-key-declarations` (`:179`), `recover-key` (`:1894`) and the per-slot arm of `project-key-slot` (`:1979`).
- Standing-rule tokenisation does not stamp the row `:sensitive? true` - it is a framework rule, not an owner's claim. Coarse-claim rows and `:rf.resource/scope-resolved` (`scope_registry.cljc:457-482`) keep their stamps.
- `classification.cljc`: delete `project-entry-key-component` (`:460`), `project-entry-params` (`:495`), `project-entry-scope` (`:511`) and the key arm of `instance-declaration-paths` (`:736`).
- `ssr.cljc`: withhold only coarse entries; delete the constant-sentinel arm of the wire-key shape test (`ssr.cljc:475-518`).
- `tooling.cljc`: delete the per-slot key arm. Xray's resources helpers: drop per-slot key matching.
- Tests: rewrite `epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj:359-374` to assert agreement; delete per-slot key-declaration tests; add registration-error tests and tuple, map and string scope tokenisation tests.

Deliberately stays: the coarse `:sensitive?` / `:large?` claim and its tokens (content-free for sensitive, canonical digest for large); `[:data ...]` per-slot declarations and their lowering; mutation `[:params ...]` declarations; privacy of params-schema validation failures, as today; SSR withholding of unaddressable (coarse) entries; on-box listeners and local Xray seeing raw values; Xray's graph export HMAC policy (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc:210-254`), which is stricter and needs no change; Spec 015's raw query vectors.

Out of scope, not filed: making a resource's `:sensitive?` also set `:sensitive? true` on its own managed request (the dossier listed it as optional; Codex treats HTTP's per-call classification as its own boundary). Route params' per-slot declarations are not decided here.

## Sequencing

- Hot zones: none expected. If the `reg-resource` registration schema in `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` documents `:sensitive` path roots, that one edit is sequenced against other Spec-Schemas holders. No new `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` row: `:rf.error/resource-bad-spec` already exists. No `spec/011-SSR.md` edit expected; if one is made, it is the one i/crlf file.
- Depends on: no bead.
- Precedes: rf2-v3ory (correlate resource attempts by an opaque per-frame id), which depends on this bead.
- Cross-dossier: coordinate with the `mcp-whole-event-drop-for-sensitive-events` ruling (the row-stamp question above). The `large-subtree-containing-sensitive-path` and `durable-app-db-classification-static-or-runtime` rulings may edit the same classification or trace-egress files; sequence with their beads if they do.

## Evidence

Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54: the test pin and docstring in fact 1; the Spec 015 query-vector rule and the mutation-only docs teaching in fact 2; scope validation and the free-scope shape walk in fact 3; the Spec 016 registration and SSR clauses; the names and line numbers of every function listed for deletion. Not yet run: nothing was compiled or tested. Unmeasured: the size (the dossier's rough estimate is several hundred source lines plus tests, mostly deletions); a search beyond shipped examples and guides for consumers of resource key declarations.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Same-row agreement: on every resource-family off-box row, the free `:scope` tag and the scope component inside `:resource/key` (and inside `:matched`, `:identities`, `:affected-keys`, `:previous-key` and a reply's `:correlation`) project to the same value. The plain-owner `:rf.resource/invalidated` test in `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj` asserts agreement instead of the raw key.
2. Every non-global scope tokenises content-free off-box - a `[tier {identity}]` tuple (tier keyword may ride), a bare map and a string or other scalar scope - and `:rf.scope/global` rides verbatim. One test per shape.
3. A plain owner's params ride off-box byte-identical (test).
4. A `:sensitive?` owner's scope, params and data tokenise content-free as today, and a `:large?` owner keeps its canonical digest token (tests).
5. `reg-resource` with a `:params`- or `:scope`-rooted path in `:sensitive` or `:large` throws `:rf.error/resource-bad-spec`, and the message names `:sensitive?`. `[:data ...]` paths and mutation `[:params ...]` declarations still register and redact (tests).
6. SSR withholds only coarse-claim entries; a plain owner's entry rides hydration with its raw scope; no per-slot sentinel re-keying remains in `ssr.cljc`.
7. A search of `implementation/` and `tools/` for `key-slot-declarations`, `redact-key-declarations`, `recover-key`, `project-entry-key-component`, `project-entry-params` and `project-entry-scope` finds nothing.

title: Teach root-declared presence in the validate-with-schemas how-to and drop boot-window-only [:maybe ...] wrappers from the examples
description:
## Ruling

A path schema registered with `reg-app-schema` constrains the value at its path only when that path exists. An absent path is not checked; a present value, `nil` included, is. Whether a key must exist is said by an enclosing schema, usually the root `[]`: `(rf/reg-app-schema [] [:map [:cart CartSchema]])`. A first registration checks a present live value and emits `:rf.schema/violation`. The rule lands in the schemas bead this one depends on. This bead removes what the old rule forced on authors: the `[:maybe …]` boot-window idiom, the how-to section that teaches it, and the example comment blocks that justify it. `[:maybe …]` goes back to meaning only "this value may be `nil`".

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. `docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md:134-157` teaches the idiom under a section titled "Every registered path is checked on every commit", ending in a warning headed "Broken in dev, fine in production". Its stated reason at `:136` ("A handler that writes only `[:showing]` is still checked against your `[:todos]` schema") has been false since commit 511e96991f (rf2-mn2ht.14, 2026-10-10) made commits skip unchanged slices. The same stale account appears in the comment blocks at `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/schema.cljs:278-293` and `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/schema.cljs:101-120`.
2. Every multi-slice example wraps every registered slice in `[:maybe …]` only to get through boot: `realworld_http/schema.cljs` (23 of 23 paths), `realworld_resources/schema.cljs` (5 of 5), `examples/patterns/boot/schema.cljs:153-156` (4 of 4), the SSR example's `ArticlesSchema` (`examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:102-113`), and 2 of 3 paths in `testbeds/large_dispatcher/core.cljs:86-90`.
3. Some of those `:maybe`s guard a real present `nil`, so they stay. For example, `(update db :favorite-pending disj slug)` at `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/favorites.cljs:224` and `:240` writes `nil` when the key was absent, and `[:favorite-pending]` is registered at `realworld_http/schema.cljs:329`.

Rejected: keeping the `[:maybe …]` teaching (it was there only for the absent-slice rule this ruling removes, and it weakens every schema for the app's whole life); stripping every `:maybe` mechanically (a `:maybe` that guards an explicit `nil` write is correct and stays).

Supersedes: the how-to section and comment blocks above, which teach the pre-ruling rule.

## Work

How-to, `docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md`:

- Rewrite `:134-157` as a section on what a path schema checks:
  - a commit checks the registered slices it writes (an `identical?` slice is skipped), and checks a parent or `[]` when a write lands beneath it;
  - an absent path is not checked, and a present `nil` is;
  - presence is declared at the root or a parent, with the `[:map [:cart CartSchema]]` example;
  - a first registration reports a present non-conforming value.
  Delete the boot-shape "two fixes" text (`:140-153`) and the "Broken in dev, fine in production" warning (`:155-157`).
- `:30` and `:32`: the `[:todos]` example's `:maybe` is justified by the old rule. Drop it unless the example writes `nil`.
- The troubleshooting rows: `:276` ("Every commit rejected, naming a path the handler never touched") either goes, or becomes the parent-required-key case; `:277` (`:rf.schema/violation` after a hot reload) also covers a first registration.

Inbound links and API doc:

- Fix every inbound link to the renamed anchor `#every-registered-path-is-checked-on-every-commit`: `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md:94` and `docs/core/how-to/build-a-form.md:74`.
- Rewrite the bullet at `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md:94`.
- `build-a-form.md:74` keeps its advice, with the reason restated: the draft slice is checked whenever a keystroke writes it.
- `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md:101` says a non-conforming slice left after re-registration gets "every later event that returns `:db` … rejected until one writes a conforming value there". That is stale under changed-slice checking. Restate it, and add the first-registration case.

Examples: drop each boot-window-only `:maybe` and the comment that justifies it. Keep a `:maybe` wherever a handler writes an explicit `nil`, and say so in one line beside it. Check each handler's actual writes before dropping anything.

- `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/schema.cljs`: the comment at `:278-293`, the registry at `:301-354`, and the boot-window remarks at `:319`, `:341` and `:349`. `[:favorite-pending]` keeps its `:maybe`.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/schema.cljs`: the comment at `:101-120` and the registry at `:137-160`. `[:settings-save-owner]`'s comment reasons that "an absent slot reads nil"; re-read it under the new rule.
- `examples/patterns/boot/schema.cljs`: `:138-156`. The root-map slots at `:89-97` hold `nil` while loading, so check whether the boot machine writes `nil` there or leaves the keys absent.
- `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:102-113`: `ArticlesSchema` and its comment.
- `testbeds/large_dispatcher/core.cljs:86-90`.

Coupled tests:

- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_resources_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs:84-87` (`every-shipped-registration-tolerates-absence`) asserts that every shipped schema accepts `nil`. Delete it, or replace it with an assertion that the bare registry boots, once the registry drops its `:maybe`s.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs` keeps its boot assertion.

Deliberately stays: `:maybe` on every path a handler can write `nil` to; all other how-to content.

## Sequencing

- Hot zones: none. All of these are docs, examples, a testbed and two example-coupled tests, which are isolated surfaces.
- Bead dependencies: depends on the schemas bead filed alongside it ("Make an absent app-db path unchecked …"). Without it, dropping the `:maybe`s deadlocks the examples' boot in dev. It can run in parallel with the Spec 009 catalogue bead.
- Cross-dossier: the app-db-schema work from one-registry-top-level-reg.md (sub-choice C-s1, deleting `with-frame` and `{:frame …}` from `reg-app-schema` call sites) edits the same how-to and the same example schema files. If both are ruled, sequence one after the other.
- Gates:
  - `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, for the renamed anchor and its inbound links;
  - `npm run test:cljs` for the boot-seed tests (this takes the machine-wide shadow-cljs lane, so get it granted);
  - the examples compile sweep (`node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs`; ask it with `--list` which builds it covers).

## Evidence

Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54: `validate-with-schemas.md:30-32, :134-157, :276-277`; `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md:94, :101`; `build-a-form.md:74`; `realworld_http/schema.cljs:274-354`; `realworld_http/favorites.cljs:222-241`; `realworld_resources/schema.cljs:101-160`; `boot/schema.cljs:89-156`; `ssr/core.cljc:100-113`; `large_dispatcher/core.cljs:80-90`; `example_realworld_resources_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs:59-87`.

The `:maybe` counts come from the reading above. Which handlers write an explicit `nil` has been checked only for `[:favorite-pending]`; the rest must be checked per path. Nothing has been run.

2. Every inbound link to the rewritten section resolves, and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `mkdocs build --strict` are green.
3. The boot-window-only `:maybe`s and their comment blocks are gone from realworld_http, realworld_resources, patterns/boot, the SSR example and `testbeds/large_dispatcher`. Every `:maybe` that remains guards a handler that writes an explicit `nil` and says so in one line (`[:favorite-pending]` among them).
4. `every-shipped-registration-tolerates-absence` is removed or replaced, the realworld boot-seed tests pass under `npm run test:cljs`, and the examples compile sweep is green.
5. The bullets at `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md:94` and `:101` describe the current rule: changed slices are checked, absent paths are not, and a first registration over a present non-conforming value emits `:rf.schema/violation`.

== MAYOR NOTE 2026-10-16 12:35 AUSEST: a consequence of the ruling to teach, from rf2-n68h3's implementation (PR #11364) ==
The root path `[]` is always present (an existing frame's app-db is `{}`). Under the ruling a first registration checks a present live value, so `(rf/reg-app-schema [] [:map [:cart CartSchema]])` registered at boot BEFORE the seed emits one `:rf.schema/violation` warning at registration. title: Rebuild the quiet JVM runner around cognitect's returning test fn, honour namespace-level ^:requires-debug in the prod-gate lane, and delete epoch's prod-gate roster script
description:
## Ruling

Rebuild `re-frame.test-quiet.runner/-main` around cognitect-test-runner's returning `test` function. The runner then decides the outer invocation's verdict from what `test` returns:

- stderr replay on red;
- the uncallable-fixture audit, over the namespaces this invocation SELECTED;
- the test-count floor;
- the exit code.

Delete the stdout banner filter, its shutdown hook and the process-global `clojure.test/report :summary` mutation. A green JVM run then shows cognitect's one `Running tests in #{…}` line (tooling Q6: yes).

In the same rebuild, make the runner honour a NAMESPACE-level `^:requires-debug` in the `:prod-gate` lane (tooling Q5, option b). A tagged namespace still loads under `-Dre-frame.debug=false`, and its tests are filtered out. Tag epoch's 22 dev-only test namespaces that way and delete `scripts/test-epoch-prod-gate.sh`. The `jvm-epoch-prod-gate` job then runs `clojure -M:test:prod-gate`. Var-level tags remain the rule for mixed suites, so core keeps its roughly 150.

This is the second bead of the tooling dossier's option (C).

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

**Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:**

1. **The verdict lives in a global report method.** `make-summary-replay-method` (`implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/runner.clj:1143-1250`) is installed on `clojure.test/report :summary` (`:1312`). It audits fixtures over `(all-ns)` (`:1217`) and calls `System/exit` (`:1216`). Any nested `run-tests` reaches it, and one does: `implementation/test-quiet/test/re_frame/test_quiet_pin_test.clj:8-13` calls `run-tests` inside a deftest. About 330 lines (`runner.clj:137-464`) plus a shutdown hook (`:1310`) exist only to erase cognitect's banner.
2. **cognitect v0.5.1 already returns the summary.** The pinned version is `dfb30dd`, at `implementation/test-quiet/deps.edn:52-53`. Its `cognitect.test-runner/test` (`src/cognitect/test_runner.clj:62-75`) prints the banner, `require`s every selected namespace, filters vars, and RETURNS the `run-tests` summary. Only `-main` (`:115-131`) calls `System/exit`, and `cli-options` (`:86`) is public. The returned summary does NOT carry the selected namespaces, so the fixture audit must take the outer selection itself rather than approximate it.
3. **Epoch's 22 exclusions are dev-only by design.** Epoch excludes 22 namespaces (`scripts/test-epoch-prod-gate.sh:129-192`), about 178 deftests, in two documented classes: the subject is elided under the gate, or the publication is. Epoch's production posture is that the artefact is off (`test-epoch-prod-gate.sh:55-80`). cognitect's `-e` reads var metadata only, so a namespace marker stays inert unless this runner honours it (`implementation/core/deps.edn:179-186`).

**Rejected:**

- *Keep the filter and the global hook.* That is about 330 lines plus a shutdown hook to hide one line, and it leaves a focused run open to failure by an unrelated loaded namespace, or to a JVM exit from a nested `run-tests`.
- *Q5 (a): var-tag all ~178 epoch deftests.* It is noisy, and every new deftest in those files would need the tag too.
- *Q5 (c): keep epoch's script as the one surviving roster.* That was the fallback only if the runner rebuild were declined, and it was not.
- *Namespace-level tags for core.* Core's suites are mixed, and var-level tags let a new deftest in a tagged namespace join the lane by default.

**Supersedes:** no bead ruling. The "var-level only, and that is the whole point" reasoning in the `:prod-gate` comments (`implementation/core/deps.edn:179-186`, `scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh:80-86`) narrows to mixed suites. This builds on rf2-9sf6u (closed: the `RF2_VERBOSE_TESTS` banners and the catch-and-replay around the delegated `-main`), which explicitly left Q6 open; keep its behaviour.

## Work

- **`runner.clj`.** `-main` parses args with cognitect's public `cli-options`, or keeps delegating for CLI errors and help, then calls `cognitect.test-runner/test` and owns everything after it:
  - red stderr replay (rf2-9sf6u's catch-and-replay);
  - the uncallable-fixture audit, over the namespaces this invocation selected. Compute that selection the way cognitect does (the dirs plus the ns-filter), not from `(all-ns)`.
  - the floor: keep the `--min-tests` main-opt if the previous bead added one; otherwise the default stays `RF2_MIN_TESTS`, else 1;
  - `--probe`;
  - the discovery checks (`verify-discovery!`, `:965`);
  - `System/exit`.

  Delete `banner-filtering-writer` and its helpers (`:137-464`), the shutdown hook (`:1310-1311`) and the `:summary` method and its install (`:1143-1250`, `:1312`). Keep whatever per-test output the quiet reporter's own `defmethod`s provide.

title: Add machine-scoped named :after delays: a root :delays map resolved from keyword :after keys
description:
## Ruling

Add XState-style named delays to machines. A machine gets a root-level `:delays` map beside `:guards` and `:actions`, shaped `{<keyword> <pos-int ms | ISO-8601 string | (fn [{:keys [snapshot]}] ms)>}`. An `:after` key that is a keyword resolves against that map, machine-locally, just as a `:guard` keyword resolves against `:guards`. A keyword that names no entry is refused at registration with the existing `:rf.error/machine-bad-after-delay`, and the message names the missing entry. No new error id is added. Inline fn keys stay, as inline guard fns stay beside named ones. The fn keeps today's `{:snapshot}` signature. Evaluation timing does not change: a named delay is resolved wherever any delay is resolved today, in the timer fx against the committed snapshot. This is part 2 of option C and follows rf2-m2x7s (part 1: removing subscription-vector delays).

The intended spelling:

```clojure
{:delays  {:idle-warning (fn [{:keys [snapshot]}] (-> snapshot :data :idle-warning-ms))}
 :states  {:active {:after {:idle-warning :warning} ...} ...}}
```

XState's equivalent is `setup({ delays: { idleWarning: ({ context }) => context.idleWarningMs } })` with `after: { idleWarning: 'warning' }`. The test seam falls out for free: `(assoc-in machine-def [:delays :idle-warning] 50)`, mirroring XState's `.provide({delays})`.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

The dossier's recommendation and the independent Codex review both chose option C. Codex scoped it as "machine-local keyword names for existing literal, ISO-string and snapshot-function delays", with inline functions and the current signature retained and registration-time missing-name feedback.

**Decisive facts (at trunk 89517e8f54):**

1. **A keyword `:after` key is refused at registration today.** `valid-after-delay-key?` accepts only a positive integer, an ISO-8601 string, a non-empty vector or a fn (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1562-1567`). XState accepts named delays from a `delays` implementation map; rf2-2n6uv.5.2 recorded that by executing XState 6.0.0-alpha.59.
2. **An inline fn delay has no readable identity.**
   - Xray renders it as `(fn)` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/sim.cljs:561-570`, `format-delay-key`, which already formats keyword keys).
   - machines-viz invents a fake vector label for it (`tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/share.cljs:258-266`).
   - The timer's dispatched event `[:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed delay-key epoch invoke-id]` carries the live fn object (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc:885-886`).
3. **Timer firing looks the carried key up in the current definition** (`get-in node [:after delay-key]`, `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:1129`, inside `:1121-1153`). After a hot reload, a freshly evaluated inline fn misses that lookup, and the firing is reported as `/stale-after` even though the epochs match. That is static reading by both reviews, not a run. A keyword key survives re-registration.

**Rejected options:**
- **No named delays (B alone), keeping the parity judgement that `(def retry-ms 500)` is the re-frame2 spelling:** that covers static values only, not a delay computed from the snapshot. It also leaves fn keys opaque in tools and in the dispatched timer event, and leaves them fragile across reload.
- **A new error id for an unresolved name:** unnecessary, because `:rf.error/machine-bad-after-delay` already owns invalid `:after` keys.
- **Removing inline fn keys in favour of names:** both recommendations keep them.

**Supersedes:** the xstate-parity judgement in rf2-2n6uv.5.2's description: "Named delays need no feature: an `:after` map key is data, so `(def retry-ms 500)` and `{:after {retry-ms :b}}` is the re-frame2 spelling (N-A for parity)." No EP is involved.

## Work

**Spec** (this assumes rf2-m2x7s has already cut §Value shape to three forms)
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md`:
  - add a `:delays` row to §Transition table top-level keys, beside `:guards` / `:actions` (`:207-208`): optional, root-only, `{<keyword> <ms | ISO string | fn>}`, referenced by keyword from `:after` keys;
  - in §Value shape (`:2361-2368`), add the keyword form: it resolves machine-locally against `:delays`, an unresolved name is refused at registration, and one sentence gives the test seam;
  - add `:named` to the `:delay-source` set in §Trace events (`:2551`);
  - check §Lessons from xstate and the deliberate-omissions list for a delays row.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`:
  - add `[:delays {:optional true} [:map-of :keyword [:or pos-int? :string fn?]]]` to `:rf/transition-table`, beside `:guards` / `:actions` (`:2549-2550`);
  - add `:keyword` to the `:after` key `[:or ...]` (`:2564-2568`);
  - mention `:delays` in the reference-resolution paragraph (`:2714`);
  - add `:named` wherever `:delay-source` is enumerated.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2373`: the `:rf.error/machine-bad-after-delay` row also covers a keyword that names no `:delays` entry.

**Code** (under `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/`)
- `lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc` (`:1540-1609`):
  - accept a keyword key iff the machine's `:delays` contains it;
  - validate each `:delays` value by the same rule as an inline key (positive integer, valid ISO string, or fn);
  - refuse a non-map `:delays`, a non-keyword key in it, and `:delays` anywhere but the root, mirroring the `:guards` / `:actions` root-only rule;
  - make the missing-name message name the key and list the available names.
- `transition.cljc` `classify-delay-source` (`:641-661`): a keyword maps to `:named`.
- Resolution:
  - every path that resolves a delay key must resolve a name. That means the initial arm (`timer.cljc` `resolve-delay-ms` at `:112`, reached from the `after-schedule` fx at `:1004-1026`) and the hydration re-arm (`timer.cljc:505-564`);
  - the keyword-to-value lookup may happen wherever the machine definition is at hand, for example `build-after-fx`, which already has the machine;
  - calling a fn value stays in the timer fx, against the committed snapshot. Do not move evaluation.
- The timer event keeps carrying the keyword as its delay key, so the firing lookup at `transition.cljc:1129` matches in a re-registered definition.
- Traces: a named delay's `/scheduled`, `/fired`, `/stale-after` and `/cancelled` rows carry the keyword as `:delay`, just as raw keys are carried today, with `:delay-source :named`. Do not attempt the ms-on-trace repair here; that is a separate bead.

**Tools**
- Xray `sim.cljs` `format-delay-key` already formats keywords. Add a test only if none pins it.
- machines-viz: make sure a keyword `:after` key renders as its name on the chart and in the share grammar (`share.cljs:247-266`). No fake-vector stand-in is needed for it.

**Docs and skills**

title: Resolve nested history initials before committing the active state
description:
PR #11428 (4629779789) fixes entry through one compound's history initial, but a valid nested compound still commits a history pseudo-state. Reproducer: :group has :initial :sh, where :sh defaults to :inner; :inner has :initial :sh2, where :sh2 defaults to :leaf. Entering [:group] from :park with no history commits [:group :inner :sh2], instead of [:group :inner :leaf]. With :rf/history {[:group] :inner, [:group :inner] :other}, it still commits :sh2 instead of :other. The committed configuration therefore misses the real child's entry and event behavior, violating Spec005 Restoring's never-occupied rule and the new initial-history contract.

Evidence: the focused Babashka probe loaded the exact merged core/machines sources from git archive, exercised compute-transition-geometry and apply-transition-once, and reproduced both cases; an explicit target to the inner history correctly restored :other. A second probe ran the actual validate-machine! and accepted the same definition. Both exited 0; logs ai/pr-audit/pr-audit-sol-oct11-11428-history-1.log and -2.log. No shadow-cljs lane was entered. The complete source Bead also acknowledges this residual; the nested-history tracker search found no other matching issue.

Cause: compute-transition-geometry selects one history node from target-base/domain-leaf; resolve-history-target then uses initial-cascade for its default or shallow recorded child (transition.cljc:1928-1944), which can stop on a second pseudo-state without resolving it. Small correction: continue the existing restore semantics when that descent reaches another history pseudo-state, until the active leaf is real, retaining the existing exit boundary and entry cascade. Pin default and recorded nested entry, including the corresponding birth path where applicable, with a focused machines/conformance regression. No new author syntax or general framework is needed.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (PR #11444, branch worker/nested-history-initials, commit 04579fa766)

Fix: resolve-history-target (implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc) now passes every cascade it runs (shallow recording, deep recording, :default-target, and the :initial fallback) through a `descend` step. When an initial-cascade lands on another history pseudo-state, `descend` resolves that pseudo-state against the same snapshot, so each level restores its own recording, else its :default-target, and the returned :leaf is always real. The exit boundary, the entry cascade and the single :rf.machine.history/restored emit are unchanged, and the emit's :resolved-leaf is now the real leaf. A `seen` set (an internal 5-arity) ends the descent at a pseudo-state already on the chain, so a :default-target that leads back to one cannot loop. In that case the result is the same as before the fix.

Birth: the flat and parallel birth cascades both go through compute-transition-geometry (bootstrap-step -> apply-transition-once), so the same fix covers them. parallel.cljc needed no change.

Registration: no change needed. Any history pseudo-state that an :initial cascade reaches is its owning compound's :initial, so the existing naa5r check (:rf.error/machine-history-bad-default-target) already refuses a nested one with no :default-target. The fix now pins that check for the nested case.

Tests (machine_history_smoke_test.clj): the nested entry is pinned three ways: nothing recorded -> [:group :inner :leaf]; inner recorded -> :other; both recorded -> :other. The tests also pin the :entry log, the restored trace's :resolved-leaf, the flat and parallel birth cascades, and the nested registration refusal. The test580 fixture gains rows 5 and 6, for a nested chain in a parallel region (default, and both levels recorded). Spec 005 §Restoring gains one sentence: a restore's own cascade resolves the chain the same way.

Red/green: on the tip engine (3fa88920c8) the smoke namespace had 3 failures, each committing [:group :inner :sh2], and the core conformance test failed on test580 rows 5 and 6, which also committed :sh2. Both exited 1. With the fix both exit 0. A planted expectation in row 5 went red (exit 1), and the restore was verified by blob hash against HEAD. Full scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh exited 0. The machines lane went from 653/1519 to 656/1526, exactly the predicted +3 tests and +7 assertions.

Finding, not built: registration accepts a :default-target that names the pseudo-state itself, or whose cascade leads back to it (validation's resolves-to-state? accepts any declared node, history nodes included). The runtime guard stops such a descent at the repeated pseudo-state instead of looping. Refusing these at registration would be a separate change.
close_reason:
Merged in #11444. transition.cljc resolve-history-target now continues every restore cascade (shallow recording, deep recording, :default-target, and the :initial fallback) whenever it lands on another history pseudo-state. Each level restores its own recording, else its :default-target, against the same post-exit snapshot, so the resolved leaf is always real. A seen set stops descent at a pseudo-state already on the chain. The exit boundary, the entry cascade and the single :rf.machine.history/restored emit are unchanged; its :resolved-leaf is now the real leaf. The flat and parallel birth paths go through compute-transition-geometry, so parallel.cljc needed no change. Registration already refuses a nested history :initial with no :default-target; that is now pinned.
Evidence:
- The new smoke tests on the tip engine exit 1 (3 failures, each committing [:group :inner :sh2]) and exit 0 with the fix.
- re-frame.conformance-test exits 1 on the tip engine (test580 rows 5-6 land on :sh2) and exits 0 with the fix; a planted expectation goes red.
- test-jvm-implementation 0. The machines lane went 653/1519 to 656/1526, as predicted.
- CI on 04579fa766: 80 checks, 0 failed.
Not built: registration accepts a :default-target that names its own pseudo-state, or whose cascade leads back to it. The seen guard keeps those inert.

title: Measure the fast-PR spine's per-tier timings, then resize the default local loop (keep a local CLJS check for CLJS diffs)
description:
Measure how long each tier of the local fast-PR spine takes, then resize the default local loop to match. Affected CLJS code must keep a useful local check.

## Ruling

Decided 2026-10-16. The tooling ruling (rf2-q50zr, rf2-agtw6, rf2-gj0wi, rf2-e9mwr, rf2-efv3u) makes CI the system of record for workers, so the default local loop should shrink.

The two reviews agreed on that and differed only on order:
- the decision dossier would make the CLJS node and isolation tiers opt-in now, treating the acceptance run as the measurement;
- an independent Codex review says to measure tier timings first, and to keep a local path for affected CLJS code.

Mike directed: "file necessary beads for the "Largely in agreement" list as outlined above". That settles it on the Codex side: measure first, then resize.

## Evidence (trunk 89517e8f54)

- AGENTS.md says the spine needs about 25 minutes against a 10-minute foreground cap, "so kill-and-restart is routine".
- Nobody has measured which tier dominates those 25 minutes.
- TESTING.md:164-168 measures the always-on static block (37 Python checkers) at 6.4 s in total, run one after another.
- CI already carries the full matrix:
  - TESTING.md says a local PASS is compatible with a red required check;
  - `check_fast_pr_gap.py` lists the required checks the spine never runs;
  - the dispatch template tells workers to declare a still-running gate "as reliance on CI".

## Work

1. **Measure.** Time each tier of `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` on at least three typical diffs: a core CLJS change, a JVM-only change and a docs/spec change. Record the per-tier wall times on this bead. Do this inside the granted shadow-cljs lane only; the build lane is machine-wide exclusive.
2. **Resize from the numbers.** The candidate shape is:
   - the static block, run in parallel;
   - the JVM suites the spine already selects;
   - the gate that AGENTS.md's "Which Gate Covers Which Edit" table names for the edit.

   Make the CLJS node and isolation tiers opt-in only to the extent the measurements show they dominate. Keep a local CLJS check whenever the diff touches CLJS sources. `--all` is unchanged.
3. **Update the docs.** TESTING.md (tier 1 and the Local commands) and AGENTS.md ("Running Gates").

## Sequencing

This lands after rf2-gj0wi (the shadow-cljs launcher with the machine-wide lock), so any opt-in CLJS tier is already lock-protected. No CLAUDE.md hot-zone files are touched. If AGENTS.md text that CLAUDE.md imports changes, keep the gate tables consistent.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The per-tier wall times for at least three typical diffs are recorded on this bead before any default changes.
2. On a typical diff, the default `test-fast-pr.sh` finishes in under 10 minutes. Quote the measured time.
3. A diff that touches CLJS sources still runs a local CLJS check by default, or the spine prints the exact opt-in command and the reason it skipped.
4. TESTING.md and AGENTS.md describe the new default. `--all` is unchanged.
notes:
== MEASUREMENT 2026-10-17 AUSEST (worker, PR #11435): per-tier wall times of scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, BEFORE any default changed ==
Method: the spine run by absolute path with every output line stamped by the shell's builtin clock (no fork per line), the spine's own exit code captured to a file; a step runs from its `==>` line to the next. Windows host, 24 cores, other workers live. Bare `python`/`python3` are the Microsoft Store stubs here, so the real interpreter was put first on PATH for every run.
- Run 1, trunk ecd8a3e6d5, `--all`, first run in a fresh worktree: always-on static/drift block 137s, docs tier 98s, clj-kondo 50s, JVM implementation/core 352s (1182 tests), test:scripts 261s then FAILED on the python3 stub (environment, not code), so the node tier's later steps did not run. Total 898s, exit 1.
- Run 2, branch at 56b254c14c (pki7q/0ruu3/1nrfo commits, spine unchanged), `--all`, shadow-cljs cache still COLD: always-on 75s, docs 131s, clj-kondo 52s, JVM implementation/core 397s, test:scripts 227s, test:cljs 350s (6182 tests / 17371 assertions), per-ns isolation 109s (+1s self-test), Fresco static gates (invariants + lint export) 6s, Fresco modules compile 119s. Total 1467s (24.5 min), exit 0. No lane wait (no `shadow-lane: waiting` line).
- Warm node-tier steps, run one after another as the spine runs them, each exit captured: test:cljs 251s, per-ns isolation 108s (+1s self-test), Fresco modules compile 71s, test:scripts 326s; all exit 0.
WHAT DOMINATES: the node tier, 811s of the 1467s cold run (55%). Within it test:cljs (the local CLJS check) is 251-350s; test:scripts 227-326s only matters to a script/manifest diff; isolation 108s and the Fresco compile 71-119s are CI-graded gates. The JVM core suite (352-397s) is the largest single step and runs for every implementation diff.
TYPICAL DIFFS UNDER THE OLD DEFAULT (classifier tiers x the times above): a docs-only diff ran always + docs, ~3.5 min; a spec page also arms the JVM tier, ~9.6 min; ANY implementation .clj/.cljc/.cljs diff arms both runtime tiers, so it ran the whole node tier after the JVM tier, ~23-25 min.

== WORKER SUMMARY 2026-10-17 01:40 AUSEST: PR #11435 (branch worker/tooling-lane-classifier), commit "build(spine): the default local loop keeps the node lanes a diff can reach, and the JVM tier overlaps the static gates" ==
WHAT CHANGED (scripts/test-fast-pr.sh; --all and the fallbacks are unchanged and still run every lane)
- A classified run narrows the node tier by the diff's own files: test:cljs and the Fresco static gates when the diff touches .clj/.cljc/.cljs/.edn (.clj included, since a macro namespace reaches CLJS) or implementation/package.json or its lockfile; test:scripts when it touches a .cjs/.mjs/.js file or a package manifest. Per-namespace isolation and the Fresco modules compile run under --all and the fallbacks; otherwise the PASS line names each with its command. A spine self-change still runs every lane. --plan prints the selection as PLAN-NODE.
- The JVM tier starts in the background at the top of the run, beside the static, documentation and lint gates, and is joined before the node tier. A red before the join reaps the background suite on exit.
- Spine self-test: six new NODE cases, 30/30 (a plant on the script trigger turns it red at 28/30). check_fast_pr_gap.py's lane notes say which lanes need --all (self-test and check exit 0). TESTING.md tier 1 and the Local commands row carry the measured times and the new default; AGENTS.md's ten-minute note no longer says kill-and-restart is routine.
FLAKE FOUND BY THE FIRST DESIGN: running the JVM suite BESIDE test:cljs failed the Story recorder's timer test (recorder_timer_child_cljs_test measured a 51ms gap against its 50ms threshold), exit 1 on the first CLJS fixture run. Hence the join before the node tier; the rerun passed.
MEASURED WITH THE NEW DEFAULT (by --repo-root fixture diffs; CPU ~90% busy with other workers' builds; each exit captured to a file):
- docs-only diff: 193s, exit 0 (always-on 76s, docs tier 115s; the JVM tier is not armed).
- spec page diff (docs + JVM): 457s, exit 0 (always-on 86s, docs tier 368s with mkdocs --strict at 274s under load against 32s in the docs run; the JVM suite ran entirely behind the docs tier).
- core .cljc diff (JVM + test:cljs + Fresco static; a .clj diff plans identically): 1024s, exit 0. The JVM suite took 730s under load against 352-397s on a quieter machine, so the static and lint gates were done at 304s and the join waited a further 426s; then test:cljs 287s and the Fresco static gates 5s.
AC STATUS
- AC1: per-tier times recorded on this bead before any default changed (the MEASUREMENT note above): two --all runs (trunk, then cold node) and warm node steps; typical diffs were derived from those tiers, then run as fixtures after the change.
- AC2: MET for docs-only (3.2 min) and spec (7.6 min) diffs. NOT MET for a Clojure source diff: 17.1 min measured under load; from the unloaded tier times the critical path is the JVM core suite (352-397s) and then test:cljs (251-350s), about 10-12.5 min. The remaining levers would each drop a check this bead or CI keeps local (the JVM core suite on a .cljc diff, or test:cljs on a CLJS diff, which AC3 requires), so they are held for Mike rather than taken.
- AC3: MET. A diff touching CLJS sources runs test:cljs and the Fresco static gates by default; the lanes it skips print their exact commands.
- AC4: MET. TESTING.md and AGENTS.md describe the new default; --all is unchanged (2301s, exit 0, including 663s of lane waits on other workers' builds).
close_reason:
Merged in #11435 (85559d7fe2). Measured first, then resized. The default local loop narrows the node tier to the lanes a diff can reach, and starts the JVM tier at the top of the run so it overlaps the static gates; it is joined before the node tier. Running JVM beside test:cljs caused a real timing flake (the Story recorder timer measured 51ms against its 50ms threshold), so they do not overlap.
Measured wall times on fixture diffs with the CPU about 90% busy: docs 193s, spec 457s, core .cljc 1024s (about 10-12.5 min estimated on a quiet machine). The spine self-test passes 30/30.
A .cljc diff stays slightly above 10 minutes. The only remaining levers are dropping the JVM core suite or test:cljs on such a diff, and the ruling requires the local CLJS check. CI is the system of record for workers, so this ruling is met.

title: Fresco test kit: runtime.cljs docstring still says test_kit/src is outside the artefact's :paths
description:
## Defect

The namespace docstring of `implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test/runtime.cljs` ends (lines 27-31) by saying that Xray's suites drive the commit seam "through the artefact's `:paths`, which this source root is outside of".

That is no longer true. `implementation/fresco/deps.edn:85` reads `{:paths ["src" "resources" "test_kit/src"]`, so the kit's source root is on the artefact's `:paths`. rf2-k33yt made that change, and rf2-6lrwv corrected four other comments but missed this one.

Verified by reading at trunk 3fa88920c8.

## Change

Rewrite the last clause in the present tense. The seam lives on the collector because it is the runtime's own seam rather than an instrument. Drop the claim about `:paths`, or state it correctly. Search the Fresco tree once more for any other comment that places `test_kit/src` outside `:paths`, and fix it in the same change.

## Acceptance

No comment or docstring under `implementation/fresco/` says that `test_kit/src` is outside the artefact's `:paths`.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (PR #11455, branch worker/ssr-fresco-hydration, commit becdf0a85d) ==
Done. The re-frame.fresco.test.runtime docstring's last clause now reads that the commit seam lives on the collector because it is the runtime's own seam rather than an instrument; the false claim that test_kit/src is outside the artefact's :paths is gone (implementation/fresco/deps.edn's :paths is ["src" "resources" "test_kit/src"]). Census of the 227 tracked files under implementation/fresco, run line by line, with whitespace collapsed, and with comment markers stripped then collapsed: only this docstring placed test_kit/src outside :paths. The line-oriented pass missed it, because the clause wraps; the two flattened passes found it.
close_reason: Merged in #11455 (087f52b0f9; commit becdf0a85d). implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test/runtime.cljs's namespace docstring no longer says test_kit/src is outside the artefact's :paths (implementation/fresco/deps.edn puts it on :paths); the clause now says the seam lives on the collector because it is the runtime's own seam. A three-way search of implementation/fresco found no other comment making the claim.

title: Plain-atom derived values throw on subscribe-container on both hosts, breaking the Spec 006 promise rf2-zuviv keeps
description:
## Defect

Spec 006 promises that `subscribe-container` works on a derived container as it does on a base container (`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` ~222, and the push clause at ~232). The plain-atom adapter breaks that promise on both hosts, and the SSR adapter reuses the same derived value:

- `subscribe-container` calls `add-watch` unconditionally (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/atom_container.cljc:26-32`).
- The plain-atom derived value cannot take a watch:
  - on CLJS it is a `reify` of `IDeref` and `IDisposable` only, with no `IWatchable` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/plain_atom.cljc:81-99`);
  - on the JVM it is an `rf.interop/make-reaction` `Reaction`, which implements `IDeref` but not `IRef` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.clj` ~97).
- So `(subscribe-container derived on-change)` throws under the plain-atom adapter, headless or SSR, on either host. Verified by reading at trunk 3fa88920c8. Not yet reproduced by a test.

rf2-zuviv (ruling 4) keeps the `:subscribe-container` derived-container observer door because Spec 006 promises it. So the fix is to make the headless adapters honour the promise, not to narrow it.

## Change

Make the plain-atom derived value observable on both hosts. Roughly: `add-watch` on the derived value installs a watch on each source container, recomputes on a source change, and calls `on-change` with the previous and new computed values when they differ. `remove-watch` removes those source watches, and disposal removes any that are left. The derived value still recomputes on deref and keeps no cache, and layered input release keeps working.

If you find that honouring the promise headlessly costs more than it is worth, STOP and report. Narrowing Spec 006 instead would reverse part of rf2-zuviv, and that is Mike's call.

## Acceptance

- A test on each host: subscribe to a plain-atom derived value over a base container, write the base container, and see one `on-change` with the old and new computed values. Unsubscribing stops further calls. Writing an unrelated value that leaves the computed value unchanged produces no call.
- The same test runs through the SSR adapter's derived value, or a test shows that SSR shares the plain-atom derived value.
- The existing plain-atom and SSR suites stay green.
notes:
== WORKER 2026-10-17 14:16:07 AUSEST: IMPLEMENTED IN PR #11457 (draft until CI is green) ==
Branch worker/substrate-leftovers, commit 52247acbab, based on 63b7046123.
- re-frame.substrate.plain-atom/make-derived-value now reifies IRef on the JVM and IWatchable on CLJS. Each add-watch watches every source for that observer, recomputes when a source changes, and calls the watch with (key ref old new) when the computed value moved by =. The observer's baseline is the value at attach. remove-watch removes that observer's source watches, and disposal removes any left. Deref still recomputes with no cache. The SSR adapter reuses this value under its own subscribe-container, so it gains the fix with no edit.
- JVM disposal keeps rf.interop Reaction's semantics: snapshot-and-clear, then fire, with no disposed-once flag. The sub-cache re-arms a held slot's on-dispose callback across substrate disposes. sub-dispose-trace-test/substrate-dispose-keeps-a-held-slot-until-its-unsubscribe went red (2 failures) under a guarded first cut, which is why the flag is absent. CLJS keeps its disposed-once guard.
- On the JVM the value implements rf.interop/IDisposeRegistry, so rf.interop add-on-dispose!/dispose! now dispatch with (satisfies? IDisposeRegistry x), where they used (instance? Reaction x). Non-implementers still take the weak fallback registry.
- Spec 006: two sentences the fix made false were edited. One is in the frame-construction paragraph (the plain-atom value installs no source watch at construction, watches its sources only while observed, and removes those watches on disposal). The other is the revertibility row (the value holds its observers' entries in the transient watch registry). There was no narrowing, so the promise stands.
- New tests:
  - core re-frame.substrate.plain-atom-derived-watch-cljs-test (.cljc, both hosts) has three tests. The first: one call per change, none after unsubscribe, none on an unchanged computed value, and deref still recomputes. The second: a layered derived value through its input, and unsubscribing releases the inner watch. The third: disposal removes an observer's source watches.
  - ssr re-frame.ssr.derived-value-watch-cljs-test runs the first case through the SSR adapter map.
- Red on tip 63b7046123: JVM core 3 errors and ssr 1 error, each ClassCastException Reaction -> IRef. CLJS 4 errors, No protocol method IWatchable.-add-watch.
- Green on bc29eb9962:
  - scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh exit 0, with core 1188/3625 -> 1191/3632 and ssr 327/1593 -> 328/1597. Every other lane is unchanged.
  - npm run test:cljs exit 0, 6191/17442 -> 6195/17453.
  - Every delta matched its prediction.
  - scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0.
- Out of fence, filed as rf2-lay42: six Fresco/Xray test comments still say the plain-atom derived value is not IWatchable, and Spec 006's illustrative plain-atom listing still shows an IDeref-only reify.
close_reason: Merged in #11457 (1b68249024; commit 52247acbab). The plain-atom derived value takes a watch on both hosts: it reifies IRef on the JVM and IWatchable on CLJS. add-watch watches each source for that one observer, recomputes on a source change, and calls the watch with old and new values when they differ by =; remove-watch removes that observer's source watches and disposal removes any left; deref still recomputes with no cache. The SSR adapter reuses this value, so it is fixed with no edit of its own. interop.clj's add-on-dispose! and dispose! check satisfies? IDisposeRegistry instead of instance? Reaction. The JVM value keeps the old Reaction dispose behaviour (a dispose-once guard turned substrate-dispose-keeps-a-held-slot-until-its-unsubscribe red, because the JVM sub-cache re-registers a held slot's dispose callback across disposes); CLJS keeps its guard. Spec 006's frame-construction paragraph and revertibility row, which the fix made false, are corrected; the promise is not narrowed. Evidence: on tip 63b7046123 JVM core 3 errors, JVM ssr 1 error (ClassCastException: Reaction cannot be cast to IRef), CLJS 4 errors (No protocol method IWatchable.-add-watch); on bc29eb9962 test-jvm-implementation.sh exit 0 (core 1188/3625 -> 1191/3632, ssr 327/1593 -> 328/1597, as predicted), npm run test:cljs exit 0 (6191/17442 -> 6195/17453), test-fast-pr.sh exit 0, CI 84 checks 0 failed. Six Fresco/Xray test comments and Spec 006's example plain-atom listing (~1771) still describe the old non-watchable value: rf2-lay42.

title: machines-viz svg-export over-redaction assertion cannot fail: assert a distinctive non-sensitive value instead of a bare "7"
description:
Mike's ruling on rf2-hxi3z restored the "non-sensitive value still renders" assertion in tools/machines-viz/test/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/export_dom_cljs_test.cljs, deftest svg-export-redacts-sensitive-live-context, "because it guards against over-redaction, which the secret-absent checks don't cover". #11439 (rf2-b9pv4) restored it exactly as ruled: :context-band {:card secret :count 7} and (is (str/includes? svg "7")). title: Delete emit-ui-tree after moving dom-attr-aliases and validate-tag-name! into html_helpers
description:
## Ruling

Delete `re-frame.ssr/emit-ui-tree`, the Spec 004B "version-1 structural tree" to HTML serialiser. It is a seam with no application caller. Before deleting it, move the two helpers the hiccup emitter borrows from it.

This deletion does NOT decide what Fresco's L2 test kit returns. The kit stays an independent consumer of Spec 004B, and its semantic-tree assertions and the 004B conversion rules stay.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned, with the instruction:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both recommendations delete `emit-ui-tree` as a separate piece of work, moving the shared tag and attribute helpers first.

Decisive facts, all at trunk 89517e8f54:
- **No server path calls it.** Its only non-test references are the facade re-export (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:44`) and an error-site name in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error.cljc:112`. Spec 004B names the producers it serves: Fresco's L2 test kit (`re-frame.fresco.test/tree`) builds the tree, and `emit-ui-tree` folds it (`spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:23-32`). Fresco's own server renders through `react-dom/server`.
- **It is large for a seam with no caller.** `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/ui_tree.cljc` is 1,240 lines, plus the 423-line `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/emit_ui_tree_cljs_test.cljc`. Its recorded defects (rf2-a5ara, rf2-gzrdp, rf2-xow4c, rf2-wt2wy, all closed) were repairs to a door no application uses.
- **The hiccup emitter borrows two things from it.** `dom-attr-aliases` and `validate-tag-name!` come from `ui_tree.cljc` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:44` require, uses at `:130`, `:364`, `:370`). So they must move before the namespace goes.

Rejected options:
- **Keep it parked for a future non-React renderer.** A serialisation boundary should be justified by a concrete consumer when one exists. Every current substrate is React-family.
- **Keep it as the input to a `ui-tree-fingerprint` adoption channel.** The companion ruling retires hash-based mismatch channels, so the deferred fingerprint candidate (`spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:628`, `:666`, `:748-749`) has nothing to serve.

Supersedes: 004B's deferred `ui-tree-fingerprint` candidate. It also overrides the 004B §The SSR consumption boundary contract (`spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:607`). It supersedes no bead ruling.

## Work

Code, under `implementation/`:
- Move `dom-attr-aliases`, `validate-tag-name!`, and anything only they need, from `ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/ui_tree.cljc` into `ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc`. Then re-point `ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc`: the require at `:44`, and the references at `:85`, `:101`, `:130`, `:267`, `:364`, `:370`.
- Delete `ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/ui_tree.cljc` and the facade def `ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:44`. Drop the `'rf.ssr/emit-ui-tree` site name in `core/src/re_frame/error.cljc:112`.
- Tests:
  - delete `ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/emit_ui_tree_cljs_test.cljc`;
  - drop the `:rf.error/ssr-ui-tree-version-unsupported` case in `ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/diagnostic_cycle_cljs_test.cljs:196`;
  - re-point `ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_attr_name_react_parity_test.clj` and `ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_boolean_attr_react_parity_test.clj` at `render-to-string`, keeping their react-dom parity rows;
  - update the mention in `ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_emit_test.clj`.

Spec:
- `spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md`:
  - Delete §The SSR consumption boundary (`:607-763`), including the deferred `ui-tree-fingerprint` candidate.
  - Trim §Producers and the consumer (`:23-50`): the L2 test kit is the producer and its assertions the consumer.
  - Trim the Coverage and Ripples mentions (`:829`).
  - KEEP the node schema, the normalization `N` and the DOM conversion table (`:449-606`). `render-to-string` and Fresco's React emitter both cite them.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2392`: delete the `:rf.error/ssr-ui-tree-version-unsupported` row. KEEP `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` (`:2391`): Fresco's test kit raises it (`implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test.cljs`).
- `spec/API.md:368` (the `emit-ui-tree` row) and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`: hand-edit them, then regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn` with `generate!` in `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`.
- Update `spec/011-SSR.md`, `spec/Conventions.md`, `spec/Ownership.md` and `spec/README.md` where they name `emit-ui-tree`. 011 is the one i/crlf file: edit it with the Edit tool or Python bytes, never `sed -i`.

Docs:
- `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md` (the `emit-ui-tree` entry, and the version-unsupported id at `:608`).
- `docs/design/fresco/production-server-arm.md:626`: change it only where it reads as a live seam.
- Leave `docs/EP/EP-0034-...` as the historical record it is.

Deliberately stays:
- the Fresco L2 test kit (`re-frame.fresco.test/tree`) and its tests;
- 004B's node schema and conversion rules;
- `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`.

Not decided here: whether L2 returns the v1 tree or normalised hiccup. That belongs to the Fresco test-kit work. Deleting this seam only makes that choice cheaper, because no SSR consumer has to stay compatible.

## Sequencing

- Hot zones touched:
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/Conventions.md`, and `spec/API.md` with both manifest sidecars;
  - `spec/011-SSR.md` (the one i/crlf file).
- Depends on rf2-qyjv2, the hash-channel deletion. Both edit `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc`, `spec/API.md`, the manifests, 009 and 011, so they run in sequence, never in parallel.
- Cross-dossier: `fresco-taught-default-or-optional.md` owns the L2 tree-shape question (Fresco OQ4). This bead must not change the test kit, and that dossier's work may follow it freely.

## Evidence

Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:
- the facade def and the error-site name;
- the emit.cljc borrowings;
- the file sizes;
- 004B's producer and consumer text and its section map;
- Fresco test kit's use of `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`.

Still needs a run: everything. No build or test was run for this ruling.

1. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/ui_tree.cljc` and `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/emit_ui_tree_cljs_test.cljc` are deleted, and `emit.cljc` has no `ui-tree` require.
2. `dom-attr-aliases` and `validate-tag-name!` live in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc`. The attribute-name and boolean-attribute react-dom parity tests drive `render-to-string`, and both pass.
3. `git grep -n -E "emit-ui-tree|ssr-ui-tree-version-unsupported|ui-tree-fingerprint"` over `implementation spec docs tools`, excluding `docs/EP` and `implementation/node_modules`, returns nothing. As a control, run it on trunk first and confirm it finds them.
4. Spec 004B still carries its node schema, its normalization `N` and its DOM conversion table. `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` keeps its 009 row, and the Fresco test-kit tests pass unchanged.
5. `spec/api-manifest.edn` is regenerated with `generate!`, and the `api-manifest` lint job is green. `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` are green, and so are the SSR JVM tests and `npm run test:cljs`.
6. `spec/011-SSR.md` keeps CRLF line endings: CR count == CRLF count, and bare LF == 0.

title: Machines timer.cljc restore-batch docstrings and owner-gone? short-circuits still assume a listener can seat a same-id successor mid-restore
description:
Found by the rf2-f0clv worker (#11491, merged), outside its fence.

Epoch perform-restore! runs inside serialize-tool-write!, which defers trace listeners until the section ends. #11491 measured that no production hook body can destroy or reseat a frame inside it.

Three docstrings in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc still say that an epoch-restore cancel batch can meet a same-id successor B, seated by a listener on the cancel trace's own stack:
- cancel-snapshotted-entry!;
- cancel-frame-timers-on-restore!;
- successor-published?-fn.
Under perform-restore! those traces are deferred, so cancel-frame-timers-on-restore!'s owner-gone? short-circuit cannot fire from a restore.

#11483 (rf2-c0yds) rewrote the batch list to name two kinds of batch as able to meet B: "epoch restore" and "a direct rearm-after-timers!". The restore half is now false.

Work:
1. Census every caller of each of these:
   - cancel-frame-timers-on-restore!;
   - rearm-after-timers!;
   - cancel-timers-absent-from!;
   - successor-published?-fn. Its callers include machines hydrate.cljc ~364 and timer.cljc ~548/~1023/~1058.
   For each caller, decide whether it runs inside a router drain, inside a serialized tool write, or neither. Re-run a hit plant with an always-fires control on each owner-gone? short-circuit.
2. A short-circuit that only tests reach (tests calling the fn directly outside any drain): delete it. Delete with it the tests that only pin it, plus successor-published?-fn if nothing else uses it.
3. A short-circuit a real out-of-drain caller reaches: keep it, and name that caller in its docstring.
4. Restate the three docstrings, and the batch list, to what is true now.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (2026-10-18 00:44:49 AUSEST): draft PR #11493, commit f10b56fa40 on worker/timer-restore (base 2b4bacec87) ==

Outcome: case 2 for every short-circuit. Each owner-gone? short-circuit in the machines timer and hydration seams fires only when a test calls the fn directly, outside any drain or serialized section. No production caller reaches one, so all of them are deleted, along with successor-published?-fn.

Caller census (the cited lines matched at tip: hydrate.cljc 364, timer.cljc 548/1023/1058):
- cancel-frame-timers-on-restore!: the :machines/on-frame-restored! hook, called from epoch quiesce-orphaned-async-host-work!, called from perform-restore!. Runs in a serialized tool write.
- rearm-after-timers!: the :rf.machine/hydrate-rearm fx, emitted by :rf/hydrate and :rf/install-frame-state. Runs in the installing event's drain. The :machines/rearm-after-hydration! hook is read only as a presence gate (ssr hydrate.cljc and core events.cljc, both some?), and nothing in tools/** names it.
- cancel-timers-absent-from!: rearm-after-timers! only.
- successor-published?-fn: hydrate rearm-after-timers! title: Core facade: delete the test-only reg-view aliases and the uncalled core-epoch clear-epoch-listeners! wrapper
description:
