title: HTTP: refuse a :retry map without :max-attempts, which today validates and then never retries
description:
## Defect

`:retry {:on #{…}}` without `:max-attempts` never retries, because the retry gate requires `(some? max-attempts)` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc` ~939-942). Yet `validate-retry!` (`handlers.cljc` ~50-101) accepts that map, while it rejects an equally inert vector `:on`.

## Change

`validate-retry!` refuses a `:retry` map that lacks `:max-attempts`, with the existing bad-retry error family.

Do not default the missing keys: a default could silently add write attempts to a request that is not idempotent. An omitted `:retry` still never retries.

## Acceptance

- A `:retry` map without `:max-attempts` is refused at issue.
- A complete map retries as it does today.
- An omitted `:retry` never retries, pinned by a test.
- Spec 014 §Retry states the rule.

Checked at trunk f4e5adad0a.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY 2026-10-19 00:52:30 AUSEST (PR #11501, branch worker/http-routing-validate, commit 195a1a8063) ==
Disposition: done.
Premise held at tip 9a69891d05: validate-retry! (http handlers.cljc) accepted a :retry map with no :max-attempts, and maybe-retry! (transport.cljc) retries only under (some? max-attempts), so such a map validated and never retried.
Change: validate-retry! now refuses a :retry map whose :max-attempts is absent or nil with :rf.error/http-bad-retry-on, ex-data :received carrying the map. It runs after the existing :on shape and membership checks, so their ex-data is unchanged. No default is supplied. The test-support stubs call the same validator, so they refuse it too.
Spec 014: the :max-attempts row reads "Required"; a paragraph after the §Retry and backoff key table states the refusal, the no-default reason (a retry re-sends a possibly non-idempotent request) and that an omitted :retry never retries; the §Request envelope :retry row's Errors cell names the new case.
Tests: http_retry_on_validation_test a-retry-map-without-max-attempts-is-refused (3 rows: no :max-attempts, :max-attempts nil, {}); http_body_prep_failure_test throwing-body-thunk-is-not-retried-without-a-retry-policy pins that an omitted :retry runs the attempt once. Scoped JVM run green, exit 0 (8 tests, 18 assertions); with the pre-change handlers.cljc planted, exit 1 with 3 failures, all in the new refusal test.
Census: every tracked :retry map literal outside test prose carries :max-attempts, except the stub test's {:on #{:rf.http/aborted}}, which still fails on :on membership first.
Outside the fence, left for a follow-up: the Spec 009 catalogue row for :rf.error/http-bad-retry-on describes only the :on cases; docs/api/re-frame.http.md line 75 says "without it nothing is retried" and its errors list (line 102) names only the :on case.
close_reason: Merged in #11501 (195a1a8063). validate-retry! now refuses a :retry map whose :max-attempts is absent or nil, with :rf.error/http-bad-retry-on (ex-data :received). It runs after the existing :on checks and supplies no default. Spec 014 §Retry states the rule. New tests: the refusal, and a pin that an omitted :retry makes exactly one attempt. The scoped JVM run exited 0 (8 tests, 18 assertions); with the pre-change file planted it exited 1 with 3 failures, all in the new test. The Spec 009 catalogue row for http-bad-retry-on and docs/api/re-frame.http.md (~75, ~102) still describe only the :on cases; that was outside the fence and is filed as a follow-up bead.

title: Machines: normalise a definition once at registration, not on every transition
description:
## Current

Registration already desugars `:timeout` and `:choice` (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc` ~2553). Even so, `machine-transition` re-runs both desugars, and `normalise-region-order`, on every call (`parallel.cljc` ~1857-1858). For a definition with no `:choice`, `any-choice?` walks the whole tree and finds nothing (`choice.cljc` ~139-155). The per-call seam exists for the conformance op, which passes raw definitions.

## Change

Normalise raw definitions at the conformance entry, or mark a registered definition as normalised and skip the seam for it. Either way, a registered machine is normalised once.

## Acceptance

- The machines JVM and CLJS suites and the machine conformance fixtures stay green.
- A test shows that a registered machine's transition does not re-run the desugarers.

Checked at trunk f4e5adad0a.
notes:
== WORKER PASS (spec-machines-adapters, PR #11499): PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD (no code change)

Checked at trunk 9a69891d05.

Registration desugars only a validation copy, not the registered definition:
- `validate-machine!` (lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc, near line 2553) binds the desugared form locally for its checks and discards it.
- The definition the machine handler closes over (`make-machine-handler`, lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc near line 953) is the as-written one; `install-region-cache` normalises only the region order.
- The `:rf/machine` registrar projection (`register-machine-event!`, near line 1270) is also the as-written definition.

So the per-call desugar in `parallel/machine-transition` and `apply-initial-entry-cascade` is load-bearing for registered machines, not a redundant re-run. A registered machine with `:choice` or `:timeout` is rebuilt on every call.

Normalising once therefore means handing the handler the desugared definition, and that is not behaviour-identical:
- cofx_attach's dispatch-time ensure-set walks the machine it is handed.
- `after-diet-for-event` looks up the timer's delay key under the node's `:after`.
- On the as-written definition, a state-level `:timeout`'s lowered `:after` entry does not exist, so the `:rf.cofx/requires` of its `:on-timeout` guard and action are not ensured. On a desugared definition they are.
- No test covers `:timeout` combined with machine cofx requires, so the suite would not notice the change.
- The `:rf/machine` projection must stay as-written in either case, because tools read the authored grammar.

Two routes, for a ruling:
(a) The handler holds the normalised definition, and the projection stays as-written. This normalises a registered machine once, and it also makes the cofx ensure-set cover `:on-timeout` transitions, a gap this same code has today.
(b) Behaviour-identical but partial: at registration, stamp a normalised marker only when normalisation is the identity (no `:choice` or `:timeout`), so the seam skips the two no-op scans in the common case. Machines with `:choice` or `:timeout` keep desugaring on every call.

== RULING (mayor, 2026-10-19 01:40 AUSEST, under the project posture): take route (a) ==
The spec-machines-adapters worker (#11499) found the bead's premise wrong as written. Registration desugars only a throwaway copy for validation; the machine handler and the :rf/machine registrar entry keep the definition as written, so the per-transition desugar is doing real work, not repeating it. It also found a live gap: the dispatch-time coeffect check reads :after on the machine it is handed, and with the as-written definition a state-level :timeout has no :after entry yet, so the :rf.cofx/requires on its :on-timeout guard and action are never ensured. No test covers this.
Route (a): the handler and the registrar entry hold the NORMALISED definition, desugared once at registration, and the per-transition desugar goes. That is what this bead asked for, and it closes the coeffect gap as a consequence. Add a test that is red at trunk: a state-level :timeout whose :on-timeout guard or action declares :rf.cofx/requires gets that coeffect ensured. Route (b), skipping only the no-op scans, is not taken.
Watch for: tools and tests that read the registrar entry and may expect the as-written shape (Xray's machine view, machines-viz, Story, conformance). Census the registrar readers and say in the PR body what each sees now.
Merged-PR audit #11499: follow-up rf2-yjgn9 — Machines: timeout transitions skip required coeffects. This is a separate open finding; the source status and ruling are preserved.
== WORKER PASS (machines-conformance, PR #11507): DONE on RULING route (a), awaiting merge

Verified at source at trunk 0b46c53541: the cited sites held (parallel.cljc machine-transition re-ran both desugars plus normalise-region-order per call, ~1857-1858; apply-initial-entry-cascade did the same, ~1993-1994; build-region-machine desugared each region body on a cache miss, ~288; validation.cljc ~2553 desugared a check-local copy; choice.cljc any-choice? ~139-155).

Change (commit 57ea2eb7b8):
- parallel/normalise-definition (new): :timeout/:on-timeout -> :after, :type :choice -> :always, canonical :region-order. Pure, idempotent.
- registration/registered-definition (new, public so registration-refusal tests can probe it): validates the definition AS WRITTEN in the existing order (region order, then index-ensure-sets' inline/requires refusals, then validate-machine!), then normalises once and attaches the region cache. register-machine-event! publishes that one value as :rf/machine and hands it to make-machine-handler, which now builds a handler over a registered definition and no longer validates.
- parallel/machine-transition, apply-initial-entry-cascade and build-region-machine no longer desugar or normalise region order. The public re-frame.machines/machine-transition (the raw-definition entry, also what the conformance :machine-transition op calls) normalises the definition it is handed.
- validate-machine! keeps its local desugar for its own structural checks and its nil return (public contract unchanged), so registration desugars twice (check, publish) and no transition desugars.
- Spec 005's spec-as-data note (Spawning section) said the :rf/machine projection returns the user-written spec verbatim; it now says it returns the spec as written, normalised once at registration, and names what is lowered.
- Present-tense docstrings in choice/timeout/cofx_attach/validation/parallel/registration.

Gap closed: the dispatch-time coeffect ensure-set walks the lowered :after, so a state-level :timeout whose :on-timeout guard or action declares :rf.cofx/requires now has that coeffect ensured.

Tests:
- machine_cofx_attach_test/on-timeout-guard-and-action-facts-are-ensured (guard case + action case) and region_initial_desugar_test/a-registered-machine-runs-without-desugaring (counts desugar-timeouts/desugar-choices calls across birth and a transition through a :choice node; requires 0). Run against trunk source first: exit 1, 3 failures (guard case stayed :waiting; action case read nil for its fact; 6 desugar calls). After the change: exit 0. Both runs 10 tests / 23 assertions.
- Registration-refusal probes that called make-machine-handler now call registration/registered-definition (parallel_test, parallel_root_on_test, region_on_done_test, region_cross_region_target_test, machine_cofx_attach_test, machine_cofx_sub_source_test). region_order_cljs_test's two refusal tests call the public machine-transition.
- Machines JVM suite: trunk export baseline 641 tests / 1505 assertions (6 errors, all docs-file reads absent from the export); after the change exit 0, 643 tests / 1509 assertions, 0 failures - delta +2 tests / +4 assertions, exactly the two new tests.
- test:cljs (node lane, build compiled from this worktree): exit 0, 6149 tests / 17321 assertions, 0 failures.
- Core JVM suite (conformance corpus incl. the machine fixtures, and the core tests reading the registrar): exit 0, 1185 tests / 3590 assertions, 0 failures.
- These local runs are on the pre-merge branch; after merging main the PR's CI is the evidence for the new base.

Registrar-reader census (every reader now sees the as-written spec except: :timeout/:on-timeout appear as their :after entry, spawn-level ones moved onto the spawn-bearing state's :after, choice nodes as :always nodes; guards/actions entries, node :source-coords, :schemas, :doc, :sensitive/:large, :spawn maps and :region-order unchanged): machine handler; resolver spec-from-registry/-snapshot consumers (spawn, destroy exit cascade - now walks the lowered :after/:always, destroy/finalize nil-checks, data_validation [:schemas :data], tooling algebra views, actor-handler-meta, hydrate active-after-decls whose own desugar is now a no-op); core_machines guard/action handler-meta (entries unchanged); epoch tool_pair machine :spec (normalised); conformance runner (:machine-transition via the public fn, :reg-machine via validate-machine!). Tools, not edited: Xray machine inspector/topology/definition detail/sim and machines-viz see the normalised definition, and machines-viz already lowers both grammars at its own boundary so charts are unchanged; Xray epoch view reads :source-coords and guard/action entries (unchanged); Story reads only the [:rf/machine id] snapshot sub; the re-frame2-pair preload machine spec and pair-mcp handler-meta return the normalised spec. No tools source reads :on-timeout or :type :choice.

Finding: an inline :rf.cofx/requires on an :on-timeout transition map used to register silently (the as-written sweep never visits :on-timeout) and was never ensured; it is now refused with :rf.error/machine-cofx-requires-inline by the sweep over the registered definition, labelled "state :w :after" (probed directly). Consistent with every other inline home; the label names :after, not :on-timeout. Not changed.
close_reason: Merged in #11507 (57ea2eb7b8), on the mayor's route (a). The new parallel/normalise-definition lowers :timeout onto :after, :choice onto :always, and fixes :region-order. The new public registration/registered-definition validates the definition as written, in the existing check order, then normalises it once and attaches the region cache. The :rf/machine registrar entry and the handler now hold that same value. The coeffect gap is closed: a state-level :timeout whose :on-timeout guard or action declares :rf.cofx/requires now has it ensured. Two new tests were red against trunk (3 failures) and are green: the :on-timeout facts are ensured, and a registered machine's birth plus a choice-node transition makes zero desugar calls. title: check-examples-compile: enumerate :builds keys with the EDN reader, not a line-anchored regex
description:
## Defect

`enumerateCompiledBuilds` (`implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs` ~166-176) finds build keys with a line-anchored regex over the whole of `shadow-cljs.edn`. So a valid declaration such as `:builds {:examples/new {`, whose first key sits mid-line, is missed.

If the other declarations still clear their per-prefix floors, reconciliation then verifies only the reduced set. No build is known to be missed today.

## Change

Enumerate the `:builds` keys with `implementation/scripts/lib/edn.cjs`, which `lib/publishable-runtimes.cjs` already uses. Check that the reader handles the current configuration, and fail explicitly on any form it does not support. Keep the summary reconciliation and a small non-empty check.

## Acceptance

A unit test shows that reformatting the same map preserves the roster, and that nested lookalikes and `#_`-discarded declarations stay excluded.

Checked at trunk f4e5adad0a.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (test-tooling, 2026-10-19 02:13 AUSEST) — DONE, PR #11505, commit a535849d31 ==

Premise verified at tip 9a69891d05: enumerateCompiledBuilds matched ^\s*:(examples|testbeds)/name\s*\{ per line, so a key mid-line was invisible; buildsMissingWarningsAsErrors sliced blocks with a second line-anchored scan (^ {2}:) and matched :warnings-as-errors true anywhere in the block.

Change (implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs): readBuildEntries reads shadow-cljs.edn with lib/edn.cjs and returns the :builds map's entries, throwing EdnReadError on an unsupported form, a non-map config, a missing :builds map, a non-keyword key or a non-map build. enumerateCompiledBuilds takes the keys under the swept prefixes; buildsMissingWarningsAsErrors reads each swept build's own [:compiler-options :warnings-as-errors] from the same parse (moved too, because the swept set and the flag check must cover the same builds). The CLI reports an EdnReadError explicitly and exits 1. Summary reconciliation and the per-prefix floors (10/10) unchanged; stripEdnComments, used only here, removed. lib/edn.cjs header lists the new consumer.

title: Story: use the restore cursor for stepper undo pre-images
description:
Audited PR #11506 at 4ed5625888408e8ada7e0b4746ad76e73103cfeb. The new re-frame.epoch/current-epoch-id is correct, but Story's actual UI consumer still chooses undo pre-images from the history tail. This is the existing behavior gap recorded outside the PR's fence in rf2-d9qnj; this separate open bug tracks the remaining consumer fix.

Concrete user sequence on a counter variant whose setup sets 0 and whose script increments:
Start -> Step (1) -> Step (2) -> Back (1) -> Step (2) -> Back.
Expected: counter 1, UI cursor 1, and the first step's settled epoch restored.
Actual source behavior: counter 2 while UI cursor is decremented to 1. The first Back restores E1 but leaves E2 at the history tail. The repeated forward step then pushes E2 as its pre-image; the next Back restores that undone step's state instead of E1. Rewind followed by stepping can select the wrong pre-image for the same reason.

Evidence:
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/stepper_state.cljs:68-73 current-epoch-id reads (-> (rf.story.assertions/epoch-history variant-id) last :epoch-id).
- step! at line 195 captures that value and pushes it on :epoch-stack after stepping.
- step-back! at line 232 restores (peek stack), pops the stack and decrements the UI/substrate cursor.
- assertions/epoch-history delegates to the ordinary epoch-history read, so it does not follow restore.
- The PR's new Story test stops after the repeated forward step, before the second Back that exposes the wrong pre-image.

Focused JVM probe against an isolated archive of this exact merge mirrors the UI's source epoch-stack algorithm using genuine public frame dispatch and epoch restore APIs; it does not compile or execute the React UI. The history-tail selector leaves count 2 and restores the wrong epoch after back-step-back. The paired control selecting re-frame.epoch/current-epoch-id returns count 1 and the correct epoch. ai/pr-audit/pr-audit-sol-oct11-11506-story-preimage-1.clj: 2 tests, 8 assertions, 2 failures, 0 errors, process exit 3. No shadow-cljs run.

Small correction: make the UI's pre-image reader use the restore-aware current-epoch-id. Preserve Story's optional epoch dependency through one normal :epoch/* late-bind publication/directory entry if needed. Add a regression covering Step, Step, Back, Step, Back through the UI stepper path, and assert both app state and cursor. No synthetic restore records or branch graph is needed.
close_reason: Already fixed on trunk by #11515 (rf2-puf33, 4388a62f81). This bead was filed against #11506 before #11515 merged. stepper_state.cljs's begin! (~157) and step! (~190) now take their pre-image from rf.story.runtime/current-epoch-id, which reads re-frame.epoch/current-epoch-id through the :epoch/current-epoch-id late-bind hook. That is the restore cursor, not the history tail. #11515's test a-second-step-back-restores-the-state-its-cursor-names drives exactly this sequence: step, step, step-back, step, step-back, step-back. It failed at the old trunk (:count 2 at cursor 1) and passes with the fix. Nothing remains.

title: Coeffects are recordable by default; :recordable? false is the ambient opt-out
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20: a coeffect is recordable by default. The alternative was to keep ambient as the default.

## Problem

Measured at trunk 8fc6369484.

`reg-cofx` grades a coeffect **ambient** unless it says `:recordable? true` (`grade` in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc`, around line 137: `(boolean (:recordable? meta))`). Spec 001 §Coeffects says so: "graded ambient (default) or recordable".

Yet the recordable grade is the one that keeps replay deterministic. It is also the one Spec 001 requires "for any fact that can affect durable frame-state". Every application coeffect in `examples/` opts in:
- `examples/core/todomvc/db.cljs:79-80`;
- `examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:223-224`;
- `examples/patterns/websocket/messages.cljs:579-584`;
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs:192-193`.

So the safe grade costs a flag and the unsafe one is free. `:recordable?` appears 195 times across 78 files.

## Change

- `:recordable?` defaults to `true`. `:recordable? false` is the explicit ambient spelling.
- Keep one key, so no new vocabulary. `:provided? true` keeps its meaning and no longer needs `:recordable? true` beside it.
- Mark every registration that is ambient today with `:recordable? false`. A recordable value must be EDN, so any supplier that returns a host object has to opt out. The non-test registrations that are ambient at 8fc6369484:
  - `:rf.server/request` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:332`), a Ring request map that need not be EDN;
  - `:rf.route/nav-token` and `:rf.route/route-id` (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/nav_token.cljc`, `nav-token-cofx-meta` and `route-id-cofx-meta`);
  - `:story/active-modes` and `:story/active-args` (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/cofx.cljc:70-78`);
  - the Xray testbed's `:standard-epochs/now` (`tools/xray/testbeds/standard_epochs/core.cljs:187`).

  Census the test registrations the same way.
- Delete the now-redundant `:recordable? true` from the examples and from the framework registrations that carry it (`:rf/time-ms`, the routing allocations, `:rf.resource/generation-allocation`).
- The `:provided?`-without-`:recordable?` error in `cofx.cljc` changes: only an explicit `:recordable? false` beside `:provided? true` is contradictory.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/001-Registration.md` §Coeffects and its summary row (around line 582).
- `spec/002-Frames.md` §Recordable coeffects. **Hot zone.**
- The `reg-cofx` row in `spec/API.md`, with both manifest sidecars if the metadata changes. **Hot zone.**
- `docs/EP/EP-0017-recordable-coeffects.md`, if it states the default as current contract.
- The coeffect how-to and guide pages. Find them by searching `docs/` and `skills/` for `:recordable?` and "ambient".

## Acceptance

- `(reg-cofx :app/x (fn [] 1))` registers a recordable coeffect: its value is recorded on the causal token and re-presented verbatim by strict replay.
- `(reg-cofx :app/x {:recordable? false} f)` registers an ambient one, as today's default does.
- Every framework and tool registration keeps its current grade, which shows as no behaviour change in their suites.
- JVM suite, `npm run test:cljs`, Story and Xray suites green.
- The `cofx` conformance fixtures pass.

## Sequencing

Hot zones: `spec/002-Frames.md`, `spec/API.md`.

Breaking for an app with an ambient coeffect that returns a non-EDN value: it must add `:recordable? false`, and the EDN check tells it so loudly. Effort S–M.

title: Routing: an in-place :query merges and a nil member removes its key; retire :query-merge
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20 that there is one way to edit the query in place. `:query-merge` retires.

- An in-place navigation's `:query` merges into the current query.
- A `nil` member removes its key.
- `:query nil` clears the whole query.
- A destination's `:query` (a navigation with `:to` or `:url`) stays literal.

## Problem

Measured at trunk cb9cb3c074.

**"In place"** means a navigation carrying neither `:to` nor `:url`, judged by key presence (`spec/012-Routing.md:484`, `:498`; `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/address.cljc:156-167`).

**Today there are two in-place spellings:**
- `:query` replaces wholesale (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url_change.cljc:215-218`);
- `:query-merge` folds its delta in, after re-spelling it through `canonical-query` (`:219-222`).

**Their exclusivity costs validity rules 3, 4 and 9** (`012:481-483`, `:488`). `classify` (`address.cljc:203-300`) refuses them under `:rf.error/navigate-bad-request` with these reasons:
- `:query-exclusive` (`:262-263`);
- `:query-merge-in-place-only` (`:265-266`);
- `:query-merge-not-map` (`:287-288`);
- the `:query-merge` member of `:url-excludes-address` (`:255-257`).

**Usage:** changing one filter (the common case) needs the merge spelling. `:query-merge` appears on 129 lines in 24 files, and in none of `examples/`, `migration/` or the conformance corpus.

## Change

- **Merge semantics:** in place, `:query` merges into the current query.
  - Its members are re-spelled through `canonical-query` before the merge, as `:query-merge`'s are today. Conformance `routing-address-extraction.edn:68-70` expects the re-spelt `{"tab" "history"}`.
  - A `nil` member removes its key. `:query nil` clears every key, as it does today (`url_change.cljc:201`).
  - A non-map, non-nil in-place `:query` is refused, taking over `:query-merge-not-map`'s job under a `:query-not-map` reason.
- **Destinations:** a `:to` or `:url` navigation's `:query` is unchanged and literal.
- **Retiring `:query-merge`:**
  - delete it and its three refusal reasons;
  - a leftover `:query-merge` is an unknown navigate key;
  - add it to `scripts/check_retired_spellings.py`, and fix that file's `query-retain` message (`:1737`), which today tells readers to use `:query-merge`.
- **Teaching changes:** in-place `:query {}` is taught today as "clear every filter" (`docs/routing/concepts.md:231-232`, `:262`; `012:462`, `:484`, `:516`; `address.cljc:89-90`, `:164`). Under merge it is a no-op, so the teaching becomes `:query nil`.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/012-Routing.md`: the request grammar and validity rules (`:462-516`) and every `:query-merge` mention (23).
- **Hot zones:**
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2174` (the bad-request reasons);
  - `spec/API.md:282` with both manifest sidecars;
  - `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3503` and `:3533`.
- Docs:
  - `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md` (8 lines);
  - `docs/routing/concepts.md` (8);
  - `docs/routing/tutorial.md` (2);
  - `docs/routing/how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md:322`;
  - the Fresco guide page that mentions it (`docs/core/fresco/`, one line at `:299`).
- The two skills files that mention it (4 lines).
- Leave `docs/EP/EP-0037` as the historical record.

## Acceptance

- In place, `{:query {:tab "a"}}` on `?q=x` yields `?q=x&tab=a`.
- `{:query {:q nil}}` removes `q`.
- `{:query nil}` clears the query.
- `{:to r :query {...}}` is literal.
- `:query-merge` is refused as an unknown key.
- Update the tests that pin either spelling:
  - `routing_address_extraction_test.clj:20-23`;
  - `routing_auth_guard_matrix_test.clj:88`, `:182-273`;
  - `routing_boundary_totality_cljs_test.cljc:99-105`;
  - `routing_navigation_test.clj:101-110`, `:479`, `:492`, `:632`;
  - `routing_query_spelling_test.clj:47`, `:64`;
  - `routing_url_trace_classification_cljs_test.cljc:122`.
- `check_retired_spellings.py` red on a planted `:query-merge`.
- JVM routing suite, `npm run test:cljs`, the api-manifest check, `mkdocs build --strict` and `check_doc_slugs.py` green.

title: Fresco: measure the boundary props hand-off walk against a children-only contract, and adopt it only if it pays
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20 to measure the boundary props hand-off walk against a narrower contract, and to adopt the narrower rule only if it saves more than it costs to teach. Passing a collection to a child is the most common thing a view does, and Fresco is the taught default.

## Problem

Measured at trunk cb9cb3c074, in `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs`.

**What the walk does.** At every boundary hand-off, `boundary-element` (`:1359-1372`) passes the whole props map, `:children` included, through `realize-deep` (`:1263-1293`, called at `:1367-1368`). The walk:
- forces every lazy seq;
- walks every non-keyword key;
- refuses any unforced `delay`, `(delay 42)` included, with `:rf.error/fresco-deferred-read-at-boundary` (`refuse-deferred!`, `:1242-1261`; the check is at `:1287`).

**What it costs.** It runs in the parent's render, before the child's memo is consulted, so a forwarded collection pays on every parent render even when the child bails out. The docstring prices it at 89% of element build for a 100-row collection prop (`:1278-1283`).

**Why it exists.** A lazy seq forced inside the child would become the child's frozen read. The governing text is `implementation/fresco/spec/authoring-contract.md:50-54`.

**What the bench measures today.** Nothing measures the shipping codec. `bench/fresco` runs a frozen donor copy (`bench/fresco/README.md`, "back-porting it is refused"). The pricing page `docs/design/fresco/studio/the-boundary-crossing-walk-priced.md` says its timing rig was not committed.

## Change

1. **Build the harness.** Write a small, committed harness against the shipping codec: a 100-row and a 1,000-row collection forwarded through three boundaries, with the child's memo bailing out. Report element-build time per parent render.
2. **Prototype the narrower contract:**
   - only `:children` is deep-realised;
   - any other prop passes as given, and subscription-bearing deferred data is the author's responsibility, realised in the supplying body or handed over as a function the receiving body calls;
   - an unforced `delay` in a non-children prop passes.

   `:children` holds Hiccup whose nested `for`s are lazy, so its walk stays deep.
3. **Compare and decide.** Compare the two on the harness. Adopt the narrower rule only if the saving is material. Otherwise keep today's walk, record the measured numbers in the codec docstring, and close.

Add no manifest, marker or second mode.

**If adopted:**
- The test kit mirrors the walk and changes with it: `implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test.cljs` `:863-882`, `:1221`, and its docstring at `:1356-1361`. So do its parity rows (`test_kit_runtime_parity_cljs_test.cljs:262-315`).
- Resolve every ownership case in `implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/read_extent_cljs_test.cljs` explicitly. Only `:550` (`an-unforced-delay-at-a-boundary-crossing-refuses`) and `:594` (`an-escaped-deferral-forced-in-another-body-is-the-declared-limit`) involve the walk.
- No shipped test pins "a lazy seq in a non-children prop is the parent's read". Today that case lives only in the bench copy (`bench/fresco/.../arm1/boundary_crossing_cljs_test.cljs:75`, `:88`). Add a shipped test pinning whichever rule wins.

## Spec and docs that move with it (only if adopted)

- `implementation/fresco/spec/authoring-contract.md:50-54` and `complaints.md:83`.
- Guide pages:
  - `docs/core/fresco/02-views-and-reads.md:287` and `:345-355`;
  - `troubleshooting.md:163-171`;
  - `15-testing.md:531`;
  - `docs/api/re-frame.fresco.md:108`.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2395` and `:2440`, if the error id's trigger changes. **Hot zone.**

## Acceptance

- The harness is committed and its numbers for both contracts are in the PR body.
- The decision is stated with them.
- If adopted:
  - forwarding a 1,000-row vector to a child whose memo bails runs no walk over the rows;
  - the read-extent and parity suites are green, with every changed row explained;
  - `npm run test:cljs` and the Fresco gates are green.

Harness committed: bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/boundary_walk_clock.cljs + boundary_walk_clock_run.cjs (hand-run from bench/fresco/). It requires the SHIPPING codec, so it prices whatever codec is in the tree: a parent render's element build (codec/as-element) with memoised boundary heads and no mount, i.e. the child's memo bailing out. Release build (:simple, goog.DEBUG false) under Node 24, 400 builds/round, 15 interleaved rounds, medians in microseconds per parent render; rows are vectors of {:id :title :done?} maps.

| shape | A: every prop (ships) | B: :children only | C: identity cache |
| dogfood row {:id :title :done?} | 1.40 | 1.00 | 2.23 |
| forward 100 rows, one hand-off | 18.95 | 0.96 | 2.01 |
| forward 100 rows, three hand-offs | 50.06 | 4.44 | 10.77 |
| forward 1,000 rows, one hand-off | 152.77 | 0.89 | 1.91 |
| forward 1,000 rows, three hand-offs | 462.93 | 3.94 | 9.49 |
| walk alone over 1,000 rows | 144.33 | - | - |
Run-to-run spread about +/-15% (a repeat of arm A read 167 and 556 us for the two 1,000-row forwards). B and C were prototypes planted in codec.cljs for the run and restored (blob hash verified); C = the shipping walk behind a WeakSet of collections already walked.

Decision: keep the every-prop walk. B saves about 0.15 us per row per hand-off (half a millisecond only at 1,000 rows crossing three boundaries in one render), and costs a SILENT fault in the commonest idiom: a `for` over reads, or a delay, handed under any prop other than :children would be forced in the child, filed under the child's edges and frozen by its cache, and :rf.error/fresco-deferred-read-at-boundary would no longer reach it. C keeps the contract but every fresh props map pays a WeakSet insertion, so the commonest call (dogfood row) pays ~60% more.

Recorded: realize-deep's docstring carries the numbers and the reason; docs/design/fresco/studio/the-boundary-crossing-walk-priced.md gains §3 with the three-arm table; read_extent_cljs_test gains `a-lazy-seq-under-any-prop-is-forced-in-the-body-that-wrote-it` (the shipped pin the bead asked for). Sabotage: with B planted, that row and `an-unforced-delay-at-a-boundary-crossing-refuses` go red (13 tests, 7 failures, 2 errors); restored, green. No spec, guide or 009 change, because the contract did not move.

Not adopted because under B a `for` over reads, or a `delay`, passed under any prop other than :children is forced in the child and frozen there SILENTLY, and the deferred-read refusal no longer reaches it. title: Fresco forms: the drafts concern is registered with no namespace, so a frame with explicit :images cannot reach forms' drafts sub or setter
description:
Found by the rf2-go1ed worker (PR #11591, merged as b842e950d2), outside its fence. implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/forms.cljs registers its :re-frame.fresco.forms/drafts concern through the rf.core-state/reg-state FN door, so the registration carries no namespace. By Spec 002 §Image resolution no :select-ns can reach a registration with no namespace, and the framework base takes such ids only under the :rf root, so an app frame made with explicit :images can never resolve Fresco forms' drafts sub or setter: Fresco forms is broken in explicit-image frames. Not reproduced for the drafts concern itself; the rf2-go1ed tip reproduction shows the same mechanism on a reg-state concern ([false false true]).

Fix sketch: register the drafts concern through the rf/reg-state MACRO in forms.cljs, so it is selectable as re-frame.fresco.forms (or otherwise make it resolvable in explicit-image frames by the smallest supported route). Then implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs's fresh! (which re-registers the same concern through the fn door, so it matches today) must change with it, or the id becomes ambiguous (:rf.error/ambiguous-registration).

Acceptance: a regression, red at tip, showing a frame whose image selects re-frame.fresco.forms reads and writes a draft; the client-only-arms test green. Gates: npm run test:cljs, the Fresco bundle-isolation gates (build:fresco-release, test:bundle-isolation; they key off the drafts concern), check_optional_module_reachability.py.

title: Schemas: one :schemas/check! seam, so every validation failure carries the same tags and a humanized explanation
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20 that every validating surface reports a failure in one shape, through one schemas-artefact seam, `:schemas/check!`. Each failure then carries the same tags, a human-readable `:explain-humanized` included, whichever surface found it. The programmer, and the AI reading traces over the pair tools, read one shape.

The caller keeps its own recovery (abort, skip, observe or throw).

## Problem

Measured at trunk cb9cb3c074.

Sites outside `implementation/schemas/` build their own failure reports from the raw late-bind hooks `:schemas/validate-with-registered-fn`, `:schemas/explain-with-registered-fn` and `:schemas/redact-validation-tags`. There are 24 lookups in 11 files. None carries `:explain-humanized`, which Spec 010:304 requires on **every** `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` trace. They also drift on other tags.

**Sites that emit a trace:**
- **Boundary check:** `implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc:168`, `:210`, `:220`, emitting at `:223-238`. A validator throw becomes a fail-closed `false`, with no `:rf.error/malformed-schema`.
- **Sub override:** `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/override_schema.cljc:62-86`. A validator throw counts as a pass.
- **Machine data and output:** `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/data_validation.cljc:200-229`, `:258`, `:430-460`. These have no `:frame`, which contradicts Spec 010:199. The data arm emits no `:rf.error/malformed-schema` on a throw; the output arm does.
- **Routing URL change:** `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url_change.cljc:151-162`, `:242-249`. It uses the redact hook as a sensitivity probe, and its trace has no `:failing-id`, which `SchemaValidationFailureTags` requires (`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1089`).
- **Coeffect values:** `implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:630`, `:698`, `:716`. This emits `:rf.error/cofx-value-invalid`, a different id, always-on, and then throws.

**Sites that throw instead of tracing:**
- **Route URLs:** `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:1264`, `:1269`, which throws `:rf.error/route-url-validation`.
- **Resource and mutation params:** `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/params.cljc:27`, `:29` and `classification.cljc:259`.
- **Story db seed:** `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:989-990`, `:1029-1043`. Its `:violations` carry raw `:value`, `:schema` and `:explain`, unredacted.

**Sites that only want a verdict:** `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:74` and Story's args panel (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/schema_validation.cljc:359`).

**The artefact's own surfaces** (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc`, about `:700-866`) do three things the outside sites drift from:
- humanize the explanation before redacting;
- emit `:rf.error/malformed-schema` when a validator throws;
- apply `:large?` elision.

## Change

- **Add one internal seam.** Add `:schemas/check!` to the late-bind directory, taking `{:category :where :id :schema :value :frame :recovery :extra-tags}`. It returns the verdict plus the redacted, humanized failure tags, and emits the standard trace unless the caller asks for the tags only.
- **One code path.** The artefact's own surfaces use it too, so there is one implementation.
- **Port the sites:**
  - the five tracing sites call it;
  - the three throwing sites build their ex-data from its redacted tags, which gives Story's db-seed violations redaction;
  - the two verdict-only sites call it in tags-only mode.
- **Normalise the drift:** every trace carries `:failing-id` and `:frame`, and a validator throw is a `:rf.error/malformed-schema` everywhere.
- **Retire the three raw hooks** once nothing outside the artefact uses them.
- **Production split.** The humanizer is dev-only (`validate.cljc:390-392`), and the boundary site builds its diagnosis under `debug-enabled?` (`spec.cljc:198-212`). Keep that split, so the boundary, coeffect, resource and route-URL checks that run in release builds pay nothing new.
- **Out of scope:** HTTP `:decode` validation, which calls `malli.core` directly (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/decode.cljc:209-217`).

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/010-Schemas.md`: §Per-step recovery (`:187-205`), §Humanize-hook (`:291-310`) and §Boundary-validation seam (`:743-749`).
- **Hot zones:**
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`: the emitter list (`:1018-1020`), the catalogue row (`:1951`) and the per-`:where` table (`:2343-2358`);
  - `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1087-1101`: `SchemaValidationFailureTags` gains `:explain-humanized`, `:frame`, `:sensitive?` and `:source`;
  - `spec/API.md` with both manifests, if any public var changes.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:308-316` and `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md:358-396`.
- Tool readers to check:
  - Xray (`tools/xray/.../panels/epoch/projection.cljc:2704-2745`, `view.cljs:5498-5510`, `:5625-5643`);
  - Story (`play/evidence.cljc:132-160`, `ui/schema_validation.cljc:103-160`);
  - story-mcp (`tools/result.cljc:228-275`), which humanizes thrown ex-data itself and can drop that.

## Acceptance

- Each of the five tracing sites emits a trace carrying `:failing-id`, `:frame` and, in dev, `:explain-humanized`. Pin this with one test per site.
- A validator throw at any site emits `:rf.error/malformed-schema`.
- Story's db-seed violation redacts a `:sensitive?` path.
- The three raw hooks have no caller outside `implementation/schemas/`.
- The release elision gates and the bundle-isolation gate are green: nothing humanizer-shaped reaches a release bundle.
- JVM, `npm run test:cljs` and the Story suite green.

title: Machines: completions emit a small work record instead of lowering onto the reply envelope
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 that machine completions keep a small work record, not the reply envelope. The machine completion lowering onto the uniform reply envelope (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/reply.cljc`) is replaced by a small producer record carrying work identity, terminal status and stale reason. Xray's reply-envelope panel keeps classifying machine, timer and join rows.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e.

- **A whole reply map is built, then mostly thrown away.** `reply.cljc` is 698 lines. Its nine builders, `success-reply` (`:214`) through `cancelled-actor-reply` (`:633-664`), each build a reply map with `:value`, a `:kind`-wrapped `:error` and `:correlation`. `trace-reply` (`:674`) then runs it through `re-frame.reply/trace-summary`, which is the namespace's only call into `re-frame.reply`.
- **Every emit site plucks a few identity keys back out.** Examples:
  - `emit-done!` (`lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc:274-298`);
  - the join sites (`lifecycle_fx/join.cljc:211-235`, `:358-373`, `:530-560`);
  - destroy (`lifecycle_fx/traces.cljc:64-90`);
  - timer cancel (`timer.cljc:272-282`);
  - `:after` (`transition.cljc:4133-4245`).

  No trace carries `:value` or `:error`. `finalize.cljc:664` reads `(:value reply)` only to recover the `result` it passed in.
- **The one consumer reads only tags.** Xray's `work-event-row` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reply_envelope.cljc:478-580`) reads the `:rf.reply/*` tags and `:rf.frame/id`. Its op table classifies the machine ops at `:253-352`.
- **The spec calls it a lowering onto the envelope:** Spec 005 §Async completions share the uniform reply envelope (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:4062-4130`), plus `:9`, `:2482` and `:3526`.

## Change

- Replace the reply-map builders with one small producer record per completion: work id, work kind, `:status`, work status, and, when present, stale reason, cancel reason, correlation and completed-at. Each emit site writes the record's facts as the trace tags it writes today.
- The tag names and values do not change, so Xray's panel needs no change. The correlation maps hold only ids, paths, generations and epochs, so they ride as plain tags without the elision pass. No record carries `:value` or `:error`.
- Keep the identity helpers: `actor-generation`, `spawn-work-generation`, `spawn-work-id` and `timer-work-id`.
- Delete the nine reply builders, `trace-reply`, `stale-spawn-trace`, `error-reply`'s `:rf.machine/spawn-error` wrapping, and the machines artefact's require of `re-frame.reply`. Rename the namespace if `reply` no longer fits.
- What stays: the public statechart API (`:on-done`, `:on-error`, `:after`, the join protocol, actor destroy), every work id, every trace op, and stale suppression itself.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/005-StateMachines.md`: rewrite §Async completions share the uniform reply envelope (`:4062-4130`) as "machine completions emit work records". Keep its work-id, stale-gate, timer and join rules; drop the reply-map wording. That includes the claim at `:4086` that the decisive child's payload rides `:value`. Also update `:9`, `:2482`, `:3526`, `:3900` and the cross-references at `:4133-4134`. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/Managed-Effects.md`: property 9 lists machine async work as completing through a reply map (`:16`, `:74`, `:80`, `:261`). Say instead that machines report work identity, status and stale reason as trace facts, with `:on-done` / `:on-error` as their native grammar.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:225-232` (the machine trace rows) already describe tags, not a reply map. Read them, and touch them only if a sentence claims a reply map. **Hot zone.**
- Leave `docs/EP/EP-0011-uniform-async-reply-envelope.md` as the historical record.
- `implementation/reply-conformance/deps.edn:37`: drop the machines dependency once its tests stop using it.

## Acceptance

- Replace the builder tests in `machines_reply_cljs_test.cljc` (`success-reply-is-canonical`, `error-reply-is-canonical`, `stale-spawn-reply-suppresses`, `after-stale-reply-is-canonical`, `after-fired-reply-is-canonical`, `cancelled-timer-reply-is-canonical`, `cancelled-actor-reply-is-canonical`) and `spawn_all_reply_envelope_test.clj` (`join-child-reply-is-canonical`) with tests on the record. Keep `actor-generation-reads-the-numeric-suffix` and `timer-work-id-names-the-after-entry`.
- Remove the `:machine` and `:timer` families from `reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:98-113`.
- These pass unchanged, because they read real emitted tags:
  - `machine_reply_lowering_test.clj` (all ten deftests);
  - `cancellation_reply_envelope_test.clj`;
  - Xray's `machine_work_identity_cljs_test.cljc` (six deftests);
  - Xray's `reply_envelope_cljs_test.cljc`.
- The JVM machines suite, `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` (reply-conformance), the Xray suite, `npm run test:cljs`, `mkdocs build --strict` and `check_doc_slugs.py` are green.

## Sequencing

Spec 005 is a hot zone; sequence after any open bead that edits it.

The machines worker writes it under 'Held for the mayor' in its PR body; the mayor lands it after 009 is released. Clears when it lands, or when that PR body says no 009 change is needed.
== WORKER (machines-work-record), 2026-10-21 21:03 AUSEST: DONE, PR #11617 (branch worker/machines-work-record)

Machine completions now emit a small work record instead of lowering onto the reply envelope. re-frame.machines.reply is renamed re-frame.machines.work. It keeps the identity helpers (actor-generation, spawn-work-generation, spawn-work-id, timer-work-id) and after-suppression-gate, and adds `record` plus two correlation helpers (actor-correlation, timer-correlation). A record is {:work-id :work-kind :status :work-status} plus whichever of :stale-reason, :cancel-reason, :correlation and :completed-at are present. The work kind comes from the work-id head, and the work status from :status. Both lookups are `case` forms, so a head or status outside the closed set throws. Two other paths release without that wait and were not examined: the alloc row, and retention_run.cjs. Check each; where it reads a post-release figure or the next arm's baseline, await the drain the same way, with the same planted control (remove the wait, see the low read or the structural failure). Its window figures are out of the drain's reach (post is read before the release; samples, work census and write read-back are taken inside one synchronous allocWindow task). The NEXT ARM'S MOUNT READ-BACK is not: mount! counts the frame's subscription cache (keys vs keysExpected) one CDP round trip after the release. Ascending-rung transitions cannot show it (their keys are subsets), and a 2-round planted run read 0 unverified for that reason. Restore verified by blob hash (default-form blob of the working file == committed blob dc52ef56c3). With the wait, same config and an identical windowOrder (12 non-subset transitions out of a Fresco arm): 0 unverified. Both runs also exit 1 on the row's scale gates at near-identical counts (falls 106 vs 111, leg refusals 205 vs 210): at B=96 the largest window rises ~11x past the ~600 KB fall threshold, independent of the wait. title: skill(re-frame-migration): orchestrating-a-large-migration endorses per-unit PRs but names no merge target or merge gate while the tree cannot compile
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 2a6fd908a6.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/orchestrating-a-large-migration.md: §5 "The all-or-nothing single compile gate" (lines 95-104) and "How it composes with the cardinal rules" (line 111). The originating note cited "§7"; the leaf has §1-§5 plus that closing section, and the per-unit-PR text is at line 111.

## What it says

- §5, line 97: "**the project does not compile until the whole sweep lands.** ... a worker that finishes its unit cannot prove it green in isolation".
- Line 104: "do not promise per-unit green".
- Line 111: "**If** you fan out, isolated worktrees are **one** clean way to keep the one-file-one-owner partition collision-free: each worker owns its files and — at the **single** gate (§5), since per-unit green is impossible — runs the consolidated build itself (cardinal rule 5) and posts command + result to a per-unit PR ... fanned-out branches merge without stepping on each other".

## What happened (generic)

The leaf endorses per-unit PRs but never says what they merge into, or what has to pass before one merges. Many projects run merge-on-green CI on a protected trunk. Under that regime a unit PR either cannot merge, because its CI is red by design, which deadlocks the fan-out, or it merges red and leaves the trunk red until the last wave lands. A downstream migration ran into this and had to invent a sweep branch and its own merge rule.

## Evidence

- `git grep -n -i -E 'integration branch|sweep branch|long-lived branch|feature branch|merge-on-green|base branch|trunk|required check' origin/main -- skills/re-frame-migration/` finds only one unrelated README line. (Control: `per-unit PR` hits this leaf once.)
- rf2-yfizt (closed) made the first-compile contract consistent across the leaves, but its text never mentions CI or branches: 0 hits for each, against 36 for the control "compile".

## Suggested change

In "How it composes", with a pointer from §5, say:

- When units land as PRs, open them against a dedicated sweep (integration) branch rather than the trunk, so the trunk stays green.
- What gates a unit PR's merge into that branch: the unit's own checks (its rule list applied, a clean codemod rescan of its files, and the expect-and-report line), plus every CI check that does not need a whole-tree compile, such as lint, format, docs and non-CLJS tests.
- ONE PR from the sweep branch to the trunk carries the consolidated §5 gate: dev and optimized compile, tests and the boot smoke-test.
- How to treat compile-dependent CI jobs on the sweep branch until then.
notes:
FENCE (2026-10-28 15:30 AUSEST). Held by a live worker in C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/migration-orchestrating on branch worker/migration-orchestrating.

TWO FENCES, TWO DIFFERENT RELEASE EVENTS. Read both before acting on either.

  1. RE-DISPATCH FENCE. Do not dispatch a second worker onto this bead or that branch.
     RELEASES ON: a completion report, or a recorded death.
     This is the condition the reaping rule uses. The test is: can you quote the
     sentence where this agent says it is done?

  2. SURFACE FENCE. The worker holds skills/re-frame-migration/references/orchestrating-a-large-migration.md
     RELEASES ON: THE PR MERGING. Not on the report.
     A reported worker still has an open PR editing those files; a second worker
     branched off trunk would not carry them, and the two diffs collide at merge.
     The test is: has the PR that edits this surface MERGED?

A YES TO THE FIRST AND A NO TO THE SECOND means: reap the worktree if you like,
but DO NOT dispatch onto that surface.
close_reason:
Changed, in PR #11653 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/11653), confined to skills/re-frame-migration/references/orchestrating-a-large-migration.md. The gap was real. §5 says the tree does not compile until the whole sweep lands, and the closing section endorsed per-unit PRs but named no merge target or merge gate. A search of SKILL.md, sequencing.md, release-compile-gate.md and runtime-smoke-test.md at 2a6fd908a6 found no account of a merge target, and none that contradicts one.

The new bullet in "How it composes with the cardinal rules" says:
- Cut a sweep (integration) branch from the trunk before M-0. Land M-0, the Wave-0.5 pre-pass and every wave there; the solo developer's plain branch is the same branch.
- A unit PR targets that branch. It merges on its §5 deliverable plus every CI check that neither compiles nor loads the migrated tree (lint, formatting, docs).
- The compile-dependent checks stay red on the sweep branch until the last wave lands. They gate no unit PR and stay switched on, because they are what the one sweep-to-trunk PR must pass.
- That PR carries the consolidated §5 gate (dev and optimized compiles, the test suite, the boot smoke-test). Its CI run is the clean-checkout done-signal of runtime-smoke-test.md.

Other edits: §5 points at the new bullet. The substrate bullet no longer has a worker post a consolidated-build result to a per-unit PR, because that PR merges before the build can pass. The solo path now reads "no per-unit PRs", and the net-shape line names the sweep PR.

Declined from the suggestion: gating a unit PR on "a clean codemod rescan of its files". Some rules' detection searches also match the rewritten v2 form (for example, :dispatch survives inside :fx), so a clean rescan is not a reliable criterion. §5's existing deliverable already says how to judge a unit.

Gates, each with its own captured exit code:
- check_skill_migration_cites, check_skill_migration_contract_drift and check_skill_migration_o1617_router_drift: 0 for both --self-test and --verbose --ci.
- check_doc_slugs: 0 for both --self-test --verbose and --verbose.
- test-fast-pr.sh: 0, with its gate root printed as this worktree.

Plant: a broken anchor in the new bullet's link made check_doc_slugs exit 1, reporting BROKEN ANCHOR at line 112. After restoring from HEAD, the file's default-form blob hash equals HEAD's (93f0f28ba4).

title: ssr-node has no distribution channel: package.json is private:true and the repo publishes no npm artefact, so the crossing recipe cannot tell an operator how to obtain the sidecar
notes:
FOUND BY SLICE F (rf2-8arzr.6), 2026-09-02, at base de3f2a00038. Slice F was told to "locate the release/distribution roster by grepping re-frame2-ssr-ring under .github/workflows/ and scripts/, and add the ssr-node package wherever shippable artefacts are enumerated". THAT PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD: there is nowhere honest to add it, because ssr-node is not a shippable artefact today and making it one is an operator decision rather than a docs sweep.

MEASURED at that base:
- implementation/ssr-node/package.json declares `"private": true` (and `"name": "@day8/re-frame2-ssr-node"`, `"version": "0.1.0"`). npm refuses to publish a private package.
- `grep -rn "npm publish|NPM_TOKEN|registry.npmjs" .github/ scripts/` returns NOTHING. The repo has no npm publishing path at all, for any package.
- .github/workflows/release.yml publishes Maven/Clojars artefacts only. Its jobs are verify-version-lockstep, test, deploy-core, deploy-leaf, deploy-ssr-ring, deploy-hicasso, github-release. The GitHub-release body (:936-949) enumerates fourteen `day8/re-frame2-*` Clojars coordinates and nothing else.
- .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh:100-140 keys ARTEFACT_PATHS off implementation/*/deps.edn entries carrying a :clein/build alias. ssr-node has NO deps.edn and no :clein/build, so the inventory guard at that site correctly leaves it alone -- it is not an omission there, it is out of that mechanism s domain entirely.

So the roster is a Clojars/Maven roster. Adding a plain Node package to it would be wrong in kind, not merely premature.

WHAT THE README ALREADY ASSUMES: implementation/ssr-node/README.md s Deployment section tells an operator to run `re-frame2-ssr-node --module <bundle>` -- the `bin` name from that same private manifest. There is no documented way to get that binary onto a production host. Today the honest answer is "from a checkout of this repo", and the recipe slice F wrote (docs/ssr/concepts.md §Render on Node) uses the bare command without claiming an install channel, which is accurate but incomplete.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS (Mike s, not a worker s): does the sidecar ship? Three coherent answers.
(a) Publish to npm -- drop `private: true`, add an npm publish job to release.yml with a token, and put the package on the release body s roster beside the Clojars coordinates. Version lockstep would then need a fourth mechanism, since the existing one is deps.edn/:clein-shaped.
(b) Vendored-only, deliberately -- keep it private, and say so in the README and the recipe: operators copy the package tree into their deployment. Cheapest, and defensible pre-alpha.
(c) Ship it inside an existing artefact s jar as a resource the JVM host can unpack.

Until one of those is ruled, the recipe and the README should not imply an install channel that does not exist. NOT URGENT: pre-alpha, and (b) is the de facto status quo and works.
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 03:5x AUSEST — SPLIT THE BEAD. DO THE HONEST-DOCS HALF NOW; THE SHIPPABILITY HALF IS MIKE'S AND GOES BEHIND THE PUBLISHING CHAIN.

Slice F refuted its OWN dispatch premise here and that refutation is the bead's most valuable content: it was told to grep for the release roster and add ssr-node wherever shippable artefacts are enumerated, and it established there is NOWHERE HONEST TO ADD IT. Measured: package.json declares private:true; a grep for npm publish / NPM_TOKEN / registry.npmjs across .github/ and scripts/ returns NOTHING, so the repo has no npm publishing path AT ALL for any package; release.yml publishes Maven/Clojars only and its GitHub-release body enumerates fourteen Clojars coordinates and nothing else; and verify-version-lockstep.sh keys its inventory off implementation/*/deps.edn entries carrying a :clein/build alias, which ssr-node has none of — so the inventory guard is not omitting it, it is correctly out of scope there. A worker sent to 'add it to the roster' would have had to invent a roster.

THE HALF THAT IS MIKE'S. Publishing an npm artefact from a repo that publishes none is a new distribution capability, not a docs sweep — a product call about what this project ships and supports. It also belongs behind the publishing chain that already holds seven items (rf2-uelji -> rf2-fo4ng -> rf2-kmqx3), because the same question — what gets published under what identity, and who verifies the group — is unresolved one level up. Surfaced to Mike; not dispatched.

THE HALF THAT IS DISPATCHABLE TODAY, and it is the half the bead's TITLE actually names: 'the crossing recipe cannot tell an operator how to obtain the sidecar'. That is a docs-truth defect with an honest answer available right now — say how an operator obtains it TODAY (from the repo, by the route that actually works) and state plainly that no published artefact exists and none is planned as of this writing. That is shippable, costs nothing, and does not pre-empt the product call. What it must NOT do is imply a package is coming, or invent a coordinate; a recipe that names an unpublished coordinate is worse than one that says there is none.

VERIFY BEFORE WRITING: re-run the three measurements above at current tip rather than trusting them — they were taken at de3f2a00038 and #9024 has since changed that tree.
DOCS HALF RESOLVED BY PR #9040, 2026-09-03. THE SHIPPABILITY HALF IS NOT ADDRESSED AND REMAINS HELD FOR MIKE — this bead is closed on the docs half ONLY, per the mayor ruling above, and the product call is untouched.

THE THREE MEASUREMENTS RE-RUN AT CURRENT TIP, as the ruling required. All three still hold; the premise has not moved since de3f2a00038:
(a) implementation/ssr-node/package.json still declares private: true, name @day8/re-frame2-ssr-node, version 0.1.0, bin re-frame2-ssr-node -> ./bin/serve.cjs.
(b) grep -rnE 'npm publish|NPM_TOKEN|registry.npmjs' .github/ scripts/ returns ZERO hits (exit 1). CONTROLLED: the same instrument over CLOJARS_USERNAME|CLOJARS_PASSWORD returns four workflow files, so the zero is a real absence rather than a broken pattern.
(c) release.yml's jobs are exactly verify-version-lockstep, test, deploy-core, deploy-leaf, deploy-ssr-ring, deploy-hicasso, github-release; the release body enumerates 14 day8/re-frame2-* Clojars coordinates and nothing else.

ONE THING THIS BEAD DID NOT MEASURE, now measured: there are FOUR release workflows, not one — release.yml plus release-story, release-xray, release-machines-viz. Measurement (b) spans all of .github/, so 'the repo has no npm publishing path at all' is confirmed across all four rather than inferred from one. That strengthens the bead's conclusion rather than weakening it.

ONE OF THIS BEAD'S PREMISES DID NOT HOLD AS STATED. It says 'There is no documented way to get that binary onto a production host.' The README's 'Using it' section already documented one — private, 'installed from its directory rather than a registry', npm install <checkout>/implementation/ssr-node or a file: entry — and it PREDATES this bead (added by 4bab8df1ae, an ancestor of this bead's own base de3f2a00038). What was genuinely missing is what this bead's TITLE names, and that is what was fixed: the crossing recipe's step 5 gave the bare command with no account of its provenance, the README's Deployment recipe named the binary at step 2 the same way, and NEITHER said that no published artefact exists.

WHAT LANDED: docs/ssr/concepts.md section Render on Node step 5, and implementation/ssr-node/README.md section Deployment, both now state plainly that there is no published artefact, the package is not on npm, it has no Clojars coordinate, none is planned as of this writing, and the repository publishes JVM artefacts only. The route that works TODAY is a checkout — installed from the package directory, a file: entry to the same effect, or the tree copied onto the host and run with node bin/serve.cjs. Because the manifest resolves nothing, copying the tree IS the install, and the version deployed is the checkout it came from, so pin that checkout as deliberately as the JVM artefact versions in the same release. NO COORDINATE IS INVENTED AND NO PACKAGE IS IMPLIED.

STILL HELD, UNTOUCHED, MIKE'S CALL: whether the sidecar ships. package.json keeps private: true, no npm publish job was added, release.yml was not edited, and the three options this bead sets out — (a) publish to npm, (b) vendored-only by decision, (c) ship inside an existing artefact's jar — remain open, behind the publishing chain rf2-uelji -> rf2-fo4ng -> rf2-kmqx3 as the ruling placed them. Nothing in PR #9040 pre-empts that choice; the docs now describe the status quo honestly, which is precisely option (b)'s de facto state without declaring it ruled.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): M-11 sizing is grep-only, but telling render-time reads from callback reads needs a parse; a lexical count found ~200 in 38 files against 228 in 45 parsed
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md §M-11, "Size it in the Phase-0a inventory" (line 27).
- The same file's §The async listener timer and error-handler class, "Phase-0a grep these" (line 294).
- inventory-and-plan.md Step 3 rows 94-95. The replacement row in open PR #11654 (rf2-0motc) also says "Count these call sites to SIZE M-11" and gives no method.

## What it says

- guided-views-m11 :27: "Count the deferred call sites up front."
- :294: "Phase-0a grep these (`addEventListener` …".
- inventory row 95: "Grep `addEventListener` / `setTimeout` / `setInterval` / `requestAnimationFrame` / `onerror` / `"error"` / JS-lib callbacks that bare-dispatch".

## What happened (generic)

Whether an ambient `dispatch` / `subscribe` is an M-11 site depends on the position of its innermost enclosing fn: the render body, or an `:on-*` value, a timer fn or a lifecycle method. A grep cannot see that. It also misses the common indirections:

- a let-bound fn later used as a handler;
- a helper called from a callback (this needs the call graph);
- keyword-arg props that carry handlers;
- destructuring defaults;
- fn-producing macros;
- fns handed to child dialogs.

On a ~170-file app, the lexical estimate was about 200 sites in 38 files; a parsed census found 228 in 45. Those counts are the worker's.

## Evidence

The quotes above. The parsed census came from a downstream unit dedicated to M-11 sizing.

## Suggested change

Add a parsed-census recipe (rewrite-clj or equivalent), and keep the grep as the fast candidate search ("candidates, not the set", as Step 5 says). The census:

1. Classifies each ambient op by its innermost enclosing fn's position.
2. Resolves let-bound fns by their use, and helpers by the call graph.
3. Treats props and keyword args that receive fns as callback positions.
4. Reconciles against a comment-stripped lexical count as its control, so every lexical hit ends up accounted for as a site or a non-site.

title: migration(corpus): M-23 lacks alpha's bare-keyword / id-plus-map sub rows and the :flow query; M-52 says run-test-sync was only a bracket; M-72 omits the path-focus trap for a root-reading v1 cofx
description:
The migration skill now carries three corrections that the corpus does not. The corpus is a hot-zone file, so the skill-side change (PR #11663) left it alone.

## Where

migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:

1. §M-23 "`re-frame.alpha` is removed", the What-to-do table (the two `sub` rows).
2. §M-52 "`run-test-sync` removed": the premise paragraph under **Type A**, **What to do**, and **Why**.
3. §M-72 "`inject-cofx` removed …", item 2 and the mechanical reshape.

## The corrections, verified at source

1. **M-23 has no row for alpha's two `sub` shorthands, and none for a `:flow` query.** In re-frame 1.4.3, `re_frame/subs/alpha.cljc` `sub` is `([q] (if (keyword? q) (sub q {}) …))` and `([id q] (sub (assoc q ::rf/q id)))`. So `(sub ::id)` is `{:re-frame/q ::id}`, which becomes `(subscribe [::id])`. And `(sub ::id {:param 1})` is the existing query-map row, which becomes `(subscribe [::id 1])`. Neither is a rename: v2's `subscribe` 2-arity is `[query-v opts]` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc), so a renamed call passes a keyword as the query, or drops its params into `opts`. Separately, `re_frame/alpha.cljc` registers `(reg :sub :flow …)`. That means `(sub :flow {:id ::f})`, and the vector `[:flow {:id ::f}]` under the "just switch the namespace" vector row, both read a flow's output. v2 flows publish no subscriptions (spec/013-Flows.md §Sub integration), so read the flow's `:output-path` through a `reg-sub`.
2. **M-52's premise is wrong about v1.** In day8.re-frame/test 0.1.5 and 0.1.7, `run-test-sync*` wraps the body in `with-temp-re-frame-state` and also runs it under `(with-redefs [rf/dispatch new-dispatch rf.router/dispatch new-dispatch] (f))`, where `new-dispatch` queues the event and drains through `rf.router/dispatch-sync`. Its docstring says it is "as though every `dispatch` in your app had been magically turned into `dispatch-sync`". So three statements are false: "the macro's only job was a snapshot/restore bracket", "a thin body wrapper, not a synchronicity primitive", and "added nothing on the drain axis". In v2, a dispatch made outside any event joins the external lane and runs on a later tick (spec/002-Frames.md §Run-to-completion dispatch, rule 2). The correction:
   - turn each `rf/dispatch` the body calls directly into `dispatch-sync`;
   - leave one inside a handler the body registers, where `dispatch-sync` is `:rf.error/dispatch-sync-in-handler`;
   - flag a dispatch that production code makes from a callback the body fires, outside any event, and await it with `ts/poll-until` or a `:rf.event/run-end` listener.

   The corpus's own M-25 before/after example already turns a body `rf/dispatch` into `dispatch-sync`. M-52's example uses `dispatch-sync` only, so it never shows the case.
3. **M-72 omits the path-focus trap.** In re-frame 1.4.3, `inject-cofx` runs `(update context :coeffects handler)`, and `path` swaps `:db` only in its own `:before`. So a v1 cofx ahead of `(rf/path …)` derived its value from the ROOT db. v2's `standard-path-interceptor` stages the focused slice as the handler's `:db` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/std_interceptors.cljc), and the M-73 codemod lowers `(rf/path …)` to that ref. So deleting such a cofx and re-reading the value from `:db` returns `nil` with no error. Add a note saying so. Read the value through `rf/subscribe-once`, in the body or as an ambient cofx (skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/cofx.md §Reading a sub from a handler), or drop the path focus. Check each removed db-reading cofx's consumers for a path ref.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): the boot smoke-test loop is first-screen and single-scenario: nothing enumerates the app's pages or boot scenarios, or maps M-11 census sites to the page that triggers them
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main d53a3faf09.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/runtime-smoke-test.md §"The boot smoke-test phase": loop steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 (lines 25, 27, 34, 35) and the done line (line 39).
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md line 238.

## What it says

- :27, step 4: "Read each sub the first screen depends on".
- :34, step 5: "Dispatch one real event per feature surface (a machine event, a managed-HTTP request, a route change)".
- :25 and :27 compare results "with the expected result for this boot scenario". A scenario is assumed, but never enumerated.
- guided-views-m11.md:238: a missed M-11 site "throws on *interaction or render* (not at ns-load) … boot the dev build, exercise each first-screen surface and its controls".

## What happened (generic)

In a multi-page app, the M-11 sites sit on every page, not only the first screen. They compile clean and throw only when their callback first fires. The loop as written drives the first screen plus "one real event per feature surface". So a page reached only by navigation, and the callbacks on it, are never exercised, and the smoke comes back clean.

The same gap applies to boot scenarios. An app with several of them (feature flags, auth modes, role or tenant variants, a deep-link boot) runs steps 2-4 against just one.

On a ~170-file app, writing the convergence smoke checklist meant enumerating the pages from the router by hand, then attaching each M-11 census site to the page that triggers it.

## Evidence

- The quotes above.
- In runtime-smoke-test.md, "route" appears only as "a route change" (:34) and "fire a route change (popstate / hashchange)" (:35), plus an unrelated "routed" at :24. "page" appears once, in step 6's "not just load the page" (:35). "scenario" appears only as "this boot scenario", "the scenario" or "its boot scenario" (:25, :27, :32, :39, :53), never as a list.

## Suggested change

Add a step 0 to the loop. It enumerates:

- (a) the app's pages or routes, from its router or route registry, attaching to each page the Phase-0a M-11 census sites and async entry points it triggers;
- (b) the boot scenarios the app supports.

Then run steps 2-4 once per scenario and steps 5-6 once per page. The done line becomes "clean for every page and every scenario listed in step 0".

title: Spec 009: the ssr-node error rows describe renderer :module's construction-time arms (opt-invalid, unreachable, build-skew)
description:
## Why

`re-frame.ssr.ring.node/renderer` gained a `:module` mode (rf2-dwtud): the renderer launches and owns the Node sidecar from resources in ssr-ring's jar, checks its ready line at construction, relaunches it when it exits, and stops it on `.close`. The implementation reuses the three existing error ids, so Spec 009 needed no new row, but three of its existing rows in §Error event catalogue now under-describe what is thrown. That file was held by another live worker when rf2-dwtud landed, so the edit was deferred to this bead.

## The three rows

1. `:rf.error/ssr-node-renderer-opt-invalid` lists the malformed opts. Add: `:module` not a non-empty string or not naming a file; `:module` named beside `:endpoint`; `:node` not a non-empty string; `:isolates` not a positive integer; `:node` or `:isolates` named without `:module`. The ex-data (`:opt`, `:got`) and recovery do not change.
2. `:rf.error/ssr-node-unreachable` says it is thrown at the render call site. Under `:module` it is also thrown AT CONSTRUCTION when the sidecar cannot start: `node` missing, the runtime missing from the classpath, the child exiting before its ready line, no ready line within 30 s, or a ready line naming a protocol other than 1. Its `:ex-message` carries the child's last stderr lines. Per request it is also thrown, with `:endpoint` nil, while an owned sidecar is down and being relaunched, and after the renderer was closed. The recovery prose ("start `re-frame2-ssr-node --module <bundle>`, or correct `:endpoint`") fits only `:endpoint` mode; the `:recovery` keyword itself stays `:start-the-sidecar-or-correct-the-endpoint`.
3. `:rf.error/ssr-node-build-skew` says it is the answer-side check. Under `:module` it is also thrown AT CONSTRUCTION when the bundle's ready-line `buildId` is not `:build-id`, with the same `:expected` / `:serving` ex-data.

The normative opts paragraph is Spec 011 §Client-side hydration boot helper, which rf2-dwtud already updated; these rows should point at it rather than restate it.

## Sequencing

`spec/009-Instrumentation.md` is a hot-zone file. Sequence this behind whatever bead holds it.

## Acceptance

The three rows describe the construction-time arms and the `:endpoint`-nil cases above. `check_doc_slugs.py` and `mkdocs build --strict` exit 0.

title: question(spec 002): is event-vector metadata carried from dispatch / :fx :dispatch to the handler's :event coeffect a documented contract? Only reply-append carriage is specified
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. This is a contract question, not a defect report.

## Spec file and section

- spec/002-Frames.md §Routing: the dispatch envelope (line 1218).
- spec/Managed-Effects.md §The reply target (line 92).

## What it says

- spec/002 :1218: "Event-vector metadata is not an opt-channel in v2; use the two-arg `(dispatch event opts)` form."
- spec/Managed-Effects :92: "…any metadata on that vector travels with the delivered event in every family, managed HTTP included; the runtime carries that metadata and reads none of it, because event-vector metadata is not an options channel".

## The question

v1 apps carry app-level guards on event-vector metadata, for example a `^{:app/origin :sso}` tag that a global interceptor checks. To migrate such a guard, an author needs to know whether these deliver the vector's metadata to the handler's `:event` coeffect and to interceptors:

- `(rf/dispatch ^{:k v} [:e])`;
- `(rf/dispatch-sync ^{:k v} [:e])`;
- `:fx [[:dispatch ^{:k v} [:e]]]`;
- `:dispatch-later`.

A downstream unit observed that the implementation keeps it. But the only specified carriage is the reply append (Managed-Effects :92; rf2-vo1dx and rf2-jd58y), and 002 :1218 reads like a warning not to rely on metadata at all. Forwarding recipes matter here too. The O-16 companion's addressed forward `(conj ev {:run …})` keeps metadata only because `conj` preserves it, and a guard survives a forwarding hop only when the forwarder builds on the original vector.

## Asked

Is metadata carriage through `dispatch` / `dispatch-sync` / `:fx` `:dispatch` / `:dispatch-later` a contract?

- **If yes:** state it in 002 §Routing beside :1218, the way Managed-Effects :92 does for replies.
- **If no:** the migration skill should say "move metadata-carried guards into the payload or the dispatch opts", and the forwarding recipes should not imply that metadata survives.

## Evidence

Observed on a ~170-file app's SSO design unit, where an origin guard rides event metadata through a forwarded event.
