- xray-replaces-10x.md:10: "Once the M-rule sweep reaches M-40 and a clean reload is verified, add the Xray dep + preload + `[data-rf-xray-host]` layout host".
- orchestrating §5: "mid-sweep there is **no clean per-file compile** — a worker that finishes its unit cannot prove it green in isolation".

## What happened (generic)

In a fanned-out migration, the Xray mount (dep, npm peers, preload, host) is naturally one unit. Per §5, that unit can only hand over a diff. Its failure modes are all compile-time and independent of app code:

- a wrong `:local/root`;
- missing `@xyflow/react` / `elkjs` (the LOUD build failure §2a describes);
- a preload namespace that does not resolve.

So they could be caught mid-sweep, but neither skill says how. They surface only at the single post-sweep gate, mixed in with every unit's errors.

The obvious shortcut does not work. `shadow-cljs compile app --config-merge '{:modules {:main {:entries [<preload-ns>]}}}'` cannot replace the module's entries, because shadow deep-merges the override and concatenates vectors. The build still pulls in the app's (uncompilable) entry namespace. This was observed on a ~170-file app.

## Evidence

- shadow-cljs 3.4.10, shadow/build.clj:329-334: the build config is `(util/reduce-> build-api/deep-merge (:config-merge cli-opts))`.
- shadow/build/api.clj:26-39: `deep-merge` on two vectors is `(->> (concat a b) (distinct) (into []))`, so `:entries` can only grow.
- shadow/cljs/devtools/api.clj:293: `(defn compile* [build-config opts] …)` compiles an arbitrary build-config map, so a replaced `:entries` is reachable from a REPL or script.
- A search of skills/re-frame-migration, skills/re-frame2-pair, skills/re-frame2 and docs/xray finds no preload-only compile recipe and no mention of `--config-merge` for this purpose.

## Suggested change

Add a short "mid-sweep check for the devtools unit" to xray-replaces-10x.md, cross-linked from orchestrating §5 as an example of a unit whose surface can be compiled before the sweep converges:

    ;; clj REPL on the project's classpath (shadow running or embedded)
    (require '[shadow.cljs.devtools.api :as shadow]
             '[shadow.cljs.devtools.config :as config])
    (-> (config/get-build! :app)
        (assoc-in [:modules :main :entries] ['day8.re-frame2-xray.preload])
        (dissoc :devtools)            ; no app :preloads pulled in
        (assoc :build-id :xray-check :output-dir "target/xray-check")
        (shadow/compile* {}))

The snippet is a sketch read from shadow-cljs source; it has not been run. Use the build's actual module id and the preload namespace the skill names. Say why `--config-merge` cannot do this (vectors append). Note that the same check works for the Pair preload. A clean compile here proves the dep, npm and preload wiring, not the mount, which still waits for M-40.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): test-layer table has no row for a fixture-less v1 test whose code under test subscribes; in v2 it throws no-frame-context unless a reset fixture with an :adapter supplies the ambient frame
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main d53a3faf09.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md §"Test-layer v1 API to v2 mapping" (lines 271-282).

## What it says

- :278: "`(ts/make-reset-runtime-fixture {:adapter adapter})` is the v2 per-test `:each` fixture that fills the same role — registrar / runtime isolation".
- Every row of the table is keyed on a v1 test-API surface the test ns already uses: the `day8.re-frame.test` require, `make-restore-fn`, `reg-event-db` in a fixture, or the post-event callbacks. A test ns that used none of them matches no row.

## What happened (generic)

In v1, a test needed no fixture to call code that subscribes or dispatches, because there was one global app-db. Under v2 (EP-0002; M-11, M-23), that code resolves its frame from the ambient scope. A fixture-less test has none, so each such call throws `:rf.error/no-frame-context`. On a ~170-file app's migrated test run, 8 of 9 errors were this.

The fix is the reset fixture with an `:adapter`, which also gives the test body its ambient frame. That role is nowhere in the table, so a census keyed on v1 test API never finds these namespaces.

## Evidence

- The quotes above.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:565-575 and :694-716: `:ambient-frame` is the frame the fixture establishes as `*current-frame*` around the test body when an adapter is installed. It defaults to `:rf/default`.
- `grep -i "ambient-frame\|fixture-less\|without a fixture"` over the skill's SKILL.md and references/ finds only the M-11 link anchor `#m-11--ambient-frame-reads-in-callbacks-…` (SKILL.md:87, auto-cross-cutting.md:374, breaking-changes.md:39, inventory-and-plan.md:96). None of them mentions the fixture's `:ambient-frame` option. The control `make-reset-runtime-fixture` finds 6 hits in auto-call-site-rewrites.md.

## Suggested change

- Add a row: "A test ns with no v1 test API whose code under test reaches subscribe, dispatch or capture-frame: install `(ts/make-reset-runtime-fixture {:adapter adapter})`. It supplies the ambient frame (`:ambient-frame`, default `:rf/default`)."
- Add a Phase-0a census line: check every test ns that has no reset fixture for whether its code path reaches a frame read.
- Say in the `make-restore-fn` row that the fixture provides the ambient frame as well as isolation.

## Also seen (adjacent)

The same file contradicts itself on `with-redefs`.

- :163: "a v1 `with-redefs` on `rf/dispatch` or `rf/subscribe` still compiles in v2 and intercepts nothing."
- :194: "`rf/subscribe` is a plain function on both hosts, so a redef of it does reach its callers."

One of the two should be corrected.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): causal-world-inputs' Generated identity ladder covers one id per event; a fold minting one id per row has no route, though docs/core/coeffects.md has the record-one-id recipe
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main d53a3faf09.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/causal-world-inputs.md §"UUID / random / browser / storage → event payloads or recordable facts", bullet "Generated identity (UUID)" (lines 110-136).

## What it says

- :110: "A durable entity id minted with `random-uuid` inside a handler is a world fact. The minting ladder's preferred rung is the **event payload**".
- :117: "When the id is genuinely fold-internal (no call site owns it), register a recordable generator", namely `(rf/reg-cofx :todo/id {:recordable? true} (fn [] (random-uuid)))`, which gives one value per event.
- :19: "a value-returning supplier sees only its own arg and **cannot read app-db**".

## What happened (generic)

v1 folds that parse or copy a collection often mint one id per item, for example `(mapv #(assoc % :id (random-uuid)) rows)`. The count depends on the payload, or on the db when the event runs. None of the ladder's rungs fits:

- The payload rung needs the caller to know the count.
- The generator rung yields a single value.
- The supplier cannot see the db to size its output.
- A parameterized `[id arg]` requires entry is fixed where the event is registered.

So the migrator either leaves `random-uuid` in the fold, which is a durable ambient read, or splits the fold into per-item child events, which loses atomicity. Observed on a ~170-file app, in an import fold that minted one id per parsed row.

## Evidence

- The quotes above.
- The framework already has the recipe. docs/core/coeffects.md §"When the number of ids depends on state" (around line 224, example at 234-256), mirrored in skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/cofx.md:97: one recordable coeffect supplies ONE fresh id, and the handler derives each item's id from it as plain data, `[copy-id i]`. Replay re-presents the one id. This was settled in rf2-v1xu2 (PR #10853), including why a seed is wrong (EP-0017: suppliers record values, never seeds) and why `hash` is avoided.
- `git grep -n -c "copy-id\|Durable join keys"` over skills/re-frame-migration finds nothing, while the same search finds docs/core/coeffects.md.

## Suggested change

Add a rung after the recordable generator:

> **Many ids in one fold** (a count the caller cannot know): record ONE fresh id, and derive each item's id as data from it plus a stable index, `[recorded-id i]`. See docs/core/coeffects.md §When the number of ids depends on state. Where the caller does know the count, a caller-minted vector of ids in the payload also works. Use per-item child events only when losing the fold's atomicity is acceptable.

Link the core recipe rather than restating it.

comments.text:
From a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (pass 7). This is a suggestion, not a work order. Verified at origin/main bafbe4028e.

This is a second observation on the same ~170-file app, from a different unit. One fold minted ids for SEVERAL row kinds at once, each with its own data-dependent count. causal-world-inputs.md:117-125 is unchanged at this tip and still covers one id per event.

The core recipe this item links, docs/core/coeffects.md §"When the number of ids depends on state" (:224-256), derives `[copy-id i]` for ONE kind of row. Applied once per kind, the derivations collide wherever the kinds share an id space: one server table, one lookup map, or the keys of a mixed list. Both kinds produce `[copy-id 0]`.

When this item's rung is added, it could say: "Record one fresh id per fold and give each kind a disjoint derivation, for example `[recorded-id :kind-a i]` and `[recorded-id :kind-b i]`, or record one fact per kind. If the ids must be UUIDs, put the kind into the derivation's input." The recipe's existing warning against `hash` still applies.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
From a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (pass 8). This is a suggestion, not a work order. Verified at origin/main e6cb299c58.

causal-world-inputs.md:107-139 still has no many-ids rung. The one commit to the file since bafbe4028e, 4b77ba24ef, touched only :5 and :20.

This is a third observation on the same ~170-file app, with a new shape: a LOAD / file-format MIGRATION path.

Loading a saved file runs the load event's migration steps, and these mint random UUIDs for entities. The number is data-dependent, spread across up to five sub-migrations, and only files saved at an old format version reach them. Two backwards-compatibility constraints apply:
- a re-saved file must store ids in the same form as today: independent random v4 UUIDs;
- a load must not drop entities.

## Why the core recipe does not fit here

1. **The derivation changes what is stored.**
   - `[copy-id i]` (docs/core/coeffects.md:244) is a vector, and the saved format needs UUIDs.
   - The recipe's UUID clause (:256-258, "derive them with a function that gives the same result on the JVM and in JavaScript, which rules out `hash`") names no function.
   - The app's own derivation adds the index into the recorded UUID's last 48-bit field. Within one load, the ids it yields share every other field.
   - The app's migration code builds one map with `zipmap` keyed by that id (checked at source). Two sub-migrations deriving from one recorded id collide without a lane per kind (pass 7's point), and the collision silently drops an entity.
2. **The rejected shapes assume a count from the db, not from the payload.** coeffects.md:262-269 and skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/cofx.md:109 (settled in rf2-v1xu2) reject:
   - "ids minted at the dispatch site (the count goes stale behind earlier queued edits)";
   - "a fixed oversized batch or one id per entity (records unused facts)".

   rf2-v1xu2's premise is a demand counted from the processing-start db. On a load path the payload the caller already holds (the file) bounds the count, so earlier queued edits cannot change it. A pool sized by that bound is never short, and its only cost is the unused recorded facts.
3. **With no route that fits, the mint stayed ambient.** The app's ruling: only legacy files reach the mint, and the current format never mints. The skill has no bucket for a durable read left ambient by ruling, so the reason is recorded only in the app's own tracker.

## Suggested addition when this item's rung lands

> **Load and format-migration paths.** Sometimes the payload the caller holds bounds the count (a file being loaded), and the stored ids must keep their random-UUID form. Then the caller mints a pool of that many fresh UUIDs, into the payload or as a provided fact in `:rf.cofx`, and the fold consumes them in order. Every id stays an independent random UUID, at the cost of unused recorded facts. Otherwise, record one id and derive from it, with a lane per kind.

Also consider scoping the recipe's "one id per entity" and "minted at the dispatch site" rejections (coeffects.md:262-269, cofx.md:109) to db-counted demand, which is the case rf2-v1xu2 settled.
